IDX.en_translation:
Wake up, wake up in the inner temple of my heart, O Mādhava, Kṛṣṇa, Gopāla! Like the fresh rising sun, wake up in my heart, O beautiful Giridhārī-lāla! 

Clouds of distress gather in my eyes. Wake up, wake up, O youthful dark Lord! Dearest to Śrīmati Rādhikā, wake up in my heart. Wake up, O Cowherd Boy of Vraja! 

O darling Son of Yaśodā! Come, O Butter-thief! O Deity of my life, come, O youthful Lord! With Rādhā on Your left, come into the Vraja of my heart, O Cowherd Boy of Vraja!

If you desire playful jokes and fun with your friends, Then heed my words, do not go, do not go, Near Keśītīrtha-ghāṭa in Mathurā. 

Assuming the form of Govinda, Hari is there, With a captivating glance in His eyes and a gentle smile on His face. What a beautiful three-fold bending posture, His complexion brilliantly dark, The beauty of new sprouts manifests on His divine limbs. 

The flute on His lips is the root cause of all unwanted things, Brother, do not even trust His peacock feather crown. Seeing that form with one's eyes, no one returns home, Indeed, it becomes complete ruin for the worldly householder. 

(Therefore, there is great fear in my heart) A great danger will occur, do not go, O worldly person, Near Keśītīrtha-ghāṭa in Mathurā.

IDX.en_translation:
May the Daughter of the Sun, the friend of the lotus, always purify me. She removes the calamity of the city of her brother Antaka (Yama). By her sight, she delivers even the great sinner from the ocean of sin. She binds the endless heart with the sweetness of her water. 

May the Daughter of the Sun, the friend of the lotus, always purify me. She adorned the great Khāṇḍava forest with her captivating stream of water. She has the dancing of rising flocks of birds in the circle of lotuses. She blinds the wealth of terrible sin of the wretches desiring to bathe. 

May the Daughter of the Sun, the friend of the lotus, always purify me. She crushes the bad destiny of the living beings touched by her spray. She increases the flood of intimate devotion to the Son of Nanda. She causes auspiciousness for those desiring the contact of her bank. 

May the Daughter of the Sun, the friend of the lotus, always purify me. She pierces the seven oceans visited by the circle of islands. She knows the great divine pastimes created by Śrī Mukunda. She mocks the multitude of sapphires with shoots of luster. 

May the Daughter of the Sun, the friend of the lotus, always purify me. She is adorned by the beautiful circle of Mathurā. She is expert in increasing the path of the Vaiṣṇavas bound by love. She worships the feet of Padmanābha with the play of her arms of waves. 

May the Daughter of the Sun, the friend of the lotus, always purify me. She is adorned with herds of cows mooing on her beautiful banks. She is smeared with the pollen of Kadamba flowers possessing divine fragrance. She rejoices in the contact of the group of devotees of the Son of Nanda. 

May the Daughter of the Sun, the friend of the lotus, always purify me. She is resounded by hundreds of thousands of swans with blooming wings and jasmine eyes. She is worshipped by the gods, Siddhas, and Kinnaras pierced by devotion. She destroys the bondage of birth by the scent of the wind on her bank. 

May the Daughter of the Sun, the friend of the lotus, always purify me. She is the form of Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, and Svaḥ (the three worlds) in the flood of water of spiritual pastimes. Even when glorified, she burns the core of the terrible sin of the proud. She has the scent of the broken body-ointments of the Son of the King of Cowherds. 

O Daughter of the Sun! O Devi! O Lotus-eyed one! Whoever praises you with this Octet with a satisfied mind, increase the flood of devotion of him who is active with pure waves and surrounded by all the gods, while liberating him from all sins.
IDX.es_translation:
Ella salva a quienes tienen que ir a la ciudad de su hermano Yamarāja (el señor de la muerte). Su mero darśhana libera a las personas más viles de un océano de pecados. Sus dulces aguas cautivan el corazón de todos. Que Yamunā-devī, la hija de Sūrya-deva [llamado en esta canción Aravinda-bandhu, el amigo de los lotos], me purifique siempre. 

Ella adorna el inmenso bosque Khāṇḍava de Indra con su encantadora corriente, y sobre sus florecidos lotos blancos danzan siempre aves como las aguzanieves. El mero deseo de bañarse en sus aguas [qué decir de bañarse en ellas] libera a un pecador de sus cuantiosos y terribles pecados. Que Yamunā-devī, la hija de Sūrya-deva, me purifique siempre. 

Una persona se libera de la reacción incluso del crimen más atroz con solo tocar una gota de sus aguas. Ella incrementa la corriente del rāgānugā-bhakti por Śhrī Nanda-nandana y otorga el máximo bien a quien simplemente desee residir en sus riberas. Que Yamunā-devī, la hija de Sūrya-deva, me purifique siempre. 

Ella es adorada por los continentes de la tierra, puesto que divide a los siete océanos (sin mezclarse con ellos, como ocurre con los ríos ordinarios), y es íntimo testigo de los divinos pasatiempos de Śhrī Mukunda. El color de sus aguas derrota al zafiro azul. Que Yamunā-devī, la hija de Sūrya-deva, me purifique siempre. 

Está ornamentada por la supremamente encantadora región de Mathurā-maṇḍala, e inspira expertamente a los vaiṣṇavas, que están llenos de prema, a avanzar en el sendero del rāgānugā-bhakti. Con sus olas, que son como juguetones brazos, ella adora los pies de loto de Padmanābha Śhrī Kṛṣṇa. Que Yamunā-devī, la hija de Sūrya-deva, me purifique siempre. 

Sus atractivas riberas están adornadas con grandes cantidades de mugientes vacas y son perfumadas por celestiales fragancias que emanan de las flores de hileras de árboles kadamba. Ella rebosa de alegría cuando los bhaktas de Śhrī Nanda-nandana se congregan [en dichas riberas]. Que Yamunā-devī, la hija de Sūrya-deva, me purifique siempre. 

Está saturada con el canto de cientos de miles de cisnes mallikākṣa que cantan dulcemente con las alas totalmente abiertas. Es adorada por devas, siddhas, kinnaras y por las personas cuyos corazones están dedicados al servicio de Śhrī Hari. El más leve contacto con la brisa de sus orillas libera de la atadura del renacimiento. Que Yamunā-devī, la hija de Sūrya-deva, me purifique siempre. 

Su corriente llena los tres mundos ―Bhuh, Bhuvah y Svah― con conocimiento trascendental (cid-vilāsa). Por hablar de sus glorias, los pecados más graves y arraigados son reducidos a cenizas. Ella se ha vuelto muy fragante debido a los ungüentos [como la pasta de sándalo y el kuṅkuma] procedentes del cuerpo de Ballavendra-nandana Kṛṣṇa. Que Yamunā-devī, la hija de Sūrya, me purifique siempre. 

¡Oh, Sūryaputri! ¡Oh, Devī! ¡Oh, Yamunā! Tus poderosas olas son purificadoras y estás rodeada por todos los semidioses. Mi súplica a tus pies es que aumentes la corriente del bhakti por Śhrī Kṛṣṇa, el de los ojos de loto, de las personas inteligentes y satisfechas que reciten esta oración.

O Mind! Worship the lotus feet of the Guru. Without the mercy of the Guru, there is no strength for sādhana; worship, O Mind, worship at every moment. Such a rare birth is not obtained [easily]; I wander in the fourteen worlds. By oh what fortune does one meet the sight of the devotees of Hari!

The blissful form of Kṛṣṇa's mercy, the reservoir of compassion for the destitute. He manifests Bhakti, Bhāva, and Prema—Śrī Guru is the savior of the fallen. 

In the Śruti, Smṛti, and Purāṇas, clear evidence is given. Offering body, mind, and life at the feet of the Guru—the constant chanting of the Holy Name.

IDX.en_translation:
O Lord Hari! When will that auspicious day be mine, when I will worship Śrī Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, becoming fully absorbed in divine love? 

I will blend my voice with beautiful instruments and sing sweet melodies, joyfully chanting the glories of Their divine forms and qualities. 

Crying out “Rādhikā-Govinda!”, I will weep loudly, and all my limbs will be drenched with tears. 

O Rūpa and Sanātana, please bestow your mercy! Raghunātha dāsa and Śrī Jīva are my very life. 

O Lalitā and Viśākhā, please bestow your mercy! And also Śrīdāma, Subala, and the other friends, in the mood of friendship. 

All of you together, please be merciful and fulfill my desire; Narottama dāsa always offers this prayer.
IDX.es_translation:
¡Oh, Hari! ¿Cuándo llegará ese auspicioso día en que serviré a Śhrī Śhrī Rādhā-Kṛsṇa desbordante de prema? 

Acompañado de instrumentos musicales, cantaré dulces melodías. Lleno de éxtasis, entonaré cantos en alabanza de la forma y las cualidades de la Pareja Divina. 

Cuando cante “Rādhikā-Govinda” lloraré intensamente y mi cuerpo entero quedará empapado con las lágrimas que brotarán de mis ojos. 

¡Oh, Rūpa Gosvāmī y Sanātana Gosvāmī! ¡Oh, Śhrī Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī! ¡Oh Śhrī Jīva Gosvāmī, mi vida y mi alma! ¡Denme su misericordia ahora! 

¡Oh, Lalitā y Viśhākhā! ¡Oh Śhrīdāma, Subala y demás amigos con sakhya-bhāva! ¡Denme su misericordia ahora! 

Todos ustedes juntos, sean por favor misericordiosos y permitan que mis deseos se cumplan. Narottama dāsa ora así constantemente.

IDX.en_translation:
On the banks of the Yamunā, in a kadamba forest—what did I see today, my friend! Śyāma, the flute-holder, upon a jeweled platform, performs His pastimes as the King of Mellows. 

Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes are a fountain of nectar. Upon an eight-petaled lotus are Śrī Rādhā and Śrī Hari, with their eight principal companions as attendants. 

With beautiful singing and dancing, all the companions please the Divine Couple. Seeing Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes, beautiful nature spreads its splendor through the forest. 

I will not go home; I will enter the forest for the sake of those pastimes and their nectar. Giving up family honor, worship the King of Vraja—this is Bhaktivinoda’s humble prayer.

IDX.en_translation:
If he had not assumed the form of Śrī Rūpa in this age of Kali, then who would have opened the doors to the storehouse of the great treasure of love for Vraja? 

Like the swan that separates milk from water, who would have provided the method for drinking the essence? Who would have abandoned everything to worship Vṛndāvana and composed all those scriptures? 

When the many flowers in the Father’s garden were in full bloom, like a row of lotus-hearts—without that bumblebee, who would have known how to drink the nectar or how to capture it? 

Who would have known Mathurā and Vṛndāvana? Who would have known the proper behavior in Vraja? Who would have known the love for Rādhā and Mādhava? Who would have known that love? 

By the mercy of his feet, everyone now sings and causes others to sing, finding happiness. At his lotus feet, Mādhava dāsa has taken shelter; your glories are held within my heart.
IDX.es_translation:
Si Rūpa Gosvāmī no hubiese aparecido en esta era de Kali, ¿quién habría abierto el valioso caudal del vraja-prema? 

¿Quién excepto Śhrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī podía haber extraído la esencia de las escrituras igual que un cisne separa el agua de la leche? ¿Quién hubiera podido abandonarlo todo para hacer bhajana en Vṛndāvana? ¿Quién hubiera podido escribir esas obras sagradas? 

Él era una abeja entre multitud de flores silvestres amarillas y encantadores lotos. Sin esa abeja, ¿quién hubiera sabido libar el néctar confinado en esas flores? 

¿Quién hubiera comprendido las glorias de Mathurā y Vrṇdāvana? ¿Quién hubiera entendido las complejidades de Vraja? ¿Quién hubiera podido entender el rati entre Śrī Rādhā y Mādhava? ¿Quién hubiera sabido de ese amor? 

Por la misericordia de sus pies de loto, todas las almas pueden cantar e inspirar a otros a que canten (acerca de las glorias del amor de Śhrī Rādhā-Mādhava), y alcanzar la dicha suprema. (Oh, Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī) Rendido a tus pies de loto, este Mādhava dāsa ora por comprender tus ilimitadas glorias.

IDX.en_translation:
O Lord Kṛṣṇa! I bow to You. Please offer the bee of my mind into the honey of the lotus of Your own feet. 

Although even Brahmā in trance does not see the ray of the tip of Your nail, O Acyuta! Hearing this, still I desire that wonderful wave of mercy. 

Although, O Mādhava! Not even a sesame seed of devotion rises in me towards You; still, Your supreme Lordship is the arranger of the most impossible events. 

O Eternal One! May this mind, having attained a weight of wonderful rasa today, reside here eternally with unwavering steadiness, finding the essence of sweetness that mocks nectar.

IDX.translation_intro: From The Harmonist, January 1928. Edited by Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī.
IDX.en_translation:
Mind, body, family, whatever is mine, Youthful Son of Nanda, I tender at Thy feet. 

In weal and woe, in life and death, I am relieved of all anxiety, preferring those feet of Thine. 

Save me or slay me as Thou wilt’st, Thou art the Master of Thy eternal servant. 

If it be Thy will to cause me to be born May I have birth in the home of Thy devotee. 

In the dwelling of Thy servant may I be born a worm, I have no desire to be born a Brahma averse to Thee. 

I crave the boon of the society of Thy devotee Who is without a particle of desire for enjoyment or freedom from misery. 

All I find in Thee,--father, mother, lover, son, Lord, preceptor, husband. 

“Hear, O Kan”, says Bhakti-vinode, “Lord of Radha, Thou art my life.”
IDX.es_translation:
¡Oh, joven hijo de Nanda! Yo ofrezco a Tus pies de loto mi mente, mi cuerpo, mi familia y todo cuanto poseo! 

En la fortuna y en el infortunio, en la vida y en la muerte, todas mis dificultades han huido al aceptar Tus pies [como mi refugio]. 

Puedes destruirme o protegerme, pues eres el propiertario de Tu eterno sirviente. 

Si por Tu deseo debo nacer otra vez, permite que lo haga en el hogar de Tu devoto. 

No me importa nacer como gusano siempre y cuando siga siendo Tu devoto. No deseo nacer como Brahmā si voy a ser contrario a Ti. 

Yo anhelo la compañía de ese devoto que carece por completo de los deseos del disfrute mundano o la liberación. 

Padre, madre, amante, hijo, amo, preceptor y esposo; Tú lo eres todo para mí. 

Bhaktivinoda dice: “¡Oh Kāna, por favor escúchame! ¡Oh Señor de Rādhā, Tú eres toda mi vida!”

IDX.en_translation:
O You who are worshiped by the greatest of sages and who remove the sorrow of the three worlds! O You whose lotus-like face is always cheerful and who sport in the groves of Vraja! O daughter of Vṛṣabhānu and companion of the son of Nanda—when will You make me an object of Your merciful sidelong glance? 

Residing in a bower of aśoka trees and creepers, with tender feet as soft and reddish as new coral sprouts—Your hands show the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, and You are a treasure house of vast wealth. When will You make me an object of Your merciful sidelong glance? 

With playful, graceful, and auspiciously arching eyebrows—by whose swift and bewildering glances the son of Nanda is continually captivated and brought under control—when will You make me an object of Your merciful sidelong glance? 

Your golden form shines brightly like lightning and golden flowers, and Your facial effulgence surpasses millions of autumn moons. Your eyes are like a pair of playful young chakora birds moving in wondrous ways. When will You make me an object of Your merciful sidelong glance? 

In the height of intoxicating youth and adorned with joyful honor, You are dyed with the hue of Your beloved's affection and are adept in artistic pastimes. You are skilled in the amorous sports of the matchlessly blessed kingdom of groves. When will You make me an object of Your merciful sidelong glance? 

Adorned with a necklace of perfect, firm, and priceless pearls representing all kinds of emotional expressions, Your breasts are firm and beautiful like golden pitchers. You are a full ocean of happiness due to Your auspicious, gentle, and sweet smile. When will You make me an object of Your merciful sidelong glance? 

Your beautiful arms move like waves of lotus stalks and vines, and Your restless blue eyes are like the dancing tips of creepers. You are the enchanting and bewildering shelter for all swaying and mingling minds. When will You make me an object of Your merciful sidelong glance? 

our conch-like neck is marked with three lines and adorned with golden necklaces, and Your three-stranded auspicious thread shines with the luster of three jewels. Your flowing blue tresses are woven with bunches of flowers. When will You make me an object of Your merciful sidelong glance? 

Your hips are adorned with a hanging flower girdle, and You are supremely charming amidst an array of beautiful tiny bells. Your thighs are beautiful like the descending trunk of an elephant. When will You make me an object of Your merciful sidelong glance? 

Your anklets emit charming melodies with Their musical sounds, and Your graceful movements possess the dignity of royal swans. Your beautiful gait imitates a swaying golden vine. When will You make me an object of Your merciful sidelong glance? 

Worshiped by Brahmā, who is humble before millions of spiritual planets, You bestow boons upon Pārvatī, Indrāṇī, and Sarasvatī. Your toenails are smeared with immense perfections and opulences. When will You make me an object of Your merciful sidelong glance? 

O Queen of sacrifices! O Mistress of activities! O Goddess of the gods! O Mistress of the threefold Vedic knowledge! O Mistress of authoritative scriptures! O Queen of beauty! O Goddess of forgiveness! O Mistress of the forest of joy! O Queen of Vraja! O Supreme Ruler of Vraja! O Śrī Rādhā! I offer my obeisances to You! 

Hearing this wonderful prayer, may the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu always make her devotee an object of Her merciful sidelong glance. Then all accumulated karma will be destroyed, and one will enter the assembly of the son of Nanda. 

A wise reader who, with a pure mind, recites this on the auspicious days of the month will attain whatever desire he cherishes. By Rādhā’s merciful sidelong glance, his devotion will become endowed with the symptoms of divine love. 

The devotee who recites this a hundred times while standing in the water of Rādhā-kuṇḍa attains all perfection for his desired ends, the power of speech, and all opulence, and he sees Rādhā with his own eyes. 

Being pleased, She immediately bestows a great boon by which one sees the beloved Kṛṣṇa with his own eyes. And the Lord of Vraja bestows entrance into His eternal pastimes. There is nothing greater than this to be attained by the devotees.
IDX.es_translation:
¡Oh, Śhrīmatī Rādhikā! Tú eres glorificada por grandes sabios y destruyes la lamentación de los tres mundos. Tu rostro de loto florece con una encantadora sonrisa y retozas en los kuñjas. ¡Oh, amada hija del Rey Vṛṣabhānu! Tú eres la más amada del hijo del rey de Vraja. ¿Cuándo me convertirás en el objeto de Tu misericordiosa mirada de soslayo? 

Tu moras en un dosel hecho de enredaderas que se ensortijan alrededor de árboles aśhoka; Tus hermosos y tiernos pies de loto tienen el color del coral y de hojas rojizas recién nacidas, y Tu mano otorga bendiciones e intrepidez. ¡Oh, morada de infinita opulencia! ¿Cuándo me convertirás en el objeto de Tu misericordiosa mirada de soslayo? 

En el escenario del solaz amoroso, en el transcurso de una auspiciosa discusion, Tú expresas asombro curvando Tus cejas como arcos, y cuando entonces lanzas las flechas de Tus miradas de soslayo, atraviesas al hijo de Śhrī Nanda con vanas esperanzas amorosas y de ese modo Él permanece eternamente bajo Tu control. ¿Cuándo me convertirás en el objeto de Tu misericordiosa mirada de soslayo? 

Tu radiante y dorada forma se asemeja al relámpago, al oro y a las flores champaka; Tu rostro de loto derrota el esplendor del brillo de millones de lunas otoñales, y Tus ojos, inquietos como los de un joven pájaro chakora, muestran nuevas y sorprendentes expresiones a cada momento. ¿Cuándo me convertirás en el objeto de Tu misericordiosa mirada de soslayo? 

Estás intoxicada con Tu juventud y decorada con Tu delicioso ornamento del enfado. Te regocijas en el apego de Tu amado por Ti, y eres supremamente experta en el arte del amor. En el reino de Tus confidenciales y maravillosos kuñjas, eres la más sabia en el conocimiento de juegos amorosos. ¿Cuándo me convertirás en el objeto de Tu misericordiosa mirada de soslayo? 

Estás decorada con los ornamentos del anubhāva, como el hāva y el bhāva, y un collar de diamantes de dulzura y gravedad. Tus pechos son como cántaros de agua de oro puro y se asemejan a los montículos en la cabeza de un elefante. ¡Oh Tú, cuya gloriosa y tierna sonrisa es como un océano de bienaventuranza! ¿Cuándo me convertirás en el objeto de Tu misericordiosa mirada de soslayo? 

Tus brazos son como los tiernos tallos de un loto que se mece sobre las olas. La mirada de Tus azules ojos recuerda a las enredaderas danzando en el viento. Tú haces que Mana-mohana Te siga y, cuando Te reúnes con Él, Le robas la mente y Lo refugias en Su estado de encantamiento. ¿Cuándo me convertirás en el objeto de Tu misericordiosa mirada de soslayo? 

Tu cuello está marcado con tres líneas —al igual que una caracola—, y adornado con collares dorados y un auspicioso tri-sūtra, <highlight>(El maṅgala-tri-sutra es un collar especial que llevan las jóvenes casadas para tener buenos auspicios)</highlight> del que cuelgan tres clases de brillantes joyas. Tus trenzas de color negro azulado y entretejidas con ramilletes de capullos de flores se balancean de un lado a otro. ¿Cuándo me convertirás en el objeto de Tu misericordiosa mirada de soslayo? 

De Tus redondeadas caderas cuelga una espiral de encantadoras flores. Tu cautivadora y delgada cintura está adornada con un espléndido cinturón de diminutas campanillas engastadas que tintinean dulcemente. Tus hermosos muslos se estrechan como la trompa del rey de los elefantes. ¿Cuándo me convertirás en el objeto de Tu misericordiosa mirada de soslayo? 

Tus campanitas tobilleras resuenan dulcemente como una letanía de mantras védicos y se parecen al gorjeo de una bandada de cisnes reales. La belleza de Tus andares se burla de los movimientos de una ondulante enredadera dorada. ¿Cuándo me convertirás en el objeto de Tu misericordiosa mirada de soslayo? 

¡Oh Tu, que eres adorada por Lakṣmī-devī —la diosa de ilimitados planetas Vaikuṇṭha— y otorgas bendiciones a Śhrī Pārvatī, Indrāṇī y Sarasvatī! Una sola de las uñas de Tus pies de loto confiere una variedad infinita de perfecciones espirituales. ¿Cuándo me convertirás en el objeto de Tu misericordiosa mirada de soslayo? 

Eres la dueña de todo tipo de sacrificios, de todas las acciones, de los mantras pronunciados en los yajñas, de todos los semidioses, de las enseñanzas de los tres Vedas, de la imposición de todos los principios de las escrituras, de la diosa de la fortuna, de la clemencia y de los deliciosos bosques [de Vṛndāvana]. ¡Oh dueña y emperatriz de Vraja! ¡Oh, Śhrīmatī Rādhikā! Yo te ofrezco mi praṇāma. 

¡Oh, hija de Vṛṣabhānu! Al escuchar esta maravillosa oración, haz que me convierta en el perpetuo objeto de Tu misericordiosa mirada de soslayo. Por Tu misericordia, mis tres clases de karma <highlight>(Las reacciones acumuladas, las reacciones que están dando fruto y las reacciones de las actividades presentes)</highlight> serán destruidas, y en ese momento entraré en el círculo del hijo del rey de Vraja y Sus queridas sakhīs.  

Un lector sensible que, con una mente pura, recite estos versos en los días auspiciosos del mes, verá cumplido cualquier deseo que albergue. Gracias a la misericordiosa mirada de soslayo de Rādhā, su devoción se verá dotada de los síntomas del amor divino. 

El devoto que recite esto cien veces mientras se encuentra de pie en las aguas de Rādhā-kuṇḍa alcanza toda la perfección para sus fines deseados, el poder de la palabra y toda opulencia, y ve a Rādhā con sus propios ojos. 

Complacida, Ella otorga de inmediato una gran bendición mediante la cual uno ve al amado Kṛṣṇa con sus propios ojos. Y el Señor de Vraja otorga la entrada a Sus pasatiempos eternos. No existe nada más grande que puedan alcanzar los devotos que esto. {3Q.json}

IDX.en_translation:
In Nadiyā, on the island of Godruma, the great soul Nityānanda has established a marketplace of the Holy Name for the sake of all living beings. 

“O faithful people! By the order of the Lord, O brothers, I beg this alms of you: chant Kṛṣṇa’s name, worship Kṛṣṇa, and follow Kṛṣṇa’s teachings. 

“Being free from offenses, chant the name of Kṛṣṇa. Kṛṣṇa is your mother, Kṛṣṇa is your father, and Kṛṣṇa is your wealth and your very life. 

“Live your life for Kṛṣṇa, giving up all sinful activities. Compassion for all souls and the chanting of Kṛṣṇa’s name—this is the essence of all religious principles.”
IDX.es_translation:
En la isla de Godruma, en la región de Nadiyā, la magnánima personalidad Śhrī Nityānanda Prabhu ha abierto el mercado del santo nombre para beneficio de todos los seres vivos. 

[Allí, Él llama:] “(¡Oh, gentes de fe, gentes de fe!) Por orden de Śhrī Gaurāṅga, oh hermanos, Yo imploro esta limosna de ustedes: canten los nombres de Kṛṣṇa, adoren a Kṛṣṇa y sigan las instrucciones de Kṛṣṇa.” 

“Canten los santos nombres de Kṛṣṇa sin ofensas. Kṛṣṇa es nuestra madre, Kṛṣṇa es nuestro padre y Kṛṣṇa es el tesoro de nuestras vidas.” 

“Abandonen la conducta pecaminosa y sitúen a Kṛṣṇa en el centro de sus vidas. La esencia de todas las religiones es mostrar compasión hacia todos los seres vivos y cantar los santos nombres de Kṛṣṇa.”

neche neche gāy re bhakativinoda taṅ’ra paḍe rāṅgā pāya re
IDX.en_translation:
In the town of Nadiyā, Nitāi dances and sings. 

He is the son of Jagannātha, Mahāprabhu Viśvambhara, the moon of Māyāpur and the nectar-moon of Navadvīpa. 

He is the son of Śacī, Gaura⋅ hari, the beautiful Nimāi—the supreme dancer covered by the mood and splendor of Rādhā. 

He is a restless boy full of the bliss of the Holy Name and devoted to His mother. He is the one whose mouth holds the universe, a debater fond of playful mischief. 

He is the charming one who stole from two student thieves, the all-in-all for pilgrims, and the one who played with village girls. 

He is the giver of boons to Lakṣmī and an arrogant boy. He is the remover of Śrī Śacī’s grief for her husband and son. 

He is the husband of Lakṣmī and the remover of all distress in the eastern countries. He is the remover of the pride of world-conquerors and the Lord of Viṣṇupriyā. 

He is the protector of the Aryan path and the one who offered rice balls in Gayā to His father. He is the disciple of Īśvara Purī and the protector of the Madhvāchārya tradition. 

He is mad with Kṛṣṇa’s name and the teacher of the Absolute Truth. He is the initiator of the congregational chanting of the Holy Name, the dharma for this age. 

He is the friend of Advaita and the household treasure of Śrīnivāsa. He is the life of Nityānanda and Gadādhara. 

He is the moon of Antardvīpa and the victor over Sīmanta. He is the wanderer of Godruma and the abode of pastimes in Madhyadvīpa. 

He is the Lord of Koladvīpa and the great Lord of Ṛtudvīpa. He is the Lord of Jahnu, Modadruma, and Rudradvīpa. 

He is the enjoyer of Navakhaṇḍa and the life of the Jāhnavī. He is the deliverer of wicked ones like Jagāi and Mādhāi. 

He is the lion of congregational chanting in the streets and the deliverer of the Kazi. He is the preacher of the pure Name and the remover of the devotees’ distress. 

He is the ocean of Nārāyaṇī’s mercy and the controller of all beings. He is the punisher of wicked students and the destroyer of the devotees’ faults. 

He is Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanyacandra, the deliverer of Keśava Bhāratī. He is the crest-jewel of wandering mendicants and the purifier of Utkala. 

He is the Lord of Ambulinga, Bhuvaneśa, and Kapoteśa. He is the ascetic who is happy to behold the Deity of Gopāla. 

He is the merciful one who accepted renunciation, the great scholar Sārvabhauma. He is the one who enjoys His own bliss and the shelter of all happiness. 

He is beautiful as pure gold and the savior of Vāsudeva. He is the friend of Rāmānanda and the remover of the Bhaṭṭa family's distress. 

He is the defeater of the bad arguments of Buddhists, Jains, and impersonalists. He is the purifier of the South and the upholder of devotional scriptures. 

He is the one who enjoys seeing the Deity of Ālālanātha and the dancer in front of the chariot. He is the savior of King Pratāparudra and the deliverer of Devānanda. 

He is the savior of wicked students by His manifestation in Kuliyā. He is the friend of Rūpa and Sanātana and the life of all beings. 

He is the embodiment of Vṛndāvana’s bliss and the companion of Balabhadra. He is the deliverer of the Yavanas and playful with Vallabha Bhaṭṭa. 

He is the giver of divine love and the deliverer of the renunciants of Kāśī. He is the punisher of monkey-like renunciants and the savior of everyone down to the most fallen outcasts. 

He is the one who glorifies His devotees and is the treasure of their lives. He is the life of Haridāsa, Raghunātha, and Svarūpa. 

In the town of Nadiyā, Nitāi dances and sings. Bhaktivinoda falls at His beautiful reddish feet.

āgaye chīra baḍhaiyā re, bhaja kṛṣṇa kanhaiyā
IDX.en_translation:
He will take our boat across; worship Kṛṣṇa Kanhaiyā, the beloved younger brother of Balarāma. Kṛṣṇa Kanhaiyā plays the flute and is the butter thief; worship Kṛṣṇa Kanhaiyā. 

Kṛṣṇa Kanhaiyā lifted Govardhana Hill and performed the rāsa dance. He will take our boat across; worship Kṛṣṇa Kanhaiyā. 

His friend Sudāmā brought a small quantity of rice; the Lord embraced him and partook of the offering. Say where He is, my brother, and worship Kṛṣṇa Kanhaiyā. 

He drove Arjuna’s chariot in battle—the dark-complexioned lifter of the hill, the enchanting Lord. He subdued the serpent Kāliya; worship Kṛṣṇa Kanhaiyā. 

When Draupadī was surrounded by wicked men, He protected her honor without delay. He came and extended her sari; worship Kṛṣṇa Kanhaiyā.

IDX.first_line: pāyo jī mhe to kṛṣṇa ratana dhana pāyo
IDX.search: payo ji mhe to krsna ratana dhana payo vastu amoka di mhare sataguru kirapa kara apanayo janama janamaki puji pai jagame sabhi khovayo kharachai na koi chora na levai dina dina badhata savayo
IDX.author: mīrābāi
IDX.verses: pāyo jī mhe to kṛṣṇa ratana dhana pāyo vastu amoka dī mhāre sataguru, kirapā kara apanāyo janama janamakī pū̐jī pāī, jagame̐ sabhī khovāyo kharachai na koī chora na levai, dina⋅ dina baḍhata savāyo satakī nāva khaivaṭiyā sataguru, bhavasāgara tara āyo mīrāke prabhu giridhara nāgara, harakha harakha jasa gāyo
IDX.en_translation:
O! I have found the treasure of the jewel of Lord Kṛṣṇa’s Name. My true Spiritual Master gave me this priceless thing and accepted me with grace. 

I have received the capital of many births and lost everything else in this world. No one can spend this treasure, no thief can take it away, and it increases day by day, growing ever more. 

With the boat of truth and my Spiritual Master as the helmsman, I have crossed the ocean of material existence. Mīrā’s Lord is Kṛṣṇa, the lifter of Govardhana Hill, and she joyfully sings His praises.

IDX.first_line: ‘rādhā kṛṣṇa’ bal bal bala re sabāi
IDX.search: radha krsna bal bal bala re sabai ei siksa diya saba nadiya fircḣe neche gaura nitai micḣe mayara vase jaccḣa bhese khaccḣa habudubu bhai jiva krsna dasa e visvasa karle ta ara duhkha nai krsna balbe jabe pulaka habe jharbe ankhi bali tai
IDX.author: sacchidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses: ‘rādhā⋅ kṛṣṇa’ bal bal bala re sabāi (ei) śhikṣā diyā, saba nadīyā, fircḣe neche gaura⋅ nitāi (micḣe) māyāra vaśhe’ jāccḣa bhese’, khāccḣa hābuḍubu, bhāi (jīva) kṛṣṇa-dāsa, e viśhvāsa, kar’le ta’ āra duḥkha nāi (kṛṣṇa) balbe jabe, pulaka ha’be, jha’rbe aṅkhi, bali tāi (rādhā⋅) kṛṣṇa bala, saṅge chala, eimātra bhikṣā chāi (yāya) sakala vipada, bhaktivinoda, balena, jakhana o⋅ nāma gāi
IDX.en_translation:
Chant “Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa!”, everyone! Giving this teaching, Gaura and Nitāi are dancing through all of Nadiyā. Falsely under the sway of illusion, you are floating away and drowning, my brothers. 

Have faith that every soul is a servant of Kṛṣṇa; if you do, there will be no more sorrow. When you chant Kṛṣṇa’s name, your body will thrill with ecstasy and tears will fall from your eyes—I tell you this is true. 

Chant “Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa!” and come along with me; this is all I beg of you. Bhaktivinoda says: all dangers depart when that Name is sung.
IDX.es_translation:
“¡Canten todos, canten, canten los santos nombres de Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa!” Śhrī Gaurāṅga Mahāprabhu y Nityānanda Prabhu danzan por todo Navadvīpa impartiendo esta instrucción a todos. “¡Oh, hermanos! Están atrapados en el remolino de la ilusoria māyā y luchan desesperadamente por mantenerse a flote.” 

“Si tan solo desarrollan fe en que la jīva es una sirviente de Kṛṣṇa, no sufrirán nunca más. En cuanto pronuncien el nombre de Kṛṣṇa, sus cuerpos temblarán de éxtasis y de sus ojos brotarán lágrimas.” 

Bhaktivinoda dice: “¡Oh, hermanos! Tan solo canten los nombres de Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa en la asociación de vaiṣṇavas. Esta es mi única súplica. Cuando canten Sus santos nombres, todas sus tribulaciones desaparecerán.”

IDX.title: rādhā-nāma parama sukhadāi
IDX.search: radhanama parama sukhadai lahara lahara sri syama jiu ki mana me mere samai rata rata radha janama vitau raja gopina ku sisa navau mahima kahi nahi jai
IDX.author: traditional hindi bhajana
IDX.verses:
rādhānāma parama sukhadāi
lahara⋅ lahara śhrī śhyāmā jiu kī,
mana me mere samāī 

raṭa⋅ raṭa rādhā janama vitāū̐,
raja⋅ gopīna ku śhīṣa navāū̐,
mahimā kahi nāhī̐ jāi 

vraja tyaja ke mai̐ kahi nahi jāū̐,
rasika santana ke darśhana pāū̐,
jaga se prīti haṭāi
IDX.en_translation:
The name of Rādhā gives supreme happiness. Wave after wave of divine Rādhā has entered and resides in my heart. 

Chanting Rādhā’s name repeatedly, I will spend my life; I will bow my head to the dust of the gopīs, for their glory cannot be expressed. 

Never will I abandon Vraja, nor will I go anywhere else. I will attain the sight of the saintly devotees who appreciate divine mellows, for I have removed my affection from the world.

IDX.title: śrī maṅgala⋅gītam
IDX.search: radhe krsna govinda gopala nanda dulala yasoda dulala jaya jaya deva hare srita kamalakucha mandala dhrta kundala e kalita lalita vanamala jaya jaya deva hare
IDX.author: jayadeva gosvāmī
IDX.verses: (rādhe kṛṣṇa govinda gopāla nanda-dulāla yaśhodā-dulāla jaya jaya deva! hare) śhrita-kamalākucha-maṇḍala! dhṛta-kuṇḍala! e kalita-lalita-vanamālā! jaya jaya deva! hare dina-maṇi-maṇḍala-maṇḍana! bhava-khaṇḍana! e muni-jana-mānasa-haṁsa! jaya jaya deva! hare kālīya-viṣa-dhara-gañjana! jana-rañjana! e yadu-kula-nalina-dineśha! jaya jaya deva! hare madhu-mura-naraka-vināśhana! garuḍāsana! e sura-kula-keli-nidāna! jaya jaya deva! hare amala-kamala-dala-lochana! bhava-mochana! e tri-bhuvana-bhavana-nidhāna! jaya jaya deva! hare janaka-sutā-kṛta-bhūṣaṇa! jita-dūṣaṇa! e samara-śhamita-daśhakaṇṭha! jaya jaya deva! hare abhinava-jaladhara-sundara! dhṛta-mandara! e śhrī-mukha-chandra-chakora! jaya jaya deva! hare tava charaṇe praṇatā vayam iti bhāvaya e kuru kuśhalaṁ praṇateṣu jaya jaya deva! hare śhrī-jayadeva-kaver idaṁ kurute mudam maṅgalam-ujjvala-gītaṁ jaya jaya deva! hare
IDX.en_translation:
Commonly sung refrain 

O You who take shelter of the round breasts of Kamala, O You whose ears are decorated with earrings and who wears an enchanting garland of forest flowers, O Deva, O Hari, may You be triumphant! 

O ornament of the sun globe, O You who severs the bondage of material existence, O swan who sports in the [lake of the] sages’ minds, O Deva, O Hari, may You be triumphant! 

O You who pulverize the pride of the venomous snake Kāliya, O You who delight the people [of Vraja], O sun that makes the lotus of the Yadu dynasty bloom, O Deva, O Hari, may You be triumphant! 

O destroyer of the demons Madhu, Mura, and Naraka, O You who ride upon Garuḍa and who inspire the demigods’ delightful play, O Deva, O Hari, may You be triumphant! 

O You whose wide eyes resemble the petals of an immaculate lotus, O You who bestow emancipation from material existence and who are the foundation of the three worlds, O Deva, O Hari, may You be triumphant! 

O You who are decorated by the daughter of King Janaka (Sītā-devī), O You who defeated the demon Dūṣaṇa and killed the ten-headed Rāvaṇa in battle, O Deva, O Hari, may You be triumphant! 

O You whose complexion is lustrous like a fresh raincloud, O You who hold the Mandara Mountain and who are the cakora bird incessantly attached to the moonlike face of Śrī Rādhā, O Deva, O Hari, may You be triumphant! 

O Lord, we have taken exclusive refuge at Your lotus feet. Please bestow auspiciousness upon Your surrendered servants [by blessing us with prema-bhakti], O Deva, O Hari, may You be triumphant! 

May this radiant and auspicious song composed by Śrī Jayadeva increase happiness [for You and for Your devotees who hear and recite it], O Deva, O Hari, may You be triumphant!

Śrī Govardhana Mahārāja, a crown shines on your head. 

Earrings adorn your ears, and a Vaijayantī garland is around your neck... 

A flute looks beautiful on your lips, and a diamond adorns your chin. 

A saffron-colored garment is on your body, and a red waistband, like red powder. 

Betel leaves and flowers are offered to you, and lamps burn for you day and night... 

The sacred Mānasī-Gaṅgā lake flows nearby, and streams of milk are offered to you... Your seven-kosa circumambulation is glorious, and the Lord of Cakaleśvara resides there.

IDX.en_translation:
On the holy day of Hari-vāsara, according to the rules of Hari-kīrtana, the Lord, the life of the universe, began to dance. 

In the courtyard of the virtuous Śrīvāsa, an auspicious beginning was made. The sound of kīrtana arose—'Gopāla', 'Govinda'. 

Mṛdaṅga, mandirā, conch, and karatālas played. All were mixed together in the saṅkīrtana. 

The sound pierced the universe, filling the sky. All inauspiciousness in the four directions was destroyed. 

From dawn, Viśvambhara danced. Groups of beautiful singers formed. 

Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita took one group, and Mukunda sang with another group. 

Taking Govinda Ghoṣa and others, everyone performed kīrtana during Gaura⋅ candra's dance. 

The mighty Nityānanda walked holding Him, while Advaita stealthily took the dust of His feet. 

Gadādhara and others, with tearful eyes, became overwhelmed with bliss in the Lord's kīrtana. 

When Lord Viśvambhara danced wildly, the earth trembled and everyone was afraid. 

Sometimes Viśvambhara danced sweetly, as if one were seeing Nanda's son, the best of dancers (Naṭavara). 

Wonderful absorption in Kṛṣṇa, wonderful dancing. All the servants watched with eyes full of joy. 

Mahāprabhu Viśvambhara danced in His own bliss. Hearing the rhythm of His feet was very enchanting. 

Due to the intensity of emotion, the garland did not stay on His neck. It broke and fell at the feet of the devotees. 

On all four sides was the auspicious saṅkīrtana of Śrī Hari. In the center danced the son of Jagannātha Miśra. 

In the bliss of whose name, Śiva forgets his clothing. For whose fame Śiva dances, He dances Himself. 

By whose name Vālmīki became rich in austerity. By whose name Ajāmila attained liberation. 

By hearing whose name, the bondage of material existence is cut. Such a Lord, having incarnated, dances in Kali-yuga. 

Singing whose name, Śuka and Nārada wander. The thousand-mouthed Lord sings whose qualities. 

The greatest atonement for all sins is the name of that Lord. That Lord dances, and the fortunate ones see it. 

Seeing the Lord's bliss, the devotees embraced one another and wept. 

Garlands of sandalwood paste shone on everyone's limbs. They sang in joy, forgetting themselves in the mellows of Kṛṣṇa. 

All the Vaiṣṇavas, absorbed in kīrtana, did not know their own bodies, what to speak of others. 

'Jaya Kṛṣṇa, Murāri, Mukunda, Vanamālī!' Day and night everyone sang, full of enthusiasm. 

Day and night Viśvambhara danced with the devotees. No one had fatigue; everyone had spiritual bodies. 

In this way, Mahāprabhu Viśvambhara danced. Only one prahara (3 hours) of the night remained. 

Such bliss took place in the town of Navadvīpa. The hero of Vaikuṇṭha sported in the mellows of love. 

Whoever hears all these sacred topics, may his mind remain with Gaura⋅ candra and His devotees. 

Know Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya and Nityānanda Cānd. Vṛndāvana Dāsa sings at Their lotus feet.
IDX.es_translation:
En Ekādaśhī, Mahāprabhu, que es la vida y el alma del universo, decretó hari-kirtana y comenzó a bailar en éxtasis. 

En el patio del piadoso Śhrīvāsa, reverberan sonoramente los auspiciosos sonidos del kīrtana —¡Gopāla! ¡Govinda! 

Los sonidos de la mṛdaṅga, la mandirā (címbalos pequeños), la caracola y los karatālas armonizan bellamente con el saṅkīrtana. 

4 Śhrī hari-vāsara significa ‘ el día del Señor Hari ‘, y hace referencia al Ekādaśhī, el Dvādaśhī o el día de la aparición del Señor. El atronador sonido penetra el universo, llena la totalidad del cielo y destruye todo lo desfavorable en las cuatro direcciones. 

Al amanecer, Viśhvambhara danza mientras los grupos [de kīrtana] cantan de un modo encantador. 

Śhrīvāsa Paṇḍita lidera un grupo, y muchos otros cantan con Mukunda Datta. 

El grupo de Govinda Ghoṣa es aún más numeroso. Cuando Gaura-chandra danza, todos hacen kīrtana. 

El poderoso Nityānanda Prabhu sostiene a Mahāprabhu y Lo acaricia suavemente, mientras Advaita Āchārya toma secretamente el polvo de Sus pies. 

Con los ojos anegados en lágrimas, Gadādhara y los demás se sienten embargados por una dicha trascendental debido al kīrtana de Mahāprabhu. 

Viśhvambhara danza con tal fuerza, que la tierra tiembla y todos se asustan. 

A veces Viśhvambhara danza de un modo tan dulce, que parece el hijo de Nanda, el mejor de los bailarines. 

Con los ojos llenos de felicidad, los sirvientes de Mahāprabhu observan Su inmensurable amor por Śhrī Kṛṣṇa y Su incomparablemente hermosa danza. 

Mahāprabhu Viśhvambhara se regocija con Su propia felicidad trascendental. El rítmico sonido de Sus pies de loto es extremadamente cautivador. 

Bajo el peso de Sus emociones extáticas, Su guirnalda, incapaz de permanecer alrededor de Su cuello, se rompe y cae a los pies de los devotos. 

Cuando el hijo de Jagannātha Miśhra danza en medio [de los devotos], la bienaventuranza del śhrī harināma saṅkīrtana se difunde por doquier.. 

Absorto en la dicha del nombre de Śhrī Hari, Śhiva se olvida hasta de su propia ropa. Aquel cuyas glorias hacen danzar a Śhiva en éxtasis, también danza. 

Por medio de Su nombre, Vālmīki obtuvo la riqueza de la austeridad, y por Su nombre Ajāmila obtuvo la liberación. 

Por escuchar Su nombre, las ataduras del mundo material son destruidas. El Señor desciende y danza en la era de Kali. 

Śhukadeva y Nārada cantan Su nombre, y el Señor de innumerables lenguas [Śhrī Anantadeva] canta Sus glorias. 

Su nombre constituye la forma de expiación más elevada. Algunos que son supremamente afortunados contemplan la danza del Señor. 

Al ver la dicha trascendental de Mahāprabhu, los asociados del Señor se abrazan unos a otros y lloran. 

Con sus cuerpos decorados con pasta de sándalo y guirnaldas e inmersos en kṛṣṇa-prema, todos cantan en éxtasis y se olvidan de sí mismos. 

Absortos en el kīrtana, los vaiṣṇavas pierden por completo la conciencia de sus cuerpos y de quienes los rodean. 

Día y noche los devotos cantan llenos de felicidad: “¡Jaya Kṛṣṇa, Murāri, Mukunda, Vanamālī!” 

Viśhvambhara y los devotos cantan día y noche sin cansarse, porque Sus cuerpos son completamente trascendentales. 

Viśhvambhara Mahāprabhu danza de ese modo toda la noche excepto durante un prahara 5 [durante el cual Él duerme]. 

La tierra de Navadvīpa se llena así de felicidad trascendental cuando el héroe de Vaikuṇṭha disfruta del prema-rasa. 5 Medida de tiempo equivalente a tres horas. 

Gaura-chandra y Sus asociados permanecen por siempre en los corazones de quienes escuchan esta auspiciosa descripción. 

Vṛndāvana dāsa ofrece esta canción a los pies de loto de Śhrī Kṛṣṇa Chaitanya y a Nityānanda Prahbu, que se asemeja a la luna.

IDX.en_translation:
Śrī Rudra said: O Best of the Self-Realized! Victory to You! O Self of all, let there be auspiciousness for me. I offer my obeisances to You, who are served by You. 

Obeisances to the Lotus-naveled One, the Soul of the subtle elements and senses. To Vāsudeva, the peaceful, the unchanging, the self-effulgent. 

To Saṅkarṣaṇa, the subtle, the endless, and the destroyer. Obeisances to the awakener of the universe, Pradyumna, the inner soul. 

Obeisances, obeisances to Aniruddha, the Master of the senses, the Soul of the senses. Obeisances to the Paramahaṁsa, the Full, the concealed Soul. 

Obeisances to Him who is the door to heaven and liberation, who always dwells in the pure heart. Obeisances to Hiraṇya-vīrya, the expander of the Cātur-hotra sacrifice. 

Obeisances to Ūrja (strength), Iṣa (food), the Lord of the three Vedas, the source of sacrifice. To the giver of satisfaction to the jīvas, obeisances to the Soul of all rasas. 

To Him whose body is all-existence, the Specific, the Grossest. Obeisances to the Protector of the three worlds, along with Ojas (vitality) and Bala (strength). 

To the Meaning-gendered, the Sky, obeisances to the Inner and Outer Soul. Obeisances to the Pious World, to that One of great splendor. 

To the active, the renounced, the Worshipable Deity of the forefathers, to Karma. Obeisances to the result of irreligion, to Death, and to the giver of misery. 

Obeisances to You, the Lord of benedictions, to Manu, to the Causal Soul. Obeisances to Dharma, the Great, to Kṛṣṇa of stunted intelligence. To the Person, the Ancient, the Lord of Sāṅkhya and Yoga. 

To Him endowed with the three energies, to the Showerer, to the Ego-soul. To the form of Consciousness, obeisances to the manifestation of Speech. 

Give us, who are eager to see, the vision worshipped by the devotees. The form most dear to Your own, the collyrium for all the senses and qualities. 

Dark like a glistening raincloud, the reservoir of all beauty. With four beautiful long arms, and a well-formed, charming face. Eyes like lotus petals, beautiful eyebrows, beautiful nose. Beautiful teeth, beautiful cheeks and face, adorned with equal earrings. 

Beautified by sidelong glances laughing with love and by locks of hair. With a garment like the filaments of a shining lotus, and polished earrings. With shining crown, bracelets, necklaces, anklets, and girdle. Endowed with the excellent opulence of conch, disc, club, lotus, garland, and jewels. 

Bearing the Kaustubha on a beautiful neck, with the shoulders of a lion. Shining on the chest, defeating the touchstone with the never-departing Śrī (Lakṣmī). 

With an abdomen beautiful with folds agitated by breathing in and out. Deep with a navel-whirlpool that seems to draw the universe back in. 

With a golden belt on a shining cloth over dark hips. With symmetrical, beautiful feet, shins, thighs, and knees—beautiful to see. 

By Your feet, which have the luster of autumn lotus petals, and by the light of Your nails which destroys our inner sin. Show us Your own feet, which remove fear, O Guru! You are the Guru of the path for those in darkness. 

This form should be meditated upon by those desiring self-purification. Whose bhakti-yoga grants fearlessness to those performing their own duty. 

You are attainable by one who has devotion, but rare for all embodied beings. Even for the King of Heaven, the goal of the knowers of the Self is desired in solitude. 

Having worshipped Him who is difficult to worship, with unalloyed devotion rare even for the saintly. Who would desire anything outside, without the root of Your feet? 

Where death does not think to enter, absorbed. Destroying the universe with eyebrows flashing with heroism and valor. 

I do not weigh heaven or liberation against even half a moment of the association of those attached to the Lord. What to speak of the benedictions of mortals? 

Therefore, let us have the association of those whose sins have been washed away by bathing internally and externally in the holy rivers of Your glories and Your sinless feet. Who are endowed with compassion and good character towards living beings. This is Your mercy upon us. 

Whose mind, bewildered by external objects, does not enter the cave of darkness, being purified. By whose bhakti-yoga, graced easily, the sage sees Your path there. 

Where this universe is manifested, which shines in the universe. You are that Brahman, the Supreme Light, expanded like the sky. 

Who created this with the Maya of many forms, maintains it again, and destroys it, being unchanging. By whom the intelligence is different, as if existing, due to the bad state of the self. We understand You, the Lord, to be independent. 

With these activities, the yogis endowed with faith worship this very thing perfectly for perfection. Characterized by the elements, senses, and inner instrument, in the Veda and Tantra, they alone are the knowers. 

You are the One, the Original Person, whose energy is asleep. By that, passion, goodness, and ignorance are divided. From whom came this: the Mahat, the Ego, the Sky, Air, Fire, Water, Earth, the Suras, Sages, and hosts of beings. 

Created by Your own energy, having entered this fourfold city with a portion of Yourself. Then they know that Person to be existing within, who enjoys the honey made by bees with the senses. 

He, this one, of very fierce speed, You pull the worlds, driving Time. Beings by beings, the Truth inferred, like the wind the clouds, unbearable. 

Thinking loudly “This is to be done,” greedy, lusty for objects. You, always alert, suddenly seize the madman, like a hungry snake a mouse licking its lips. 

What learned person abandons Your lotus feet, when You remove the banner of disrespect? Out of fear, our Guru worshiped, without argument, the fourteen Manus. 

Now You are ours, O Brahman, O Supreme Soul of the wise! The universe is destroyed by the fear of Rudra; You are the destination of the fearless. 

Chant this, may it be well with you, O pure sons of the King! Performing your own duty, with minds offered to the Lord. 

Worship, praise, and meditate on that very Self situated in the self, situated in all beings—Hari. 

Accepting the order of yoga, observing the vow of silence, holding. With concentrated minds, all of you practice this with respect. 

This the Lord, the Master of the creators of the universe, spoke to us in the past. Desiring to create, to the sons like Bhṛgu who were desiring to create. 

We, all the Prajāpatis, urged by that in the creation of progeny. By this, our darkness destroyed, we desire to create various progeny. 

Now, a person constantly engaged in chanting this with attention. He quickly attains the ultimate good, devoted to Vāsudeva. 

Of all benedictions here, knowledge is the supreme beatitude. He crosses the ocean of misery, difficult to cross, on the boat of knowledge, happily. 

He who studies this hymn to the Lord sung by me with faith. He worships Hari, who is difficult to worship. 

A person obtains from Him whatever he desires quickly. From Him, the only beloved of benedictions, who is well-pleased by the song sung by me. 

A mortal who, rising at dawn, with folded hands and endowed with faith. Hears or causes to hear this, is released from the bondages of karma. 

This hymn of the Supreme Person, the Supreme Soul, sung by me, O sons of the King! Chanting with one-pointed minds, perform great austerity; at the end, you will obtain the desired from Him.

IDX.en_translation:
The feet of Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī are my only treasure; they are my devotion and my worship. They are the wealth of my life, my ornament, and the very life of my life. 

They are my ocean of divine mellows and the fulfillment of all my desires; they are the essence of the Vedas for me. They are my vow, my austerity, my sacred mantra, and my every action. 

If destiny becomes favorable, then perfection will be attained at those feet, and I will behold them with these eyes. That abundance of beauty and sweetness, like the moon to the lotus of my heart, will blossom day and night. 

The snake of Your absence has poisoned my being, and my life is eternally afflicted. O Lord, please show mercy! Give me the shade of Your feet; Narottama takes refuge there.
IDX.es_translation:
Los pies de loto de Śhrī Rūpa Mañjarī son mi más preciado tesoro, y el objeto supremo de mi bhajana y mi adoración. Ellos son mi mayor riqueza, el adorno de mi vida y la esencia de mi existencia. 

Sus pies de loto son el manantial del rasa, el logro de mis deseos y la conclusión de todos los Vedas. Sus pies de loto son la meta de mis votos y austeridades, el objeto de mi recitación del mantra y la culminación de todas mis prácticas espirituales. 

Cuando la providencia se muestre favorable, alcanzaré los pies de loto de Śhrī Rūpa Mañjari y los contemplaré con estos dos ojos. La abundante y dulce belleza de los pies de loto de Śhrī Rūpa Mañjarī brillará como la luna en el loto azul de mi corazón y lo hará florecer de júbilo tanto de día como de noche. 

Tu ausencia de mi visión es como una serpiente que ha corroído mi corazón con su veneno. Pasaré el resto de mis días ardiendo en el fuego de la separación. ¡Oh, Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī! Sé bondadoso y concédeme la sombra de tus pies de loto. Narottama se refugia allí.

IDX.en_translation:
O You who take shelter of the round breasts of Kamala, O You whose ears are decorated with earrings and who wears an enchanting garland of forest flowers, O Deva, O Hari, may You be triumphant! 

O ornament of the sun globe, O You who severs the bondage of material existence, O swan who sports in the [lake of the] sages’ minds, O Deva, O Hari, may You be triumphant! 

O You who pulverize the pride of the venomous snake Kāliya, O You who delight the people [of Vraja], O sun that makes the lotus of the Yadu dynasty bloom, O Deva, O Hari, may You be triumphant! 

O destroyer of the demons Madhu, Mura, and Naraka, O You who ride upon Garuḍa and who inspire the demigods’ delightful play, O Deva, O Hari, may You be triumphant! 

O You whose wide eyes resemble the petals of an immaculate lotus, O You who bestow emancipation from material existence and who are the foundation of the three worlds, O Deva, O Hari, may You be triumphant! 

O You who are decorated by the daughter of King Janaka (Sītā-devī), O You who defeated the demon Dūṣaṇa and killed the ten-headed Rāvaṇa in battle, O Deva, O Hari, may You be triumphant! 

O You whose complexion is lustrous like a fresh raincloud, O You who hold the Mandara Mountain and who are the cakora bird incessantly attached to the moonlike face of Śrī Rādhā, O Deva, O Hari, may You be triumphant! 

O Lord, we have taken exclusive refuge at Your lotus feet. Please bestow auspiciousness upon Your surrendered servants [by blessing us with prema-bhakti], O Deva, O Hari, may You be triumphant! 

May this radiant and auspicious song composed by Śrī Jayadeva increase happiness [for You and for Your devotees who hear and recite it], O Deva, O Hari, may You be triumphant!

IDX.en_translation:
The particle of dust of the feet of the pure devotee conduces to devotion, To serve the devotee is the supreme success, the root of the tender creeper of love 

The tithi of Madhaba, mother of devotion, I serve with care ; The abode of Krishna I prefer with all my heart as my dwelling place 

All those places whither my Gaura travelled for pastime, I will visit in the company of loving devotees 

The mind ever longs for opportunity of listening to the music of the mridanga The heart dances with joy on hearing the kirtana ordained by Gaur 

I experience the greatest happiness as I behold the Images of the Divine pair The world is overcome by honouring the prasada 

Goloka flashes in the house every day when I notice there the service of Krishna My happiness knows no bounds on seeing the Ganges, that stream of nectar issued from the divine feet 

My life is soothed by the sight of the tulasi knowing that she ministers to the pleasure of Govinda, I find life worth living by honouring the shaka (leaves) that is loved of Gaura 

Whatever Bhakativinode chances to have that is favourable for the service of Krishna He accepts daily with the greatest joy.
IDX.es_translation:
El polvo de los pies de loto de los devotos puros es sumamente favorable para el bhajana, y el servicio al devoto puro es la perfección suprema y la raíz de la enredadera del prema. 

Yo observo con gran cuidado los días sagrados de Mādhava [como Ekadasī y Janmāṣṭamī], pues ellos son la madre de la devoción. Puesto que Kṛṣṇa reside en esos días sagrados, ellos son objeto de mi veneración y los acepto también como mi residencia. 

En compañía de los devotos que poseen amor trascendental, contemplaré los lugares por los que anduvo mi Gaura lleno de bienaventuranza. 

Mi corazón ora sin cesar por la oportunidad de escuchar el sonido de la mṛdaṅga, y cuando escucho el kīrtana en glorificación de Śhrī Gaura, mi corazón danza de dicha. 

Al contemplar las formas de la deidad de la Pareja Divina experimento la felicidad más grande. Honrar Su prasāda nos capacita para conquistar el mundo material de cinco elementos. 

Mi hogar se transforma en Goloka Vṛndāvana cuando veo que en él se realiza bhajana de Śhrī Rādhā Kṛṣṇa. Cuando contemplo el Gaṅgā, que es el néctar (que emana) de los pies del Señor, mi felicidad no conoce límites. 

Cuando veo a Tulasī, mi corazón se siente satisfecho, pues sé que ella complace a Mādhava. Cuando honro el śhāk (preparaciones de hojas verdes), que le es muy querido a Gaura, considero que mi vida es un éxito. 

Bhaktivinoda acepta diariamente y lleno de dicha todo lo que es favorable para el kṛṣṇa-bhajana.

The beautiful darling Son of Mother Śacī dances during the congregational chanting of Lord Hari’s Name. On His forehead is an enchanting mark of sandalwood, and curly locks of hair adorn His cheeks. 

On His head a unique crown is seen, and a garland of forest flowers sways upon His chest. Dressed in beautiful yellow silk garments, His ankle bells jingle upon His feet. 

Someone sings the Names of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, and someone else sings the glories of Lord Hari. To the sweet and relishable beats of the drum and cymbals, someone sings in great ecstasy.

The crimson sun arose in the eastern sky; the jewel of the twice-born, Gorā, immediately awakens. Taking the assembly of devotees with Him, He went to the villages of the town. 

“Tāthoi tāthoi” resounds the drum, and repeatedly the sound of cymbals joins in. His golden form is overflowing with divine love, and ankle bells ring on His feet. 

“Mukunda, Mādhava, Yādava, Hari!” Chant, chant with a full voice! The night passed uselessly in the grip of sleep, and the day is spent in decorating the body. 

Having obtained such a rare human body, what are you doing? Ponder this: if you do not worship the son of Yaśodā now, in the end, you will fall into shame. 

When the risen sun sets, saying “the day is gone,” you will be agitated. Then why are you lazy now, and do not worship the King of your heart? 

Know for certain that life is temporary, and it carries the burden of various dangers. Taking shelter of the Holy Name with care, remain engaged in your own duty. 

Drinking the nectar of Kṛṣṇa’s name, cool down the soul of Bhaktivinoda. Without the Holy Name, there is nothing else within the fourteen worlds. 

With the desire to bring auspiciousness to the living entities, this sweet Name has come to the world. In the form of a sun to the darkness of ignorance, it shines brightly in the sky of the heart.
IDX.es_translation:
Cuando el rojizo sol comenzaba a despuntar por el este, Śhrī Gaurāṅga, la joya de los brahmanes, se levantaba enseguida e iba a los pueblos y aldeas de Navadvīpa con Sus devotos. 

“Tāthai, tāthai”, resonaban las mṛdaṅgas acompañadas en sincronía por los karatālas. Desbordante de prema, la dorada forma de Śhrī Gaurāṅga se movía elegantemente haciendo que Sus campanillas tobilleras repicaran. 

“¡Mukunda! ¡Mādhava! ¡Yādava! ¡Hari! ¡Canten todos! ¡Canten y llenen sus bocas con los santos nombres del Señor! Pasan las noches en vano cautivados por el sueño y los días decorando sus cuerpos.” 

“¿Ninguno de ustedes reflexiona sobre lo que está haciendo tras obtener este excepcional cuerpo humano? Si no adoran al hijo de Yaśhodā ahora, en el momento de la muerte se hallarán en una condición lamentable.” 

“Tras cada salida y puesta del sol, se afanan por contar los días que pasan. ¿Por qué permanecen ociosos y no adoran al Señor en el corazón?” 

“Comprendan este hecho fundamental: la vida material es temporal y está llena de cargas y problemas. Deben refugiarse seriamente en los santos nombres mientras realizan sus deberes cotidianos.” 

Beban el néctar puro del kṛṣṇa-nāma y aplaquen así el corazón ardiente de Bhaktivinoda. En los catorce mundos no existe nada excepto el santo nombre. 

Estos dulces santos nombres descendieron al mundo material para el bien de todas las entidades vivientes. Ellos brillan como el sol en el cielo del corazón y destruyen la oscuridad de la ignorancia.

I offer my obeisances to that Supreme Person, the foremost of thieves, who is famous in Vraja as the butter-thief and the stealer of the garments of the gopīs. He is also the thief of sins accumulated over many births. 

I offer my obeisances to that Supreme Person, the foremost of thieves, who is the thief of Rādhikā’s heart and the thief of the luster of a fresh dark cloud. He is also the thief of everything for those who take shelter of His feet. 

Who else has ever seen or heard of such a formidable thief in the three worlds, who makes those who take shelter of His feet utterly poor and homeless mendicants? 

No one has ever seen or heard of such a wondrous thief, whose very name takes away mountains of sins. 

“O thief! Where are you fleeing today after stealing all my wealth, honor, senses, and life-breaths? You are now captured and restrained by me with the rope of devotion.” 

You cut the terrible bonds of the lord of death, and You break the formidable bonds of material existence. You sever all bonds for everyone, but You never cut the bond made by Your devotee. 

“O thief! O Lord! You are now confined for a long time in the dreadful prison of my mind, which is filled with dense darkness and suffering. Receive the punishment that is appropriate for Your crime of thievery!” 

O Kṛṣṇa! O thief of everything! Reside forever in the prison of my heart, unmoving, firmly bound by the ropes of my devotion. I will not release You from my heart even after millions and millions of cataclysms.

IDX.verses: vṛndāvanavāsī jata vaiṣṇavera gaṇa prathame vandanā kari sabāra charaṇa nīlāchalavāsī jata mahāprabhura gaṇa bhūmite paḍiyā vando sabhāra charaṇa navadvīpavāsī jata mahāprabhura bhakta sabhāra charaṇa vando hañā anurakta mahāprabhura bhakta jata gauḍadeśhe sthiti sabhāra charaṇa vando kariyā praṇati je⋅ deśhe je⋅ deśhe baise gaurāṅgera gaṇa ūrdhvabāhu kari’ vando sabāra charaṇa hañācḣena hoibena prabhura jata dāsa sabhāra charaṇa vando dante kari’ ghāsa brahmāṇḍa tārite śhakti dhare jane jane e veda⋅ purāṇe guṇa gāy jebā śhune mahāprabhura gaṇa saba patita⋅ pāvana tāi lobhe muñi pāpī loinu śharaṇa vandanā karite muñi kata śhakti dhari tamo⋅ buddhi⋅ doṣe muñi dambha mātra kari tathāpi mūkera bhāgya manera ullāsa doṣa kṣami’ mo⋅ adhame kara nija dāsa sarva-vāñcḣā siddhi haya, jama⋅ bandha⋅ cḣuṭe jagate durlabha hañā prema-dhana luṭe manera vāsanā pūrṇa achirāte haya devakīnandana dāsa ei lobhe kaya
IDX.en_translation:
To all the devotees residing in Vṛndāvana, first I offer obeisances at everyone’s feet. 

To all the associates of Lord Caitanya residing in Purī, falling on the ground I offer obeisances at everyone’s feet. 

To all the devotees of the Lord residing in Navadvīpa, I offer obeisances at everyone’s feet with great attachment. 

To all the devotees of the Lord who reside in Bengal, I offer prostrated obeisances at everyone’s feet. 

Wherever the associates of Lord Caitanya reside, raising my arms, I offer obeisances at everyone’s feet. 

To all the past and future servants of the Lord, I offer obeisances at everyone’s feet, holding grass in my teeth in utmost humility. 

Each and every one of them possesses the power to deliver the universe; their glories are sung in the scriptures by whoever hears them. 

All the associates of the Lord are saviors of the fallen; therefore, with great hope, I—a sinner—take refuge in them. 

What power do I have to offer obeisances? Due to the fault of my darkened intelligence, I am merely boastful. 

Nevertheless, it is the fortune and joy of my heart; forgiving my faults, please make me, the most fallen, your servant. 

All desires are fulfilled, the bondage of death is broken, and the treasure of divine love—which is rare in the world—is attained. 

The heart’s desires are quickly fulfilled. Devakīnandana dāsa speaks this out of this great hope.
IDX.es_translation:
Ante todo glorifico los pies de todos los vaiṣṇavas de Vṛndāvana. 

Me postro y oro a los pies de los asociados de Śhrīman Mahāprabhu que residen en Nīlāchala. 

Cada vez más lleno de sentimientos afectuosos, ofrezco mi glorificación a los pies de todos los devotos de Mahāprabhu que residen en Navadvīpa. 

Oro y me inclino respetuosamente a los pies de todos los devotos de Mahaprabhu situados en Gauḍadeśha. 

Con los brazos en alto, yo presento mi glorificación a los pies de todos los asociados de Gaurāṇga sea cual sea el país donde vivan. Sosteniendo paja entre los dientes, presento mi glorificación a los pies de todos los que fueron y serán sirvientes de Mahāprabhu. 

Cada uno de Sus devotos tiene el poder de liberar al universo entero. Los Vedas y Purāṇas proclaman las glorias de esta cualidad divina de los vaiṣṇavas para quien desee escucharlas. 

Todos los asociados de Mahāprabhu son salvadores de los caídos, y puesto que soy un pecador, yo me refugio fervientemente en ellos. 

¿Qué poder tengo yo para glorificarlos? Debido a mi ignorancia, solo muestro engreimiento. 

Pero incluso alguien tan necio (como yo) se siente sumamente afortunado y dichoso (de tener la oportunidad de glorificarlos). (Oh, vaiṣṇavas), ignoren las faltas de esta alma vil y conviértanme en su sirviente. 

(Por la misericordia de los vaiṣṇavas) se perfeccionan los deseos, se rompen rápidamente las cadenas de Yama (el señor de la muerte), y el tesoro del prema, que difícilmente se encuentra en este mundo, es desvalijado (y distribuido). 

Ellos satisfacen de inmediato todos los anhelos del corazón. Devakīnandana ofrece este vaiṣṇava-vandanā en honor a los vaiṣṇavas pies.

IDX.verses: a, aśheṣa guṇera nidhi gaurāṅgasundara ā, ānande vibhora sadā premera sāgara i, indu jini’ vadanera śhobhā manohara ī, īśhvara, brahmādi jāṅ’re bhāve nirantara u, uddhārilā jaga-jane diyā premadhana ū, ūna pāpī-tāpī nāhi kailā vichāraṇa ṛ, ṛṇa śhudhibāre prabhu śhrīmatī rādhāra ṝ, rītimata nadīyāya hailā avatāra ḷ, lipta śhrī-gaurāṅga-tanu śhrī-harichandane ḹ, līlāvalī sabe heri’ haya achetane e, emana dayālu prabhu nāhi ha’be āra ai, aikāntika kṛṣṇa-bhakti karila prachāra o, oḍhradeśhe jāiyā prabhu bahu līlā kaila au, audārya-guṇete sārva-bhaume nistārila chaturdaśha svarāvalī je kare kīrtana achire labhaye sei gaurāṅga-charaṇa śhrī-jāhnavā-rāmachandra-pada kari’ āśha chaturdaśha svarāvalī gāya premadāsa
IDX.en_translation:
A - Gaurāṅgasundara is a treasure trove of endless virtues. Ā - He is always immersed in joy, an ocean of divine love. 

I - The charm of His face surpasses the moon. Ī - The Supreme Lord, whom Brahmā and others meditate upon constantly. 

U - He delivered the people of the world by giving the wealth of love. Ū - He did not consider anyone less, whether sinner or distressed. 

Ṛ - To repay the debt to Śrīmatī Rādhā-rāṇī, Ṝ - He properly incarnated in Nadīyā. 

Ḷ - Śrī Gaurāṅga’s body is anointed with sandalwood paste. Ḹ - Seeing His divine pastimes, everyone becomes enraptured. 

E - There will never be another Lord so merciful. Ai - He preached exclusive devotion to Lord Kṛṣṇa. 

O - Going to the land of Odisha, the Lord performed many pastimes. Au - By His quality of magnanimity, He delivered Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭāchārya. 

Whoever chants these fourteen vowels soon attains the lotus feet of Lord Gaurāṅga. 

With hope in the feet of Śrī Jāhnavā and Rāmacandra, Premadāsa sings these fourteen vowels.

If Rādhā shows mercy, She removes all obstacles. What remains for me to achieve in the paths of vaidhi or rāgānugā bhakti? If She speaks even a little with a gentle smile, what is the need for the liberation of merging into the effulgence, which is cherished by the best of brāhmaṇas? 

O Śyāmasundara! O One who wears a peacock feather! O One with a gentle smile! O Enchanter of the flute! O Connoisseur of Rādhikā! O Ocean of Mercy! Please make me the maidservant of the feet of Your beloved. 

O Lord of my life! O Son of Nanda! O bee who is greedy for the nectar of the lotus face of the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu! O Crest-jewel of rasikas! I worship You, who have taken shelter at the lotus feet of Rādhikā. 

Holding a straw between my teeth, O Lord, I pray to You, O Son of the King of Vraja! O Enchanter! May Your beloved Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī be my worshipable Queen birth after birth.
IDX.es_translation:
Si Śhrīmatī Rādhikā es misericordiosa conmigo, desaparecerán los ilimitados obstáculos [en mi devoción]. Entonces no habrá nada que lograr, pues habré recibido los excelentes frutos que ofrecen los senderos del vaidhī y el rāga. Y si dice algo sonriendo dulcemente y revela así el fulgor de Sus hileras de dientes de perlas, ¿qué sentido tendrá entonces la ostra de la liberación? 

¡Oh, Śhyāmasundara! Tu cabeza está adornada con plumas de pavo real, Tu rostro está agraciado con una jovial sonrisa, Tu flauta muralī encanta la mente y eres sumamente experto en saborear rasa con Śhrīmatī Rādhikā. ¡Oh, océano de misericordia! Conviérteme por favor en una kiṅkarī (sirvienta) a los pies de Tu amada. 

Tú eres el Amo de la vida de la hija de Vṛṣabhānu Mahārāja y, como una abeja, estás siempre ansioso por saborear el néctar de Su rostro de loto. ¡Oh, Rasikendra-śhekhara (rasika supremo) que estás situado a los pies de Śhrīmatī Rādhikā! Yo Te adoro. 

¡Oh, hijo del rey de Vraja! ¡Oh Tú que eres omnipresente! ¡Oh, Mohana (que encantas las mentes de todos)! Sosteniendo una brizna de hierba entre los dientes, yo Te oro para que el amor de Tu vida [Śhrī Rādhā] sea mi diosa adorable vida tras vida.

Advaita Āchārya is directly the Supreme Lord. His glory is not comprehensible to the ordinary soul. 

Lord Mahā-Viṣṇu performs the activities of creation of the universe. His incarnation is directly Advaita Āchārya. 

Advaita is the auspiciousness of the world and the abode of auspicious qualities. His character is always auspicious, and His Name is also “Auspicious.” 

He is the one with lotus eyes, in whom there is both the “limb” and the “portion” of the Lord. He bears the Name “Kamalākṣa” as an ornament. 

Advaita is a portion of Lord Mahā-Viṣṇu and is the abode of all qualities. He is non-different from the Supreme Lord; therefore His full Name is “Advaita.” 

Without teaching devotion, He has no activity. Therefore, His Name became “Advaita Āchārya.” 

Advaita Āchārya is the best portion of the Supreme Lord. His spiritual identity, Name, and qualities are all wonderful. 

By His offering of Tulasī leaves and by His roar, Lord Caitanya incarnated with His own associates. 

Through Him the Lord propagated congregational chanting and delivered the world. 

The qualities and glory of Advaita Āchārya are boundless. At his feet, I offer millions of obeisances. 

All glories, all glories to Advaita Āchārya, the venerable associate of Lord Caitanya! Please grant me devotion at your feet.

Abandoning ego, false pride, bad association, and ignorance, worship the lotus feet of your spiritual master. Perform self-surrender with your body, home, and relatives, for the words of the guru are of supreme importance. 

Constantly serve Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, the bestower of the wish-fulfilling tree of divine love. The son of the King of Vraja is Rādhā's treasure of life—all these topics are wonderful. 

Appearing in Navadvīpa and accepting the mood of Rādhā, Her luster became the adornment of His body. Desiring to fulfill three wishes, He manifested in the womb of Mother Śacī, taking along His associates. 

Gaura-hari descended, creating a flood of divine love, and accomplished the three works of His heart. In what mood the beloved of Rādhā constantly cries—only the society of devotees understands this. 

If perfection is attained secretly through the nine processes of devotional service, I will always pray with humility. By performing the congregational chanting of the Holy Name with a mind always absorbed, all obstacles are removed for the desired attainment. 

In the marketplace of the material world, lust binds and kills with its noose. A servant of the Lord loudly proclaims: “Seek the association of devotees and engage in the joyful pastimes of loving discussions; then all dangers will be destroyed.” 

Wife, sons, and all relatives—hundreds and hundreds will die. Be careful of yourself! I am ruined by these material affairs; I did not worship the lotus feet of the Lord. For me, there is no more deliverance. 

My purpose lies in the association of Rāmacandra Kavirāja. Without his association, everything is void. If I am reborn, may I attain his association; then Narottama will be blessed. 

I will not speak of the topics of my devotional service indiscriminately here and there; be careful in this regard. Let no one be angry, and do not take my fault. Offer obeisances to the feet of the devotees.

O Lord of Nīlācala! Like a mighty elephant, please trample upon the lotus grove of my distress. 

The king of elephants, Gajendra, meditated while in the midst of terrible waters. You, the wielder of the disc, destroyed the crocodile and saved him. 

In a dense forest, a fawn was trapped. From what great calamity did You save her? 

Hearing Draupadī’s appeal in the assembly of the Kauravas, O Lord, You averted her shame by bestowing millions of garments. 

Rāvaṇa’s brother, Vibhīṣaṇa, took refuge in You. Protecting his feet, You made him the king of Laṅkā. 

Prahlāda’s father was very wicked and terrible. You emerged from the pillar and instantly tore him apart. 

The poet Kālavega says: “I am a person of humble origin. I am appealing at Your lotus feet.”

El magnánimo Nityānanda Prabhu, la personificación de la bienaventuranza trascendental suprema, jamás siente ira. Libre de ego falso, Nitāi camina por el pueblo. 

Él distribuye libremente el harināma mahā-mantra de puerta en puerta en las casas de las almas más caídas y abyectas. 

Sosteniendo una brizna de paja entre Sus dientes, Él dice a todo el que ve: “¡Cómprame, por favor, adorando a Gaurahari!” 

Diciendo esto, Nityānanda Prabhu rueda en el suelo y parece una montaña dorada tambaleándose en el polvo. 

Lochana dāsa dice: “El pecador que no ha experimentado el despertar del afecto por un avatār como este, vaga inútilmente (en este ilimitado ciclo de nacimientos y muertes)”.

In every grove resides Rādhikā. She hears the sound of the flute. 

Mīrā’s Lord is the clever lifter of Govardhana Hill. Without worship, a person’s life is tasteless.

Will that Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, the incarnation of the mercy of Śrī Caitanyadeva and the reservoir of unlimited compassion and virtues, who is the very energy of Lord Gaura, again become visible to my eyes? 

Will Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, who is dear to Śrīla Jagannātha dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja and one in heart with Śrīla Gaurakiśora dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja, always remain in my memory, full of the mercy of Śrī Gaura? 

Will Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, who established the ideal standard of conduct by widely preaching the wish-fulfilling jewel of the Holy Name, always remain awake in the temple of my memory? 

Will Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, who mercifully revealed to the living entities the glories of the Holy Name free from offenses, remain seated in my memory? 

Will Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, the associate of Gaura who revealed the Lord’s hidden and manifest abodes, as well as the difference between truth and untruth, and true joy and false theater, always be the object of my remembrance? 

Will Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, who like King Bhagīratha removed all obstacles and delivered the whole world by bringing down the current of the Ganges of devotion, be the object of my eternal meditation? 

Will Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, who preached the message of Lord Caitanya throughout the world, glorified the greatness of the Guru and Vaiṣṇavas, and is the ideal of chanting the Holy Name, always remain in my heart? 

Will Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, whose teachings established the ultimate goal (Prayojana), the process (Abhidheya), and the conclusion of devotion, and who is intimately connected with Śrīla Gaurakiśora dāsa Bābājī, remain within my heart? 

Will Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, who bestowed the mercy of Lord Caitanya by publishing books such as “Śrī Śikṣāmṛta”, “Sajjana-toṣaṇī”, “Harināma-cintāmaṇi”, and “Jaiva-dharma”, be held in my heart? 

On the new moon day of Āṣāḍha, he who was non-different from Śrī Gadādhara Paṇḍita, the energy of Lord Gaura, left his earthly pastimes. Will Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura not again become visible to us?

Lord, there is now nothing left that may be called mine, Thou alone art my father, friends, brother. 

Friends, wife, sons, daughters are now Thy servants: My efforts for them are on Thy account. 

Wealth, followers, house, way, — in as much as they belong to Thee, — I maintain, myself being a mere servant. 

For Thy service I earn riches, And bear the expenses of Thy household. 

I know neither evil nor good, I only serve, A watchman set to guard the properties of Thy household. 

My senses I exercise according to Thy direction And desire to hear, see, smell and taste. 

Nothing I do for my own pleasure, “Thy pleasure is the essence,” says Bhakti-vinode.
IDX.es_translation:
¡Oh, Señor! Aparte de Ti no poseo nada. Tu eres mi padre, mi amigo y mi hermano. 

Mis amigos, mi esposa y mis hijos e hijas son Tus sirvientes; yo los mantengo únicamente en base a esa relación. 

Mi riqueza, familia, hogar y todo cuanto poseo Te pertenece, y lo protejo solo en calidad de sirviente. 

Ganaré dinero como un servicio a Ti, y con él mantendré a Tu familia. 

No sé lo que es bueno o malo. Solo soy el vigilante que vela por el interés de Tu hogar. 

Yo ocupo mis sentidos —el oído, la vista, el olfato y el gusto— según Tu voluntad. 

Ya nunca actúo para mi placer. Śhrī Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura dice: “Tu felicidad es la esencia [de mi vida]”.
