IDX.en_translation:
I sing very happy news: in the fragrant Surabhi grove, Lord Nitāi Himself has opened a marketplace of the Holy Name. 

There is a very interesting thing there: for the price of faith, the pure Name is sold in that market. 

All the devotees sit there and, seeing who is qualified, they sell the Name after settling the price. 

If you want to buy the Name, dear brother, come with me—let’s go to those great souls. 

You will buy the name of Kṛṣṇa; I will take a small commission, and your desire will be fulfilled. 

The very merciful Nityānanda, taking only faith in return, gives supreme bliss. 

If He once sees tears in your eyes as you call out “Gaura!”, Nitāi gives you all his resources. 

He gives the pure teachings of Kṛṣṇa and does not wait for caste, wealth, or the strength of knowledge. 

Immediately the net of illusion is released. Whether you stay at home or in the forest, you will be free from trouble. 

There is no more fear of the Kali age. To everyone, down to the most fallen outcast, the merciful Nitāi gives the Holy Name. 

Bhaktivinoda calls out and says: “Without the feet of Lord Nitāi, there is no other refuge.”
IDX.es_translation:
¡Canto noticias saturadas de felicidad! En Surabhi-kuñja, Śhrī Nityānanda Prabhu ha abierto el mercado del santo nombre. 

Es motivo de gran regocijo que esté vendiendo el santo nombre en el mercado por tan solo el precio de la fe. 

Tras examinar la aptitud de cada uno en la asamblea de devotos que desean comprar el santo nombre, Él regatea con cada persona por el precio justo. 

Queridos hermanos, si desean comprar el santo nombre puro, vengan conmigo a conocer a esta magnánima personalidad. 

Ustedes comprarán el santo nombre puro, yo recibiré la comisión estipulada, y todos nuestros deseos serán colmados. 

Śhrī Nityānanda Prabhu es extraordinariamente misericordioso. Por el mero precio de la fe, Él otorga la felicidad divina suprema. 

Si Nitāi ve a alguien cantando aunque sea una vez el nombre de Gaura con lágrimas en los ojos, Él concede todo Su apoyo a esa persona. 

Él otorga a esa persona enseñanzas genuinas acerca de Śhrī Kṛṣṇa sin restricciones de casta, fortuna o capacidad intelectual. 

Las trampas de māyā son inmediatamente destruidas. Uno puede permanecer en la casa [con su familia] o en el bosque [como renunciante], pues se acabaron las dificultades. 

Ya no hay necesidad de temer a la era de Kali, porque el magnánimo Nitāi da el santo nombre a todos; incluso a los más caídos. 

Bhaktivinoda proclama en voz alta: “¡Aparte de los pies de loto de Śhrī Nitāi-chandra no hay ningún otro refugio!”

Rādhā-Śyām, Śyāmā-Śyām! You give happiness to the minds of the people of Vraja. 

Peacock-feather crown, shark-shaped earrings, Vaijayantī garland around the neck. Sweet ankle-bells on the feet. Rādhā-Śyām, Śyāmā-Śyām! 

Beautiful face, eyes like lotus petals, Your crooked glance is captivating. Enchanting player of the flute. Rādhā-Śyām, Śyāmā-Śyām! 

Grazing cows in Vṛndāvana, stealing the minds of the gopīs. Holder of Śrī Govardhana. Rādhā-Śyām, Śyāmā-Śyām! 

Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, both have now met, incarnating as the Golden Form (Gaura). Preaching the religion of kīrtana. Rādhā-Śyām, Śyāmā-Śyām! 

Without You, I have no one else; the Name and Form are the Avatāra. I surrender at Your feet; Nārāyaṇa (Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī) surrenders. Rādhā-Śyām, Śyāmā-Śyām!

His raised neck is charming beyond limit, and His demeanor enchants the minds of all in the world. 

All glories to the Son of Śacī! He is worshipped by the three worlds and is the destroyer of the fear of the serpent of the Age of Kali. 

His entire body is covered with goosebumps from ecstasy, and His heart is overwhelmed with divine love. 

His gentle smile, His faltering speech, and the countless streams of tears that flow from His eyes!

IDX.en_translation:
O my mind! Abandon the company of those who are averse to Lord Hari. By their association, evil thoughts arise and one’s devotional service is interrupted. 

What is the use of giving milk to a snake? It will never abandon its poison. What is the point of feeding camphor to a crow or bathing it in the Ganges? 

What is the use of applying fragrant paste to a donkey or adorning a monkey with ornaments? What is the point of bathing an elephant in the river if it returns home and immediately smears mud upon its body? 

A stone cannot be pierced by an arrow, and a hollow bamboo only empties the quiver. Sūrdāsa says: “For a wicked person who is like a black blanket, no other color will ever stick.”

Where was I? I came here. I do not think about where I will go. Despite how much I hear from the saints and scriptures, still I did not understand. 

Coming and going is the essence, all else is insubstantial. Even if explained, I do not understand. Whatever the lack may be, despite thinking in many ways, my innate nature could not be abandoned. 

I will surely have to go, for all is uncertain. The right way was not known. What shall I do, alas? I always think, yet my desires did not end. 

I always think in my mind how much suffering I have endured in birth after birth. Knowing the talk of suffering, pain arises, yet that pain did not go away. 

I hear that by performing spiritual practice for Lord Hari, all suffering comes to an end. My mind is distressed by this thought. 

How much advice, in my own country and foreign lands, I have given and heard. Now I think, alas, that I will take my leave, and I do not know what will go with me. 

I had found You, O Lord Hari! The boatman of material existence, the true spiritual master in this world. But I will be unable to cross over this boundless ocean, despite having proclaimed it with a loud voice. 

The end has come, and I bow at Your feet. The servant Santa says: “Please give me a place at Your lotus feet, O Master! I desire a place at the feet of Lord Hari.”

The bank of Rādhā-kuṇḍa is made of wish-fulfilling jewels, with many hundreds of groves there. The trees and creepers are made of coral and red coral, bent low with pearls. 

A small cottage is beautifully situated within the enchanting grove known as Svānanda-sukhada-kuñja. Sitting there, when will I sing Kṛṣṇa’s name, longing for His service? 

At such a time, the song of the flute will enter the ears of this maidservant. I will become ecstatic with joy and forget everything by the song of Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s flute. 

Saying “Rādhe Rādhe,” the flute will call the name of my Queen. Hearing this, this maidservant will be startled and stand up; how then will I sustain my life?
IDX.es_translation:
La ribera de Śhrī Rādhā-kuṇda está hecha de piedras de toque trascendentales. En sus alrededores hay cientos y cientos de hermosos kuñjas. Los árboles y las enredaderas de corales están colmados de innumerables frutos de perlas. 

En medio del encantador jardín llamado Svānanda-sukhada-kuñja hay una casita. ¿Cuándo me sentaré allí y cantaré los santos nombres de Kṛṣṇa con el deseo de obtener Su servicio? 

En ese momento, la melodía de la flauta trascendental penetrará en los oídos de esta sirvienta. Debido al sonido de la flauta de Kṛṣṇa, quedaré embargada por el éxtasis y lo olvidaré todo. 

Diciendo “Rādhe, Rādhe”, la flauta emitirá el nombre de mi adorada ama. Al escuchar ese sonido, esta sirvienta se levantará enseguida conmovida y turbada preguntándose cómo vivirá.

IDX.translation_intro: Pañcama-adhyāya - Translation by Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī.
IDX.en_translation:
I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, the first progenitor who is tending the cows, yielding all desire, in abodes built with spiritual gems, surrounded by millions of purpose trees, always served with great reverence and affection by hundreds of thousands of lakṣmīs or gopīs. 

I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, who is adept in playing on His flute, with blooming eyes like lotus petals with head decked with peacock’s feather, with the figure of beauty tinged with the hue of blue clouds, and His unique loveliness charming millions of Cupids. 

I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, round whose neck is swinging a garland of flowers beautified with the moon-locket, whose two hands are adorned with the flute and jeweled ornaments, who always revels in pastimes of love, whose graceful threefold-bending form of Śyāmasundara is eternally manifest. 

I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, whose transcendental form is full of bliss, truth, substantiality and is thus full of the most dazzling splendor. Each of the limbs of that transcendental figure possesses in Himself, the full-fledged functions of all the organs, and eternally sees, maintains and manifests the infinite universes, both spiritual and mundane. 

I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, who is inaccessible to the Vedas, but obtainable by pure unalloyed devotion of the soul, who is without a second, who is not subject to decay, is without a beginning, whose form is endless, who is the beginning, and the eternal puruṣa; yet He is a person possessing the beauty of blooming youth. 

I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, only the tip of the toe of whose lotus feet is approached by the yogīs who aspire after the transcendental and betake themselves to prāṇāyāma by drilling the respiration; or by the jñānīs who try to find out the nondifferentiated Brahman by the process of elimination of the mundane, extending over thousands of millions of years. 

He is an undifferentiated entity as there is no distinction between potency and the possessor thereof. In His work of creation of millions of worlds, His potency remains inseparable. All the universes exist in Him and He is present in His fullness in every one of the atoms that are scattered throughout the universe, at one and the same time. Such is the primeval Lord whom I adore. 

I adore the same Govinda, the primeval Lord, in whose praise men, who are imbued with devotion, sing the mantra-sūktas told by the Vedas, by gaining their appropriate beauty, greatness, thrones, conveyances and ornaments. 

I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, residing in His own realm, Goloka, with Rādhā, resembling His own spiritual figure, the embodiment of the ecstatic potency possessed of the sixty-four artistic activities, in the company of Her confidantes [sakhīs], embodiments of the extensions of Her bodily form, permeated and vitalized by His ever-blissful spiritual rasa. 

I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, who is Śyāmasundara, Kṛṣṇa Himself with inconceivable innumerable attributes, whom the pure devotees see in their heart of hearts with the eye of devotion tinged with the salve of love. 

I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, who manifested Himself personally as Kṛṣṇa and the different avatāras in the world in the forms of Rāma, Nṛsiṁha, Vāmana, etc., as His subjective portions. 

I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, whose effulgence is the source of the nondifferentiated Brahman mentioned in the Upaniṣads, being differentiated from the infinity of glories of the mundane universe appears as the indivisible, infinite, limitless, truth. 

I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, who is the absolute substantive principle being the ultimate entity in the form of the support of all existence whose external potency embodies the threefold mundane qualities, viz., sattva, rajas, and tamas and diffuses the Vedic knowledge regarding the mundane world. 

I worship Govinda, the primeval Lord, whose glory ever triumphantly dominates the mundane world by the activity of His own pastimes, being reflected in the mind of recollecting souls as the transcendental entity of ever-blissful cognitive rasa. 

Lowest of all is located Devī-dhāma [mundane world], next above it is Maheśa-dhāma [abode of Maheśa]; above Maheśa-dhāma is placed Hari-dhāma [abode of Hari] and above them all is located Kṛṣṇa’s own realm named Goloka. I adore the primeval Lord Govinda, who has allotted their respective authorities to the rulers of those graded realms. 

The external potency Māyā who is of the nature of the shadow of the cit potency, is worshiped by all people as Durgā, the creating, preserving and destroying agency of this mundane world. I adore the primeval Lord Govinda in accordance with whose will Durgā conducts herself. 

Just as milk is transformed into curd by the action of acids, but yet the effect curd is neither same as, nor different from, its cause, viz., milk, so I adore the primeval Lord Govinda of whom the state of Śambhu is a transformation for the performance of the work of destruction. 

The light of one candle being communicated to other candles, although it burns separately in them, is the same in its quality. I adore the primeval Lord Govinda who exhibits Himself equally in the same mobile manner in His various manifestations. 

I adore the primeval Lord Govinda who assuming His own great subjective form, who bears the name of Śeṣa, replete with the all-accommodating potency, and reposing in the Causal Ocean with the infinity of the world in the pores of His hair, enjoys creative sleep [yoga-nidrā]. 

Brahmā and other lords of the mundane worlds, appearing from the pores of hair of Mahā-Viṣṇu, remain alive as long as the duration of one exhalation of the latter [Mahā-Viṣṇu]. I adore the primeval Lord Govinda of whose subjective personality Mahā-Viṣṇu is the portion of portion. 

I adore the primeval Lord Govinda from whom the separated subjective portion Brahmā receives his power for the regulation of the mundane world, just as the sun manifests some portion of his own light in all the effulgent gems that bear the names of sūryakānta, etc. 

I adore the primeval Lord Govinda, whose lotus feet are always held by Gaṇeśa upon the pair of tumuli protruding from his elephant head in order to obtain power for his function of destroying all the obstacles on the path of progress of the three worlds. 

The three worlds are composed of the nine elements, viz., fire, earth, ether, water, air, direction, time, soul and mind. I adore the primeval Lord Govinda from whom they originate, in whom they exist and into whom they enter at the time of the universal cataclysm. 

The sun who is the king of all the planets, full of infinite effulgence, the image of the good soul, is as the eye of this world. I adore the primeval Lord Govinda in pursuance of whose order the sun performs his journey mounting the wheel of time. 

I adore the primeval Lord Govinda, by whose conferred power are maintained the manifested potencies, that are found to exist, of all virtues, all vices, the Vedas, the penances and all jīvas, from Brahmā to the meanest insect. 

I adore the primeval Lord Govinda, who burns up to their roots all fruitive activities of those who are imbued with devotion and impartially ordains for each the due enjoyment of the fruits of one’s activities, of all those who walk in the path of work, in accordance with the chain of their previously performed works, no less in the case of the tiny insect that bears the name of indragopa than in that of Indra, king of the devas. 

I adore the primeval Lord Govinda, the meditators of whom, by meditating upon Him under the sway of wrath, amorous passion, natural friendly love, fear, parental affection, delusion, reverence and willing service, attain to bodily forms befitting the nature of their contemplation. 

I worship that transcendental seat, known as Śvetadvīpa where as loving consorts the Lakṣmīs in their unalloyed spiritual essence practice the amorous service of the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa as their only lover; where every tree is a transcendental purpose tree; where the soil is the purpose gem, all water is nectar, every word is a song, every gait is a dance, the flute is the favorite attendant, effulgence is full of transcendental bliss and the supreme spiritual entities are all enjoyable and tasty, where numberless milk cows always emit transcendental oceans of milk; where there is eternal existence of transcendental time, who is ever present and without past or future and hence is not subject to the quality of passing away even for the space of half a moment. That realm is known as Goloka only to a very few self-realized souls in this world.

IDX.en_translation:
The bank of Rādhā-kuṇḍa is made of wish-fulfilling jewels, with many hundreds of groves there. The trees and creepers are made of coral and red coral, bent low with pearls. 

A small cottage is beautifully situated within the enchanting grove known as Svānanda-sukhada-kuñja. Sitting there, when will I sing Kṛṣṇa's name, longing for His service? 

At such a time, the song of the flute will enter the ears of this maidservant. I will become ecstatic with joy and forget everything by the song of Śrī Kṛṣṇa's flute. 

Saying “Rādhe Rādhe,” the flute will call the name of my Queen. Hearing this, this maidservant will be startled and stand up; how then will I sustain my life?
IDX.es_translation:
La ribera de Śhrī Rādhā-kuṇda está hecha de piedras de toque trascendentales. En sus alrededores hay cientos y cientos de hermosos kuñjas. Los árboles y las enredaderas de corales están colmados de innumerables frutos de perlas. 

En medio del encantador jardín llamado Svānanda-sukhada-kuñja hay una casita. ¿Cuándo me sentaré allí y cantaré los santos nombres de Kṛṣṇa con el deseo de obtener Su servicio? 

En ese momento, la melodía de la flauta trascendental penetrará en los oídos de esta sirvienta. Debido al sonido de la flauta de Kṛṣṇa, quedaré embargada por el éxtasis y lo olvidaré todo. 

Diciendo “Rādhe, Rādhe”, la flauta emitirá el nombre de mi adorada ama. Al escuchar ese sonido, esta sirvienta se levantará enseguida conmovida y turbada preguntándose cómo vivirá.

IDX.en_translation:
Forever, Lord Gorācāndra’s joy is boundless. He speaks to His devotees about His previous pastimes. 

Instantly His body was filled with emotion from head to toe, as if golden filaments were blooming like a Kadamba flower bud. 

His heart was filled with divine emotion and His speech was choked. With great care, destiny fulfilled His hopes. 

The golden Lord, the Son of Mother Śacī, is the life’s treasure of His community. Hearing the words from His moon-like face, the heart is soothed. 

Whoever has faith in Lord Gorācāndra’s pastimes—humble Kṛṣṇa-dāsa is a servant of their servants.

I offer my obeisances to the sacred feet of Kesava, which are the desired treasure of the eternally liberated souls, the wish-fulfilling tree worshiped by the giver of wealth (Kubera), and which wander in the spiritual abode adorned with trees. 

I offer my obeisances to the sacred feet of Kesava, which revealed the excellent abode of Kuliya (Navadvipa) like the boar incarnation, and which destroyed the darkness of the mass of accumulated sins. 

I offer my obeisances to the sacred feet of Kesava, which are beautiful with the art of loving emotions fond of dancing, which are the eternal Lord shining in the eternal abode, and which are the jewel of accomplishment in the ocean of Prabhupāda’s mellows. 

I offer my obeisances to the sacred feet of Kesava, which are devoted to renunciation like Raghunatha Dasa, which are the divine form of the supreme blazing attachment (ujjvala-raga), and which are the best of gods, pleasing and satisfying the surfactant gods. 

I offer my obeisances to the sacred feet of Kesava, which hold the internal mood of Prabhupāda, which are a human form devoid of the dull enjoyments of the earth, and which are full of the ecstatic emotions of the pastimes of the human-like form. 

I offer my obeisances to the sacred feet of Kesava, whose feet are a holy place giving fearlessness to the surrendered, which deliver the fallen souls who have taken shelter of them, and which remove the material existence of the living entities eager to cross over. 

I offer my obeisances to the sacred feet of Kesava, who is the shelter of the disciples devoted to the mood of their father (guru), who is the best of the peaceful, arranging for their destination and liberation, and whose feet are the auspicious destination for the wicked who have surrendered. 

I offer my obeisances to the sacred feet of Kesava, who holds new fame in the assembly of vedanta, who is devoted to Lord Gaura, the deliverer of the people of the earth. I bow to the dust of his lotus feet, which are worshipable by others.

The jīva is a particle of consciousness; Kṛṣṇa is the sun of consciousness. Seeing Kṛṣṇa eternally, he shows affection to Kṛṣṇa. 

Turning away from Kṛṣṇa, desiring enjoyment, the Māyā nearby catches him and holds him tight. 

Just as one’s intelligence becomes covered when possessed by a ghost, that state arises in the jīva gripped by Māyā. 

Forgetting the fact “I am an eternal servant of Kṛṣṇa,” he becomes a slave of Māyā and wanders forever. 

Sometimes a king, sometimes a subject, sometimes a brāhmaṇa, a śūdra. Sometimes unhappy, sometimes happy, sometimes a small insect. 

Sometimes in heaven, sometimes in the mortal world, or sometimes in hell. Sometimes a god, sometimes a demon, sometimes a servant, a master. 

Wandering in the material world in this way, some person becomes aware of his own truth in the association of a saint. 

Knowing his own truth, he no longer wants the material world. He laments, “Alas, alas! Why did I worship Māyā?” 

Weeping, he says: “O Kṛṣṇa, I am Your servant. Leaving Your feet, I have been ruined.” 

If he calls Kṛṣṇa once with piteous words, Kṛṣṇa mercifully releases him from the material world. 

Keeping Māyā behind, he looks towards Kṛṣṇa. Worshipping and worshipping, he attains Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet. 

Kṛṣṇa gives him the strength of His own spiritual energy. Māyā, becoming weak, lets go of her attraction. 

“Kṛṣṇa-nāma in the association of saints”—this is all I want. There is no other object to conquer the material world.

Union is of two kinds: primary and secondary. Its expansion is vast. Know both of them to be of four kinds: “brief” (saṁkṣipta), “narrow” (saṅkīrṇa), “accomplished” (sampanna), and “enriched” (samṛddhimān), according to the previous emotional state.

IDX.en_translation:
In this material world which is burning like a forest fire, I worship the lotus feet of the spiritual master—an ocean of good qualities who bestows the water of mercy like a cloud of compassion for the deliverance of the suffering souls. 

He remains deeply immersed in the congregational chanting of the Lord’s names with dance, song, and musical instruments. Thrills of ecstasy, trembling, and tears manifest on his body due to love for Lord Caitanya. I worship those lotus feet of the spiritual master. 

Always engaged in the worship of the Deity, in decorating Him and cleaning the temple, he engages his obedient followers in these services. I worship those lotus feet of the spiritual master. 

The delicious foods offered to Kṛṣṇa—to be chewed, sucked, licked, and drunk—are extremely palatable. By tasting them, the spiritual master remains satisfied. I worship those lotus feet of the spiritual master. 

The spiritual master’s mind is always greedy to relish the names, forms, and qualities of Śrī Rādhā and Mādhava and Their endless sweet pastimes. I worship those lotus feet of the spiritual master. 

To increase the loving affairs of the youthful Divine Couple, he devises means with the companions of Rādhā in Vṛndāvana. He is very expert in this among the dearmost ones. I worship those lotus feet of the spiritual master. 

All scriptures sing of the true nature of the Lord, and the devotees meditate on Him accordingly. But the spiritual master is the most beloved form of the Lord. I worship those lotus feet of the spiritual master. 

By his grace we obtain Kṛṣṇa’s mercy; without his grace, there is no other path. O brother, meditate on his glories three times daily. I worship those lotus feet of the spiritual master. 

This prayer glorifying the spiritual master should be recited with great care and chanted loudly during the auspicious hour before dawn. Thus one obtains the service of Śrī Hari, the Lord of Vṛndāvana, at the time of attaining the ultimate goal.

My mind, dance by chanting ‘Dayāl Nitāi Caitanya’. Dance, oh my mind, dance, oh my mind.

His lotus-like eyes and pure face surpass the beauty of the autumn moon. All the residents of the town run in one direction, hearing the sound of “Hari! Hari!” 

Blessed is the Age of Kali because of the incarnation of the golden Lord. Those who possess Him are the wealthiest of all. Without the golden Lord, they accept no one else—Vāsudeva Ghoṣa says this, knowing it well.

nija-sthūla-parichaya 
nayane heriba, vraja-pura-śhobhā, 
nitya chid-ānanda-maya 

vṛṣabhānu-pure, janama loiba, 
jāvaṭe vivāha ha’be 
vraja-gopī-bhāva, hoibe svabhāva, 
āna-bhāva nā rahibe 

nija siddha-deha, nija siddha-nāma, 
nija rūpa-sva-vasana

IDX.en_translation:
And by me unawares When shall I forget The memory of my gross self? Shall behold with my eyes The beauty of the realm of Braja Full of the eternal spiritual bliss? 

In Brishabhanu’s town When shall I have my birth, Shall be married in Yabata? The mood of the milkmaid of Braja Will be my nature, And there be no other disposition? 

My own realised body, My own realised name, My own form, my own apparel, By the power of Radha’s mercy, O when shall I gain? And initiation into the love of Krishna? 

Going out to fetch The water of the Yamuna Shall understand the love of the Divine pair? And smitten by love, Like a distracted maiden, Shall sing the praise of Radha?
IDX.es_translation:
¿Cuándo desaparecerá de mi visión la concepción corporal que tengo de mi persona? En ese momento contemplaré con mis propios ojos la exquisita belleza de Vraja llena de conocimiento y bienaventuranza espirituales y eternos. 

Cuando eso ocurra, naceré en el pueblo de Vṛṣabhānu Mahārāja y me casaré en Yāvaṭa. Mi única inclinación y naturaleza será la de una vraja-gopī. No tendré ningún otro sentimiento.. 

¿Cuándo obtendré, por la misericordia de Rādhā, mi identidad espiritual eterna, mi nombre, mi forma y mi vestido ―la verdadera iniciación en el reino del kṛṣṇa-prema? 

Cuando vaya a buscar agua al Yamunā, comprenderé las melosidades confidenciales de los intercambios amorosos de la Pareja Divina, y, rebosante de prema, cantaré las glorias de Śhrī Rādhā como una demente.

deva deva deva kṛṣṇa, dīna-bandhu pāhi mām 
nīla megha śhyāma kṛṣṇa, nitya mukta rakṣa mām 

nanda-nandana mukunda-rāma, rāma-kṛṣṇa pāhi mām 

veṇu gāna lola kṛṣṇa, vimala lola pāhi mām 
viśhvarūpa vāsudeva, vīra rāma rakṣa mām 

putanānāśha hare kṛṣṇa, bhuvana-nātha pāhi mām

IDX.en_translation:
O Lord Kṛṣṇa! O Friend of the distressed! Please protect me. O Kṛṣṇa, dark like a blue cloud! O eternally liberated Lord! Please save me. 

O Son of Nanda! O Giver of liberation! O Rāma and Kṛṣṇa! Please protect me. 

O Kṛṣṇa, enchanted by the song of the flute! O pure and playful Lord! Please protect me. O Lord of the universal form! O Son of Vasudeva! O heroic Lord Rāma! Please save me. 

O Destroyer of Pūtanā! O Hare Kṛṣṇa! O Lord of the universe! Please protect me. O lotus-eyed Lord Kṛṣṇa! O perfect form! Please save me.

IDX.verses: deva-loka pitṛ-loka-pāya tāra mahā-sukha sādhu sādhu bale anukṣaṇa yugala bhajaye jara-premānande bhāse tāra tāṇdera nicḣani tri-bhuvana pṛthak āyāsa-yoge-duḥkha-maya-viṣaya-bhoge vraje vāsa govinda-sevana kṛṣṇa-kathā kṛṣṇa-nāma-satya-satya rasa-dhāma vraja-jane-saṅge anukṣaṇa sadā sevā-abhilāṣa-manete kari’ viśhvāsa sadā-kāla haiya nirbhaya narottama-dāsa bole paḍinu asat-bhole paritrāṇa kara mahāśhaya
IDX.en_translation:
Those who attain the heavenly planets and the world of the forefathers find great happiness there. They always exclaim, “Excellent, excellent!” But for those who worship the Divine Couple and float in the ecstasy of Their love, the three worlds are insignificant in comparison. 

Abandoning separate endeavors for sense enjoyment, which is full of misery, one should reside in Vraja and serve Govinda. Topics of Kṛṣṇa and the Holy Name of Kṛṣṇa are truly, truly the abode of nectar, always to be enjoyed in the company of the residents of Vraja. 

Always maintaining the desire for service and keeping faith in the mind, one becomes fearless at all times. Narottama Dāsa says, “I have fallen, bewildered by illusion. Please deliver me, O great soul.”

The Supreme Lord Gaura-candra is in the temple of Gaurīdāsa Paṇḍita. Gaura enjoys pastimes in Ambikā with Nityānanda. 

He who wears a beautiful red seed garland on His lotus heart has lotus feet that are lovingly served by Brahmā and the goddess of fortune. 

His bodily effulgence is like molten gold, like the reddish glow of the morning; He desires the loving attachment of Rādhikā and loving devotional service. 

The son of Śacī, Gaura-candra, is joyful in His heart. He sports merrily with Nityānanda, the vanquisher of all heresies. 

Nityānanda and Gaura-candra are in the temple of Gaurīdāsa Paṇḍita, who hopes for the deliverance of all living entities.
IDX.es_translation:
El Señor de señores, Śhrī Gaura-chandra, acompañado por Nityānanda Prabhu, disfruta de agradables pasatiempos en la casa de Gaurīdāsa Paṇḍita en Ambikā-kālnā. 

Lleva una hermosa guñjā-māla roja que Le llega hasta Su corazón de loto. Brahmā y Lakṣmī adoran Sus pies de loto con mucho respeto. 

Su cuerpo brilla resplandeciente como el oro fundido y Su vestidura tiene el color del sol naciente. Él desea el prema-bhakti saturado de anurāga de Śhrīmatī Rādhikā. 

El hijo de Śhachī, Śhrī Gaura-chandra, es internamente dichoso. Él camina gozoso con Nityānanda Prabhu, el vencedor de los ateos. 

Tanto Nityānanda como Gaura-chandra están en la casa de Gaurīdāsa, que anhela que liberen a todas las jīvas.

devi! sureśhvari! bhagavati! gaṅge!

tava jala-mahimā nigame-khyātaḥ 
nāhaṁ jāne tava mahimānaṁ 
trāhi kṛpāmayi! māmajñānam

vibudha-vādhu-kṛta-taralāpāṅge! 

tava kṛpayā chet srotaḥ-snātaḥ 
punar api jaṭhare so‛pi na jātaḥ 
naraka-nivāriṇi! jāhnavi! gaṅge! 
kaluṣa-vināśhini! mahimottuṅge! 

parilasad-aṅge! puṇya-taraṅge!

IDX.en_translation:
O Devi! O Mistress of the gods! O Goddess! O Gaṅgā! O Deliverer of the three worlds! O You with restless waves! O You who dwell on the head of Śaṅkara! O Pure One! May my mind always rest at Your lotus feet. 

O Bhāgīrathī! O Giver of happiness! O Mother! The glory of Your water is famous in the Vedas. I do not know Your glory; O Merciful One! Protect me, who am ignorant. 

O Gaṅgā, who sports at the lotus feet of Hari! Your waves are white like snow, the moon, and pearls. Please remove the burden of my sins; by Your mercy, help me cross the ocean of material existence. 

He by whom Your pure water is drunk has indeed attained the supreme abode. O Mother Gaṅgā! He who is a devotee of Yours—Yama is unable to even look at him. 

O Deliverer of the fallen! O Jāhnavī! O Gaṅgā! Your meandering flow is adorned by the rocks of the King of Mountains (Himālaya). O Mother of Bhīṣma! O Daughter of the great sage (Jahnu)! O Deliverer of the fallen! O You who are glorious in the three worlds! 

You are like a wish-fulfilling creeper granting fruits in this world. He who bows to You does not suffer grief. O Gaṅgā, who sports in the ocean! You are gazed upon by the restless eyes of the celestial damsels. 

If, by Your mercy, one bathes in Your current, he is not born again in a womb. O Preventer of hell! O Jāhnavī! O Gaṅgā! O Destroyer of sins! O You of towering glory! 

O You of shining limbs! O Wave of piety! Glory, glory to You, O Jāhnavī! O You of merciful glance! Your feet are illuminated by the jewels of Indra’s crown. O Giver of happiness! O Giver of auspiciousness! O Shelter of Your servants! 

O Bhagavatī! Please take away my disease, sorrow, suffering, sin, and heaps of wicked thoughts. O Essence of the three worlds! O Necklace of the Earth! You are indeed my refuge in this material world. 

O Alakānandā! O Supreme Bliss! Be merciful to me, O You who are worshipped by the distressed! He who resides near Your banks—his residence is verily in Vaikuṇṭha. 

It is better to be a tortoise or a fish in Your waters here, or a tiny lizard on Your bank, or a wretched dog-eater living near You, than to be a king of noble birth far away from You. 

O Queen of the Universe! O Pious One! O Blessed One! O Goddess! O Embodiment of water! O Daughter of the great sage! The person who recites this spotless prayer to Gaṅgā daily—he truly becomes victorious. 

Those in whose heart devotion to Gaṅgā dwells—for them there is always happiness and liberation. This prayer is adorned with sweet, captivating rhyming verses, filled with supreme bliss. 

This Gaṅgā Stotram is the essence of worldly existence, the bestower of desired fruits, and the remover of burdens. Composed by Śaṅkara (achārya), the servant of Śaṅkara (Lord Śiva). Whoever reads it, his materi al entanglement ends.
IDX.es_translation:
¡Oh, brillante diosa! ¡Oh, soberana de todos los semidioses! ¡Oh Bhagavati, amada del Señor Supremo! ¡Oh Gaṅgā que liberas los tres mundos! Tus olas son juguetonas y resides en la corona del Señor Śhaṅkara [Śhiva]. ¡Oh, inmaculada! Que mi atención quede fija a tus pies de loto. 

¡Oh Bhāgirathī que respondiste a las oraciones del rey Bhāgiratha! ¡Oh madre que otorgas bienaventuranza! Los Vedas describen las glorias de tus aguas. Yo desconozco por completo tu magnificencia. ¡Oh, misericordiosa! Salva por favor a este necio. 

¡O Gaṅgā, tú que retozas a los pies de loto de Śhrī Hari! Tus olas son blancas como la nieve, blancas como la luna y blancas como las perlas blancas. Erradica por favor la carga de mis pecados. Ten compasión de mí y condúceme a través del océano de la existencia material. 

Quienquiera que bebe tu agua pura alcanza el destino supremo. ¡Oh, Madre Gaṅgā, Yama, el dios de la muerte, no puede ni siquiera mirar a aquellos que tienen devoción por ti. 

¡Oh, salvadora de los caídos! ¡Oh Gaṅgā, hija del sabio Jahnu! Tus riachuelos son adornados por la mejor de las montañas. ¡Oh, madre de Bhīṣma! Eres sin duda la hija del mejor de los sabios. ¡Oh, salvadora de los caídos! Tus glorias se expanden por los tres mundos. 

Al igual que los árboles de los deseos, tú satisfaces todos los deseos. Quienquiera que te ofrece sus respetos jamás perece de tristeza. ¡Oh Madre Gaṅgā que juegas entre dos orillas! Las esposas de los semidioses te miran de reojo inquietas. 

Si por tu misericordia alguien se baña por casualidad en tus aguas, no vuelve a nacer de nuevo del vientre de una madre. ¡Oh Gaṅgā, hija del sabio Jahnu, tú salvas del infierno y eliminas las reacciones pecaminosas. Tus glorias no tienen límite. 

Tu cuerpo está integrado por numerosos ríos y tus olas son sagradas. ¡Toda gloria a ti, oh Jāhnavi, cuyo cuerpo entero está hecho de compasión! La corona de Indra, incrustada de piedras preciosas, decora siempre tus pies. ¡Oh tú, que otorgas felicidad y bondad! Tú eres el refugio de tus sirvientes. 

¡Oh, Bhagavati! Llévate por favor mi enfermedad, mi angustia, mis sufrimientos, mis pecados y mi ilusión. Tu presencia es esencial en los tres mundos. Tú eres el valioso collar que embellece la tierra. Y eres sin duda mi único refugio en el repetido ciclo de nacimiento y muerte. 

¡Oh Alakānanda que desciendes del Himalaya! ¡Oh tú, que personificas la dicha suprema! Ten misericordia de mí, pues eres adorada por todos los caídos. Quien habita en tus orillas reside en verdad en la morada trascendental de Vaikuṇṭha. 

Es mejor ser una tortuga o un pez en tus aguas, un pequeño lagarto en tus orillas o incluso un vil comedor de perros viviendo a dos krośhas (seis kilómetros y medio) de ti, que ser un rey de noble linaje viviendo lejos de ti. 

¡Oh, Señora del universo! ¡Oh tú, bendita y gloriosa! ¡Oh diosa de forma líquida! ¡Oh hija del mejor de los sabios! La persona que recita siempre esta oración impecable en alabanza de Gaṅgā-devī es sin duda victoriosa. 

Aquellos cuyos corazones son la morada de la devoción por el Gaṅgā, son propietarios de la dicha y la liberación. Los extraordinarios versos de este Gaṅgā-stotra, que están saturados de un gozo supremo, han sido compuestos por Śhaṅkarāchārya, el sirviente del Señor Śhaṅkara, en la encantadora métrica conocida como pajjhatika. El presente stotra otorga el resultado deseado y libera a la persona de toda clase de cargas. Así finaliza esta oración que es cantada regularmente por gente de bien. 

Este Gaṅgā Stotram es la esencia de la existencia terrenal, el que otorga los frutos deseados y el que libera de las cargas. Fue compuesto por Śhaṅkara (achārya), el sirviente de Śhaṅkara (el Señor Śhiva). Quienquiera que lo lea, quedará libre de sus enredos materiales.

IDX.verses: dhana, jana, deha, geha kṛṣṇe samarpaṇa kariyācḣa, śhuddha chitte karaha smaraṇa tabe kena ‘mama suta’ bali’ kara duḥkha? kṛṣṇa nila nija-jana tāhe tā’ra sukha kṛṣṇa-iccḣā-mate saba ghaṭaya ghaṭanā tāhe sukha-duḥkha-jñāna avidyā-kalpanā jāhā iccḣā kare kṛṣṇa, tāi jāna bhāla tyajiyā āpana iccḣā ghuchāo jañjāla deya kṛṣṇa, neya kṛṣṇa, pāle kṛṣṇa sabe rākhe kṛṣṇa, māre kṛṣṇa, iccḣā kare jabe kṛṣṇa-iccḣā-viparīta je kare vāsanā tā’ra iccḣā nāhi fale, se pāya jātanā tyajiyā sakala śhoka śhuna kṛṣṇa-nāma parama ānanda pā’be, pūrṇa ha’be kāma bhakativinoda māge śhrīvāsa-charaṇe ātmanivedana-śhakti jīvane-maraṇe
IDX.en_translation:
Wealth, family, body, and home—all have been surrendered to Kṛṣṇa. You have done this; now remember it with a pure heart. 

Then why do you lament, saying, “My son”? Kṛṣṇa has taken His own; in that is His joy. 

Everything happens according to Kṛṣṇa’s will. The notion of happiness and sorrow in this is simply ignorance and imagination. 

Whatever Kṛṣṇa desires, know that to be good. Abandon your own desires and remove this entanglement. 

Kṛṣṇa gives, Kṛṣṇa takes, and Kṛṣṇa nourishes all. Kṛṣṇa protects and Kṛṣṇa destroys whenever He desires. 

Whoever desires something contrary to Kṛṣṇa’s will finds that his desires bear no fruit, and he only experiences suffering. 

Abandon all sorrow and listen to Kṛṣṇa’s name. You will attain supreme bliss, and your desires will be fulfilled. 

Bhaktivinoda begs at the feet of Śrīvāsa for the power of self-surrender in life and in death.

IDX.author: narottama-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: dhana mora nityānanda, pati mora gaura-chandra, prāṇa mora yugala-kiśhora advaita-āchārya bala, gadādhara mora kula, narahari vilasai mora vaiṣṇavera pada-dhūli, tāhe mora snāna-keli, tarpaṇ mora vaiṣṇavera nāma vichāra kariyā mane, bhakti-rasa āsvādane, madhyastha śhrī-bhāgavat-purāṇa vaiṣṇavera uccḣiṣṭa, tāhe mora mano-niṣṭha, vaiṣṇavera nāmete ullāsa vṛndāvane chautārā, tāhe mora mano-gherā, kahe dīna narottama-dāsa
IDX.en_translation:
My treasure is Nityānanda. My Lord is Gaura-candra. My very life is the Divine Youthful Couple, Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. My strength is Advaita Āchārya. My family is Gadādhara Paṇḍita. And Narahari Sarakāra is my delight. 

The dust from the feet of the devotees is my joyful bath. My sacred offering is the names of the devotees. When I deeply ponder in my mind how to relish the mellow of devotion, the Śrīmad-Bhāgavata Purāṇa serves as my guide. 

The remnants of the devotees are my firm conviction. I find great joy in the names of the devotees. My mind is forever encircled by the courtyards of Vṛndāvana. Thus speaks the humble Narottama dāsa.
IDX.es_translation:
El Señor Nityānanda es mi riqueza, el Señor Gaurachandra es mi amo y la joven Pareja Divina de Vraja son mi vida. Advaita Achārya es mi fuerza, Gadādhara Paṇḍit mi familia y Narahari Sarakāra mi felicidad. 

Mi baño lo constituye el polvo de los pies de los devotos, mi satisfacción está en los nombres de los vaiṣṇavas, y he comprendido que el mejor medio para saborear el bhakti-rasa es el Śrīmad- Bhāgavatam. 

Mi mente cree firmemente en los remanentes de los devotos y rebosa de alegría al recordar los nombres de los vaiṣṇavas. Mi mente está completamente rodeada por los límites de Vṛndāvana. Así habla el indigno Narottama dāsa.

IDX.search: dharma bali vede jare eteka prasamsa kare adharma baliya ninde jare taha kicḣu nahi kara dharmadharma parihara hoo rata nigudha vyapare jachi mana dhari tava paya se sakala parihari vrajabhume vasa kari rata hoo yugalasevaya sri sachi nandana dhane sri nanda nandana sane eka kari karaha bhajana srimukunda priyajana gurudeve jana mana toma lagi patita pavana jagate prakata bhai tanha vina gati nai jadi chao apana kusala tanhara charane dhari tadadesa sada smari e bhaktivinode deha bala
IDX.author: sacchidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses: ‘dharma’ bali vede jāre, eteka praśhaṁsā kare, ‘adharma’ baliyā ninde jā’re tāhā kicḣu nāhi kara, dharmādharma parihara, hoo rata nigūḍha vyāpāre jāchi’ mana, dhari’ tava pāya se-sakala parihari’, vrajabhūme vāsa kari’, rata hoo yugalasevāya śhrī-śhachī-nandana-dhane, śhrī-nanda-nandana-sane, eka kari’ karaha bhajana śhrīmukunda-priyajana, gurudeve jāna mana, tomā’ lāgi’ patita-pāvana jagate prakaṭa, bhāi, tāṅhā vinā gati nāi, jadi chāo āpana kuśhala tāṅhāra charaṇe dhari’, tadādeśha sadā smari’, e bhaktivinode deha bala
IDX.en_translation:
That which the Vedas call religious duty and praise so much, and that which they condemn as unrighteousness—do not do any of those. Give up both and engage instead in the confidential activities of devotion. 

O my mind! I beg you while holding your feet: give up all of those things and reside in the land of Vraja, and engage yourself in the service of the Divine Couple. 

Understand that Lord Caitanya and Lord Kṛṣṇa are one, and worship Them together. Understand in your mind that the Spiritual Master, who is most dear to Lord Kṛṣṇa, is the deliverer of the fallen for your sake. 

He is manifest in this world, O brother, and without Him there is no path if you desire your own welfare. Holding His feet and always remembering His instructions, please give strength to this Bhaktivinoda.

IDX.search: dharma pathe thaki kara jivana japana bhai harinama kara sada ore o bhai hari vina bandhu nai je kona vyavasa dhari jivana nirvaha kari bala mukhe hari hari ei matra bhiksa chai gauranga charane maja anya abhilasa tyaja vrajendra nandane bhaja tabe bada sukha pai ami chanda baula dasa kari tava krpa asa janaiya abhilasa nityananda ajna gai

IDX.verses: dharma-pathe thāki’ kara jīvana jāpana, bhāi harināma kara sadā (ore o bhāi) hari vinā bandhu nāi je-kona vyavasā dhari’, jīvana nirvāha kari’, bala mukhe ‘hari hari’, ei-mātra bhikṣā chāi gaurāṅga-charaṇe maja’, anya-abhilāṣa tyaja, vrajendra-nandane bhaja, tabe baḍa sukha pāi āmi chāṅda-bāula dāsa, kari tava kṛpā-āśha, jānāiyā abhilāṣa, nityānanda-ājñā gāi
IDX.en_translation:
O brother, live your life on the path of righteousness. Always chant the Holy Name, for there is no friend other than Hari. 

Whatever occupation you may adopt to sustain your life, chant “Hari! Hari!” with your mouth; this is all I beg of you. 

Absorb yourself in the lotus feet of Gaurāṅga, give up all other desires, and worship the son of the King of Vraja; then you will find great happiness. 

I, Cānd Bāul, hope for your mercy. Expressing my desire, I sing the command of Nityānanda.

dīkṣā-guru kṛpā kari’ mantra-upadeśha 
kariyā dekhāna kṛṣṇa-tattvera nirdeśha 

śhikṣā-guru-vṛnda kṛpā kariyā apāra 
sādhake śhikhāna sādhanera aṅga-sāra 

śhikṣā-guru-gaṇa-pāde kariyā praṇati 
upadeśha-mālā boli nija-manaḥ prati
IDX.en_translation:
The initiating spiritual master, by mercifully giving instruction in the sacred sound, reveals the direction regarding the truth about Kṛṣṇa. 

The assemblage of instructing spiritual masters, by performing boundless mercy, teach the practitioner the essential limbs of spiritual practice. 

Offering obeisances at the feet of the assembly of instructing spiritual masters, I speak this garland of instructions to my own mind.

IDX.verses:
dīnabandhu dayitārī, duḥkha na galā moharī 
helaki niṣṭhura chitta, nīlāchale vije kari 

lakṣe jojanāra gaja, ḍākilā he devarāja 
tā ḍākaku chaturbhuja śhunila śhravaṇa ḍerī 

kurupati sabhātaḍe, daupadī ātaṅgakāḍe 
koṭī vastra dei heḍe, lajjāru karicḣa pāri 

balavanta prabhu bali, baḍe muye āśhrākali 
dekhu dekhu bhāsi gali, ke ethu kariba pāri 

rakha vā nā rakha mote, śharaṇa to pādagate 
kahe vanamālī gīte, basiyācḣi mu dhyāna kari
IDX.en_translation:
O Friend of the distressed! O Remover of sorrow! My suffering does not cease. It is a great delusion. O Lord, while You reside in Puruṣottama Kṣetra, my heart remains cruel. 

The elephant Gajendra, from hundreds of thousands of miles away, called out to You. You, the four-armed Lord, heard that call with attentive ears. 

In the assembly hall of Duryodhana, when Draupadī was in great fear, You saved her from shame by bestowing millions of garments. 

Saying “O powerful Lord!”, I took great shelter of You. Yet, I see myself drowning in this material world. Who can save me from this? 

Whether You save me or not, I have taken refuge at Your feet. Vanamālī sings this song while sitting and meditating upon You.

pitur iha vṛṣabhānor anvavāya-praśhastiṁ 
jagati kila samaste suṣṭhu vistārayantīm

IDX.en_translation:
I worship Śrī Rādhikā, who performs the play of a wagtail bird in every direction with the graceful, playful movements of her wandering eyes. She is the jasmine creeper for the bee of the heart of the Son of the king of cowherds, and is profound with all virtues. 

I worship Śrī Rādhikā, who beautifully spreads the glory of her father Vṛṣabhānu’s lineage throughout the entire world. She plays with the Prince of Vraja and her sakhīs in her fragrant own pond. 

I worship Śrī Rādhikā, whose gently smiling face has taken a vow to surpass the fame of the accumulated moonlight of the full autumn moon. Her sidelong glances towards the killer of Aghāsura heighten the stage of the god of love, and she is endowed with waves of inherent beauty. 

I worship Śrī Rādhikā, whose flowing, beautiful braid, adorned with a multitude of blossoming flowers, surpasses the splendor of proud peacock feathers. Her pure cheeks glow brightly with the red color of betel nut ejected from the moon-like face of Kṛṣṇa. 

I worship Śrī Rādhikā, whose heart is pure and drenched in unblemished affection, famous for her friendship with all types of sakhīs, including Lalitā and Viśākhā. She is the jewel casket of invaluable love for the killer of Aghāsura, and she delights in sweet pastimes. 

I worship Śrī Rādhikā, who is crowned queen in the incomparably glorious kingdom of Vṛndāvana. She is the presiding deity of Kārtika, and the chief among the unlimited beloveds of Mukunda. Her fame removes the sins of the world. 

I worship Śrī Rādhikā, who considers even the slightest touch of Hari’s toenails to be dearer than millions of lives. She is the initiating teacher of the wisdom of the joyful, intoxicated-eyed sakhīs, and has exceptionally great fame. 

I worship Śrī Rādhikā, who is fair like saffron ground on a pure golden slab, a young maiden surrounded by waves of sweetness. Embraced by Hari’s arms, she experiences a thrill of ecstasy, wearing a glistening reddish garment. 

Whoever properly recites this excellent eight-verse prayer in praise of Rādhā, which is the very embodiment of that pure sweetness, the auspicious moon of the Yamunā riverbank, Kṛṣṇa, being pleased, will clearly fulfill all his desires.

IDX.translation_intro: Vaiṣṇava Ke? “Who is a devotee?”
IDX.en_translation:
O wicked mind, what kind of Vaiṣṇava are you? In a solitary room, for the sake of prestige, your chanting of the holy name is simply cheating. 

Material prestige is the stool of a hog; do you not know that it is the opulence of Māyā? Gold, women, day and night—what is the use of thinking about them? They are all temporary. 

Your gold is the progenitor of enjoyment; serve Mādhava using that gold. The desire for women is not your abode; their only owner is Yādava. 

The tree of the desire for prestige, the desert of material illusion—Rāvaṇa could not obtain it even by fighting with Rāghava. Be fixed in the prestige of a Vaiṣṇava; if you do not worship that, you will attain the Raurava hell. 

Envy of the devotees, the misery of desiring prestige—why do you glorify that? There is a desire for prestige in a Vaiṣṇava, but that is never a temporary opulence. 

That is related to Hari, devoid of the scent of Māyā; it is never the cheating of the material world. The dog-eating witch of prestige, the net of solitude—know both to be the illusory Raurava. 

“I will give up kīrtana and smear myself with prestige”—what is the use of seeking such “glory”? Mādhavendra Purī never committed theft in the storehouse of perception; always know this. 

Your prestige is the stool of a hog; never consider it equal to a human being. Controlled by envy, you have drowned in material rasa, abandoning the beauty of kīrtana. 

Therefore, O wicked mind, you are deceitfully preaching the opulence of a false yogī as “solitary worship.” Contemplate all the instructions that were given to Sanātana Prabhu with great care. 

Do not forget those two words at all; chant the holy name of Hari loudly. “Phalgu” (false) and “Yukta” (proper), “bound” and “liberated”—never think of them all as one. 

Gold, women, and the tigress of prestige—he who has given them up is indeed a Vaiṣṇava. He is unattached, he is a pure devotee; material existence is defeated there. 

Accepting what is appropriate, there is no disease there; he is unattached—what more shall I say? Devoid of attachment, possessing relationship, all objects are Mādhava. 

That is “yukta-vairāgya” (proper renunciation), that is indeed good fortune; that is the opulence of Hari within the material world. For one whose kīrtana is a collection of prestige, his wealth is simply cheating. 

“Desiring liberation from objects” and “hungry for enjoyment”—O mind, reject both; both are non-Vaiṣṇavas. Relationship with Kṛṣṇa, a transcendental body—that is never possible in matter. 

The Māyāvādī, whose mind is not on Kṛṣṇa, criticizes the Vaiṣṇava in his pride of liberation. O servant of the Vaiṣṇava, your hope is devotion; why then do you call for the battle of solitude? 

That “falgu-vairāgī” who calls himself a renunciate can never be a Vaiṣṇava. Abandoning the feet of Hari, increasing solitude—what fruit is gained? That is “falgu” opulence. 

Remaining in the service of Rādhā, give up the snake of enjoyment; the desire for prestige is not the glory of kīrtana. Rādhā’s eternal person—abandoning that, O mind, why the cheating of solitary worship? 

The residents of Vraja are the wealth of the preachers; they are not beggars for prestige, nor are they dead bodies. They have life, therefore they preach; all the topics of Kṛṣṇa are free from the desire for prestige. 

Śrī Dayita-dāsa’s hope is in kīrtana; chant the sound of Hari-nāma loudly. By the influence of kīrtana, remembrance will come; at that time, solitary worship is possible.

IDX.verses:
e duṣṭa hṛdaye kāma-ādi ripu cḣaya 
kuṭinaṭi, pratiṣṭhāśhā, śhāṭhya sadā raya 

hṛdaya-śhodhana āra kṛṣṇera vāsanā 
nṛsiṁha-charaṇe more ei ta’ kāmanā 

kāṅdiyā nṛsiṁha-pade māgiba kakhana 
nirāpade navadvīpe yugala-bhajana 

bhaya, bhaya pāya jāṅra darśhana, se hari 
prasanna hoibe kabe more dayā kari’ 

jadyapi bhīṣaṇa mūrti duṣṭa jīva prati 
prahlādādi kṛṣṇa-bhakta-jane bhadra ati 

kabe vā prasanna ha’ye sakṛpā-vachane 
nirbhaya karibe ei mūḍha akiñchane 

‘svaccḣande voisa he vatsa, śhrī-gaurāṅga-dhāme 
yugala-bhajana hou, rati hou nāme 

mama bhakta-kṛpābale vighna jābe dūra 
śhuddha-chitte bhaja rādhā-kṛṣṇa-rasapura’ 

ei bali’ kabe mora mastaka-upara 
svīya śhrī-charaṇa harṣe dharive īśhvara 

amani yugala-preme sāttbika-vikāre 
dharāya luṭiba āmi śhrī-nṛsiṁha-dvāre
IDX.en_translation:
In this wicked heart, the six enemies such as lust, crookedness, the desire for fame, and deceit always reside. 

My only prayer at the feet of Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva is for the purification of my heart and for a sincere desire to serve Lord Kṛṣṇa. 

When will I weep at the feet of Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva and beg to safely perform the worship of the Divine Couple in Navadvīpa? 

When will Lord Hari—whose very sight frightens even fear itself—be pleased and show mercy to me? 

Although His form is terrifying toward wicked beings, He is extremely kind to devotees of Lord Kṛṣṇa like Prahlāda Mahārāja. 

When, being pleased, will He make this foolish and insignificant soul fearless with His merciful words? 

“Freely reside, O child, in the holy land of Lord Gaurāṅga. Let there be the worship of the Divine Couple, and let there be attachment to the Holy Name.” 

“By the mercy of My devotees, all obstacles will be removed. With a pure heart, worship Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, the source of all nectar.” 

Saying this, when will the Lord happily place His own divine feet upon my head? 

Then, with ecstatic transformations due to the love of the Divine Couple, I will roll on the ground at the door of Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva.

IDX.verses: e ghora saṁsāre, paḍiyā mānava, nā pāya duḥkhera śheṣa sādhu-saṅga kari’, hari bhaje jadi, tabe anta haya kleśha saṁsāra-anale, jvalicḣe hṛdaya, anale bāḍaye anala aparādha cḣāḍi’ laya kṛṣṇa-nāma, anale paḍaye jala nitāi-chaitanya, charaṇa-kamale, āśhraya loila jei kṛṣṇadāsa bale, jīvane maraṇe, āmāra āśhraya sei
IDX.en_translation:
Having fallen into this terrible saṁsāra, man finds no end to suffering. If one associates with sādhu and worships Hari, then suffering comes to an end. 

In the fire of saṁsāra, the heart burns, and fire increases fire. Giving up aparādha and chanting Kṛṣṇa-nāma is like water falling into the fire. 

Whoever takes refuge at the lotus feet of Nitāi-Caitanya - Kṛṣṇa-dāsa says - that is my refuge in life and death.
IDX.es_translation:
Tras caer en este terrible mundo material, el ser humano no halla fin a su sufrimiento, mas si se asocia con devotos y sirve a Śhrī Hari, toda su agonía cesará. 

Su corazón arde en el fuego de la existencia material, que aumenta incesantemente por sí solo. El canto de los nombres de Kṛṣṇa evitando las ofensas vierte agua sobre ese fuego. 

Kṛṣṇa-dāsa dice: “La persona que se ha refugiado en los pies de loto de Nitāi-Chaitanya es mi refugio en la vida y en la muerte”.

IDX.verses: e mana! āra ki mānuṣa habe bhārata-bhūmete, janama labhiye, ki kāja karili kabe prathame jananī-, kolete kautuka, nāhi cḣila jñāna āra śhiśhura sahite, khelāli beḍāli, paugaṇḍa emati pāra prakṛti artha, anartha hoila, se made hoili bhora bujhite nāriye, kāminī-sāpinī, mātiye rākhili kroḍa suta-sutā laye, magana rahili, bhuliye pūrava kathā māyera udare, kata nā kahili, jakhana pāili vyathā chaturthe āsiye, jarāya gherila, sāmarthya hoila hīna tabu ‘tora’ ‘mora’, nā ghuche vachana, śhamana gaṇicḣe dina kubuddhi cḣāḍiye, ‘hari hari’ bala, nikaṭe śhamana bhāi kahe premānanda, je-nāma loile, śhamana-gamana nāi
IDX.en_translation:
O my mind! Will you ever truly become a human being? Having taken birth in this sacred land, what spiritual work have you done so far? 

At first, you were in your mother’s lap, full of playfulness, without any spiritual knowledge. You played and roamed with other children, and thus your childhood passed. 

Then your very nature became a calamity as you became intoxicated by the pursuit of wealth. Unable to understand that the objects of your desire were like a serpent, you remained infatuated. 

With your children, you remained engrossed, forgetting the promises you made previously. In your mother’s womb, you pledged so much when you were suffering in pain. 

As the fourth stage of life arrived, old age enveloped you and your strength diminished. Still, your talk of “yours” and “mine” does not cease, while the God of Death counts your days. 

Abandoning your evil intellect, chant “Hari! Hari!” the God of Death is near, O brother. Premānanda says: “By taking that Name, there is no more fear of death.”

IDX.en_translation:
O my mind! Make the Holy Name of Lord Hari your only essence. This ocean of material existence will then become like a mere sandbank, and you will easily cross it by walking. 

Religious duties, worldly actions, chanting, austerity, speculative knowledge, yoga, sacrifices, and meditation—no, no, no! In this Age of Kali, the only means of success is the Name of Govinda. 

Whether it be worldly enjoyment or liberation—do not develop any attachment to them. Such destinations are only as permanent as the coolness found in the shadow of a passing cloud. 

Filling your mouth, chant “Hari! Hari!” When will such an easy opportunity ever come again? A human birth in this sacred land—will it ever happen again? 

See the evidence in all the Purāṇas: there is nothing equal to the Holy Name. When attachment to the Name awakens, divine love arises, and through that love, we attain Lord Hari. 

Constantly engage in hearing and chanting His glories, giving up all useless talk. Premānanda Dāsa says: “Make this human birth successful; do not waste it.”

IDX.en_translation:
O my mind! What do social class and family lineage really accomplish? In whichever family one may be born, devotion is the only essential thing. 

In the monkey lineage, the heroic Hanumān is blessed as the foremost devotee of Lord Rāma. Though born a demon, Vibhīṣaṇa sits in the midst of the Lord’s assembly. 

Though born from a demon, Prahlāda Mahārāja kept his fame throughout the world. Within a crystal pillar, Lord Nṛhari appeared, becoming subservient to him. 

Though he was an outcaste, Guhaka became a friend of the Lord. Tell me, what noble family did Vidura have? Yet, the Lord ate in his house. 

See how the gopīs of Gokula performed their spiritual practice. What did their caste or family traditions accomplish then? For Lord Hari, only those who serve Him are dear. 

Everyone has the right to worship Lord Kṛṣṇa; there is no room for pride of lineage. Premānanda says: “He who takes pride in his family background is utterly foolish, my brother.”

O my mind! For what purpose did you come to this material world? In such a rare human birth, you have not worshipped Lord Hari. When will you truly act as a human being? 

What is the use of having a human form if you perform only the acts of a ghost? Otherwise, why do you not utter the Names of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Govinda with your mouth? 

Even birds like parrots and mynahs will chant the Name if taught. Yet you are lazy in this matter—how can this be appropriate? 

Day and night you can speak nonsense and engage in idle chatter. In the midst of all that, why can you not utter the Name of Lord Govinda? 

You came to this world promising to worship the Lord, but having forgotten that, what happiness have you found? I understand that you will eventually drown in hell in the city of the God of Death. 

If you wholeheartedly chant the Name of Lord Hari, it will do you no harm. Premānanda says: “Only then will you certainly escape the grasp of the God of Death.”

IDX.verses: e mana! tu baḍa kalira bhūta kara bala jāri, śhūnye diyā bāḍi, hāsaye tapana-suta bhūtera bāpera, śhrāddha kara niti, bhūtera vegāra khāṭa lāja nāhi mukhe, kāla kāṭa’ sukhe, chalicḣa jamera bāṭa kāminī-kāñchana, hṛdaya-rañjana, tāhāte magana thāka o dike tomāra, ki daśhā ghaṭicḣe, tāra kicḣu khoja rākha chaurāśhī narake, jābe eke eke, patha pariṣkāra prāya kapālera jora, baḍa baṭe tora, bāhādurī habe tāya mūrakha barbvara, suyukati dhara, jadi taribāre chāo kahe premānanda, manera ānande, sadā hari-guṇa gāo
IDX.en_translation:
O my mind! You are a great ghost of the Age of Kali. You keep exerting useless force and striking out into the void, while the Son of the Sun-god laughs at you. 

You always perform the rituals for the ghost’s father and work as a forced laborer for ghosts. You have no shame; you pass your time happily while walking straight on the path to the God of Death. 

You remain engrossed in women and gold, which delight your heart. On the other hand, do you keep any track of the terrible condition that is befalling you? 

You will go to the eighty-four hells one by one—the path is almost clear. Your fate is truly strong; there will be great “heroism” in that. 

O foolish barbarian! Adopt good reasoning if you wish to cross over this ocean. Premānanda says: “With a joyful mind, always sing the glories of Lord Hari.”

IDX.first_line: e mana tumi ki bhevecḣa sukha
IDX.search: e mana tumi ki bhevecḣa sukha supatha cḣadiya kupathe gamana e tora kemana buka sthavara yonite krame je janama hoiya vimsati laksa jala jantu majhe nava laksa ara jalei vasati bhaksya ekadasa laksa krmite janama dasa laksa joni paksa pasura majhare krame tetrisa laksa manava chatur laksa manuse asiya kutsit dvi laksa sudradi dvisatavara brahmana kulete pare ekabara ta sama nahika ara kateka kalapa bhramiya manusa emana janame papa samane bandhiya puna na felabe abara tomare bapa vadana bhariya hari hari bala asata bhavana cḣada kahe premananda tabe se chatura e saba jatana eda
IDX.author: premānanda-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: e mana! tumi ki bhevecḣa sukha supatha cḣāḍiyā, kupathe gamana, e tora kemana buka sthāvara-yonite, krame je-janama, hoiyā viṁśhati lakṣa jala-jantu-mājhe, nava lakṣa āra, jalei vasati bhakṣya ekādaśha lakṣa, kṛmite janama, daśha lakṣa joni pakṣa paśhura mājhāre, krame tetriśha lakṣa, mānava chatur lakṣa mānuṣe āsiyā, kutsit dvi-lakṣa, śhūdrādi dviśhatavāra brāhmaṇa-kulete, pare ekabāra, tā-sama nāhika āra kateka kalapa, bhramiyā mānuṣa, emana janame pāpa śhamane bāndhiyā, puna nā felābe, ābāra tomāre bāpa vadana bhariyā, ‘hari hari’ bala, asata-bhāvanā cḣāḍa kahe premānanda, tabe se chatura, e saba jātanā eḍa
IDX.en_translation:
O mind! What have you thought to be happiness? Leaving the good path, going on the bad path—what kind of heart is this of yours? 

In the species of unmoving beings (plants), birth after birth, becoming twenty lakhs (2,000,000). Among the water-animals, nine lakhs (900,000) more; residence and food in the water. 

Eleven lakhs (1,100,000) birth in worms; ten lakhs (1,000,000) bird species. Among the animals, in sequence thirty-three lakhs (3,300,000); humans four lakhs (400,000). 

Coming into human (species), ugly (uncivilized) two lakhs (200,000); Śūdras etc. two hundred times. In the Brāhmaṇa family, afterwards one time; there is nothing equal to that. 

Wandering for how many Kalpas, (you attain) such a birth; (if you commit) sin (in this birth). Binding (you), Yamarāja will not drop (you into this birth) again, O dear one. 

Filling the mouth, say “Hari! Hari!”, give up bad thoughts. Premānanda says: Then he is clever; avoid all this suffering.

IDX.first_line: e mana tumi se kevala bhūta
IDX.search: e mana tumi se kevala bhuta kusanga smasane satata basicḣa paiya parama juta mala mutra jata asata pachala e tora bhaksana sukhe rama krsna hari gopala govinda balite naricḣa mukhe je kara tomara govinda pujane tiratha bhramite pa ya se dui rakhile churiye dariye tabe ki ulta naya jata na karicḣa sadhura helana se tora anala mukhe dekha na tahate apani dahicḣa emati gonabi dukhe krsnera vasati sadhura hrdaye sukhera visrama bhumi emana durdaiva tanhara parasa karite naricḣa tumi sri hari charana karaha sarana gaya ganga saba tate kahe premananda tabe se uddhara nahile va habe kate
IDX.author: premānanda-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: e mana! tumi se kevala bhūta kusaṅga-śhmaśhāne, satata basicḣa, pāiyā parama juta mala mūtra jata, asata pachāla, e tora bhakṣaṇa sukhe ‘rāma kṛṣṇa hari’, ‘gopāla govinda’, balite nāricḣa mukhe je ‘kara’ tomāra, govinda-pūjane, tīratha bhramite pā-ya se dui rākhile, churiye dāriye, tabe ki ulṭā naya jata nā karicḣa, sādhura helana, se tora anala mukhe dekha nā tāhāte, āpani dahicḣa, emati goṅābi dukhe kṛṣṇera vasati, sādhura hṛdaye, sukhera viśhrāma-bhūmi emana durdaiva, tāṅhāra paraśha, karite nāricḣa tumi śhrī-hari-charaṇa, karaha śharaṇa, gayā-gaṅgā saba tā’te kahe premānanda, tabe se uddhāra, nahile vā habe kā’te
IDX.en_translation:
O my mind! You are merely a ghost, always sitting in the cremation ground of bad company, finding it very suitable there. 

All impure and rotten things are your food for pleasure. You cannot even utter the names “Rāma,” “Kṛṣṇa,” “Hari,” “Gopāla,” or “Govinda.” 

Your hands are meant for worshipping Lord Govinda, and your feet are meant for traveling to holy places—if you keep them idle, stealing away their true purpose, then is that not utterly wrong? 

All the disrespect you show to the saintly is like fire in your mouth. See how you are burning in it yourself, and thus you will pass your life in misery. 

Lord Kṛṣṇa’s abode is in the hearts of the saintly—a resting place of true happiness. Such is your misfortune that you are unable to obtain their touch. 

Take refuge at the feet of Lord Hari; all holy places like Gayā and the Ganges are contained therein. Premānanda says: “Only then will you be delivered; otherwise, who will achieve it?”

IDX.first_line: e mana tumi vā bhulecḣa kise
IDX.search: e mana tumi va bhulecḣa kise tomare dekhiya samana kinkara hate tali diya hase ratri dine kata asata pachalo sri hari kahite naro emana durlabha janama paiye ki sukhe e ksepa haro dhana jane jata apana balicḣa ke tora jaibe sathe gayera gumane picḣu na ganili thekali samana hate dekhiye suniye bujhite narili asare janili sara apanara matha apani bhangili bala na e dosa kara ekhana takhana kakhana ki jani hasite khelite padi e sukha smaribe galaya jakhana chadibe chamera dadi vadana bhariya hari hari bala samana taribe sukhe kahe premananda hari na bhajili kali chuna tora mukhe
IDX.author: premānanda-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: e mana! tumi vā bhulecḣa kise tomāre dekhiyā, śhamana-kiṅkara, hāte tāli diyā hāse rātri-dine kata, asata pachālo, ‘śhrī-hari’ kahite nāro emana durlabha, janama pāiye, ki sukhe e kṣepa hāro dhana-jane jata, āpanā balicḣa, ke tora jāibe sāthe gāyera gumāne, picḣu nā gaṇili, ṭhekāli śhamana-hāte dekhiye śhuniye, bujhite nārili, asāre jānili sāra āpanāra māthā, āpani bhāṅgili, bala nā e doṣa kā’ra ekhana takhana, kakhana ki jāni, hāsite khelite paḍi e sukha smaribe, galāya jakhana, chaḍibe chāmera daḍi vadana bhariyā, ‘hari hari’ bala, śhamana taribe sukhe kahe premānanda, ‘hari’ nā bhajili, kāli chuṇa tora mukhe
IDX.en_translation:
O my mind! What have you forgotten? Seeing your condition, the servants of the God of Death clap their hands and laugh. 

Day and night you waste your time in useless talk and can never utter “Śrī Hari.” Having obtained such a rare human birth, for what supposed pleasure do you lose this opportunity? 

Of all the wealth and people you consider your own, who among them will go with you in the end? In the pride of your body, you did not consider the end, and now you have fallen into the hands of death. 

Even after seeing and hearing the truth, you could not understand it; you considered the temporary to be essential. You have brought this ruin upon yourself—tell me, whose fault is it? 

Who knows when, whether now or then, you will suddenly fall while laughing and playing? You will remember your current pleasures when the rope of the God of Death tightens around your neck. 

Chant “Hari! Hari!” with a full heart and you will happily cross over the kingdom of death. Premānanda says: “If you do not worship Lord Hari, there will be nothing but disgrace upon your face.”

IDX.first_line: e mana vichāri kena nā chāo
IDX.search: e mana vichari kena na chao dekha bhava roga te kene ghuche na kata na ausadha khao kata na karicḣa prasada bhaksana charana dhauta jala e saba ausadhi pana kara tabu dhatute nahika bala jihvara parase je hari namete premete bhasaya tanu se nama loiye ardra na hoili lohara pinda se janu bhaviya dekha na ausadhe ki kare kupathya cḣadite naro kupathya thakile roga na cḣadibe aruchi badibe aro anupana jani ausadhi khao to rogera damana habe ekhano ta jadi bujhite na para tabe se bujhibe kabe ksudhati badaye ruchiti janame khaite ananda jala kahe premananda tabe se janiha ausadhi dharana fala
IDX.author: premānanda-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: e mana! vichāri kena nā chāo dekha bhava-roga, te kene ghuche nā, kata nā auṣadha khāo kata nā karicḣa, prasāda bhakṣaṇa, charaṇa-dhauta jala e saba auṣadhi, pāna kara tabu, dhātute nāhika bala jihvāra paraśhe, je hari-nāmete, premete bhāsāya tanu se nāma loiye, ārdra nā hoili, lohāra piṇḍa se janu bhāviyā dekha nā, auṣadhe ki kare, kupathya cḣāḍite nāro kupathya thākile, roga nā cḣāḍibe, aruchi bāḍibe āro anupāna jāni, auṣadhi khāo to, rogera damana habe ekhano tā jadi, bujhite nā pāra, tabe se bujhibe kabe kṣudhāṭī bāḍaye, ruchiṭī janame, khāite ānanda-jala kahe premānanda, tabe se jāniha, auṣadhi-dhāraṇa-fala
IDX.en_translation:
O my mind! Why do you not think and see for yourself? Behold the disease of material existence—why does it not disappear, even though you take so many “medicines”? 

How much food offered to the Lord do you partake, and how much water that has washed His feet? You drink all these medicines, yet there is no spiritual strength in your constitution. 

The Holy Name of Lord Hari, by its very touch upon the tongue, can float the entire body in divine love. Yet taking that Name, your heart has not become softened; such a person is like a lump of iron. 

Just think—what can medicine do if you cannot give up unwholesome food? If you continue to eat such things, the disease will not leave you, and your aversion to spiritual life will only increase. 

If you take the medicine with the correct knowledge and proper following of instructions, the disease will be suppressed. If you still cannot understand this, then when will you ever understand? 

Only when spiritual hunger increases and a taste for divine bliss awakens should you know that the medicine is truly taking effect. Premānanda says: “Only then will you know the true fruit of the medicine.”

IDX.first_line: e tina bhuvana mājhe avanī maṇḍala sāje
IDX.search: e tina bhuvana majhe avani mandala saje tahe punah ati anupama soka duhkha tapatraya jara nama santi haya hena sei santipura grama kuvera pandita taya suddha sattva dvijaraya nabha devi tahara grhini santipure kare sthiti krsna puja kare niti bhakti hina dekhiya avani kalihata jiva dekhi mane duhkha paya ati bhakte aradhaye bhagavana se aradhana kaje nabhadevira garbhajhe mahavisnu hailena adhisthana magha mase subhaksane sukla saptami dine avatirna hailena mahasaya dekhiya pandita ati haila harasita mati nayane ananda dhara vaya achambite jagajane ananda paila mane ki lagiya keha nahi jane e vaisnava dase bole uddhara haiba bale patita pasandi dina hine
IDX.author: vaiṣṇava-dāsa
IDX.verses: e tina bhuvana mājhe, avanī maṇḍala sāje tāhe punaḥ ati anupāma śhoka duḥkha tāpatraya, jāra nāma śhānti haya hena sei śhāntipura grāma kuvera paṇḍita tāya, śhuddha sattva dvijarāya nābhā-devī tāhāra gṛhinī śhāntipure kare sthiti, kṛṣṇa-pūjā kare niti bhakti-hīna dekhiyā avanī, kalihata jīva dekhi, mane duḥkha pāya ati bhakte ārādhaye bhagavāna se ārādhana kaje, nābhādevīra garbhājhe mahāviṣṇu hailena adhiṣṭhāna māgha-māse śhubhakṣaṇe, śhuklā saptamī dine avatīrṇa hailena mahāśhaya dekhiyā paṇḍita ati, haila haraṣita mati nayane ānanda-dhārā vaya āchambite jagajane, ānanda pāila mane ki lāgiyā keha nāhi jāne e vaiṣṇava-dāse bole, uddhāra haiba bale patita pāṣaṇḍī dīna hīne
IDX.en_translation:
Within these three worlds, the earthly realm is beautifully adorned, and within it, there is a most incomparable place. It is the village of Śāntipura, where the very name means “peace from grief, sorrow, and the three-fold miseries.” 

There lived Kuvera Paṇḍita, a pure and saintly king among the twice-born, and his wife was Nābhā-devī. They resided in Śāntipura, always performing the worship of Lord Kṛṣṇa, and they were grieved to see the world devoid of devotion. 

Seeing the living entities afflicted by the age of Kali, Kuvera Paṇḍita felt great sorrow in his heart. As a devotee, he worshipped the Supreme Lord. In response to that worship, Lord Mahā-Viṣṇu appeared within the womb of Nābhā-devī. 

In the month of Māgha, at an auspicious moment on the seventh day of the bright fortnight, that great personality descended. Seeing Him, the Paṇḍita’s heart was filled with joy, and streams of bliss flowed from his eyes. 

Suddenly, everyone in the world felt a strange joy in their minds, but no one knew the reason for it. Vaiṣṇava Dāsa says: “By the power of this descent, the fallen, the atheists, and the most distressed will all be delivered.”

IDX.first_line: ei bāra karuṇā kara chaitanya nitāi
IDX.search: ei bara karuna kara chaitanya nitai mo sama pataki ara tri bhuvane nai muni ati mudhamati mayara nafara ei saba pape mora tanu jara jara mleccḣa adhama jata cḣila anachari ta saba hoite mora papa ati bhari asesa papera papi jagai madhai ta dohare uddharile tomara duti bhai lochana bale mo adhame daya naila kene tumi na karile daya ke karibe ane
IDX.author: lochana-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: ei-bāra karuṇā kara chaitanya-nitāi mo-sama pātakī āra tri-bhuvane nāi muñi ati mūḍhamati māyāra nafara ei saba pāpe mora tanu jara jara mleccḣa adhama jata cḣila anāchārī tā-sabā’ hoite mora pāpa ati bhārī aśheṣa pāpera pāpī jagāi-mādhāi tā-dohāre uddhārile tomarā du’ṭī bhāi lochana bale mo-adhame dayā naila kene tumi nā karile dayā ke karibe āne
IDX.en_translation:
O Lord Caitanya and Lord Nitāi! Please show Your mercy this time. There is no sinner like me in all the three worlds. 

I am very foolish and a servant of illusion. My body is tormented by all these sins. 

Compared to all the most fallen and unrighteous persons, my sins are much heavier. 

You two brothers delivered Jagāi and Mādhāi, who were the greatest of sinners. 

Locana Dāsa says: “Why is there no mercy for a fallen soul like me? If You do not show mercy, who else will?”

IDX.first_line: ei bāra karuṇā kara vaiṣṇava gosāi
IDX.search: ei bara karuna kara vaisnava gosai patita pavana toma bine keha nai kahara nikate gele papa dure jaya emana dayala prabhu keba kotha paya gangara parasa hoile paschate pavana darsane pavitra kara ei tomara guna hari sthane aparadhe tare harinama toma sthane aparadhe nahika edana tomara hrdaye sada govinda visrama govinda kahena mama vaisnava parana prati janme kari asa charanera dhuli narottame kara daya apanara bali
IDX.author: narottama-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: ei-bāra karuṇā kara vaiṣṇava-gosāi patita-pāvana tomā bine keha nāi kāhāra nikaṭe gele pāpa dūre jāya emana dayāla prabhu kebā kothā pāya? gaṅgāra paraśha hoile paśhchāte pāvana darśhane pavitra kara—ei tomāra guṇa hari-sthāne aparādhe tā’re harināma tomā-sthāne aparādhe nāhika eḍāna tomāra hṛdaye sadā govinda viśhrāma govinda kahena, ‘mama vaiṣṇava parāṇa’ prati-janme kari āśhā charaṇera dhūli narottame kara dayā āpanāra bali’
IDX.en_translation:
Now bestow your mercy, O Vaiṣṇava, Without you, there is no one who can purify the fallen. 

approaching whom do sins go away? Such a merciful master, who can find anywhere else? 

Purification from touching the Gaṅgā comes later; You purify by mere sight-this is your quality. 

If one offends Hari, the holy name of Hari saves them; But if one offends you, there is no escape. 

In your heart, Govinda always rests; Govinda says, “The Vaiṣṇava is My very life”. 

In every birth, I hope for the dust of your feet. Show mercy to Narottama, accepting him as your own.
IDX.es_translation:
¡Vaiṣṇava Gosāi, dame por favor tu misericordia ahora! Tú eres el salvador de los caídos. Solo tú puedes salvarme. 

Por estar cerca de ti, todos los pecados se alejan. ¿Dónde encontrar a alguien tan misericordioso como tú? 

Uno se purifica al tocar el Gaṅgā, pero tu extraordinaria cualidad es que cualquiera se purifica solo con verte. 

Las ofensas cometidas contra los pies de loto de Śhrī Hari son absueltas por el harināma, pero no hay forma de liberarse de las ofensas contra ti. 

Śrī Govinda descansa siempre en tu corazón. Por eso Él dice: “Los vaiṣṇavas son Mi vida y Mi alma”. 

Yo aspiro a obtener el polvo de tus pies en cada nacimiento. Por favor, sé compasivo con este Narottama dāsa y considérame tuyo.

IDX.first_line: ei bāra pāile dekhā charaṇa du’khāni
IDX.search: ei bara paile dekha charana dukhani hiyara majhare rakhi judaba parani tare na dekhiya mora mane bada tapa anale pasiba kimva jale diba jhanpa mukhera mucḣaba ghama khaoyaba pana guya ghamete vatasa diba chandanadi chuya vrndavanera fulera ganthiya diba hara vinaiya bandhiba chuda kuntalera bhara kapale tilaka diba chandanera chanda narottama dasa kahe viparitera fanda
IDX.author: narottama-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: ei-bāra pāile dekhā charaṇa du’khāni hiyāra mājhāre rākhi’ juḍā’ba parāṇī tā’re nā dekhiyā mora mane baḍa tāpa anale paśhiba kiṁvā jale diba jhāṅpa mukhera mucḣāba ghāma, khāoyāba pāna guyā ghāmete vātāsa diba chandanādi chūyā vṛndāvanera fulera gāṅthiyā diba hāra vināiyā bāndhiba chūḍā kuntalera bhāra kapāle tilaka diba chandanera chāṅda narottama-dāsa kahe viparītera fāṅda
IDX.en_translation:
If I can see Your two lotus feet this time, I will keep them within my heart and soothe my soul. 

Not seeing You, there is great burning in my mind. I will enter into fire or jump into the water. 

I will wipe the sweat from Your face and feed You betel nuts. When You sweat, I will fan You and apply sandalwood paste and other scents. 

I will string a garland of Vṛndāvana flowers and give it to You. I will braid Your hair and tie it into a topknot. 

I will place a tilaka mark of sandalwood paste on Your forehead like a moon. Narottama Dāsa says, “This is a trap of the contrary situation (separation).”

IDX.search: ei rupe nitya lila kare dui jana dina bhede lila bheda kariba varnana radha kunde govardhane lila dinamane ratri lila jamuna puline vrndavane vrndavana sola krosa lila ayatana mahidhara chatur dike bahu tirtha gana sarovara rupe sobha kare anuksana acḣena manasa ganga giriraja pase nauka lila kare krsna jathaya ullase sujyotsna moksana malyahara gauri sara sumana vanari dhvaja gandharva sagara tathaya arista kunda ara radha kunda sarva tirtharaja jatha sobhe tarusanda radha kunda uttare je ghata manohara tannikate astadala svarupa chatvara ananga ranga ambuja kunja manohara janha lalitara gana seve nirantara lalitanandada kunja acḣaye tathaya tannikate bahu kunja gana sobha paya tahara isane kunja madana sukhada svananda sukhada kunja bada sukhaprada visakha ananda nama kunja sukhaprada radha kunda purvabhage chitrananda nama chitrasakhi kunja jatha radhara visrama radha kunda agnikone purnendu samjnaka indulekha kunja krsna ananda vardhaka radha kunda daksine champakalata kunja parama ananda prada nama hemakunja kundera nairta kone kunja manohara syama kunja nama rangadevi kunjavara radha kunda paschime aruna kunja nama tungavidya seve tatha nitya radha syama sudevira kunja radha kunda vayukone harit kunja bali khyata kaila sakhigane ei astasathi kunje jatha sarva kala radha krsna lila kare parama rasala
IDX.author: sacchidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
ei-rūpe nitya-līlā kare dui-jana 
dina-bhede līlā-bheda kariba varṇana 

rādhā-kuṇḍe govardhane līlā dinamāne 
rātri-līlā jāmuna-puline vṛndāvane 

vṛndāvana ṣola krośha līlā-āyatana 
mahīdhara chatur-dike bahu tīrtha-gaṇa
