IDX.en_translation:
In this manner, the Divine Couple perform Their eternal pastimes. I will now describe the distinctions in Their pastimes according to the different times of the day. 

During the daytime, Their pastimes take place at Rādhā-kuṇḍa and Govardhana Hill. The nighttime pastimes occur on the banks of the Yamunā in Vṛndāvana. 

Vṛndāvana, which is about thirty-two miles in area, is the abode of Their pastimes. On all four sides of Govardhana Hill there are many holy places which constantly shine beautifully in the form of lakes. 

Mānasagaṅgā is situated near Govardhana Hill, where Lord Kṛṣṇa joyfully performs His boating pastimes. 

There are also the lakes of Sujyotsnā, Mokṣaṇa, Mālyahāra, Gaurīsara, Sumana, and the Gandharva-sāgara. 

Furthermore, Ariṣṭa-kuṇḍa and Rādhā-kuṇḍa are located there, where the king of all holy places shines amidst groves of trees. 

To the north of Rādhā-kuṇḍa is a charming bathing place, and nearby is an eight-petaled courtyard. 

There is the enchanting lotus grove where Cupid plays and where Lalitā’s followers render constant service. 

The grove that gives bliss to Lalitā is situated there, and near it many other groves of the gopīs shine brightly. 

To its northeast is the grove named Madana-sukhad, which is very pleasing to Cupid. The grove of self-bliss is also very pleasing, as is the grove of Viśākhā’s bliss. 

In the eastern part of Rādhā-kuṇḍa is the grove named Citrānanda, which is the resting place of Rādhā. 

In the southeast corner of Rādhā-kuṇḍa is the grove known as Pūrṇendu, which enhances Lord Kṛṣṇa’s bliss. 

To the south of Rādhā-kuṇḍa is the supremely blissful golden grove of Campakalatā. 

In the southwest corner of the lake is the charming dark grove of Raṅgadevī. 

To the west of Rādhā-kuṇḍa is the reddish grove where Tuṅgavidyā eternally serves Rādhā and Śyāma. 

The green grove of Sudevī is in the northwest corner of Rādhā-kuṇḍa. 

In these groves of the eight principal gopīs, Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa perform Their supremely delightful pastimes at all times.

IDX.en_translation:
The river of Gaura-candra’s divine mellow came as a bank of clouds, inundating the land of Bengal with a rain of divine love. 

Lord Nityānanda became the helping wind, carrying it to those places where there was no such rain of love. 

With a thunderous roar came Śrī Advaita; Rāya Rāmānanda was a stream of watery mellow accompanying him. 

The sixty-four great souls came and beautified the clouds; Śrī Rūpa and Sanātana became the lightning within them. 

Kṛṣṇa dāsa Kavirāja, the treasurer of divine mellows, carefully preserved that love, filling a golden pot with it. 

Now, taking that divine love, he gave it to the people of the world. But this servant, Locana, by his own destiny, did not receive even a drop.
IDX.es_translation:
El río de gaura-rasa llegó como una masa de nubes de lluvia e inundó la región de Gauḍa con un torrente de prema. 

Nityānanda Rāya asistió como el viento, aventando el torrente de prema allá donde no había caído. 

Śhrī Advaita-chandra hizo su aparición como los truenos y Rāmānanda Rāya como la lluvia, y desataron la corriente del rasa. 

Los sesenta y cuatro grandes santos embellecieron la masa de nubes con su presencia, y Śhrī Rūpa-Sanātana iluminaron como sus rayos. 

Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja se convirtió en el mercader del rasa. Él colectó el prema y lo guardó cuidadosamente en un recipiente de oro. 

Ellos distribuyeron ese prema al mundo entero. Pero, para su desgracia, Lochana dāsa no recibió ni una sola gota.

IDX.en_translation:
There is no one like Gaurāṅga! Has such an incarnation ever appeared before, or will one ever appear again, who preaches such divine love? 

He did not kill even the most wicked, fallen, or sinful. Instead, He purified their hearts by going door to door, begging them to accept the Holy Name. 

He poured out upon the world that divine love desired even by Śiva and Brahmā. The poor and destitute received it, and they danced and clapped their hands in joy. 

Laughing, crying, and rolling on the ground in divine love, their bodies were covered in ecstatic thrills. When was such a sight ever seen—outcasts and priests embracing one another? 

Shouting and calling out, they roam about singing and running with drums and cymbals. Seeing this, the god of death became frightened and slammed shut his door. 

All the three worlds were filled with joy, and auspicious sounds arose. Premānanda says: for such a Gaurāṅga, no love has awakened in my heart.
IDX.es_translation:
¡No hay nadie como Gaurāṅga! Ninguna otra encarnación pasada, presente o futura ha predicado un prema tan extraordinario. 

Él no aniquiló a los pecadores o a los ateos, sino que purificó el corazón de todos yendo de puerta en puerta y distribuyendo libremente el santo nombre. 

Él derramó sobre el mundo entero el prema que desean incluso Śhiva y Brahmā. Las personas desposeídas danzan y aplauden llenos de dicha cuando reciben y beben este prema. 

Riendo y llorando, ellos ruedan por el suelo saturados de prema y sus cuerpos manifiestan erizamiento del vello. Hasta los chaṇḍālas (comedores de perros) y los brahmanes se abrazan mutuamente. ¿Cuándo se había visto antes una escena tan extraordinaria? 

Gritando y sollozando, con mṛdaṅgas y karatālas, Él y Sus devotos cantan y corren de un lado a otro. Al ver esto, Yamarāja (el Señor de la muerte) se ha asustado y ha cerrado su puerta. 

Los tres mundos se han llenado de bienaventuranza con el auspicioso tumulto del kīrtana. Premānanda dāsa se lamenta diciendo: “En mi corazón no ha surgido rati (afecto) por ese Gaurāṅga”.

IDX.translation_intro: Canción basada en un verso escrito por Śhrīla Prabodhānanda Sarasvatī en el Chaitanya-chandrāmṛta (130) que comienza con premā nāmādbhutārthaḥ.
IDX.en_translation:
Without the son of Śacī, who would have ever heard of the wondrous name of “prema”? 

Who else could have revealed the inherent glories of Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s name? Who would have entered the deep sweetness of the forests of Vṛndāvana? 

Who else would have made known the sweetness of Rādhā and her wonderful excellence in rasa? Who else was aware of her ecstatic transformations and experiences? 

The pastimes in Vraja—the rāsa and mahā-rāsa dances—the principle of paramour love, the glories of the gopīs, and the heights of their transitory emotions: who understood all this so deeply? 

All glories to the age of Kali! All glories to Nitāi and Caitanya, who out of supreme mercy filled the world by revealing the ecstatic symptoms of divine love, which are beyond the reach of ordinary rules. 

They did not discriminate between the exalted and the fallen but embraced everyone. Premānanda says: hold such a Gaurāṅga within your heart.
IDX.es_translation:
De no haber sido por el hijo de Madre Śhachī...
...¿Quién hubiera podido tener conocimiento de esa cosa extraordinaria y maravillosa llamada prema? 

¿quién hubiera revelado las gloriosas cualidades de los santos nombres de Śhrī Kṛṣṇa? ¿quién hubiera podido adentrarse en la dulzura suprema de los bosques de Vṛndā-devī? 

¿quién hubiera podido hablarnos de las extraordinarias glorias de las dulcísimas melosidades que experimenta Śhrī Rādhā? ¿quién hubiera podido percibir Sus anubhāvas o experimentar Sus extáticas transformaciones corporales? 

¿quién hubiera podido comprender plenamente los pasatiempos amorosos de Vraja, el excelso rāsa-līlā, las verdades fundamentales del amor de amante (parakīya-prema), las glorias de las gopīs y los límites de las emociones espirituales? 

Al otorgar la misericordia más grande, Śhrī Nitāi y Śhrī Chaitanya han hecho que esta bendita era de Kali sea supremamente gloriosa. Han saturado al mundo con revelaciones sobre el prema y sus transformaciones que están más allá de la comprensión incluso del Señor Brahmā. 

Sin discriminar entre elevados y caídos, Ellos abrazan libremente a todos. Premānanda dice, “¡Atesora a Gaurāṅga en tu corazón!”

IDX.translation_intro: Canción basada en un verso escrito por Śhrīla Prabodhānanda Sarasvatī en el Chaitanya-chandrāmṛta (130) que comienza con premā nāmādbhutārthaḥ.
IDX.en_translation:
Without the son of Śacī, who would have ever heard of the wondrous name of “prema”? 

Who else could have revealed the inherent glories of Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s name? Who would have entered the deep sweetness of the forests of Vṛndāvana? 

Who else would have made known the sweetness of Rādhā and her wonderful excellence in rasa? Who else was aware of her ecstatic transformations and experiences? 

The pastimes in Vraja—the rāsa and mahā-rāsa dances—the principle of paramour love, the glories of the gopīs, and the heights of their transitory emotions: who understood all this so deeply? 

All glories to the age of Kali! All glories to Nitāi and Caitanya, who out of supreme mercy filled the world by revealing the ecstatic symptoms of divine love, which are beyond the reach of ordinary rules. 

They did not discriminate between the exalted and the fallen but embraced everyone. Premānanda says: hold such a Gaurāṅga within your heart.
IDX.es_translation:
De no haber sido por el hijo de Madre Śhachī...
...¿Quién hubiera podido tener conocimiento de esa cosa extraordinaria y maravillosa llamada prema? 

¿quién hubiera revelado las gloriosas cualidades de los santos nombres de Śhrī Kṛṣṇa? ¿quién hubiera podido adentrarse en la dulzura suprema de los bosques de Vṛndā-devī? 

¿quién hubiera podido hablarnos de las extraordinarias glorias de las dulcísimas melosidades que experimenta Śhrī Rādhā? ¿quién hubiera podido percibir Sus anubhāvas o experimentar Sus extáticas transformaciones corporales? 

¿quién hubiera podido comprender plenamente los pasatiempos amorosos de Vraja, el excelso rāsa-līlā, las verdades fundamentales del amor de amante (parakīya-prema), las glorias de las gopīs y los límites de las emociones espirituales? 

Al otorgar la misericordia más grande, Śhrī Nitāi y Śhrī Chaitanya han hecho que esta bendita era de Kali sea supremamente gloriosa. Han saturado al mundo con revelaciones sobre el prema y sus transformaciones que están más allá de la comprensión incluso del Señor Brahmā. 

Sin discriminar entre elevados y caídos, Ellos abrazan libremente a todos. Premānanda dice, “¡Atesora a Gaurāṅga en tu corazón!”

IDX.search: eo ta eka kalira chela matha neda kapni para tilaka nake galaya mala dekhte vaisnavera mata asala sakta kajera bela sahaja bhajana karcḣena mamu sange laye parera bala sakhibhave bhajcḣena tare nije haye nandalala krsna dasera kathara cḣale mahajanake diccḣena sala nava rasika apane mani khaccḣena abara mana kala baula bale dohai o bhai dura kara e lilakhela

IDX.verses:
eo ta’ eka kalira chelā 
māthā neḍā, kapni parā, 
tilaka nāke, galāya mālā 

dekhte vaiṣṇavera mata, 
āsala śhākta kājera belā 
sahaja-bhajana karcḣena māmu, 
saṅge la’ye parera bālā 

sakhībhāve bhajcḣena tā’re, 
nije ha’ye nandalālā 
kṛṣṇa-dāsera kathāra cḣale 
mahājanake diccḣena śhalā 

nava-rasika āpane māni’, 
khāccḣena ābāra mana-kalā 
bāula bale, dohāi o bhāi, 
dūra kara e līlākhelā
IDX.en_translation:
This is indeed a disciple of Kali (the current age). Shaven-headed, wearing a kaupīna (loincloth), With tilaka on the nose, and mālā (beads) around the neck. 

Looking like a Vaiṣṇava, But actually a Śākta (worshipper of the Divine Mother) in practice. The uncle is performing sahaja-bhajana (a pseudo-devotional practice), Taking another’s woman along. 

Worshipping her in the mood of a sakhī (female confidante of Rādhā), thinking himself to be Nandalāla. Under the pretext of Kṛṣṇa-dāsa’s words, He is giving “advice” (or subtly criticizing) the mahājana (great souls). 

Considering himself a nava-rasika (a new “expert” in divine mellows), He is again indulging in “mana-kolā” (self-deception/sense gratification). The Baul says, “I beg you, O brother, Abandon this līlā-khelā (pretense).”

IDX.en_translation:
O Lord Gaura-hari! Please come into the temple of my heart. I will gaze upon You in the form of the five spiritual truths to my heart’s content. 

In Vraja, You were a cowherd boy, O Lord Gaura! In Nadīyā, You became the child of a brāhmaṇa. You were dark-complexioned, and now You have become golden—what secret desire do You hold in Your heart? 

The dark form of Lord Kṛṣṇa was beautiful, but Your golden form is even more beautiful than that. O Son of Mother Śacī! Now I cannot bear to see Your form as a renunciant. 

Around Your neck was a garland of forest flowers—who has taken that away now? They have placed a necklace of Tulasī beads around Your neck and decorated Your nose with the sacred markings of a devotee. 

To whom did You give Your enchanting crown? To whom did You give Your yellow garments? How is it that You have a shaven head and wear the saffron garments of a sannyāsī? 

Chanting “Rādhā! Rādhā! Rādhā!” You used to play Your enchanting flute, but now, without a flute, You are always chanting “Hari! Hari!” with that very mouth. 

O Moon of Nadīyā! Please come into the core of my heart. By seeing Your golden form with my own eyes, I will make my human birth successful.

IDX.translation_intro: From The Harmonist, June 1928. Edited by Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī.
IDX.en_translation:
I have surrendered my all at Thy feet; I have thrown myself on Thy household. Thou, the Supreme Lord, as Thy dog May Thou accept me. 

Chaining me close to Thee Thou wilt maintain me; I shall lie at Thy door-step. Who is opposed to Thee I will not allow to enter. I will ever keep him outside the bounds. 

What is left over of the favour of the refuse of Thy meals After being honoured by Thy own. Will be my food every day; On it I will feed with the greatest joy. 

Sitting up or lying down, on Thy feet I will meditate without a pause: And dancing hie to Thee with joy Whenever Thou call’st. 

I never will think for my own nourishment; I will ever cherish love. Bhaktivinode elects Thee As his Protector.
IDX.es_translation:
Tras entregarlo todo a Tus pies de loto, me hallo postrado ante Tu casa. Tú eres mi Señor; ten la bondad de aceptarme como Tu perro. 

Átame cerca y mantenme. Yo vigilaré Tu puerta y no permitiré que entren personas contrarias a Ti. Las mantendré fuera de Tu fortaleza. 

Me mantendré cada día lleno de dicha con el festín de los remanentes que dejen Tus devotos tras honrar el prasāda. 

Ya esté sentado o postrado, meditaré siempre en Tus pies de loto, y cuando me llames acudiré enseguida danzando de felicidad. 

Permaneceré siempre inmerso en bhāva y nunca pensaré en mi propio sustento. Bhaktivinoda Te acepta como su único mantenedor.

IDX.en_translation:
As I sang the Holy Name, what a state I reached! “I am Kṛṣṇa’s eternal servant” manifested in my heart. 

I realized that in this material world, bound by illusion, I suffer in various ways due to separation from Govinda. 

This worldly life no longer seems good to me. “Where shall I go to see Kṛṣṇa?”—this thought is vast. 

As I weep, my eyes pour down a rain-like torrent. 

A moment has become like a hundred eons for me. I am no longer able to bear separation from Govinda. 

The earth is empty; looking all around, my heart becomes indifferent. What shall I do? I cannot remain steady, and my life itself seems to depart. 

O residents of Vraja, save my life! Show me the Lord of Rādhā. Bhaktivinoda makes this humble request: please take him along with you. 

I can no longer tolerate separation from Śrī Kṛṣṇa. My life will depart in just a few days.

While singing the name of Govinda, a multitude of divine emotions arose. I saw on the banks of the Yamunā, along with the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu, Kṛṣṇa—the best of dancers—playing His flute at the base of a kadamba tree. 

Seeing that Divine Couple, my mind became restless and I lost all consciousness. I do not know how much time passed before I regained consciousness, but the vision was gone. 

O friend, how will I sustain my life? A moment feels like an eon. 

A stream of tears like the rains of Śrāvaṇa pours from my eyes; the whole world has become void. In separation from Govinda, my life cannot remain; tell me, how will I survive? 

Bhaktivinoda, becoming restless, again takes shelter of the Holy Name. He calls out to the Lord of Rādhā: “By granting Your vision, please save my life, otherwise I will die!”

IDX.en_translation:
He walks with the gait of a lordly elephant, gazing with compassion. The earth trembles under the weight of His steps. Conquering the pride of a mad lion, He makes the earth shake, and the atheists become distressed upon hearing His roar. 

Here comes the Avadhūta, the ocean of mercy! His mind is overwhelmed with divine love, and He performs the congregational chanting of Hari. He is the purifier of the fallen and the friend of the humble. 

He walks with a roar, shaking the movable and immovable. The assembly of demigods floats in love. With His companions, in the joy of various pastimes, He accomplishes all tasks unseen. 

He is Lord Saṅkarṣaṇa resting on Ananta Śeṣa, the source of all incarnations, Nārāyaṇa. His parts and portions are countless. He is the ocean of mercy, the giver of devotion, and the benefactor of the world. He is Lord Rāma (Balarāma), the son of Rohiṇī. 

His pastimes are an abode of beauty, sung in the Āgamas and Vedas. His form captivates even Cupid. Now, in the guise of a humble mendicant, the Lord wanders from land to land, liberating the three worlds. 

He is the essence of the charm of Vraja and all other pastimes. If your mind desires to attain them, Balarāma Dāsa says: “Your desires will be fulfilled. Just worship, worship His divine lotus feet.”

IDX.en_translation:
Lord Nityānanda walks slowly and majestically like a lordly elephant. Whomever He sees, He immerses them in the ocean of divine love. 

Going from house to house of the fallen, the distressed, and the sinful, He begs them to accept the divine love that is rare even for Lord Brahmā. 

To those who do not accept it, He says, holding a straw between His teeth, “Please purchase Me as your servant by chanting the name of Gaura-hari!” 

“For the sake of all of you, Lord Kṛṣṇa has incarnated. Listen, O brother! He is Gaurāṅgasundara of Nadiyā.” 

“That Lord, who was the son of Nanda Mahārāja in Gokula, has now incarnated for all of you.” Hearing this, the sinners cry, holding His feet, their bodies filled with ecstasy and their hearts overwhelmed. 

Embracing them, Lord Nityānanda goes to another place. In this way, He inundated every town and village with divine love. 

Devakīnandana Dāsa says: “I am so unfortunate. I have drowned in the well of material sense gratification, not having worshipped Lord Nityānanda.”

IDX.en_translation:
O Vṛndā Devī! Your inner self is bathed by a stream of splendor that surpasses gold, jasmine flowers, and lightning! O You whose divine garments possess the effulgence of a red flower! O Vṛndā Devī, I offer obeisances to Your lotus feet. 

O Vṛndā Devī! Your gentle smile emanates from lips like a red fruit, and Your face is illuminated by the luster of the pearls on the tip of Your nose. O You who are enriched by the beauty of various jeweled ornaments! O Vṛndā Devī, I offer obeisances to Your lotus feet. 

O Vṛndā Devī! You have been given authority by the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu in Lord Kṛṣṇa’s most fortunate abode, Vṛndāvana, which is the crest jewel of all the spiritual planets! O Vṛndā Devī, I offer obeisances to Your lotus feet. 

O Vṛndā Devī! By Your order, the pleasure groves of Kṛṣṇa are splendidly decorated with tender leaves, flowers, bees, deer, honey, and other things! O Vṛndā Devī, I offer obeisances to Your lotus feet. 

O Vṛndā Devī! By Your ambassadorship, the playful pastimes of the very eager young couple, Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, in the groves are perfected! Who can describe Your great fortune? O Vṛndā Devī, I offer obeisances to Your lotus feet. 

O Vṛndā Devī! The desire for the rāsa dance, residence in Vṛndāvana, and service to the lotus feet of Your Lord are all attainable by people only by Your mercy! O Vṛndā Devī, I offer obeisances to Your lotus feet. 

O Vṛndā Devī! You are glorified by those who know the scriptures as the energy of Kṛṣṇa named Līlā! Indeed, Your very form is Tulasi in the human world. O Vṛndā Devī, I offer obeisances to Your lotus feet. 

O Vṛndā Devī! We who are devoid of devotion, assailed by millions of offenses and thrown into the midst of the waves of lust and other material desires, have taken shelter of You, O merciful one! O Vṛndā Devī, I offer obeisances to Your lotus feet. 

Whoever hears or reads these eight verses glorifying Vṛndā becomes a bee at the lotus feet of the Lord of Vṛndāvana. He attains eternal residence in Vṛndāvana and, having achieved his goal, attains loving devotional service to Him.

He whose gait mocks the very intoxicated elephant; whose teeth censure the beautiful jasmine and Kunda flowers; whose luster destroys the pride of the beauty of ten million Cupids; whose charming face has a blossom of a beautiful smile. 

He who steals the joy of others by the vocalized flute; whose lotus eyes dance with intoxication; who is devoted to pastimes that expand the flood of rasa; the Goal of the people devoted to the supreme object. 

He whose movements adorn the land of the bank of the Yamunā; whose beautiful feet are praised by the Lord of the world; the luster of whose soft neck is bright with a medallion; who is very lovely, having taken a tilaka of pigment. 

He whose head is surrounded by trembling peacock feathers; whose arm is engaged in holding the King of Mountains; who holds a festival on the courtyard of the hoods of the King of Snakes; whose heart is greedy for playing in the caves of the Mountain. 

To whom a festival is given by His kind-hearted friends; who has shaken off Kali by the multitude of glorious topics; who holds all unconquerable strength of arms; who is accompanied by the strong boys of the cowherds. 

The desire tree desired by the beneficial saints; the fresh flower-arrow of the group of young women; most expert in protecting the surrendered; the fierce sun for the lotuses of the assembly of the wicked. 

A bunch of flowers meeting in His lotus hand; a lion to the intoxicated elephant of the Baka demon; the low sound of whose flute captivates the herds of deer; whose throat is bright with the low sound of the cuckoos. 

Who cut down the wicked people in battle for the sake of the pious people; the source of the creeper of fame auspicious for the people; Agastya for the ocean of material existence; without material qualities; whose group of devotees is devoid of attachment to the modes. 

Shining with divine qualities beyond counting; whose excellent face is the brother of the ray of His smile; the cloud for the wife of the excellent proud bull-demon (Ariṣṭa); consisting of pastimes in dense, amorous dress. 

The full moon for the destruction of the darkness of the son of Maya (Vyomāsura); who distressed the host of demon kings. I bow down here to Hari, the delight of the family. 

I worship Hari, shining on His chest with Indirā (Lakṣmī), shining with a garland like a temple of bees, the true sandalwood of auspiciousness for the very auspicious women.

When will my body shiver while saying “Gaurāṅga”? When will tears flow from my eyes while saying “Hari Hari”? 

When will Nitāi-cānda be merciful? When will my worldly desires become insignificant? 

When will my mind be purified by giving up sense objects? When will I see Śrī Vṛndāvana? 

When will there be eagerness for the feet of Rūpa and Raghunātha? When will I understand the love of the Divine Couple? 

My hope rests at the feet of Rūpa and Raghunātha; Narottama Dāsa always makes this prayer.
IDX.es_translation:
¿Cuándo se erizarán los vellos de mi cuerpo al cantar “Gaurāṅga”? ¿Cuándo se llenarán mis ojos de lágrimas al cantar “Hari Hari”? 

¿Y cuándo me dará Su misericordia la luna de Nityānanda Prabhu? ¿Cuándo se volverán insignificantes mis deseos materiales? 

¿Cuándo renunciaré al disfrute material y se purificará de ese modo mi mente? ¿Cuándo contemplaré Śhrī Vṛndāvana? 

¿Cuándo desarrollaré anhelo por los pies de loto de Śhrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī y Śhrīla Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī? Por su misericordia seré capaz de comprender el amor (prīti) de la Pareja Divina. 

Mi única aspiración es alcanzar los pies de loto de Śhrī Rūpa y Śhrī Raghunātha dāsa. Esta es la oración constante de Narottama dāsa.

Narottama Dāsa, the servant of the servant of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Prabhu, always makes this prayer.

Atrapados en la red de māyā, dedican sus vidas a actividades vanas. Obtengan ahora una conciencia plena y canten los nombres de Rādhā-Mādhava.

IDX.verses:
gāya gorā madhura svare 
hare kṛṣṇa hare kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa hare hare 
hare rāma hare rāma rāma rāma hare hare 

gṛhe thāka, vane thāka, sadā ‘hari’ bo’le ḍāka, 
sukhe duḥkhe bhula nā’ka, 
vadane harināma kara re 

māyājāle baddha ha’ye, ācḣa micḣe kāja la’ye, 
ekhanoo chetana pe’ye, 
rādhā-mādhava nāma bala re 

jīvana hoila śheṣa, nā bhajile hṛṣīkeśha, 
bhaktivinoda- (ei) upadeśha, 
ekabāra nāmarase mātare
IDX.en_translation:
Gaura-candra sings in a sweet voice: Hare Kṛṣṇa Hare Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa Hare Hare, Hare Rāma Hare Rāma Rāma Rāma Hare Hare. 

Whether you stay at home or in the forest, always call out “Hari!” In happiness or sorrow, never forget Him; chant the Holy Name with your mouth. 

Bound by the net of illusion, you are engaged in useless work. Now that you have regained consciousness, chant the names of Rādhā and Mādhava. 

Life will come to an end if you do not worship the Lord of the senses. This is the instruction of Bhaktivinoda: become intoxicated just once in the sweetness of the Holy Name.

gāy gorāchaṅda jīvera tare 
hare kṛṣṇa hare 

hare kṛṣṇa hare kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa hare hare, 
hare rāma hare rāma rāma rāma hare hare 

ekabāra bala rasanā uccḣaiḥsvare 
(bala) nandera nandana, jaśhodā-jīvana, 
śhrī-rādhā-ramaṇa prema-bhare 

(bala) śhrī-madhusūdana, gopī-prāṇadhana, 
muralīvadana nṛtya ka’re 
(bala) agha-nisūdana, pūtanā-ghātana, 
brahma-vimohana, ūrdhva-kare
IDX.en_translation:
Gaura-candra sings for the sake of all souls: “Hare Kṛṣṇa!” 

Hare Kṛṣṇa Hare Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa Hare Hare, Hare Rāma Hare Rāma Rāma Rāma Hare Hare 

O tongue, just once call out loudly: “Chant the names of the son of Nanda, the life of Yaśodā, and the enjoyer of Śrī Rādhā with great love! 

“Chant the names of the slayer of Madhu, the treasure of the gopīs’ lives, and the flute-player, while dancing. Chant the names of the slayer of Agha, the killer of Pūtanā, and the one who bewildered Brahmā, with Your arms raised high!”
IDX.es_translation:
Para beneficiar a las entidades vivientes, Śhrī Gaura-chandra canta: “Hare Kṛṣṇa Hare!” 

“Hare Kṛṣṇa Hare Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa Hare Hare, Hare Rāma Hare Rāma Rāma Rāma Hare Hare.” 

“Canten una vez en voz alta, ‘Nanda-nandana, Yaśhodā-jīvana, Śhrī Rādhā-Ramaṇa!’ llenos de prema.” 

“Canten, ‘Śhrī Madhusūdana, Gopī-prāṇa-dhana, Muralī-vadana!’ mientras bailan [de felicidad].” 

“Canten, ‘Agha-nisūdana, Pūtanā-ghātana, Brahma-vimohana!’ con los brazos en alto.”

IDX.verses:
gāyata rādhā mādhava-līlaṁ, 
kuruta matiṁ rasarañjita-śhīlām 

vṛndāraṇya charāchara vṛndaṁ 
śhrayata mahā-rasa vaibhava-vandam 

paśhyata rādhā keli nikuñjaṁ 
prakaṭa mahādbhuta-rati-rasa-puñjam 

puline puline tapana-sutāyāḥ 
bhramatha na jatra prasarati-māyā 

paramānanda rasāmṛta-sāre 
nayata mano vraja-rāja-kumāre 

muñchata viṣaya-viṣama rasa-gandhaṁ, 
ghaṭayata haripade dṛḍha-rati-bandham 

mṛgayata rādhā-pada-rasa-bhājaṁ, 
parichinūtojvalara-rasa bāram 

iti hita-sāra sarasvatī-gītaṁ, 
janayata kañchana bhāvam-adhitama
IDX.en_translation:
Sing of the pastimes of Rādhā and Mādhava. Make your mind joyful with pure transcendental mellows. 

In the Vṛndāvana forest, the multitude of all living beings takes shelter in the adoration of its great opulent mellows. 

Behold Rādhā’s playful grove, where an abundance of wonderful divine love is manifested. 

On every sandy bank of the Yamunā, wander where illusion does not spread. 

Bring your mind to the Son of Nanda Mahārāja, who is the essence of the nectar of supreme bliss. 

Give up the poisonous scent of material objects and fix a firm attachment at the feet of Lord Hari. 

Seek those devoted to the mellow of Śrīmati Rādhā-rāṇī’s feet, realizing the brilliant essence of divine love. 

Thus this song by Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī, ardently presented, generates some spiritual emotion.

IDX.en_translation: sādhāraṇa-vandanā (General Obeisance) I offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of the Spiritual Master and the assembly of devotees. I offer my respectful obeisances to Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, who has risen along with Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu. I offer my respectful obeisances to Śrī Nanda-nandana and the lotus feet of Śrīmati Rādhikā, accompanied by the gopīs, who make Vṛndāvana so enchanting. I offer my respectful obeisances to the Spiritual Master, to Lord Gaura-candra, to Śrīmati Rādhikā and Her abode, to Lord Kṛṣṇa, to His devotees, and to the devotees of His devotees. śrī-guru-vandanā (Obeisance to Śrī Guru) I bow down to that Śrī Guru, by whose abundant mercy I have attained the greatest name, the mantra, Śrī Śacī-nandana here, Śrī Svarūpa Dāmodara, Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī and his elder brother Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī, the great city of Mathurā, the cowherd village, Śrī Rādhā-kuṇḍa, Govardhana Hill, and the hope of attaining Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Mādhava. Obeisance to you, O Gurudeva, the bestower of all perfection, the embodiment of all auspiciousness, and the source of all bliss. O Śrī Guru, giver of divine knowledge, friend of the destitute, bestower of your own bliss, ocean of mercy, residing in Vṛndāvana! O incarnation of welfare! Please be merciful to me, O preacher of Rādhā’s love. Save me, O Master of the Universe, O Guru! I am burnt by the fire of material existence and bitten by the serpent of time. I have taken shelter of you. śrī-guru-rūpa-sakhī-vandanā (Obeisance to Guru as a Sakhī) I constantly offer obeisances to her, who is the abode of shelter for Mādhava, the cohesive energy facing Rādhā, residing in the company of the sakhīs. You are a gopī near the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu. O Guru, having the authority of service! Having given me the service of your own lotus feet, please make me happy in the ocean of bliss, in the mellow of serving the feet of Śrī Rādhā in the forest of Vraja. śrī-vaiṣṇava-vandanā (Obeisance to Vaiṣṇavas) I offer obeisances to those Vaiṣṇavas who are fully submerged in the waves of the excellent nectar of Vṛndāvana, which is the pure ocean of the nectar of Śrī Caitanyacandra’s character, and who purify the world by their own qualities and are devoted to the Holy Name of Hari. caturyugīya vaiṣṇava-vandanā (Obeisance to Vaiṣṇavas of the Four Ages) Svayambhū, Nārada, Śambhu, the Kumāras, Kapila, Manu, Prahlāda, Janaka, Bhīṣma, Bali, Vaiyāsaki, and us. Mārkaṇḍeya, Ambarīṣa, Vasu, Vyāsa, Vibhīṣaṇa, Puṇḍarīka, Bali, Śambhu, Prahlāda, Vidura, and Dhruva. Dālbhya, Parāśara, Bhīṣma, Nārada, and others are to be served by the Vaiṣṇavas. I serve Hari; otherwise, I would commit a great offense. śrīman-madhvāchārya-vandanā (Obeisance to Śrī Madhvāchārya) May the renunciate named Ānanda Tīrtha be victorious! He is an abode of happiness, and the wise praise him as the boat for crossing the ocean of material existence. śrīla-mādhavendra-purī-vandanā (Obeisance to Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī) I offer obeisances to Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī, the best of sannyāsīs, along with his disciples. By him, the wish-fulfilling tree of Kṛṣṇa-bhakti was made to sprout in this world. śrīla-sanātana-gosvāmī-vandanā (Obeisance to Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī) I take shelter of that master, Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī, the ocean of mercy, who is distressed by the suffering of others. With great effort, he made me drink the nectar of devotion mixed with renunciation, even though I was unwilling and blind. śrīla-rūpa-gosvāmī-vandanā (Obeisance to Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī) Holding a straw between my teeth, I beg this again and again: may I become the dust of the lotus feet of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī birth after birth. When will Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī himself give me the shelter of his own feet? He who established on this earth the innermost heart’s desire of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. śrīla-rūpa-raghunātha gosvāmī-vandanā (Obeisance to Śrīla Rūpa and Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmīs) O tongue! Always chant the name “Rūpa”. O mind! Remember Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, the embodiment of mercy. Bow your head to Śrīla Rūpa, whose glance is full of compassion, and to his second beautiful form, Śrīla Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī. śrīla-gopāla-bhaṭṭa-jīva-gosvāmī-vandanā (Obeisance to Śrīla Gopāla Bhaṭṭa and Jīva Gosvāmīs) I bow to Śrīla Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī, who fulfills the desires of the devotees, whose heart is flooded with eternal love, who is distinguished by the friendship of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, and whose only life is Śrī Rādhā-Ramaṇa. I constantly offer obeisances to Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī, who is attached to the lotus feet of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, who is a resident of Vraja, and who gives bliss to the ignorant. śrī-ṣaḍ-gosvāmī-vandanā (Obeisance to the Six Gosvāmīs) I offer obeisances to Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī along with his elder brother, to the merciful Raghunātha Dāsa, to Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī, and to the two Bhaṭṭas, who bestow happiness upon the saintly. I hold on my head the dust of the feet of these Gosvāmīs, who are naturally affectionate, again and again, for the destruction of all obstacles. śrī-pañca-tattva-vandanā (Obeisance to the Pañca-tattva) I bow to Lord Kṛṣṇa, who appears as the Pañca-tattva: in the form of a devotee, the manifestation of a devotee, the incarnation of a devotee, the pure devotee, and the devotional energy. I offer obeisances to the Gurus, the devotees of the Lord, the Lord Himself, His incarnations, His manifestations, and His energies. I bow to the Lord known as Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya. O Viśvambhara! O abode of the great nectar of mellows! O ocean of love! O son of mother Śacī! O You whose heart melts with compassion! You are the best friend of the fallen! O Lord of Sītā! O Master of the moving and non-moving! O You who are capable of bringing down the Gaura avatar! O object of affection for Śrīvāsa and Gadādhara! You are my shelter, You are my goal. śrī-śrīvāsa-vandanā (Obeisance to Śrī Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita) I praise Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita, the dear associate of Lord Gaurāṅga. By even a drop of his mercy, attachment to Lord Gaurāṅga is born. O Śrīvāsa! O bliss of kīrtana! O beloved of the assembly of devotees! I bow to you, O great mystic! You are Nārada Muni in the form of a devotee. I bow with joy to that Śrīvāsa, the foremost Paṇḍita, the recipient of Śrī Gaurāṅga’s mercy, whose mind finds bliss in kīrtana. śrī-gadādhara-paṇḍita-vandanā (Obeisance to Śrī Gadādhara Paṇḍita) I offer obeisances to Śrī Gadādhara Paṇḍita, the delight of Śrī Madhvāchārya, the embodiment of Mahābhāva, whose form is non-different from Śrī Caitanya. Obeisances forever to Śrī Gadādhara, who is the form of Śrīmati Rādhā-rāṇī, the wealth of Lord Gaurāṅga’s love. O merciful one! O Gadādhara! Obeisances to you, the embodiment of the Hlādinī-śakti, the companion of Lord Gaurāṅga, the bestower of devotional energy. śrī-śrī-advaita-prabhu-vandanā (Obeisance to Śrī Advaita Prabhu) Mahā-Viṣṇu, the creator of the universe, who creates this world through Māyā; this Advaita Āchārya is indeed His avatar, the Supreme Controller. I take shelter of that Advaita Āchārya, who is the Supreme Lord, the incarnation of a devotee. He is called “Advaita” because He is non-different from Hari, and “Āchārya” because He teaches devotion. O Śrī Advaita! Obeisances to you, the ocean of mercy for the people of Kali-yuga. Obeisances to the Lord of Śrī Sītā Ṭhākurāṇī, the bestower of love for Gaura. I offer obeisances to Śrīla Advaita Prabhu, the giver of loving devotion, who is dear to Śrīman Mādhavendra Purī and belongs to the Śrī Mādhava Sampradāya. Obeisances to Advaita, the Great Lord, the Great Soul, by whose mercy attachment to the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya is born. śrī-śrī-nityānanda-prabhu-vandanā (Obeisance to Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu) O Nityānanda! Obeisances to You, the giver of the bliss of divine love. Obeisances to the Lord of Jāhnavā Devī, for the destruction of the impurities of Kali-yuga. O son of Hāḍāi Paṇḍita! O ocean of mercy! O son of Padmāvatī! Your lotus feet are the shelter of all holy places! You are the wish-fulfilling tree of love, the avatar who removes all distress! Please protect me, a sinner, an orphan who has no other friend. I constantly offer obeisances to that Nityānanda, the Spiritual Master of the Universe, by whom this entire joyless world was made the abode of the bliss of love. I offer obeisances to Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu, who has a pearl shining in His ear, and who purified the earth by appearing as the elder brother of Śrī Caitanya. I constantly bow to Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu, the Lord who increases the ocean of love. In generosity, He surpasses the wish-fulfilling cows, celestial trees, moons, and gems. In beauty, He defeats the Cupids. He is the reservoir of the happiness of Brahman. In motherly affection, He challenges the herds of cows. I offer obeisances to Śrīman Nityānanda Candra, the embodiment of mercy, whose body is non-different from Śrī Caitanya, and who is dear to everyone. śrī-śrī-gaurāṅga-mahāprabhu-vandanā (Obeisance to Śrī Gaurāṅga Mahāprabhu) I offer obeisances to Your lotus feet, O Great Personality! You are always to be meditated upon. You destroy the insult of material life and fulfill all desires. You are the abode of all holy places, praised by Śiva and Brahmā. You are the only shelter, the reliever of the distress of Your servants, the protector of the surrendered, and the boat for crossing the ocean of material existence. I offer obeisances to Your lotus feet, O Great Personality! Abandoning the opulence of royalty desired by the gods, which is hard to renounce, You, the most righteous one, went to the forest in honor of the word of a brāhmaṇa, and ran after the illusionary deer desired by Your beloved. Obeisances, obeisances to You, O Śrī Caitanyacandra! Your form is full of blissful pastimes. You are beautiful with a brilliant golden luster, and You are the bestower of the great nectar of love. All glories to the power of the new lamp of Navadvīpa, the lion who defeats the elephants of atheism! Śrī Caitanyacandra, the Supreme Lord Murāri, holds the chanting beads of His own Holy Name. He is victorious! His valor is pure, He shines like gold, His eyes are large like lotus petals, His arms extend to His excellent knees, and He dances, manifesting the nectar of devotion in many ways. O Śrī Caitanyacandra! Please give me the support of Your lotus feet. I have fallen into the ocean of the misery of material existence, swallowed by the crocodiles and sharks of lust, anger, and greed, fettered by wicked desires, and I am without shelter. O Śrī Caitanyacandra! Make the lily of my heart bloom and delight it with the play of the bumblebee of Your own remembrance. Having shaken off the dense darkness of offenses, O merciful one, please make me, this unfortunate soul, drink the nectar of Your lotus feet. May that son of Mother Śacī always shine in the cave of your heart. He is Śrī Hari Himself, glowing with a multitude of beautiful golden rays. He descended in the Age of Kali out of mercy to bestow the wealth of His own devotion, the elevated brilliant mellow of Vraja, which had not been offered for a long time. I praise the form of Kṛṣṇa, now appearing as Śrī Caitanya, with the luster of the emotions of Śrī Rādhā. These two—the Hlādinī-śakti and the Śaktimān—are eternally one identity, yet previously on earth, They attained separate bodies. Now, They have again obtained unity in the form of Śrī Caitanya. śrī-śrī-gaura-nityānanda-vandanā (Obeisance to Śrī Gaura and Nityānanda) I offer obeisances to the two compassionate avatars, Śrī Gaura and Śrī Nityānanda, who make the world happy. They are the protectors of the religion of the age. Their arms extend to Their knees, Their complexion is golden, They are the fathers of the Saṅkīrtana movement, Their eyes are broad like lotuses. They are the sustainers of the universe and the best of the brāhmaṇas. I offer obeisances to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya and Śrī Nityānanda, who have risen together on the horizon of Gauḍa like the sun and the moon. They are wonderful, bestowers of all auspiciousness, and dispellers of the darkness of ignorance. I worship the two brothers, Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya and Śrī Nityānanda, who have descended to this world. They are the embodiments of compassion, accompanied by Their associates, and are the Masters of the saintly. śrī-navadvīpa-dhāma-vandanā (Obeisance to Śrī Navadvīpa Dhāma) I offer obeisances to that Navadvīpa, which gives supreme happiness. It is the spiritually risen forest of Vraja. The Chāndogya Upaniṣad calls it the city of the Supreme Brahman, the Smṛti scriptures call it the abode of Viṣṇu named Vaikuṇṭha, others call it Śvetadvīpa, and a rare Rasika calls it the forest of Vraja. I offer obeisances to Śrī Navadvīpa, which maddens everyone with new mercy and possesses a new taste. It is the abode of the Master of the new golden form, Lord Gaura, and the new devotion. It is surrounded by rows of new forests and refreshed by breezes from the new celestial Gaṅgā. It is the place for the performance of the new loud chanting, full of the nectar of Śrī Śrī Rādhā and Hari.

IDX.translation_intro: Gopīnātha song 1
IDX.en_translation:
Gopīnātha, please hear my appeal. I am a worldly, wicked person, always engrossed in material desires. I have no good qualities. 

Gopīnātha, You are my only hope. I take refuge at Your feet; I am Your servant. 

Gopīnātha, how will You purify me? I know no devotion, my mind is dull in action, and I have fallen into the whirlpool of material existence. 

Gopīnātha, everything is Your illusion. I have no strength, nor pure knowledge; this body is not independent. 

Gopīnātha, this fallen one constantly begs for a place at Your feet; weeping, I ask You to please bestow Your mercy. 

Gopīnātha, You can do everything. It is Your power to deliver the wicked; who else is there for a sinner like me? 

Gopīnātha, You are an ocean of mercy. For the sake of all souls, You came into this material world and extensively performed Your divine pastimes. 

Gopīnātha, what fault have I committed? All the demons received the shelter of Your feet, yet Bhaktivinoda remains left behind.
IDX.es_translation:
¡Oh, Gopīnātha!, escucha por favor mi súplica. Soy un vil materialista adicto a satisfacer los deseos mundanos y no poseo ninguna cualidad. 

¡Oh, Gopīnātha! Tú eres mi única esperanza, y por eso me he refugiado en Tus pies de loto. Soy Tu sirviente. 

¡Oh, Gopīnātha! ¿Cómo me purificarás? No sé lo que es la devoción y mi mente materialista está absorta en las actividades mundanas. He caído en esta oscura y peligrosa existencia material. 

¡Oh, Gopīnātha!, todo lo que me rodea es Tu māyā. Yo no tengo fuerzas ni conocimiento espiritual, y este cuerpo mío no está libre del control de la naturaleza material. 

¡Oh, Gopīnātha!, este pecador solloza implorando un lugar eterno a Tus pies de loto. Concédeme Tu misericordia. 

¡Oh, Gopīnātha!, Tú lo puedes todo. Tienes el poder de liberar a los pecadores. ¿Quién más podría liberar a este pecador? 

¡Oh, Gopīnātha! Tú eres un océano de misericordia. Por el bien de las entidades vivientes, vienes a este mundo material de cinco elementos y exhibes Tus divinos pasatiempos. 

¡Oh, Gopīnātha! Soy sumamente pecador. Todos los demonios alcanzaron Tus pies de loto, pero este Bhaktivinoda simplemente espera.

IDX.translation_intro: Gopīnātha song 2
IDX.en_translation:
Gopīnātha, dispel the pains of material existence. I can no longer tolerate the agony of ignorance and the cycle of birth and death. 

Gopīnātha, I am truly a servant of lust. Material desires awaken in my heart, setting the trap of actions and reactions. 

Gopīnātha, when will I awaken? I will cast away the enemy of lust, and You will manifest in my heart. 

Gopīnātha, I am indeed Your person. Leaving You, I worshipped the material world, forgetting my own true treasure You. 

Gopīnātha, You know everything. Punishing Your own person now, please grant me a place at Your lotus feet. 

Gopīnātha, is this Your judgment? Seeing my aversion, You abandon Your own person, showing no drop of mercy. 

Gopīnātha, I am indeed very foolish. I never understood what is good for me, therefore such is my condition. 

Gopīnātha, You are indeed the wisest. You will seek the welfare of this fool; do not consider this servant a stranger.
IDX.es_translation:
¡Oh, Gopīnātha! Elimina por favor el tormento que sufro debido a esta existencia mundana. Soy incapaz de tolerar por más tiempo el dolor de la ignorancia y el ciclo del nacimiento y la muerte reiterados. 

¡Oh, Gopīnātha! Soy el sirviente de la lujuria. El deseo de disfrute sensual se ha despertado en mi corazón y me ha atrapado con la soga de las acciones fruitivas. 

¡Oh, Gopīnātha!, ¿cúando despertaré y lanzaré bien lejos al enemigo del deseo de gratificación sensual? Cuando eso ocurra, Tú Te manifestarás en mi corazón. 

¡Oh, Gopīnātha! Soy Tuyo, pero por querer disfrutar del mundo material Te abandoné y olvidé mi verdadera riqueza. 

¡Oh, Gopīnātha!, Tú lo sabes todo. Ahora puedes castigar a Tu sirviente. Muestra Tu bondad y concédeme un lugar a Tus divinos pies de loto. 

¡Oh, Gopīnātha! ¿Es así como piensas? ¿Viendo que soy adverso a Ti abandonas a Tu sirviente sin darle siquiera una gota de misericordia? 

¡Oh, Gopīnātha! Soy un completo necio y nunca he sabido qué es lo que me conviene. Por eso me encuentro en esta condición. 

¡Oh, Gopīnātha!, Tú eres la persona más sabia y buscarás la manera de favorecer a todos los necios de este mundo. Por favor, no consideres a este sirviente Tuyo como un extraño.

IDX.translation_intro: Gopīnātha song 3
IDX.en_translation:
Gopīnātha, I have no other recourse. If You mercifully accept me, I will find deliverance from material existence. 

Gopīnātha, I have fallen into the trap of illusion. Wealth, wife, and children have surrounded me, and desire has kept me entangled. 

Gopīnātha, my mind is truly mad. It does not obey any discipline, is always bewildered, and remains deeply absorbed in worldly affairs. 

Gopīnātha, I have accepted defeat. Many efforts have been in vain. Now You are my only hope. 

Gopīnātha, how will I make any spiritual progress? The powerful senses and my subjugated mind do not give up their attachment to sense objects. 

Gopīnātha, sitting in my heart and pacifying my mind, please draw me toward Yourself. Then this terrible danger will cease. 

Gopīnātha, seeing me as helpless, You—the Lord of the senses—please control my senses and deliver me from the dreadful cycle of material existence. 

Gopīnātha, a noose has been tied around my neck. Taking the sword of Your mercy and cutting this bondage, please make Bhaktivinoda Your servant.
IDX.es_translation:
¡Oh, Gopīnātha!, soy incapaz de ver el modo de liberarme. Solo si me concedes Tu misericordia inmotivada y me llevas contigo a Tu reino, podré liberarme de esta existencia material. 

¡Oh, Gopīnātha!, he caído presa de los peligros de la ilusión material. Riquezas, esposa e hijos me han cercado por completo y me tienen bajo el control del ansia de dar placer a los sentidos. 

¡Oh, Gopīnātha!, mi mente ha enloquecido por completo. En su ignorancia, ella no acepta ninguna disciplina y permanece siempre en el terrorífico pozo del disfrute sensual. 

¡Oh, Gopīnātha!, he aceptado mi derrota. Todos mis esfuerzos han sido en vano. Ahora Tú eres mi única esperanza. 

¡Oh, Gopīnātha!, ¿cómo podré salvarme? Mis poderosos sentidos han controlado a mi mente y no renuncian a su adicción por el disfrute mundano. 

¡Oh, Gopīnātha!, reside por favor en mi corazón y controla mi mente llevándola hacia Ti. De ese modo pondrás fin a este terrible peligro. 

¡Oh, Gopīnātha!, ya ves que no tengo un amo. Tú eres el amo de los sentidos, de modo que contrólalos y libérame de esta oscura y peligrosa existencia mundana. 

¡Oh, Gopīnātha!, una soga aprieta fuertemente mi cuello. Corta esa atadura con la espada de Tu misericordia y haz que este Bhaktivinoda sea Tu sirviente.

gopya ūchuḥ: 
jayati te‛dhikaṁ janmanā vrajaḥ 
śhrayate indirā śhaśhvad atra hi 
dayita dṛśhyatāṁ dikṣu tāvakās 
tvayi dhṛtāsavas tvāṁ vichinvate 

śharad-udāśhaye sādhu-jāta-sat- 
sarasi jodara śhrī-muṣā dṛśhā 
surata-nātha te‛śhulka-dāsikā 
vara-da nighnato neha kiṁ vadhaḥ 

viṣa-jalāpyayād vyāla-rākṣasād 
varṣa-mārutād vaidyutānalāt 
vṛṣa-mayātmajād viśhvato bhayād 
ṛṣabha te vayaṁ rakṣitā muhuḥ 

na khalu gopīkā-nandano bhavān 
akhila-dehinām antarātma-dṛk 
vikhanasārthito viśhva-guptaye 
sakha udeyivān sātvatāṁ kule 

virachitābhayaṁ vṛṣṇi-dhūrya te 
charaṇam īyuṣāṁ saṁsṛter bhayāt 
kara-saroruhaṁ kānta kāma-daṁ 
śhirasi dhehi naḥ śhrī-kara-graham 

vraja-janārti-han vīra yoṣitāṁ 
nija-jana-smaya-dhvaṁsana-smita 
bhaja sakhe bhavat-kiṅkarīḥ sma no 
jala-ruhānanaṁ chāru darśhaya 

praṇata-dehināṁ pāpa-karṣaṇaṁ 
tṛṇa-charānugaṁ śhrī-niketanam 
faṇi-faṇārpitaṁ te padāmvujaṁ 
kṛṇu kucheṣu naḥ kṛndhi hṛch-cḣayam 

madhurayā girā valgu-vākyayā 
budha-manojñayā puṣkarekṣaṇa 
vidhi-karīr imā vīra muhyatīr 
adhara-sīdhunāpyāyayasva naḥ 

tava kathāmṛtaṁ tapta-jīvanaṁ 
kavibhir īḍitaṁ kalmaṣāpaham 
śhravaṇa-maṅgalaṁ śhrīmad ātataṁ 
bhuvi gṛṇanti ye bhūri-dā janāḥ 

prahasitaṁ priya prema-vīkṣaṇaṁ 
viharaṇañ cha te dhyāna-maṅgalam 
rahasi saṁvido yā hṛdi spṛśhaḥ 
kuhaka no manaḥ kṣobhayanti hi 

chalasi yad vrajāch-chārayan paśhūn 
nalina-sundaraṁ nātha te padam 
śhila-tṛṇāṅkuraiḥ sīdatīti naḥ 
kalilatāṁ manaḥ kānta gaccḣati 

dina-parikṣaye nīla-kuntalair 
vana-ruhānanaṁ bibhrad āvṛtam 
dhana-rajasvalaṁ darśhayan muhur 
manasi naḥ smaraṁ vīra yaccḣasi 

praṇata-kāma-daṁ padma-jārchitaṁ 
dharaṇī-maṇḍanaṁ dhyeyam āpadi 
charaṇa-paṅka-jaṁ śhantamañ cha te 
ramaṇa naḥ staneṣv arpayādhi-han 

surata-vardhanaṁ śhoka-nāśhanaṁ 
svarita-veṇunā suṣṭhu chumbitam 
itara-rāga-vismāraṇaṁ nṛṇāṁ 
vitara vīra nas te‛dharāmṛtam 

aṭati yad bhavān ahni kānanaṁ 
truṭir yugāyate tvām apaśhyatām 
kuṭila-kuntalaṁ śhrī-mukhañ cha te 
jaḍa udīkṣatāṁ pakṣma-kṛd dṛśhām 

pati-sutānvaya-bhrātṛ-bāndhavān 
ativilaṅghya te‛nty achyutāgatāḥ

kūrpādibhir bhramati dhīr bhavad-āyuṣāṁ naḥ 

śhrī-śhuka uvācha: 
iti gopyaḥ pragāyantyaḥ 
pralapantyaśh cha chitradhā 
ruruduḥ su-svaraṁ rājan 
kṛṣṇa-darśhana-lālasāḥ 

tāsām āvirabhūch cḣauriḥ 
smayamāna-mukhāmbujaḥ 
pītāmbara-dharaḥ sragvī 
sākṣān manmatha-manmathaḥ
IDX.translation_intro: Translation from Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Swami’s Śrīmad Bhāgavatam (10.31.1-19, 10.32.1-2)
IDX.en_translation:
The gopīs said: O beloved, Your birth in the land of Vraja has made it exceedingly glorious, and thus Indirā, the goddess of fortune, always resides here. It is only for Your sake that we, Your devoted servants, maintain our lives. We have been searching everywhere for You, so please show Yourself to us. 

O Lord of love, in beauty Your glance excels the whorl of the finest, most perfectly formed lotus within the autumn pond. O bestower of benedictions, You are killing the maidservants who have given themselves to You freely, without any price. Isn’t this murder? 

O greatest of personalities, You have repeatedly saved us from all kinds of danger - from poisoned water, from the terrible man-eater Agha, from the great rains, from the wind demon, from the fiery thunderbolt of Indra, from the bull demon and from the son of Maya Dānava. 

You are not actually the son of the gopī Yaśodā, O friend, but rather the indwelling witness in the hearts of all embodied souls. Because Lord Brahmā prayed for You to come and protect the universe, You have now appeared in the Sātvata dynasty. 

O best of the Vṛṣṇis, Your lotuslike hand, which holds the hand of the goddess of fortune, grants fearlessness to those who approach Your feet out of fear of material existence. O lover, please place that wish-fulfilling lotus hand on our heads. 

O You who destroy the suffering of Vraja’s people, O hero of all women, Your smile shatters the false pride of Your devotees. Please, dear friend, accept us as Your maidservants and show us Your beautiful lotus face. 

Your lotus feet destroy the past sins of all embodied souls who surrender to them. Those feet follow after the cows in the pastures and are the eternal abode of the goddess of fortune. Since You once put those feet on the hoods of the great serpent Kāliya, please place them upon our breasts and tear away the lust in our hearts. 

O lotus-eyed one, Your sweet voice and charming words, which attract the minds of the intelligent, are bewildering us more and more. Our dear hero, please revive Your maidservants with the nectar of Your lips. 

The nectar of Your words and the descriptions of Your activities are the life and soul of those suffering in this material world. These narrations, transmitted by learned sages, eradicate one’s sinful reactions and bestow good fortune upon whoever hears them. These narrations are broadcast all over the world and are filled with spiritual power. Certainly those who spread the message of Godhead are most munificent. 

Your smiles, Your sweet, loving glances, the intimate pastimes and confidential talks we enjoyed with You - all these are auspicious to meditate upon, and they touch our hearts. But at the same time, O deceiver, they very much agitate our minds. 

Dear master, dear lover, when You leave the cowherd village to herd the cows, our minds are disturbed with the thought that Your feet, more beautiful than a lotus, will be pricked by the spiked husks of grain and the rough grass and plants. 

At the end of the day You repeatedly show us Your lotus face, covered with dark blue locks of hair and thickly powdered with dust. Thus, O hero, You arouse lusty desires in our minds. 

Your lotus feet, which are worshiped by Lord Brahmā, fulfill the desires of all who bow down to them. They are the ornament of the earth, they give the highest satisfaction, and in times of danger they are the appropriate object of meditation. O lover, O destroyer of anxiety, please put those lotus feet upon our breasts. 

O hero, kindly distribute to us the nectar of Your lips, which enhances conjugal pleasure and vanquishes grief. That nectar is thoroughly relished by Your vibrating flute and makes people forget any other attachment. 

When You go off to the forest during the day, a tiny fraction of a second becomes like a millennium for us because we cannot see You. And even when we can eagerly look upon Your beautiful face, so lovely with its adornment of curly locks, our pleasure is hindered by our eyelids, which were fashioned by the foolish creator. 

Dear Acyuta, You know very well why we have come here. Who but a cheater like You would abandon young women who come to see Him in the middle of the night, enchanted by the loud song of His flute? Just to see You, we have completely rejected our husbands, children, ancestors, brothers and other relatives. 

Our minds are repeatedly bewildered as we think of the intimate conversations we had with You in secret, feel the rise of lust in our hearts and remember Your smiling face, Your loving glances and Your broad chest, the resting place of the goddess of fortune. Thus we experience the most severe hankering for You. 

O beloved, Your all-auspicious appearance vanquishes the distress of those living in Vraja’s forests. Our minds long for Your association. Please give to us just a bit of that medicine, which counteracts the disease in Your devotees’ hearts. 

O dearly beloved! Your lotus feet are so soft that we place them gently on our breasts, fearing that Your feet will be hurt. Our life rests only in You. Our minds, therefore, are filled with anxiety that Your tender feet might be wounded by pebbles as You roam about on the forest path. 

Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: O King, having thus sung and spoken their hearts out in various charming ways, the gopīs began to weep loudly. They were very eager to see Lord Kṛṣṇa. 

Then Lord Kṛṣṇa, a smile on His lotus face, appeared before the gopīs. Wearing a garland and a yellow garment, He directly appeared as one who can bewilder the mind of Cupid, who himself bewilders the minds of ordinary people.
IDX.es_translation:
[Las gopīs dijeron:] Tu nacimiento en Vraja ha vuelto a esta tierra aún más gloriosa que Vaikuṇṭha y otros planetas. Por eso Lakṣmī, la diosa de la belleza y la fortuna, la decora siempre con su presencia. ¡Oh, amado! En esta dichosa tierra de Vraja solo nosotras, las gopīs, no somos felices. Mantenemos nuestras vidas únicamente por Ti y, angustiadas por la separación, Te buscamos de bosque en bosque. Muéstrate por favor ante nosotras. 

¡Oh señor del placer amoroso! ¡Oh Tú que otorgas bendiciones! Somos Tus sirvientas no remuneradas. Nos estás matando con esa mirada de Tus ojos que roba hasta la orgullosa belleza del verticilo de los encantadores lotos otoñales que florecen exquisitamente en los estanques. ¿Acaso matar con la mirada no es considerado un delito en este mundo? 

¡Oh, joya entre los hombres! Tú nos salvaste una y otra vez de las garras de la muerte —de las venenosas aguas de Kāliya-hṛada en el Yamunā donde residía la serpiente Kāliya, de la pitón Aghāsura, y de la torrencial tormenta de lluvia de Indra. Nos salvaste del demonio tornado Tṛṇāvarta, de lo rayos de Indra, del terrible fuego forestal, del demonio con forma de toro Ariṣṭāsura, del hijo de māyā llamado Vyomāsura, y de un sinfín de amenazas más. 

¡Oh, amigo! Tú no eres únicamente el hijo de Yaśhodā, sino también el Alma Suprema que mora en el corazón de todos los seres. Tú apareciste en la dinastía de devotos en respuesta a la oración del Señor Brahmā para proteger al universo. 

¡Oh Tú, el mejor de la dinastía Yadu! ¡Oh, amado! Tu mano de loto vuelve audaces a las almas que se rinden a Tus pies de loto por temor al ciclo de nacimiento y muerte. ¡Oh Tú, que satisfaces nuestros deseos! Coloca por favor sobre nuestras cabezas esa misma mano de loto que otorga valor y que aceptó las dos manos de Lakṣmī. 

¡Oh Tú, que acabas con el sufrimiento de los habitantes de Vraja! ¡Oh Tú, el mejor entre los héroes! Tu sonrisa abate el orgullo de los seres queridos por Ti que surge de su buena fortuna y del enfado (māna) que resulta de dicho orgullo. ¡Oh, querido amigo! Colma los deseos de Tus desvalidas sirvientas. Haznos felices, al menos esta vez, mostrándonos Tu hermoso rostro de loto. 

Tus pies de loto destruyen todos los pecados de los seres encarnados que se refugian en ellos, y van detrás de las vacas y los terneros que pastan en los prados. Esos pies de loto son la morada de Lakṣmī-devī, la diosa de la fortuna y la belleza, y Tú los colocaste en las cabezas de una serpiente (Kāliya). Coloca ahora por favor esos pies en nuestros pechos y pon así fin a la lujuria que se ha despertado en nuestros corazones. 

¡Oh, héroe de ojos de loto! Estas obedientes sirvientas han quedado confundidas y exánimes al escuchar Tu dulce voz y esas encantadoras palabras Tuyas que cautivan incluso las mentes de eruditos inteligentes y expertos en el rasa. ¡Oh, héroe! Nosotras gopīs somos Tus sirvientas y cumplimos con cada orden Tuya. Devuélvenos la vida con el divino néctar de Tus labios. 

Las nectáreas narraciones acerca de Ti son la vida misma de los que sufren por la separación de Ti. Dichas narraciones son transmitidas por personalidades muy sabias como Brahmā, Śhiva y los cuatro Kumāras, y aniquilan el sufrimiento que ocasionan los pecados. Quien las escucha alcanza toda buena fortuna y, sobre todo, el tesoro del prema. El néctar de esas narraciones es difundido por quienes glorifican Tus pasatiempos y, por lo tanto, esos narradores son los mayores benefactores del mundo. 

¡Oh, amado! Meditar en Tu sonrisa, Tus dulces y amorosas miradas, los pasatiempos íntimos y las conversaciones confidenciales que disfrutábamos contigo en lugares solitarios es sumamente auspicioso, pues nos conmueve profundamente. Pero por otro lado,¡oh engañador!, esos pensamientos agitan sobremanera nuestras mentes. 

¡Oh, amado! Cuando sales de Vraja para pastorear las vacas y otros animales, las plantas de Tus pies, que son más suaves que los lotos, deben sufrir terriblemente a causa de las afiladas piedras, hierba y granos secos. Cuando nos surgen estos pensamientos, nuestras mentes experimentan un gran desasosiego. 

¡Oh, amado héroe! Cuando regresas del bosque al final del día, Tu rostro de loto está parcialmente cubierto por rizos de Tu cabello negro azulado y una ligera capa de polvo que han levantado las pezuñas de las vacas. En esos momentos, cuando nos muestras Tu hermoso rostro de loto tan exquisitamente ornamentado, haces que surjan deseos amorosos en nuestras mentes. 

¡Oh, amadísimo que destruyes todo el sufrimiento! Tus pies de loto, que satisfacen los deseos de Tus devotos rendidos a Ti y que son adorados por Brahmā, el que nació de un loto, son el ornamento que embellece la tierra. Por meditar en ellos desaparecen todas las calamidades, y cuando aceptan servicio otorgan la dicha suprema. Ten la bondad de colocar esos pies de loto en nuestros pechos. 

¡Oh, héroe! El néctar de Tus labios incrementa el placer del encuentro amoroso y elimina el dolor de la separación de Ti. Tus nectáreos labios son besados apasionadamente por Tu cantarina flauta y hacen que quien lo saborea una vez olvide cualquier otro apego. ¡Oh, héroe! Haznos beber el néctar de Tus labios. 

Cuando vas a pasar el día en el bosque y no podemos verte, cada momento es como un milenio para nosotras. Y cuando regresas del bosque al caer la tarde, aunque contemplamos ávidamente Tu hermoso rostro de loto adornado con los rizos de Tu cabello, nos sentimos muy perturbadas por el ocasional parpadeo de nuestros ojos. En esos momentos pensamos que el creador de los párpados es un inepto. 

Querido Achyuta, sabes que hemos rechazado a nuestros esposos, hijos, hermanos, amigos y a toda nuestra familia debido al hechizo de Tu flauta. Desoyendo sus deseos, hemos desobedecido las órdenes de todos ellos y hemos venido a Ti. ¡Oh, engañador! ¿Quién sino Tú abandonaría a unas jóvenes como nosotras que acuden así a verlo en mitad de la noche? 

Después de verte conversando íntimamente con nosotras en lugares secretos —con Tu sonriente rostro que estimula nuestros deseos amorosos, el modo en que nos miras con amor y Tu amplio pecho que es el eterno lugar de descanso de la diosa de la fortuna—, nuestro anhelo por encontrarnos contigo ha aumentado hasta tal punto, que nuestras mentes están constantemente perturbadas. 

¡Oh, Krsna! Tu aparición destruye por completo el dolor de los residentes de Vraja y es causa de ilimitada buena fortuna para el mundo. Nuestros corazones, que solo Te desean a Ti, agonizan debido a nuestro mal de amores. Por lo tanto, abandona toda mezquindad y ten la bondad de donar un poco de esa medicina que puede curar a Tus seres queridos. 

¡Oh, amado! Temerosas de herir Tus delicados pies de loto, los colocamos cuidadosamente sobre nuestros duros pechos. Esta noche Te encaminas con esos suaves pies hacia alguna parte de este bosque apartado. ¿Acaso Tus pies de loto no sienten dolor al ser heridos por cosas afiladas como las piedras y los granos secos? ¡Oh Tú, que lo eres todo para nosotras! Nuestra inteligencia se halla ofuscada por pensamientos acerca de Ti.

IDX.verses:
gorā bhaja, gorā bhaja, gorā bhaja bhāi 
gorā vinā e jagate guru āra nāi 

jadi bhajibe gorā, sarala kara nija-mana 
kuṭināṭi cḣāḍi’ bhaja gorāra charaṇa 

manera kathā gorā jāne, fāṅki kemane dibe 
sarala ha’le gorāra śhikṣā bujhiyā laibe 

ānera mana rākhite giyā āpanāke dibe fāṅki 
manera kathā jāne gorā, kemane hṛdaya ḍhāki 

gorā bale,-āmāra mata karaha charita 
āmāra ājñā pālana kara, chāha jadi hita 

‘gorāra āmi, gorāra āmi’, mukhe balile nāhi chale 
gorāra āchāra, gorāra vichāra, laile fala fale 

loka dekhāna gorā-bhajā tilaka mātra dhari’ 
gopanete atyāchāra gorā dhare churi 

adhaḥ-patana ha’be bhāi kaile kuṭināṭi 
nāma-aparādhe tomāra bhajana ha’be māṭi 

nāma loo je kare pāpa, haya aparādha 
era mata āra kibā ācḣe bhakti-bādha? 

nāma karite kaṣṭa nāi, nāma sahaja dhana 
oṣṭha-spandana-mātre haya nāmera kīrtana 
tāhāo nā haya jadi haya nāmera smaraṇa 

tuṇḍa vandhe, chita-braṁśhe, śhravaṇa tavu haya 
sarvapāpa-kṣaye jīvera mukhya falodaya 

bahu-janma archanete ei fala dhare 
kṛṣṇa-nāma nirantara tuṇḍe nṛtya kare 

karma-jñāna-yogādira sei śhakti nahe 
vidhi-bhaṅga-doṣe fala-hīna, śhāstre kahe 

se-saba cḣāḍa bhāi, nāma kara sāra 
ati alpadine tabe jinibe saṁsāra
IDX.en_translation:
Worship Lord Gaura, worship Lord Gaura, worship Lord Gaura, O brother! Without Lord Gaura, there is no other Guru in this world. 

If you wish to worship Lord Gaura, then make your own mind simple. Abandoning all duplicity, worship the lotus feet of the Lord. 

Lord Gaura knows the thoughts of your mind—how can you deceive Him? If you become simple, you will understand the Lord’s teachings. 

Trying to please others, you only deceive yourself. Lord Gaura knows the thoughts of your mind—how can you hide your heart? 

Lord Gaura says: “Act according to My example. Obey My command, if you desire your own well-being.” 

Just saying “I belong to Lord Gaura” with your mouth does not work. Taking up His behavior and His philosophy bears true fruit. 

If you only display worship for others by wearing forehead markings while secretly committing atrocities, the Lord will catch your theft. 

You will fall down, brother, if you act with duplicity. Due to offenses against the Holy Name, your worship will be ruined. 

To chant the Name while committing sins is an offense. What greater impediment to devotion is there than this? 

There is no difficulty in chanting the Holy Name; it is an easy treasure. Just by the vibration of the lips, the chanting of the Name occurs. If even that is not possible, then simply remember the Name. 

Even if the mouth is closed and the mind is disturbed, hearing still occurs. The destruction of all sins is the primary result for the living entity. 

This fruit is achieved after many births of Deity worship. But the Name of Lord Kṛṣṇa constantly dances on the tongue. 

The processes of fruitive action, speculative knowledge, and mystic yoga do not have that power. Due to the fault of breaking regulations, they become fruitless, as the scriptures say. 

Give up all these other paths, O brother, and make the Holy Name your only essence. Then, in a very short time, you will conquer this material world.

IDX.verses: gorā pahuṅ nā bhajiyā mainu prema-ratana-dhana helāya hārāinu adhane jatana kari’ dhana teyāginu āpana karama-doṣe āpani ḍubinu satsaṅga cḣāḍi’ kainu asate vilāsa te-kāraṇe lāgila je karmabandha-fāṅsa viṣaya viṣama viṣa satata khāinu gaurakīrtana-rase magana nā hainu kena vā ācḣaye prāṇa ki sukha pāiyā narottama-dāsa kena nā gela mariyā
IDX.en_translation:
I died without worshiping Gaurāṅga Prabhu. I carelessly lost the treasure of the jewel of divine love. 

Caring for what is worthless, I gave up true wealth. By my own faults, I have drowned myself. 

Giving up the association of devotees, I indulged in bad company. For that reason, the noose of karmic bondage has caught me. 

I constantly consumed the deadly poison of material enjoyment. I did not immerse myself in the nectar of chanting the glories of Gaura. 

Why do I still have life? What happiness have I gained? Why did Narottama dāsa not simply die?
IDX.es_translation:
Por no adorar a mi Señor Gaurasundara, he invitado a la muerte; y por menospreciar la inestimable joya del prema, la he perdido. 

Por dedicarme a nimiedades inútiles, he derrochado mi verdadera riqueza. Me he ahogado en mis propias fechorías. 

Abandoné la asociación de los devotos y en lugar de ello me enredé con no-devotos, y ahora me estoy ahogando en la trampa de mis actos. 

Bebí sin cesar el mortal veneno del disfrute sensual material, y a causa de ello no me impregné del dulce néctar del gaura-kīrtana. 

¿Para qué clase de felicidad mantengo la vida? Narottama dāsa se lamenta: “¿Por qué no muero?”

My Nitāi is overwhelmed with Gaura-prema. From His reddish eyes, a stream like the Ganges flows. 

Extensive hairs standing on end beautify His golden body. He walks swaying to and fro with the gait of the king of elephants. 

Seeing the fallen souls, He spreads His two arms; taking them in His lap, He makes them deeply call out “Hari! Hari!”. 

Who else will be such an ocean of mercy? Narahari says: He is the Avatāra to deliver the lowest.

IDX.en_translation:
Receiving Lord Caitanya’s order, the household residents immediately bring the dead son into the courtyard. 

Then Gaura-hari, the remover of the impurities of the Kali age, asks, “Child, why are you leaving the home of Śrīvāsa?” 

From the dead child’s mouth, the soul submits: “Lord, Your actions are for the education of the people. 

You are indeed the Supreme Truth, infinite and non-dual. Your supreme energy is Your non-different principle. 

That supreme energy, manifesting in three ways, performs Your pastimes according to Your will. 

In the form of internal potency, manifesting eternal pastimes, She gives You joy as the bliss-giving potency. 

Becoming the marginal potency, Your rays of consciousness manifest the living entities through their marginal nature. 

Becoming the external potency, She creates the material world and binds the averted souls within it.” 

Bhaktivinoda says: “Due to the fruit of offenses, I have become averse and am in the clutches of the material world.”

Govardhana is the best of hills, a completely solitary place; Rāi and Kānu will be lying down. Along with Lalitā and Viśākhā, I will serve joyfully at Their blissful reddish feet. 

Making a golden box, filling it with camphor and betel nuts, I will supply it to Their lotus mouths. Bringing a jeweled girdle and jeweled anklets, I will put them on Their feet. 

Filling a golden cup, making a paste of fragrant sandalwood, I will pour it on the beautiful bodies of Both. With the guru-rūpā sakhī on the left, I will fan Them with a whisk in Their three-fold bending posture. 

Seeing the lotus eyes of Both with hairs standing on end, I will touch Both of Their feet with my hands. The servant of the servant of Caitanya—this only desire in the mind always manifests in Narottama Dāsa.

IDX.translation_intro: Selected verses
IDX.en_translation:
Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Viṣṇu, enemy of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, O Supreme Lord Murāri, who is compassionate to the devotees, protect me, O Keśava, O Lord of the worlds, O Govinda, Dāmodara, Mādhava! 

O Gopāla, O holder of the flute, O ocean of beauty, O Lord of the universe, O Nārāyaṇa, O friend of the poor, always chant with a loud voice: Govinda, Dāmodara, Mādhava! 

O tongue, knower of taste, you are fond of sweetness, I tell you the supreme truth for your benefit, please chant these sweet syllables: Govinda, Dāmodara, Mādhava! 

Govinda, Govinda, Hare, Murāri! Govinda, Govinda, Mukunda, Kṛṣṇa! Govinda, Govinda, holder of the chariot wheel! Govinda, Dāmodara, Mādhava! 

Śrī Kṛṣṇa, beloved of Rādhā, Lord of Gokula, O Gopāla, O Lord of Govardhana Hill, O Viṣṇu, O tongue, drink this very nectar: Govinda, Dāmodara, Mādhava! 

O Master of the Goddess of Fortune, O Lord of the universe, O form of the universe, O Son of Devakī, O enemy of the demons, O tongue, drink this very nectar: Govinda, Dāmodara, Mādhava! 

O Lord of the gopīs, O enemy of Kaṁsa, O Mukunda, O Lord of Lakṣmī, O Keśava, O Vāsudeva, O tongue, drink this very nectar: Govinda, Dāmodara, Mādhava! 

O delighter of the gopīs, O King of Vraja, You who entered the forest to graze the cows, O tongue, drink this very nectar: Govinda, Dāmodara, Mādhava! 

O Lord of my life, O maintainer of the universe, O enemy of Kaiṭabha, O Vaikuṇṭha, O Nārāyaṇa, O holder of the discus, O tongue, drink this very nectar: Govinda, Dāmodara, Mādhava! 

Hare, Murāri, Madhusūdana, the Primeval One, Śrī Rāma, beloved of Sītā, enemy of Rāvaṇa, O tongue, drink this very nectar: Govinda, Dāmodara, Mādhava! 

O King of the Yādavas, O lifter of the hill, O lotus-eyed one, expert in giving happiness to the cows, gopas, and gopīs, O tongue, drink this very nectar: Govinda, Dāmodara, Mādhava! 

O reliever of the earth’s burden, clad in the dress of a cowherd, who performs pastimes with friends and Śeṣa, O tongue, drink this very nectar: Govinda, Dāmodara, Mādhava! 

O enemy of Pūtanā, Baka, Aghāsura, and Dhenuka, expert in destroying Keśī and Tṛṇāvarta, O tongue, drink this very nectar: Govinda, Dāmodara, Mādhava! 

O life of Jānakī, Rāmacandra, enemy of the demons, O elder brother of Bharata, O tongue, drink this very nectar: Govinda, Dāmodara, Mādhava! 

O Nārāyaṇa, O Ananta, O Hare, O Nṛsiṁha, remover of Prahlāda’s pain, O merciful one, O tongue, drink this very nectar: Govinda, Dāmodara, Mādhava! 

O Lord who accepts a human-like form for pastimes as Rāma, who made all kings Your servants by Your power, O tongue, drink this very nectar: Govinda, Dāmodara, Mādhava! 

Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Govinda, Hare, Murāri! O Master, Nārāyaṇa, Vāsudeva! O tongue, drink this very nectar: Govinda, Dāmodara, Mādhava! 

O tongue, always worship the beautiful and captivating names of Kṛṣṇa, which destroy the suffering of all devotees: Govinda, Dāmodara, Mādhava! 

I beg you alone, O tongue, please grant me this: when the God of Death arrives, this sweet name must be spoken with great devotion: Govinda, Dāmodara, Mādhava! 

At the end of happiness, this alone is the essence, at the end of sorrow, this alone is to be sung, at the end of life, this alone is to be chanted: Govinda, Dāmodara, Mādhava!

IDX.verses:
gṛhastha-vairāgī-duhe bale gorārāya 
dekha bhāi! nāma vinā jena dina nāhi jāya 

bahu aṅga-sādhane bhāi nāhi prayojana 
kṛṣṇa-nāmāśhraye śhuddha karaha jīvana 

baddha-jīve kṛpā kari’ kṛṣṇa haila ‘nāma’ 
kali-jīve dayā kari’, kṛṣṇa haila gaura-dhāma 

ekānta sarala-bhāve bhaja gaura-jana 
tabe ta’ pāibe bhāi śhrī-kṛṣṇa-charaṇa 

gaura-jana-saṅga kara ‘gaurāṅga’ baliyā 
‘hare kṛṣṇa’ nāma bala nāchiyā nāchiyā 

achire pāibe bhāi nāma-prema-dhana 
jāhā vilāite prabhura nade āgamana
IDX.en_translation:
Lord Gorārāya says to both the householder and the renunciate: “See, O brother! Let not a single day pass without the Holy Name.” 

“O brother, there is no need for many elaborate spiritual practices. Make your life pure by taking shelter of the Holy Name of Kṛṣṇa.” 

“Showing mercy to the conditioned souls, Lord Kṛṣṇa became the Holy Name. Showing compassion to the souls of Kali-yuga, Lord Kṛṣṇa became the abode of Gaura.” 

“Exclusively worship the followers of Lord Caitanya with a simple heart. Then, O brother, you will certainly attain the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.” 

“Associate with the followers of Lord Caitanya, chanting “Gaurāṅga”, and enthusiastically chant the “Hare Kṛṣṇa” name while dancing.” 

“Very soon, O brother, you will attain the treasure of love for the Holy Name, which the Lord came to Nadīyā to distribute.”

gurau goṣṭhe goṣṭhālayiṣu sujane bhūsura-gaṇe 
sva-mantre śhrī-nāmni vraja-nava-yuva-dvandva-śharaṇe 
sadā dambhaṁ hitvā kuru ratim apūrvām atitarām 
aye svāntar bhrātaśh chaṭubhir abhiyāche dhṛta-padaḥ 

na dharmaṁ nādharmaṁ śhruti-gaṇa-niruktaṁ kila kuru 
vraje rādhā-kṛṣṇa-prachura-paricharyām iha tanu 
śhachī-sūnuṁ nandīśhvara-pati-sutattve guru-varaṁ 
mukunda-preṣṭhatve smara param ajasraṁ nanu manaḥ 

yadīccḣer āvāsaṁ vraja-bhuvi sa-rāgaṁ prati-janur 
yuva-dvandvaṁ tach chet paricharitum ārād abhilaṣeḥ 
svarūpaṁ śhrī-rūpaṁ sa-gaṇam iha tasyāgrajam api 
sfuṭaṁ premṇā nityaṁ smara nama tadā tvaṁ śhṛṇu manaḥ 

asad-vārtā-veśhyā visṛja mati-sarvasva-haraṇīḥ 
kathā mukti-vyāghryā na śhṛṇu kila sarvātma-gilanīḥ 
api tyaktva lakṣmī-pati-ratim ito vyoma-nayanīṁ 
vraje rādhā-kṛṣṇau sva-rati-maṇi-dau tvaṁ bhaja manaḥ 

asach-cheṣṭā-kaṣṭa-prada-vikaṭa-pāśhālibhir iha 
prakāmaṁ kāmādi-prakaṭa-patha-pāti-vyatikaraiḥ 
gale baddhvā hanye‛ham iti bakabhid vartmapa-gaṇe 
kuru tvāṁ futkārān avati sa yathā tvāṁ mana itaḥ 

are chetaḥ prodyat-kapaṭa-kuṭi-nāṭī-bhara-khara- 
kṣaran-mūtre snātvā dahasi katham ātmānam api mām 
sadā tvaṁ gāndharvā-giridhara-pada-prema-vilasat- 
sudhāmbhodhau snātvā svam api nitarāṁ māṁ cha sukhaya 

pratiṣṭhāśhā dhṛṣṭā śhvapacha-ramaṇī me hṛdi naṭet 
kathaṁ sādhuḥ-premā spṛśhati śhuchir etan nanu manaḥ 
sadā tvaṁ sevasva prabhu-dayita-sāmantam atulaṁ 
yathā tāṁ niṣkāśhya tvaritam iha taṁ veśhayati saḥ 

yathā duṣṭatvaṁ me davayati śhaṭhasyāpi kṛpayā

śhachī-lakṣmī-satyāḥ paribhavati saubhāgya-valanaiḥ 
vaśhī-kāraiśh chandrāvalī-mukha-navīna-vraja-satīḥ

manaḥ-śhikṣa-daikādaśhaka-varam etan madhurayā
