IDX.verses:
hari he! (2) 
arthera sañchaye, viṣaya-prayāse, 
āna kathā prajalpane 
āna adhikāra, niyama-āgrahe, 
asat-saṅga-saṁghaṭane 

asthira siddhānte, rahinu majiyā, 
hari-bhakti raila dūre 
e hṛdaye mātra, parahiṁsā-mada, 
pratiṣṭhā, śhaṭhatā, sfure 

e saba āgraha, cḣāḍite nārinu, 
āpana doṣete mari’ 
janama bifala, hoila āmāra, 
ekhana ki kari’ hari 

āmi ta’ patita, patita-pāvana, 
tomāra pavitra nāma 
se-sambandha dhari’, tomāra charaṇe, 
śharaṇa loinu hāma
IDX.translation_intro: From The Harmonist, April 1929. Edited by Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī.
IDX.en_translation:
Hari! Gathering wealth, Striving after things of this world, Idle talk on topics of the hour, Misunderstanding the sphere of my duties, Adherence to the letter of the law, Contriving to mix with worldly people, 

Uncertainty of principle, - Continue to enamour me still. Devotion to Hari is afar off. This heart only breeds Malice against others, pride, Desire for fame and cunning, 

All these inclinations I could not leave. I am ruined by my own fault, This birth of mine Is rendered useless Hari! what now I am to do? 

I am fallen, indeed, Thy Holy Name Is Saviour of those gone astray. By this relationship At Thy feet I take Refuge.
IDX.es_translation:
¡Oh, Hari! Por haber acumulado excesiva riqueza y buscado el disfrute sensual, por dedicarme a mantener conversaciones frívolas y querer aceptar reglas y regulaciones inapropiadas para mi nivel, por mantener una mala asociación... 

.… y absorberme en concepciones veleidosas, la devoción por Hari se mantiene muy alejada de mí. En mi corazón no hay más que envidia, locura, arrogancia y mezquindad. 

Incapaz de dominar todas estas tendencias, me estoy muriendo a causa de mis propios vicios. Mi nacimiento ha resultado inútil. ¿Qué puedo hacer, oh Hari? 

Soy sumamente caído, pero Tu inmaculado nombre es ‘Salvador de los Caídos’ (patita-pāvana). Aferrándome a esta cualidad Tuya, yo me refugio en Tus pies de loto.

IDX.first_line: hari he! 3 bhajane utsāha bhaktite viśhvāsa
IDX.search: hari he 3 bhajane utsaha bhaktite visvasa prema labhe dhairya dhana bhakti anukula karma pravartana asat sanga visarjana bhakti sadachara ei cḣaya guna nahila amara natha kemane bhajiba tomara charana cḣadiya mayara satha garhita achare rahilama maji na karinu sadhu sanga laye sadhu vesa ane upadesi e bada mayara ranga e hena dasaya ahaituki krpa tomara paiba hari sri guru asraye dakiba tomaya kabe va minati kari
IDX.author: sacchidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
hari he! (3) 
bhajane utsāha, bhaktite viśhvāsa, 
prema-lābhe dhairya-dhana 
bhakti-anukūla, karma-pravartana, 
asat-saṅga visarjana 

bhakti-sadāchāra, ei cḣaya guṇa, 
nahila āmāra nātha! 
kemane bhajiba, tomāra charaṇa, 
cḣāḍiyā māyāra sātha 

garhita āchāre, rahilāma maji’, 
nā karinu sādhu-saṅga 
la’ye sādhu-veśha, āne upadeśhi, 
e baḍa māyāra raṅga 

e hena daśhāya, ahaitukī kṛpā, 
tomāra pāiba, hari! 
śhrī guru-āśhraye, ḍākiba tomāya, 
kabe vā minati kari’
IDX.translation_intro: From The Harmonist, April 1929. Edited by Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī.
IDX.en_translation:
Hari! Zeal in serving, Faith in devotion, The treasure of patience in attainment of love, Devising act That conduces to devotion, Abandonment of worldly association, 

Approved devotional practice, These six good qualities, Lord, have never been mine. How worship Thy feet, Giving up all affinity with Thy delusive power? 

Of improper activities I am so enamoured; Association with sadhus I have not practised. Assuming the garb of a sadhu I instruct others. This is a funny contrivance of Maya! 

In such condition I shal! receive, Hari, Thy cause-less mercy. Under the guidance of the good preceptor, O, when shall I call upon Thee With humble entreaty?
IDX.es_translation:
¡Oh, Hari! Entusiasmo por el bhajana, fe en el proceso del bhakti, la riqueza de la paciencia en el logro del objetivo del prema, realizar actos favorables al bhakti, abandonar la mala asociación… 

… y mantener un buen comportamiento favorable para el bhakti —jamás he tenido ninguna de estas seis cualidades. ¡Oh, Señor! ¿Cómo voy a servir Tus pies de loto y abandonar mi afiliación a māyā? 

Permanezco inmerso en una conducta execrable y nunca me asocio con personas santas. Y, aun así, con el atuendo de santo me dedico a instruir a otros. Así es la gran ironía de māyā. 

¡Oh, Hari! ¿Obtendré Tu misericordia sin causa en semejante condición? ¿Cuándo, tras refugiarme en śhrī guru, elevaré mis súplicas a Ti?

IDX.first_line: hari he! 4 dāna pratigraha mitho gupta kathā
IDX.search: hari he 4 dana pratigraha mitho gupta katha bhaksana bhojana dana sangera laksana ei cḣaya haya ihate bhaktira prana tattva na bujhiye jnane va ajnane asate e saba kari bhakti harainu samsari hoinu sudure rahile hari krsna bhakta jane e sanga laksane adara kariba jabe bhakti mahadevi amara hrdaya asane basibe tabe josit sangi jana krsnabhakta ara duhu sanga parihari tava bhakta jana sanga anuksana kabe va hoibe hari
IDX.author: sacchidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
hari he! (4) 
dāna-pratigraha, mitho gupta-kathā, 
bhakṣaṇa, bhojana-dāna 
saṅgera lakṣaṇa, ei cḣaya haya, 
ihāte bhaktira prāṇa 

tattva nā bujhiye, jñāne vā ajñāne, 
asate e’ saba kari’ 
bhakti hārāinu, saṁsārī hoinu, 
sudūre rahile hari 

kṛṣṇa-bhakta-jane, e saṅga-lakṣaṇe, 
ādara kariba jabe 
bhakti-mahādevī, āmāra hṛdaya-, 
āsane basibe tabe 

joṣit-saṅgī jana, kṛṣṇābhakta āra, 
dūhu-saṅga parihari’ 
tava bhakta-jana-, saṅga anukṣaṇa, 
kabe vā hoibe hari
IDX.translation_intro: From The Harmonist, August 1929. Edited by Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī.
IDX.en_translation:
Hari! Making and receiving gifts, Mutual confidential talk, Accepting and offering food, These six are indications Of intimate association; These are the life of devotion. 

Not understanding the truth,- Consciously or unconsciously, Enacting these with sinners I have missed devotion, Am become a worldling; Thou, Hari, art left afar. 

When I shall cherish those Who are devoted to Krishna By these indications of intimacy, The high goddess of devotion Will then take her seat On the throne of my heart. 

Those who are addicted to women, Those who are averse to Krishna,- Abandoning the society of both, When shall I cultivate, O Hari, Constant association with Thy devotees?
IDX.es_translation:
¡Oh, Hari! Ofrecer y recibir obsequios; compartir y comentar asuntos confidenciales; aceptar y ofrecer prasāda —estas son las seis características de la asociación [devocional] que constituyen la vida del bhakti. 

Por no haber comprendido esta verdad esencial y haber realizado consciente o inconscientemente esos intercambios con no-devotos, he perdido toda la devoción y me he convertido en un materialista. Como resultado de ello, oh Hari, Tú Te mantienes muy alejado. 

Cuando respete a los devotos de Śhrī Kṛṣṇa según estas clases de asociación, Bhakti-Mahādevī se sentará en el trono de mi corazón. 

¡Oh, Hari! ¿Cuándo, evitando la compañía de quienes están apegados a las mujeres y de los no-devotos, tendré la asociación constante de Tus devotos?

IDX.first_line: hari he! 5 saṅga doṣa śhūnya dīkṣit ādīkṣita
IDX.search: hari he 5 sanga dosa sunya diksit adiksita jadi tava nama gaya manase adara kariba tanhare jani nija jana taya diksita hoiya bhaje tuwa pada tanhare pranati kari ananya bhajane vijna jei jana tanhare seviba hari sarva bhute sama je bhaktera mati tanhara darsane mani apanake dhanya se sanga paiya charitartha hoilu jani niskapata mati vaisnavera prati ei dharma kabe paba kabe e samsara sindhu para haye tava vraja pure jaba
IDX.author: sacchidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
hari he! (5) 
saṅga-doṣa-śhūnya, dīkṣit-ādīkṣita, 
jadi tava nāma gāya 
mānase ādara, kariba tāṅhāre, 
jāni’ nija-jana tā’ya 

dīkṣita hoiyā, bhaje tuwā pada, 
tāṅhāre praṇati kari 
ananya-bhajane, vijña jei jana, 
tāṅhāre seviba, hari! 

sarva-bhūte sama, je bhaktera mati, 
tāṅhāra darśhane māni 
āpanāke dhanya, se-saṅga pāiyā, 
charitārtha hoilū jāni 

niṣkapaṭa mati, vaiṣṇavera prati, 
ei dharma kabe pā’ba 
kabe e saṁsāra-, sindhu pāra ha’ye, 
tava vraja-pure jā’ba
IDX.translation_intro: From The Harmonist, August 1929. Edited by Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī.
IDX.en_translation:
Hari- If one, initiated, or no, who is free From the offence of evil association, Sing Thy Name,- In my mind I will him esteem, Knowing him to be my kin. 

To one who serves Thy Feet Being initiated, I make my obeisance. One who is an adept In exclusive devotion to Thee, Hari, him I’ll serve. 

By the sight of the devotee Whose mind regards with equanimity All animate beings I feel myself exalted, By obtaining his society I know that my want is fulfilled. 

O, when shall I have the quality Of a guileless mind Towards the Vaishnava? O, when shall I hie To Thy abode of Braja After crossing the ocean of this world?
IDX.es_translation:
¡Oh, Hari! Si una persona que está libre de la mala asociación canta Tu nombre, la honraré mentalmente, tanto si está iniciada como si no, considerándola un alma gemela. 

A quien está iniciado y sirve Tus pies de loto, le ofreceré reverencias, y serviré al que está inmerso en el bhajana exclusivo,¡oh, Hari! 

Me considero afortunado de haber recibido el darśhana del devoto que es ecuánime con todos los seres vivos. Por haber obtenido su asociación, mi vida es un éxito. 

¿Cuándo lograré la virtud de ser sincero en mi actitud con los vaiṣṇavas? ¿Cuándo cruzaré este océano de la existencia mundana y alcanzaré Tu morada de Vraja?

IDX.first_line: hari he! 6 nīra dharma gata jāhnavī salile

IDX.verses:
hari he! (6) 
nīra-dharma-gata, jāhnavī-salile, 
paṅka-fena dṛṣṭa haya 
tathāpi kakhana, brahma-drava-dharma, 
se salila nā cḣāḍaya 

vaiṣṇava-śharīra, aprākṛta sadā, 
svabhāva-vapura dharme 
kabhu nahe jaḍa, tathāpi je ninde, 
paḍe se viṣamādharme 

sei aparādhe, yamera jātanā, 
pāya jīva avirata 
he nanda-nandana! sei aparādhe, 
jena nāhi hoi hata 

tomāra vaiṣṇava, vaibhava tomāra, 
āmāre karuna dayā 
tabe mora gati, ha’be tava prati, 
pā’ba tava pada-cḣāyā
IDX.translation_intro: From The Harmonist, November 1929. Edited by Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī.
IDX.en_translation:
Hari! In the stream of the Ganges Are found mud and froth Inherent in the nature of water. Yet that fluid Never is divested Of the quality of its Divine solvency. 

The body of the Vaishnava Is ever super sensuous By its nature. It is never a dead thing; Those who yet malign, Thereby fall into mortal sin. 

For this offence To the sufferings of death The fallen snul is for ever doomed. Darling Son of Nanda! May T not be killed By committing sueh transgression! 

The Vaishnava is Thy own, An expression of Thy Divine power. May I obtain bis mercy! Then my steps Will turn toward Thee And I shall attain the shade of Thy feet.
IDX.es_translation:
¡Oh, Hari! Puede que se observe barro y espuma en las aguas de Jāhnavī (el Ganges), que posee una naturaleza acuosa, pero la naturaleza de trascendencia líquida jamás abandona esas aguas.. 

Del mismo modo, el cuerpo del vaiṣṇava es siempre trascendental. Desde toda perspectiva, su naturaleza y su cuerpo no son nunca mundanos. Por consiguiente, quien lo critica comete una consumada herejía. 

Por esa ofensa, el alma recibe perpetuamente sufrimientos por parte de Yamarāja. ¡Oh, Nanda-nandana! Que no sea yo destruido por semejante ofensa. 

Tus vaiṣṇavas son Tu gloria. Que ellos tengan misericordia de mí. Entonces mi travesía me llevará hacia Ti y alcanzaré la sombra de Tus pies de loto.

IDX.first_line: hari he! 7 tomāre bhuliyā avidyā pīḍāya
IDX.search: hari he 7 tomare bhuliya avidya pidaya pidita rasana mora krsna nama sudha bhala nahi lage visaya sukhete bhora prati dina jadi adara kariya se nama kirtana kari sitapala jena nasi roga mula krame svadu haya hari durdaiva amara se name adara na hoila dayamaya dasa aparadha amara durdaiva kemane hoibe ksaya anudina jena tava nama gai kramete krpaya tava aparadha jabe name ruchi habe asvadiva namasava

IDX.verses:
hari he! (7) 
tomāre bhuliyā, avidyā-pīḍāya, 
pīḍita rasanā mora 
kṛṣṇa-nāma-sudhā, bhāla nāhi lāge, 
viṣaya-sukhete bhora 

prati-dina jadi, ādara kariyā, 
se-nāma kīrtana kari 
sitapala jena, nāśhi’ roga-mūla, 
krame svādu haya, hari! 

durdaiva āmāra, se nāme ādara, 
nā hoila dayāmaya! 
daśha aparādha, āmāra durdaiva, 
kemane hoibe kṣaya 

anudina jena, tava nāma gāi, 
kramete kṛpāya tava 
aparādha jā’be, nāme ruchi ha’be, 
āsvādiva nāmāsava
IDX.translation_intro: From The Harmonist, November 1929. Edited by Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī.
IDX.en_translation:
Hari! Forgetting Thee The tip of my tongue Is embittered by the distemper of un-truth; On it the nectar of the Name Krishna Does not taste sweet; I am delirious with the taste of worldly pleasures. 

If perchance daily With warm affection I sing that Name, Hari, then, like the lump of sugar, Rooting out billiousness that makes it taste bitter, It turns mellow by degrees. 

But such is my lot, Most merciful Lord! I feel no attraction for that Name. The ten offences, My calamitous fate, How are they to cease? 

May I daily without fail Sing Thy Name; Then in proper sequence, by Thy mercy, Offence will vanish, Liking for the Name appear, And T shall taste the nectarine sweetness of the Name!
IDX.es_translation:
¡Oh, Hari! Por haberte olvidado, mi lengua padece la ictericia de la ignorancia. Inmerso como me hallo en placeres mundanos, la ambrosía del santo nombre de Kṛṣṇa es desagradable para mí. 

Si canto diariamente y con mucho amor el santo nombre, que actúa como el caramelo de azúcar que erradica la ictericia, gradualmente ese nombre se volverá dulce para mí,¡oh Hari! 

Mi desgracia es no haber desarrollado una actitud amorosa hacia ese nombre. ¡Oh, Señor misericordioso! ¿Cuándo desaparecerán para siempre las diez ofensas [al santo nombre] que son la causa de mi infortunio? 

Si canto Tu santo nombre cada día, por Tu misericordia todas mis ofensas desaparecerán gradualmente, se desarrollará en mí un gusto por Tu santo nombre y saborearé el néctar de ese nombre.

IDX.first_line: hari he! 8 śhrī rūpa gosāi śhrī guru rūpete

hari he! (8) 
śhrī rūpa-gosāi, śhrī guru-rūpete, 
śhikṣā dilā mora kāṇe 
“jāna mora kathā, nāmera kāṅgāla! 
rati pā’be nāma-gāne 

“kṛṣṇa-nāma-rūpa-, guṇa-sucharita, 
parama jatane kari’ 
rasanā-mānase, karaha niyoga, 
krama-vidhi anusari’ 

“vraje kari’ vāsa, rāgānugā haiyā, 
smaraṇa, kīrtana kara 
e nikhila kāla, karaha jāpana, 
upadeśha-sāra dhara” 

hā! rūpa-gosāi, dayā kari’ kabe, 
dibe dīne vraja-vāsā 
rāgātmika tumi, tava padānuga, 
hoite dāsera āśhā
IDX.translation_intro: From The Harmonist, June 1930. Edited by Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī.
IDX.en_translation:
Hari! Sri Rupa Goswami In the form of Sree Guru Taught in my ear,- Learn the meaning of my words, You who beg for the gift of the Nameo ; You will then find attraction in chanting the Name. 

The Name, Form, Quglity, The excellent Deeds of Krishna, With the utmost care, Apply to thy tongue And mind, in order Following the Scriptural injunction. 

Dwelling in Braja, Following the spontaneous bent of love Practise chanting and recollection. In this manner employ Thy whole time, Accept this as the essence of all teaching. 

Ah! Rupa Gosain! When wilt thou, out of mercy, Grant this wretch to live in Braja! Thy soul is love; To be the follower of thy feet Is the hope of thy servant.
IDX.es_translation:
¡Oh, Hari! Srila Rūpa Gosvāmī, en forma de śhrī guru, susurró el siguiente consejo en mi oído: “Entiende mis palabras, oh mendigo del nāma, y obtendrás rati (afecto) por el canto del nombre”. 

“Dedica cuidadosamente tu lengua y tu mente al nombre, la forma, los atributos y los pasatiempos de Śhrī Kṛṣṇa según el método gradual [dado en las escrituras]”. 

“Reside en Vraja como un rāgānuga-bhakta, dedícate al smaraṇa y el kīrtana del Señor, y ocupa todo tu tiempo de este modo. Acepta esto como la esencia de todas las instrucciones.” 

¡Oh, Śhrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī! ¿Cuándo otorgarás misericordiosamente residencia en Vraja a este alma indigna y vil? Tú eres rāgātmikā 1 y el deseo de este sirviente es seguir tus pasos. 1 Residente de Vraja cuyo corazón está saturado de apego espontáneo por Kṛṣṇa. 

Las seis clases de rendición son (1) aceptar lo que es favorable para el bhakti, (2) rechazar lo que es desfavorable, (3) tener fe en la protección de Kṛṣṇa, (4) aceptar que el Señor es el único sustentador, (5) entregar sumisamente todo el ser y (6) humildad.

IDX.search: hari he dayala mora jaya radhanatha barabara ei bara laha nija satha bahu joni bhrami natha loinu sarana nija gune krpa kara adhamatarana jagata karana tumi jagata jivana toma cḣada kara nahi he radha ramana bhuvanamangala tumi bhuvanera pati tumi upeksile natha ki hoibe gati bhaviya dekhinu ei jagata majhare toma vina keha nahi e dase uddhare

IDX.verses:
hari he dayāla mora jaya rādhānātha 
bārabāra ei bāra laha nija sātha 

bahu joni bhrami’ nātha, loinu śharaṇa 
nija-guṇe kṛpā kara adhamatāraṇa 

jagata-kāraṇa tumi jagata-jīvana 
tomā cḣāḍā kā’ra nahi, he rādhā-ramaṇa 

bhuvanamaṅgala tumi bhuvanera pati 
tumi upekṣile nātha ki hoibe gati 

bhāviyā dekhinu ei jagata-mājhāre 
tomā vinā keha nāhi e dāse uddhāre
IDX.en_translation:
O Lord Hari, my merciful one! All glories to the Lord of Rādhā! This time, please take me as Your own companion. 

Having wandered through many species, O Lord, I have finally taken Your shelter. By Your own mercy, please be kind, O deliverer of the fallen. 

You are the cause of the universe, and You are the life of the universe. Without You, I belong to no one, O enjoyer of Rādhā. 

You are the welfare of all worlds, and You are their Lord. If You neglect me, O Lord, what will be my fate? 

Having thought it over, I have realized that in this world, no one can deliver this servant but You.
IDX.es_translation:
¡Oh, Hari! ¡Oh, misericordioso Rādhānātha! ¡Toda gloria a Ti! Te lo he pedido una y otra vez, y ahora Te suplico que me concedas Tu compañía íntima. 

¡Oh Señor! Tras deambular por multitud de especies de vida, me he refugiado en Ti. En Tu grandeza, ten compasión y libera a este miserable. 

Eres la causa de la creación y su vida misma. Te pertenezco solo a Ti,¡oh Rādhā-Ramaṇa! 

Eres el manantial de todo lo auspicioso y el benéfico amo del mundo. Si me abandonas, oh Señor, ¿cuál será mi final? 

He llegado a la conclusión de que en este mundo material nadie excepto Tú puede liberar a este sirviente.

IDX.en_translation:
O Hari! O merciful Lord, Your two lotus feet adorn the crown of the Vedas. And upon the heads of the spiritual masters, they are a hundred times more glorious; seeing this, my heart is soothed. 

They are the goal of every soul’s desires, just like a wish-fulfilling tree. They are the ancestral wealth of the soul, eternally worshipable, and the ultimate destination. 

The two feet of the lotus-eyed Lord are supremely blissful. By serving them sincerely and constantly, Bhaktivinoda desires to always satisfy them by following in the footsteps of the devotees.

Lord Hari is great, but His Name is greater. The Lord is great, but the Lord’s Name is greater. In the end, this is the ultimate conclusion. 

Remember the Name without seeing the Form. It costs not a single penny. Bound by the Name, He will be drawn to you. In the end, one day Lord Śyāma will come. 

When Draupadī called out the Name, Lord Ghanaśyāma immediately came. Duḥśāsana was defeated while pulling her sari; Lord Śyāma extended the sari endlessly. 

The elephant king Gajendra called out while drowning in the water. The Lord came even before half the Name was uttered. The one who bears the Name is worried that His Name should not be dishonored. 

The ocean which Lord Rāma could not cross without a bridge—Hanumān leaped across that very same ocean by taking the Name of Lord Hari. 

Those who have hearts but no Name of God within them will drown. But even stones will float if the Name of Lord Rāma is written upon them.

IDX.en_translation:
Your Holy Name has many manifestations: the son of Yaśodā, the bestower of joy, the son of Nanda, and a wellspring of divine mellows. 

He is the killer of Pūtanā, the killer of Tṛṇāvarta, the breaker of the cart demon, and the protector of the cows. With His flute at His lips, He is the subduer of Agha and Baka and the cowherd boy who lifted Govardhana Hill. 

He is the subduer of Keśī, the bewilderer of Brahmā, and the destroyer of Indra’s pride. He is the killer of Ariṣṭa, the enchanter of the gopīs, and the enjoyer of pastimes on the banks of the Yamunā. 

He is the delighter of Rādhā, the elixir of the rāsa dance, and the enjoyer of pastimes in the groves of Rādhā-kuṇḍa. He is Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, and Hari; He is Mādhava and Lord Narasiṁha, incarnating in forms like the fish and others. 

He is Govinda, Vāmana, and the slayer of Madhu; He is the moon of the Yadu dynasty and the wearer of a forest garland. He is the subduer of Kāliya and the delighter of Gokula, and He finds happiness in the worship of Rādhā. 

May my deep affection and attachment increase for all these Names, which are fully manifested in Their true forms. Bhaktivinoda prays, holding the lotus feet of Rūpa Gosvāmī and Svarūpa Dāmodara as his true treasure.
IDX.es_translation:
¡Oh, Harinäma! Tú posees ilimitadas formas. Eres el amado hijo de Yaśhodā, el que incrementa la bienaventuranza de Gokula, el hijo querido de Nanda Mahārāja y el inagotable manantial de rasa. 

Tú eres el exterminador de la bruja Pūtanā y el demonio Tṛṇāvarta, el destructor del demonio Śhakaṭa [el demonio con forma de carro] y el protector de las vacas. Tú eres el que toca la flauta, el aniquilador de los demonios Aghāsura y Bakāsura, el que levantó la colina de Govardhana y un pastorcillo. 

El que derrota al demonio Keśhī, confunde al Señor Brahmā y hace trizas el orgullo del rey de los semidioses [el Señor Indra]. El destructor del demonio Ariṣṭa, el encantador de las gopīs y el que realiza lúdicos pasatiempos en las riberas del Yamunā. 

El que deleita a Śhrīmatī Rādhikā, aporta elixir de vida a la danza rāsa y disfruta de pasatiempos en los kuñjas de Rādhā-kuṇḍa. El manantial del placer, el que atrae a todos los seres, el que elimina todo lo desfavorable, el esposo de la diosa de la fortuna, la encarnación mitad hombre mitad león conocida como Nṛsiṁhadeva y la fuente de todas las demás encarnaciones comenzando con el pez Matsya. 

El que protege a las vacas, la encarnación como el brahmán enano, el destructor del demonio Madhu, la luna de la dinastía Yadu y el que lleva hermosas guirnaldas de flores silvestres. El castigador de la serpiente Kālīya, el deleite de Gokula, y el que disfruta adorando a Śhrīmatī Rādhikā y meditando en Ella. 

Bhaktivinoda se aferra a los pies de loto de Śhrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī y Śhrī Svarūpa Dāmodara comprendiendo que son su único tesoro, y suplica humildemente: “Que mi amor y mi apego por todas estas formas del santo nombre que han aparecido por su dulce voluntad se incrementen sin cesar”.

Lord Hari, seeing His own incomparable self reflected in a mirror in Vraja and desiring to taste His own sweetness completely—just as Rādhā or Her dearmost companions do—took another golden form and was born in the land of Bengal. Will the Son of Mother Śacī ever again come before my eyes? 

He is sweet like a bath in the honey of love within Advaita Āchārya’s heart. His feet are repeatedly worshipped by Govinda Dāsa’s excellent service. His face is offered ārati by Svarūpa Dāmodara’s millions of life-breaths. Will the Son of Mother Śacī ever again come before my eyes? 

Wearing a loincloth and over it an outer saffron cloth, His grand body, like a golden mountain, is completely served by its own effulgence. Joyfully and loudly singing His own sweet Holy Names, will the Son of Mother Śacī ever again come before my eyes? 

That which was unknown even to previous sages—the creeper of devotion, hidden in the Vedas and bearing the fruit of pure, brilliant ecstatic love—the merciful Lord manifested that with great mercy in Bengal. Will the Son of Mother Śacī ever again come before my eyes? 

The Lord accepted the devotees from Bengal as His own. Instructing them like a father, He said: “Chant the Names of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa according to a counting method, O devotees!” Will the Son of Mother Śacī ever again come before my eyes? 

Seeing the Lord of Purī in front of Him with great streams of love, His tall and effulgent body is bathed by the flowing tears from His eyes. He always stands at the Garuḍa pillar in the temple. Will the Son of Mother Śacī ever again come before my eyes? 

Joyfully biting His lower lip with His teeth and placing His left hand on His hip, He shines beautifully. With countless ecstatic shivers and eager to dance, He rises up in love. Will the Son of Mother Śacī ever again come before my eyes? 

Overwhelmed by separation from the Moon of Gokula on the banks of a river, He creates another river with the incessant flow of His tears. Repeatedly falling into unconsciousness, He makes the entire world appear like a corpse. Will the Son of Mother Śacī ever again come before my eyes? 

This eight-verse prayer of the Son of Mother Śacī bestows all desires. He who recites this with a very clear mind due to increasing humility—Lord Caitanya, being overwhelmed by intense mercy, will immerse him in the great ocean of love, which is famous for bestowing divine nectar.

A young woman awakens her husband: “O Lord of my life! Wake up and abandon sleep! This is the time to sing the Lord’s song: O Govinda! O Dāmodara! O Mādhava!”

IDX.verses: hede he nāgaravara, śhuna he muralīdhara, nivedana kari tuyā pāya charaṇa-nakhara-maṇi, jena chāṅdera gāṅthani, bhāla śhobhe āmāra galāya śhrīdāma-sudāma-saṅge, jakhana vane jāo raṅge, takhana āmi duyāre dāṅḍāye mane kari saṅge jāi, gurujanāra bhaya pāi, āṅkhi rahe tuyā pāne cheye chāi navīna meghapāne, tuyā bandhu paḍe mane! elāile keśha nāhi bāṅdhi randhana-śhālāte jāi, tuyā vadhu guṇa gāi, dhūyāra cḣalanā kari’ kāndi maṇi noo, māṇika noo, āṅchale bāṅdhile roo, fula noo je keśhe kari veśhe nārī nā karita vidhi, tuyā hena guṇanidhi, loiyā firitāma deśhe deśhe aguru chandana hoitāma, tuyā aṅge mākhā roitāma, ghāmiyā paḍitāma rāṅgā pāya ki mora manera sādha, vāmana haye chāṅde hāta, vidhi ki sādha pūrābe āmāya narottama-dāse kaya, śhuna ohe dayāmaya, tumi āmāya nā cḣāḍiha dayā je dina tomāra bhāve, āmāra parāṇa jābe, sei dina dio padacḣāyā
IDX.en_translation:
O best among the charming lovers! Listen, O flute-player! I offer this plea at Your feet. The jewels of Your toenails are like a string of moons; how well they would adorn my neck! 

When You go to the forest with joy in the company of Śrīdāma and Sudāma, I stand at my doorway. I think of going with You, but I fear my elders; thus my eyes remain fixed upon You. 

I look at the new clouds and remember You, my beloved! My hair has come loose, yet I do not tie it. I go to the kitchen and sing Your glories, pretending that my tears are caused by the smoke. 

You are not a jewel or a ruby that I can tie in the end of my cloth, nor are You a flower to adorn my hair. If fate had not made me a woman, I would take such a treasure of virtues as You and wander from country to country. 

I wish I were aloe wood or sandalwood paste, so I could remain smeared on Your body. Sweating, I would fall upon Your reddish feet. What a desire is in my mind—like a dwarf reaching for the moon! Will fate ever fulfill this desire for me? 

Narottama dāsa says: listen, O compassionate Lord! Please do not withdraw Your mercy from me. On the day my life departs, immersed in Your love, please grant me the shade of Your feet.

I offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Śrīla Bhakti Vilāsa Tīrtha Gosvāmī Mahārāja. His beautiful body is like molten gold, he is established in truth, and he possesses a pure character. He is full of compassion and is always joyful. 

I offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Śrīla Tīrtha Mahārāja. He is expert in destroying the miseries of material existence. His beautiful face is adorned with a gentle smile, and his charming speech is filled with the true principles of devotional service. 

I offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Śrīla Tīrtha Mahārāja. He enriched the glories of Śrīdhāma Māyāpura and was very knowledgeable in the path of Deity worship. He graced the renowned Caitanya Maṭha like a blooming lotus. 

I offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Śrīla Tīrtha Mahārāja. He established the beautiful house of Lord Caitanya’s teachings and was adorned with profound spiritual glories. 

I offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Śrīla Tīrtha Mahārāja. His peaceful mind is free from the three-fold miseries, and he shines with the marks of a great personality. He is the joy of the transcendental sannyāsī community. 

I offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Śrīla Tīrtha Mahārāja. He is the abode of ultimate welfare and follows the path of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī. He is intoxicated by drinking the nectar of Lord Gaura’s pastimes. 

I offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Śrīla Tīrtha Mahārāja. He is bathed in the most brilliant nectar of divine love and is knowledgeable in the confidential mysteries of the Vṛndāvana forest. He is enchanted by the Names of Śrīmati Rādhikā and Lord Mādhava. 

I offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Śrīla Tīrtha Mahārāja. He is supremely worthy of refuge and is exceedingly expert in the knowledge of transcendental sound. He is my very life.

IDX.en_translation:
When will that time come, when Vilāsa Mañjarī and Anaṅga Mañjarī, seeing me, will with great mercy speak these essential words: 

“Come, come, friend! We will acknowledge you today among Śrī Lalitā’s associates. Leaving aside household concerns, worship Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, abandoning worldly shame.” 

Hearing those sweet words, I will take shelter at their lotus feet, and both of them, with mercy, will take me to Lalitā’s abode. 

Beautiful Lalitā, becoming merciful, will make me her maidservant. In her own bower’s cottage, she will give me residence, knowing my desire to serve.

IDX.en_translation:
All glories to the beautiful Lord who sports in the groves! His complexion is like a sapphire, His ears are adorned with fully blossomed nīpa flowers, and He wears a garland of berries on His broad chest. 

All glories to the charming Lord who sports in the groves! He is like the chakora bird for the moon-like face of Rādhā, the thief of the steadfastness of all the cowherd girls, and skillful in His dancing. 

All glories to the Lord who sports in the groves! He is renowned for destroying the festival of Indra, thereby removing his pride, and for lifting a mountain to protect the cowherd community with His pastimes. 

All glories to the Lord who sports in the groves! With the enchanting movements of His flute, He declares the festival of Cupid. His character is praised by flocks of parrots and mynas. 

All glories to the Lord who sports in the groves! His lower garment surpasses the luster of pure gold, His topknot is adorned with peacock feathers, and He delights the young women of Vraja with His fresh youth. 

All glories to the Lord who sports in the groves! He is smeared with fragrant sandalwood paste for decoration, His waist is resplendent with a golden belt, and He is like an elephant playing with the beauty of Rādhā. 

All glories to the Lord who sports in the groves! His forehead shines brightly with sacred markings, His garland of jasmine flowers sways playfully, and He secretly meets the beautiful-browed maidens in mountain caves. 

All glories to the Lord who sports in the groves! With the dance of His restless and charming sidelong glances, He disrupts all the duties of the cowherd women, and He is the lover of the love-intoxicated daughter of Vṛṣabhānu. 

Whoever recites this charming eight-verse song about the sweet pastimes of the Lord who sports in the groves will attain great fortune and devotion to the worship of His lotus feet.
IDX.es_translation:
Su tez tiene el encantador color del zafiro. Sus orejas están adornadas con radiantes flores kadamba y Su ancho pecho está decorado con un guñjā-mālā. ¡Toda gloria al hermoso Kuñja-bihārī! 

Él es el pájaro cakora que bebe la luz de luna del rostro de Śhrī Rādhā. Él roba la compostura de las castas esposas de los gopas y danza expertamente al ritmo conocido como charcharī. ¡Toda gloria a Kuñja-bihārī! 

Él detuvo el famoso y tradicional sacrificio a Indra, aplastando así el orgullo de este, y para proteger a las gentes de Vraja levantó alegremente la colina de Govardhana. ¡Toda gloria a Kuñja-bihārī!! 

Su vaṁśhī está decorada con diferentes rāgas y rāginīs, mediante los cuales Él anuncia [a las gopīs] el festival del Cupido trascendental. [Al oír el dulce sonido de la vaṁśhī], bandadas de loros machos y hembras prendados de Él ensalzan Su carácter. ¡Toda gloria a Kuñja-bihārī! 

Su hermosa vestimenta resplandece como el oro. Su cabeza está decorada con una pluma de pavo real, y hace las delicias de las alegres y siempre lozanas doncellas de Vraja. ¡Toda gloria a Kuñja-bihārī! 

Su cuerpo está untado con fragante pasta de sándalo. Sus caderas están decoradas con un cinturón de oro. Él es el elefante atado por la cuerda de los erguidos pechos de Śhrī Rādhikā. ¡Toda gloria a Kuñja-bihārī! 

La belleza de Su frente se ve realzada por tilaka hecho con minerales dorados. Su guirnalda champaka se mece juguetonamente de un lado a otro. Él se encuentra con las hermosas gopīs en las palaciegas cuevas de la colina de Govardhana. ¡Toda gloria a Kuñja-bihārī! 

Sus inquietas y danzarinas miradas de soslayo hacen que las gopīs abandonen todos sus deberes domésticos. Él es el amante de la hija de Vṛṣabhānu, que está locamente enamorada de Él. ¡Toda gloria a Kuñja-bihārī! 

Quien lea estos ocho versos sobre los dulces y festivos pasatiempos de Kuñja-bihārī, alcanzará sin duda la mayor de las fortunas: anurāga por la adoración de los pies de loto del Señor.

IDX.en_translation:
If your heart is always intent on drinking the nectar-like taste of Hari’s lotus feet, abandoning the home full of the mood of Kali-yuga, worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

Wealth, youth, life, and the happiness of a kingdom are not eternal; they are constantly perishing. Give up all mundane talks, which are useless. Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

And O friend, the happiness of association with women, in the end, is fearful and takes away one’s human goals. Being intoxicated by the nectar-like taste of Hari-nāma, worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

The taste of mundane poetry is not true poetic taste. The taste of Gaura, who purifies Kali-yuga, is indeed the true taste. Enough of cultivating other topics. Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

Whose beautiful left side is accompanied by Vṛṣabhānu-sutā; the hero on the bank of the Yamunā, son of Nanda; engaged in the joyous sweet music of the flute- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

Situated in the midst of Hari-kīrttana with His own associates, surrounded by them, Hari with a golden luster; the sole ocean of mercy for the people of Gaura-deśa- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

Whose home is surrounded by Girirājasutā; the master of the nine continents, captivating the minds of ascetics; praised by hosts of demigods, with His beloved- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

Holding the mood of a club for the dogs of Kali; intent on giving the great medicine of Hari-nāma; embodying a beautiful form, full of compassion for the distressed fallen- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

Whose mercy makes no distinction between enemy and friend, constantly arising from His lotus-like face; that Akṛṣṇa here, the son of Vraja-rāja- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

Here, the all-pervading Lord praised in the Upaniṣads; the son of Dvijarāja, Hari with a golden luster; plays in His own abode with His friends- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

The best of all avatāras, fully complete; the Supreme Truth, full of self-manifested pastimes here; the hidden rasa of the ocean of Vraja-dhāma- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

Whose mercy is not dependent on Vedic knowledge, social status, or wealth, powerful in generating devotion without these. O friend, He is indeed the path of causeless ecstatic love- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

Even when in the grip of a crocodile, in the middle of a lake, He delivered that distressed living entity. He is unborn; whose strength is inconceivable, a desire-tree of auspiciousness- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

With a mind pleased by the penance of Surabhīndra, Hari, possessing a beautiful complexion, appeared. That eternal happiness, who steals the patience of the sages- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

All desires, and the mentality of non-difference; give up all of this, both inauspicious and auspicious. With favor and beloved service, worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

Intent on the duty of serving Hari’s servants; delighted in drinking the nectar of Hari-nāma’s rasa; endowed with humility, meekness, and compassion- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

Chant Yādava, Mādhava, Kṛṣṇa, Hare! Chant Rāma, Janārddana, Keśava, O! Always the beloved Lord of Vṛṣabhānu-sutā- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

Chant “Lord of the forest and mountains on the bank of the Yamunā!” Chant “Sound of the clusters of groves in Gokula forest!” Chant “O Gaura-Hari, the elixir of Rāsa!”- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

Go to the nine-part forest of Gaura. Read the pastimes of Gaura-Hari with joy. Roll on the bank of the Gaṅgā marked with Gaura’s footsteps- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest. 

Remember the playful arts of Gaura and Gadādhara. Become a follower of Gaura and Gadādhara. Hear the charming narrations of Gaura and Gadādhara- Worship the splendor of the groves in Godruma forest.

jamalārjuna-bhañjanam āśhrita-rañjanam ahigañjana-ghana-lāsya-bharaṁ

go-maṇḍala-rakṣiṇam anukṛta-pakṣiṇam atidakṣiṇam amitātma-sukham 
guru-gairika-maṇḍitam anunaya-paṇḍitam avakhaṇḍita-puruhūta-makhaṁ

navanīpa-karambita-vana-rolambitam avalambita-kala-kaṇṭha-kalam 
durjana-tṛṇa-pāvakam anuchara-śhāvaka-nikarāvakam aruṇoṣṭha-dalaṁ

IDX.en_translation:
Breaker of the twin Arjuna trees, You delight those who take shelter of You. Your heavy dancing shames the dark clouds. You are the best among the protectors of the cowherds; approaching the caves, You are exceedingly beautiful, with lotus-like hands. Worshiped by excellent cowherd girls and holding a new flute with abundant sweet sounds, You are an expert in amorous pastimes and possess all extraordinary bodily characteristics. 

You are a fortress for the surrendered, wearing yellow garments—a lion to Your elephant-like enemies, with a moon-like face. Protector of the cowherd community, imitating the birds, You are very benevolent and possess unlimited inner happiness. Adorned with red chalk and expert in persuasion, You thwarted Indra’s sacrifice. You illuminate the lotus of Vṛndāvana with an excellent vermilion mark and exceedingly reddish nails. 

Your moving, creeper-like eyebrows set the sharpened arrows of the god of intoxicated love in motion. Humbling the arrogant, with lotus-like eyes, You are the liberator from sins, bowed to by hosts of demigods. You possess supreme glory and a brilliant fragrance, greatly delighting in the cowherd girls. With tender sprout-like feet, Your playful gait and dark beauty are difficult to attain even by the desires of Your most beloved devotees. 

With broad shoulders and strong arms adorned with captivating bracelets, You move through the forests. Playing amidst forests intertwined with fresh kadamba flowers and surrounded by buzzing bees, Your sweet voice is echoed by the sweet-throated birds. You are a fire to the grass-like wicked and the protector of Your young followers, with reddish petal-like lips. Your arms are anointed with Your own valor, and Your strength torments the proud demons. 

Adorned with the jewels of the Vedas, Your splendor conquers the sun-god, and Your sidelong glances shame the bees. Your beloveds attain deep love through Your intoxicating words, and flowers are spread for You on the banks of the Yamunā. We worship You, who are worshiped by Nanda, whose family is glorious, and who blinded the intelligence of the wicked king Kaṁsa. O Dāmodara, brother of Balarāma, remove our fear and grant us constant devotion.

IDX.verses: janama safala tā’ra, kṛṣṇa daraśhana jā’ra, bhāgye hoiyācḣe eka-bāra vikaśhiyā hṛn-nayana, kari’ kṛṣṇa-daraśhana, cḣāḍe jīva chittera vikāra vṛndāvana-keli- chatura vanamālī tri-bhaṅga-bhaṅgima rūpa, vaṁśhī-dhārī aparūpa, rasa-maya nidhi, guṇa-śhālī varṇa nava-jaladhara, śhire śhikhi-piccḣa-vara, alakā tilaka śhobhā pāya paridhāne pītavāsa, vadane madhura hāsa, hena rūpa jagata mātāya indranīla jini’, kṛṣṇa-rūpa-khāni, heriyā kadamba-mūle mana uchāṭana, nā chale charaṇa, saṁsāra gelāma bhule (sakhi he) sudhāmaya, se rūpa-mādhurī dekhile nayana, haya achetana, jhare prema-maya vāri kibā chūḍā śhire, kibā vaṁśhī kare, kibā se tri-bhaṅga-ṭhāma charaṇa-kamale, amiyā ucḣale, tāhāte nūpura-dāma sadā āśhā kari’, bhṛṅga-rūpa dhari’, charaṇa-kamale sthāna anāyāse pāi, kṛṣṇa-guṇa gāi, āra nā bhajiba āna
IDX.en_translation:
Successful is the birth of one who has had the vision of Kṛṣṇa even once by great fortune. By opening the eyes of the heart and beholding Kṛṣṇa, the soul abandons all mental perversions. 

He is the expert lover adorned with forest flowers in His Vṛndāvana pastimes; with His unparalleled threefold-bending form and holding His flute, He is a treasure-trove of mellows endowed with all good qualities. 

His complexion is like a fresh rain cloud, and on His head is a beautiful peacock feather; curly locks and a sacred tilaka adorn Him. Dressed in yellow garments with a sweet smile on His face, such a form enchants the world. 

Surpassing the beauty of sapphire, gazing at Kṛṣṇa’s beautiful form at the base of a kadamba tree, my mind becomes agitated, my feet cannot move, and I forget the material world. 

O my friend! Nectarine and sweet is that beautiful form. Upon seeing it, the eyes become unconscious and tears of divine love flow. 

Oh, what a crown on His head! Oh, what a flute in His hand! Oh, what a charming threefold-bending posture! Nectar overflows from His lotus feet, which are adorned with anklets. 

I always hope to assume the form of a bee and easily attain a place at His lotus feet. I will sing the glories of Kṛṣṇa and serve no one else.
IDX.es_translation:
El nacimiento de quien, por una gran fortuna, ha tenido el darśhana de Kṛṣṇa aunque sea una vez es un éxito. Al ver a Kṛṣṇa con los ojos del corazón, la jīva abandona todas las perversiones de la conciencia. 

Engalanado con guirnaldas de flores silvestres, Él [Kṛṣṇa] realiza expertos pasatiempos amorosos en Vṛndāvana. Colocado en Su forma curvada en tres lugares y sosteniendo Su flauta, Él muestra Su belleza sin precedentes. Él es un océano de melosidades trascendentales y el manantial de todas las cualidades. 

Su piel tiene el color de una fresca nube de lluvia. Lleva una pluma de pavo real sobre Su cabeza y Su frente está hermosamente decorada con símbolos de pasta de sándalo. Ataviado con vestimentas doradas y sonriendo dulcemente, Él enloquece al mundo entero con Su belleza. 

Cuando contemplo esa forma de Kṛṣṇa, que es más hermoso que la negruzca joya indranīla (zafiro), de pie bajo un árbol kadamba, mi mente se trastorna, mis pies no pueden moverse y olvido el mundo material. 

¡Oh, sakhī! Su dulce forma está llena de néctar. Quien la ve pierde el conocimiento y de sus ojos brotan incesantes lágrimas de amor. 

¡Cuán maravillosa es la corona con una pluma de pavo real de Su cabeza! ¡Cuán maravillosa es la flauta de Sus manos! ¡Cuán maravillosa es Su forma curvada en tres lugares! Sus pies de loto, que están atados por campanillas tobilleras, derraman néctar. 

Deseo siempre adoptar la forma de una abeja y alcanzar el refugio de Sus pies de loto. Estoy dispuesto a cantar las glorias de Kṛṣṇa y nunca adoraré a ningún otro.

hena prabhu avatari kaliyuge nāche 

jāṅra nāma loi śhuka-nārada beḍāya 
sahasra vadana prabhu jāra guṇa gāya 

sarva-mahā-prāyaśhchitta je prabhura nāma

IDX.en_translation:
By hearing whose Name the bondage of material existence is removed—such a Lord has incarnated and dances in this Age of Kali. 

Taking whose Name, the great sages Śukadeva and Nārada wander and preach; the Lord with a thousand mouths sings whose glories. 

The Name of that Lord is the greatest atonement for all sins; that Lord now dances, and only the fortunate ones are able to see this. 

Know Them to be Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya and Lord Nityānanda. Vṛndāvana Dāsa sings at Their lotus feet.

jaśhomatī-nandana, vrajavara-nāgara, 
gokula-rañjana kāna 
gopī-parāṇadhana, madana-manohara, 
kālīya-damana-vidhāna 

amala harināma amiya-vilāsā 
vipina-purandara, navīna-nāgaravara, 
vaṁśhī-vadana, suvāsā 

vraja-jana-pālana, asurakula-nāśhana, 
nanda-godhana-rākhooyālā 
govinda, mādhava, navanīta-taskara, 
sundara nanda-gopālā 

jāmuna-taṭachara, gopī-vasanahara,

IDX.en_translation:
The son of Yaśomatī, the chief lover of Vraja, Kṛṣṇa, who delights Gokula. The wealth of the gopīs’ lives, the enchanter of Cupid, and the subduer of the serpent Kāliya. 

Pure Harināma is a nectarine pastime. He is the Lord of the forests, the ever-fresh supreme lover, the flute-player adorned with beautiful garments. 

The protector of the people of Vraja, the destroyer of the demon dynasty, and the protector of Nanda’s cows. He is Govinda, Mādhava, the butter thief, and the beautiful cowherd boy of Nanda. 

He roams on the banks of the Yamunā, stole the garments of the gopīs, and enjoys the rāsa dance, full of mercy. He is the beloved of Śrī Rādhā, the supreme dancer of Vṛndāvana, and the shelter of Bhaktivinoda.

bhajāmi rādhām aravinda-netrāṁ 
smarāmi rādhāṁ madhura-smitāsyām 
vadāmi rādhāṁ karuṇa-bharārdrāṁ 
tato mamānyāsti gatir na kāpi 

mahā-bhāva-svarūpā tvaṁ kṛṣṇa-priyā-varīyasi 
prema-bhakti-prade devi rādhike tvāṁ namāmy aham 

rādhe vṛndāvanādhīśhe karuṇāmṛta-vāhini 
kṛpayā nija-pādābja-dāsyaṁ mahyaṁ pradīyatām 

vande nanda-vraja-strīṇāṁ, pāda-reṇum abhīkṣṇaśhaḥ 
jāsāṁ hari-kathodgītaṁ, punāti bhuvana-trayam 

tavaivāsmi tavaivāsmi, na jīvāmi tvayā vinā 
iti vijñāya devi tvaṁ, naya māṁ charaṇāntikama
IDX.en_translation:
When will I be the sweeper of the courtyard of the play-grove of the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu, the ocean of rasa? The Supreme Person with a peacock-feather crown (Kṛṣṇa) always speaks many plaintive words to Her maidservants. 

I remember that dust of Rādhikā’s feet, which is the infinite power, the powder that instantly subdues that Person who is not easily perceived by Brahmā, Rudra, Śuka, Nārada, Bhīṣma, and others. 

Even Madhusūdana, whose path is difficult for the best of yogīs to attain, considers Himself successful by the most fortunate breeze arising from the playful movement of the corner of Her cloth. Obeisances to Her, and even to the direction of Vṛṣabhānu’s daughter. 

O Devi! I indeed never beg for anything else at any time except for the excellent service of Your lotus feet. Obeisances to Your friendship; obeisances always. May my taste be for Your service; may it be true. 

Alas, O Devi! Today, with a voice choked with piteous words, falling on the ground like a stick, I beg with intense distress: bestowing mercy on this ignorant person, O Gāndharvikā, please count me among Your own people. 

Without worshipping the dust of Rādhā’s lotus feet, without taking shelter of the forest of Vṛndā which bears Her footprints, without conversing with those whose hearts are deep with Her mood—how can one enter the ocean of the rasa of Śyāma? 

I worship Rādhā who has lotus eyes; I remember Rādhā who has a sweet smile on Her face; I speak of Rādhā who is melted by the burden of compassion. Therefore, I have no other goal. 

You are the form of Mahābhāva, the best of Kṛṣṇa’s beloveds. O Devi Rādhikā, bestower of loving devotion, I bow to You. 

O Rādhe! Queen of Vṛndāvana! River of the nectar of mercy! Please mercifully give me the service of Your lotus feet. 

I repeatedly offer obeisances to the dust of the feet of the women of Nanda’s Vraja, whose loud singing of the topics of Hari purifies the three worlds. 

I am Yours alone, I am Yours alone, I cannot live without You. Knowing this, O Devi, lead me to the vicinity of Your feet.

IDX.author: vidyāpati
IDX.verses:
jatane jateka dhana, pāpe vaṭāralo, 
meli meli parijana khāya 
maraṇaka beri, koi nā pucḣoi, 
karama saṅge chali jāya 

e hari vando tuyā pada-nāya 
tuyā pada parihari, pāpa-payonidhi, 
pāra haba kon upāya 

jāvata janama hāma, tuyā pada nā sevinu, 
juvatī matimaya meli 
amṛta tyaji kiye, halāhala piyanu, 
sampade vipadahi bheli 

bhaṇahū vidyāpati, leha mane gaṇi, 
kahile ki bāḍhaba kāje 
sāṅjhaka beri, seva koi māgoi, 
heroite tuyā pada lāje
IDX.en_translation:
Whatever wealth I accumulated with effort, I earned through sin, and my family consumed it. At the time of death, no one will care; only my past actions will go with me. 

O Lord Hari! I worship Your lotus feet. Having abandoned Your feet, how can I cross this ocean of sin? 

Throughout my life, I did not serve Your feet, being absorbed in the intoxication of youth and delusion. Abandoning nectar, I drank poison, and my prosperity has turned into misfortune. 

Vidyāpati says: “Consider this in your heart—what more will be gained by speaking? At the end of my life, who will ask for service? I am ashamed to even look at Your lotus feet.”

Glory to Śrī Guru and Śrī-Gaurāṅga, and victory to the expert in musical arts who lifts Govardhana Hill and plays joyful pastimes, Rādhā-Vinoda-bihārī! 

Victory to the one who has entered the eternal pastimes and resides at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, His Divine Grace Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī, King among renunciates! 

Glory to the one who has entered the eternal pastimes and resides at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, His Divine Grace Bhaktivedānta Vāmana Gosvāmī, King among renunciates! 

Victory to the one who has entered the eternal pastimes and resides at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, His most respectful Divine Grace Bhaktivedānta Svāmī, King among renunciates! 

Glory to the one who has entered the eternal pastimes and resides at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, His most respectful Divine Grace Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī, King among renunciates! 

Victory to the one who has entered the eternal pastimes and resides at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa, His most respectful Divine Grace Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Gosvāmī Prabhupāda! 

Glory to the one who has entered the eternal pastimes, the topmost supreme devotee of the Lord, His Divine Grace Gaurakiśora dāsa Bābājī, King among renunciates! 

Victory to the one who has entered the eternal pastimes, His Divine Grace Saccidānanda Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura! 

Glory to the one who has entered the eternal pastimes, the universal emperor of all Vaiṣṇavas, His Divine Grace Jagannātha dāsa Bābājī, King among renunciates! 

Victory to the illustrious Gauḍīya Vedānta teacher, His Divine Grace, Master Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa! 

Glory to Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura! 

Victory to the trio of masters, Śrīla Narottama Ṭhākura, Śrīnivāsa Āchārya, and Śyāmānanda Prabhu! 

Glory to His Grace the literary poet Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī Prabhu! 

Victory to the six Gosvāmī of Vṛndāvana: Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī, Sanātana Gosvāmī, Bhaṭṭa Raghunātha Gosvāmī, Śrī Jīva Gosvāmī, Gopāla-bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī, and Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī! 

Glory to the assembly of Śrī Gaura’s intimate associates, beginning with Śrī Svarūpa Dāmodara and Rāya Rāmānanda! 

Victory to the master of the Holy Name, Śrīla Haridāsa Ṭhākura! 

Proclaim with love: Glory to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu, Prabhu Nityānanda, Śrī Advaita Āchārya, Gadādhara Paṇḍita, Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura, and all the assembly of Gaura’s devotees! 

Glory to Śrī Navadvīpa-dhāma, the sacred abode which is comprised of the nine islands: Śrī Māyāpura at the center, surrounded by Sīmantadvīpa, Godrumadvīpa, Madhyadvīpa, Koladvīpa, Ṛtudvīpa, Jahnudvīpa, Modadrumadvīpa, and Rudradvīpa! 

Glory to Śrī Vraja-maṇḍala, which consists of twelve forests and is home to Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, the cowherd boys, the damsels, the cows, and Govardhana Hill! 

Victory to the Śrī Rādhā-kuṇḍa and Śyāma-kuṇḍa ponds, Gaṅgā and Yamunā rivers, Tulasī the Goddess of devotion! 

Glory to the forest messenger, Śrīmatī Vṛndā-devī! 

Victory to the spiritual master of the vraja-vāsīs, Śrī Paurṇamāsī Yogamāyā! 

Glory to the gatekeeper of Vṛndāvana, Śrī Gopīśvara Mahādeva! 

Victory to the respected Śrī Jagannātha, Baladeva, Subhadrā, and Sudarśana Cakra! 

Glory to Śrī Kṣetra-maṇḍala, Jagannātha Purī! 

Victory to the destroyer of all obstacles, the half-man half-lion Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva! 

Glory to the foremost among the highest of devotees, King Prahlāda! 

Victory to the four sacred abodes! <highlight>[Badarī-nārāyaṇa, Jagannātha Purī, Rāmeśvaram, and Dvārakā Purī]</highlight> 
Glory to the four authorized disciplic successions! <highlight>[Śrī Sampradāya, Brahma Sampradāya, Rudra Sampradāya, and Kumāra Sampradāya]</highlight> 
Victory to the four foundational teachers! <highlight>[Śrī Rāmānujāchārya, Śrī Madhvāchārya, Śrī Viṣṇusvāmī, and Śrī Nimbāditya]</highlight> 

Glory to the original fountainhead and supreme leader of all monasteries, Śrī Caitanya Maṭha! 

Victory to Śrī Śrī Keśavajī Gauḍīya Maṭha and the entire assembly of its branch monasteries! 

Glory to the absolute pinnacle of all sacred scriptures, Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam! 

Victory to the large-scale distribution of transcendental literature! 

Glory to the congregational chanting of the Holy Names of Śrī Hari! 

Victory to the endless millions of Vaiṣṇavas! 

Glory to the assembled devotees! 

In the divine love of Śrī Nitāi-Gaura, chant: Hari, Hari!

IDX.verses:
jaya godruma-pati gorā 

nitāi-jīvana, advaitera dhana, 
vṛndāvana-bhāva-vibhorā 

gadādhara-prāṇa, śhrīvāsa-śharaṇa, 
kṛṣṇabhakta-mānasa-chorā
IDX.en_translation:
All glories to Gaura-candra, the Lord of Godruma! 

He is the life of Nitāi and the treasure of Advaita, absorbed in the mood of Vṛndāvana. 

He is the life of Gadādhara and the shelter of Śrīvāsa—the thief of the minds of the devotees of Kṛṣṇa.
IDX.es_translation:
¡Toda gloria a Śhrī Gaurāṅga, el Señor de Godruma! 

Él es la vida de Nitāi y el tesoro de Advaita, y está absorto en el bhāva de Śhrī Vṛndāvana. 

Él es la vida de Gadādhara y el refugio de Śhrīvāsa, y roba los corazones de los devotos de Śhrī Kṛṣṇa.

IDX.en_translation:
All glories to Govinda, all glories to Gopāla! Keśava, Mādhava, the Friend of the distressed! Śyāmasundara, the beloved Kanhaīyālāla, the Lifter of Govardhana Hill, the beloved Son of Nanda! 

Acyuta, Keśava, Śrīdhara, Mādhava, Gopāla, Govinda, Hari! On the banks of the Yamunā, He plays the flute, appearing as the supreme dancer.

IDX.verses: jaya jaga-tāraṇa-kāraṇa dhāma ānanda-kanda nityānanda nāma ḍagamaga lochana-kamala ḍhulāyata sahaje athira gati jiti matoyāra bhāiyā abhirāma bali ghana ghana ḍāka-i gaura prema-bhare chala-i nā pāra gada gada ādhamadhura vachanāmṛta lahu lahu hāsa-vikaśhita ganta pāṣaṇḍa khaṇḍana śhrī-bhuja-maṇḍana kanaka- khachita avalamvana daṇḍa kali-yuga kālabhujaṅgama daṁśhala dagadhala sthāvara jāṅgama dekhi prema-sudhā-rasa jaga bhari barikhala govinda-dāsa ke kāṁhe upekhi
IDX.en_translation:
All glories to the abode that is the cause of the world’s deliverance, the root of all bliss, whose Name is Nityānanda. 

His lotus-like eyes sway unsteadily with ease. His wavering gait outdoes even an intoxicated person. Calling out “O brother Abhirāma!” again and again, Gaura is unable to walk, overwhelmed with divine love. 

Faltering, half-sweet, nectarous words gently flow from His mouth, His face blossoming with a soft smile. The destroyer of atheists, He holds a golden staff inlaid with gold, which adorns His beautiful arms. 

Seeing all beings, both moving and non-moving, bitten and scorched by the serpent of the Age of Kali, He showered the entire world with the nectarean essence of divine love. Why then does He neglect Govinda Dāsa?

IDX.author: vṛndāvana-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: jaya jaya adbhuta, so pahū advaita, suradhunī sannidhāne āṅkhi mudi’ rahe, prema-nadī vahe, vasana titila ghāme nija pahū mane, ghana garajane, uṭhe joḍe joḍe lamfa ḍāke bāhu tuli’, kāṅde fuli’ fuli’, dehe viparīta kampa advaita-huṅkāre, suradhunī-tīre, āilā nāgara-rāja tāṅhāra pīrite, āilā tvarite, udaya nadīyā-mājha jaya sītānātha, karala vekata, nandera nandana hari kahe vṛndāvana, advaita-charaṇa, hiyāra mājhāre dhari
IDX.en_translation:
All glories, all glories to the amazing one! There, the master Advaita, near the Suradhunī, remains with closed eyes. A river of love flows, his clothes are drenched in sweat. 

In his own mind, the master, with a deep roar, leaps again and again. He calls with raised arms, he weeps profusely, his body trembles violently. 

By the roar of Advaita, on the bank of the Suradhunī, the Nāgara-rāja arrived. Out of love for him, he quickly came, appearing in Nadīyā. 

All glories to Sītānātha! He made manifest Hari, the son of Nanda. Vṛndāvana says, holding the lotus feet of Advaita within my heart.

IDX.en_translation:
Glory, glory to the merciful Advaita Āchārya! By whose roaring call the Avatāra Gaura appeared. 

The giver of love, the Lord of Sītā, the ocean of compassion. By the nectar of whose love, the Hero of Vraja came. 

To whomsoever He desires to give mercy, that person sings the qualities of Caitanya in the mellows of love. 

Whoever took shelter at His feet, that person attained the great treasure of Gaura-prema. 

Why did I not worship such a reservoir of mercy? Locana says, “I have struck a thunderbolt on my own head.”
IDX.es_translation:
Toda gloria al muy misericordioso Advaita Āchārya. Śhrī Gaura descendió gracias a su potente rugido. 

Él otorga prema, es el señor de Sīta-devī y es un océano de compasión. El héroe de Vraja descendió de nuevo debido a su nectáreo amor. 

Aquel a quien él desea otorgar misericordiosamente su gracia canta las glorias de Chaitanya Mahāprabhu inmerso en prema-rasa. 

Quien se refugia en sus pies de loto obtiene el tesoro supremo del gaura-prema. 

Lochana dāsa dice: “¿Por qué no adoré a ese manantial de misericordia? ¡En lugar de ello he golpeado mi propia cabeza con un rayo!”

IDX.en_translation:
All glories, all glories to Śrīla Gadādhara Paṇḍita Gosvāmī! By the power of his mercy, I sing the glories of Lord Caitanya. 

Such is his love for Lord Gaurāṅgacandra that he is famously known as “Gadādhara-prāṇanātha” (the Lord of Gadādhara’s life). 

His life is completely absorbed in Lord Gaura. Who can truly understand his love? For the sake of Lord Gaura, he gave up his residence in Jagannātha Purī and even his direct service to Lord Kṛṣṇa. 

Gaurāṅga belongs to Gadādhara, and Gadādhara belongs to Gaurāṅga. They are just like Śrī Rāma and Śrīmati Sītā-devī, appearing in one divine form. 

Just as Śrīmati Rādhā-rāṇī and Vṛndāvanacandra are one soul, so are Lord Gaura and Śrīla Gadādhara Paṇḍita—a vast wave of divine love. 

Śivānanda Sena says: “In whose deep affection Lord Kṛṣṇa, whose body is the color of a dark cloud, became Gaurāṅga and now begs for divine love.”
IDX.es_translation:
¡Toda gloria a Śhrī Gadādhara Paṇḍita! Por la potencia de su misericordia se pueden cantar las cualidades de Śhrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu. 

Su amor por la luna de Gaurāṅga es tal, que se conoce a Gaurāṅga como Gadādhara-prāṇanātha, el Señor de la vida de Gadādhara. 

¿Quién puede entender el prema de aquel cuyo corazón es uno con Gaurāṅga, por el cual abandonó su kṣetra-vāsa (su promesa de permanecer siempre en la sagrada ciudad de Purī) y su sevā a Śhrī Kṛṣṇa (en Ṭoṭa Gopīnātha)? 

Gaurāṅga es de Gadādhara y Gadādhara es de Gaurāṅga, al igual que Śhrī Rāma y Jānakī (Sīta-devī) son un solo cuerpo. 

Al igual que Śhrī Rādhā y Śhrī Vṛndāvana-chandra son un solo corazón, olas de prema fluyen entre Gaura Gadādhara. 

Śhivānanda dice: “Es debido a su anurāga (el profundo apego de Śhrī Rādhā) que Śhyāma-tanu (el Kṛṣṇa de tez oscura) se ha convertido ahora en Śhrī Gaurāṅga, y suplica por ese prema.”

jaya jaya gadādhara premera sāgara 
gaurāṅgera priyottama paṇḍita pravara 

“mādhava miśhrera putra-śhrī-gadādhara nāma 
śhiśhu haite saṁsāre virakta bhāgyavān 

viṣṇu-bhakti-tejomaya divya kalevara 
ākṛti, prakṛti-dui parama sundara 

āpane chaitanya baliyācḣe bāra bāra 
‘gadādhara mora vaikuṇṭhera paribāra’ 

niravadhi gadādhara thākena saṁhati 
prabhu-gadādharera viccḣeda nāhi kati 

ki bhojane, ki śhayane, paryaṭane 
gadādhara prabhure sevena anukṣaṇe 

gadādhara sammukhe paḍena bhāgavata 
śhuni prabhu hana premarase mahāmatta 

gadādhara-vākye mātra prabhu sukhī haya 
bhrame gadādhara saṅge vaiṣṇava-ālaya 

paṇḍite prabhura prasāda kahana nā jāya 
‘gadādhara-prāṇanātha’ nāma haila jāya 

gadādhara-pāda-padme mora namaskāra 
gaura-chandra-saṅge jāṅra kīrtana vihāra”
IDX.en_translation:
Glory, glory to Gadādhara, the ocean of love! The dearest of Gaurāṅga, the best of Paṇḍitas. 

The son of Mādhava Miśra, named Śrī Gadādhara. From childhood, he was detached from the world and fortunate. 

A divine body full of the brilliance of devotion to Viṣṇu. Both his form and nature were supremely beautiful. 

Caitanya Himself has said again and again: “Gadādhara is My family from Vaikuṇṭha.” 

Gadādhara remains constantly in His company. There is never any separation between the Lord and Gadādhara. 

Whether eating or sleeping or travelling, Gadādhara serves the Lord at every moment. 

Gadādhara reads the Bhāgavata in front of Him. Hearing it, the Lord becomes greatly maddened in the rasa of love. 

The Lord becomes happy only by the words of Gadādhara. He wanders to the homes of Vaiṣṇavas with Gadādhara. 

The Lord’s mercy on the Paṇḍita cannot be described. His name became “Gadādhara-Prāṇanātha” (Lord of Gadādhara’s life). 

My obeisances to the lotus feet of Gadādhara, whose kīrtana-pastime is with Gaura-candra.

IDX.translation_intro: Ārati song with traditional alaṅkāras
IDX.en_translation:
All glories, all glories to the beautiful ārati of Śrī Gaurāṅga being performed in a forest on the banks of the Jāhnavī (Gaṅgā), attracting the minds and hearts of all. 
<highlight>(Captivating the minds and hearts of all people. The beautiful ārati of Śrī Gaurāṅga captivates the minds and hearts of everyone. In the forest on the bank of the Jāhnavī, it captivates the minds and hearts of all people.)</highlight> 

On the right of Gaurāṅga is the moonlike Nityānanda Prabhu (nitāi-cānda), on the left is Gadādhara Paṇḍita, and on the sides are Advaita Prabhu and Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita, who holds the umbrella. 
<highlight>(Śrīvāsa holds the ceremonial umbrella. During Gaurāṅga’s ārati, Śrīvāsa holds the ceremonial umbrella.)</highlight> 

Śrī Gaurāṅga is seated on a jeweled throne. 
<highlight>(The jeweled throne is filled with radiant effulgence.)</highlight> 
Brahmā is performing the ārati along with other demigods. 
<highlight>(The hosts of demigods perform the ārati. During the ārati of Gaura and Nityānanda, the demigods perform the ārati. Brahmā and the other demigods perform Śrī Gaurāṅga’s ārati.)</highlight> 

Narahari Sarakāra Ṭhākura and others fan with cāmaras as many others like Saṣjaya Paṇḍita, Mukunda Daṭṭa and Vāsudeva Ghoṣa sing songs. 
<highlight>(Vāsu Ghoṣa sings devotional songs. Crying, “All glories to Nitāi! All glories to Gaura!” Vāsu Ghoṣa sings. Singing with the hope, “May I receive Gaura’s mercy,” Vāsu Ghoṣa sings. Praying, “Please bestow Your mercy upon me,” Vāsu Ghoṣa sings.)</highlight> 

The sounds of the conch, bell and karatālas mix with the sweet sound of the mṛdaṅgas, producing the most relishable ambrosia for the ears. 
<highlight>(Sweetly, imitating a sweet, honey-like sound, the instruments resound. During the ārati of Gaura and Nityānanda, the instruments resound with sweet, honey-like tones. The conch, bell, khol, and karatālas resound with sweet, honey-like melodies.)</highlight> 

Śrī Gaurāṅga’s brilliant face conquers the glow of many millions of moons, and the garland of forest flowers about His neck splendorously shines. 
<highlight>(The garland glitters and sparkles brilliantly. The garland of forest flowers around Gaura’s neck sparkles with dazzling brilliance. The garland sways by itself, even without anyone moving it. The garland woven by Gadādhara sways on its own, though no one moves it. The forest-flower garland around Gaura’s neck sways by itself, though untouched.)</highlight> 

Śiva, Śukadeva Gosvāmī and Nārada Muni’s voices have become choked up with prema. Thus, Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura is seeing the glories of Śrī Gaurāṅga. 
<highlight>(Only such a person beholds Gaurāṅga’s divine treasure glories. One who knows nothing but to call out “Gaura! Gaura!” truly beholds Gaurāṅga’s divine treasure. One who has dedicated his very life at Gaurāṅga’s lotus feet truly beholds His divine treasure. One who knows only to cry, “O Gaura!” truly beholds Gaurāṅga’s divine treasure.)</highlight>
IDX.es_translation:
Toda gloria a la hermosa ceremonia del ārati de Śhrī Gaura-chandra que se realiza en un bosque en las riberas del Jāhnavī (Gaṅgā) y que atrae las mentes de las personas del universo entero. 

A la derecha [de Gaurāṅga] está la luna de Nityānanda Prabhu, a Su izquierda está Gadādhara Paṇḍita, y cerca de ellos se encuentran Advaita Āchārya y Śhrīvāsa Paṇḍita, el cual sostiene una sombrilla [sobre la cabeza del Señor]. 

Śhrī Gaura-chandra está sentado en un trono enjoyado y el Señor Brahmā y otros semidioses ejecutan Su ārati. 

Narahari Sarakāra y otros abanican al Señor con chāmaras, mientras Sañjaya Paṇḍita, Mukunda Daṭṭa, Vāsudeva Ghoṣa y otros cantan [Sus glorias]. 

El resonar de la caracola, el tañido de la campana, el repiqueteo los karatālas y el dulce ritmo de la mṛdaṅga se juntan para crear el rasa supremo. 

El brillante rostro de Śhrī Gaurāṅga conquista el destello de miles de lunas, y la guirnalda de flores que cuelga de Su cuello brilla esplendorosamente. 

Las voces del Señor Śhiva, Śhukadeva Gosvāmī y Nārada Muni brotan entrecortadas debido al prema. De ese modo, Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura contempla las glorias de Śhrī Gaurāṅga.

IDX.en_translation:
All glories, all glories to Śrī Gurudeva Bhakti-prajñāna! Your supremely enchanting form delivers the distressed. 

You are the personification of Śrī Vedānta, the destroyer of inauspiciousness. You proclaimed, “Bhakti is the scripture, Śrī Vedānta.” 

In the lamp of the Vedānta Samiti, the light of siddhānta (philosophical conclusion) shines; Your ārati is performed there incessantly. 

The lamp is filled with the oil of the current of Śrī Vinoda; The ten directions are perfumed by the incense of the followers of Rūpa. 

Grave in all scriptures, soft with mercy; simultaneously, Your lotus face is very beautiful. 

The beauty of Your divine limbs defeats the luster of gold; Wearing the dress of a sannyāsī, You bring auspiciousness to the world. 

In various styles, the saintly persons wave the cāmara; The associate of Gaura sings very sweetly in a loud voice. 

The devotees perform the auspicious nīrājana; From a distance, the wicked-minded Trivikrama watches.
IDX.es_translation:
Toda gloria a nuestro divino maestro, Śhrī Śhrīmad Bhakti Prajñāna Keśhava Mahārāja, cuya atractiva figura libera a las sufrientes almas. 

Tú eres es la personificación del Vedānta y el aniquilador de todo lo inauspicioso. Tú declaraste audazmente que el Śhrī Vedānta es una escritura sobre el bhakti. 

Tú ārati es perpetuamente llevado a cabo con la lámpara del Śhrī Gauḍīya Vedānta Samiti sobre la cual brilla la espléndida luz del siddhānta. 

Esa lámpara contiene el aceite de la corriente [de las concepciones] que fluye de Śhrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura. Las diez direcciones son dulcemente aromatizadas con el incienso [los sentimientos] de los seguidores de Śhrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī. 

Tu hermoso rostro de loto es simultáneamente grave debido a tu profunda comprensión de las escrituras, y suave en virtud de tu profunda compasión. 

El brillo de tu hermoso cuerpo derrota la refulgencia del oro fundido. Al llevar los hábitos de la renuncia, has beneficiado al universo entero. 

Śhrī Sajjana 1 te abanica artísticamente con una cāmara, mientras Śhrī Gaura-nārāyaṇa 2 canta sonoramente y con voz muy dulce. 

A cierta distancia, el indigno Trivikrama observa a los devotos que realizan este auspicioso ārati. 1 Nombre de brahmacārī de Śhrī Śhrīmad Bhaktivedānta Vāmana Gosvāmī Mahārāja. 2 Nombre de brahmacārī de Śhrī Śhrīmad Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja.

IDX.verses: jaya jaya harināma, chidānandāmṛta dhāma, paratattva akṣara-ākāra nija-jane kṛpā kari’, nāmarūpe avatari’, jīve dayā karile apāra jaya hari-kṛṣṇa-nāma, jagajana suviśhrāma, sarvajana-mānasa-rañjana munivṛnda nirantara, je nāmera samādara, kari’ gāy bhariyā vadana ohe kṛṣṇa-nāmākṣara, tumi sarvaśhaktidhara, jīvera kalyāṇa-vitaraṇe tomā vinā bhavasindhu, uddhārite nāhi bandhu, āsiyācḣa jīva-uddhāraṇe ācḣe tāpa jīve jata, tumi saba kara hata, helāya tomāre ekabāra ḍāke jadi kona jana, ha’ye dīna akiñchana, nāhi dekhi’ anya pratikāra tava svalpasfūrti pāya, ugratāpa dūre jāya, liṅga-bhaṅga haya anāyāse bhakativinoda kaya, jaya harināma jaya, pa’ḍe thāki tuyā pada-āśhe
IDX.en_translation:
All glories, all glories to the Holy Name, the abode of conscious bliss and nectar, the Supreme Truth in the form of syllables! Out of mercy for Your own people, You have descended in the form of the Name and bestowed unlimited compassion upon the souls. 

All glories to the names of Hari and Kṛṣṇa, the supreme rest for all living beings and the delight of everyone’s mind! Groups of sages constantly honor this Name and sing it with a full voice. 

O imperishable Name of Kṛṣṇa, You possess all potencies for bestowing welfare upon the souls. Without You, there is no friend to deliver us from the ocean of material existence; You have come for the soul’s deliverance. 

Whatever miseries exist for the soul, You destroy them all if a person calls out to You just once, becoming humble and destitute, seeing no other remedy. 

Upon receiving Your slightest manifestation, fierce miseries vanish and the subtle body is easily destroyed. Bhaktivinoda says: victory to the Holy Name! I remain in the hope of Your feet.
IDX.es_translation:
Toda gloria a harināma, la morada del néctar del conocimiento trascendental y la dicha divina, y la Verdad Suprema en forma de sílabas. Él descendió en forma de Sus nombres por Su misericordia, mostrando así Su inmensa compasión por todos los seres. 

Toda gloria a los santos nombres de Hari y Kṛṣṇa, que son el refugio supremo de todas las entidades vivientes y que deleitan las mentes de todos. Multitud de grandes santos, que tienen verdadero respeto por estos nombres, los cantan eternamente y llenan sus bocas [con el nāma]. 

¡Oh, sílabas del nombre de Kṛṣṇa! ¡Oh, nāma! Tú posees todos los poderes y otorgas el bien supremo a todas las entidades vivientes. Aparte de ti no hay ningún otro amigo para liberarnos del océano de la existencia material. Tú has venido ciertamente para liberar a todas las jīvas. 

Si una jīva invoca Tu nombre aunque sea una vez o de forma impulsiva sintiéndose insignificante y desposeída y no hallando otro remedio a su aflicción, Tú eliminas todo su sufrimiento. 

Cuando se obtiene aunque sea una visión momentánea de Ti, toda clase de terribles sufrimientos se desvanecen, y los cuerpos burdo y sutil son fácilmente destruidos. Bhaktivinoda dice: “¡Toda gloria, toda gloria a los santos nombres de Śhrī Hari! Yo me postro con la esperanza de obtener Tus pies de loto.”

IDX.first_line: jaya jaya jadu kula jalanidhi chandra
IDX.search: jaya jaya jadu kula jalanidhi chandra vraja kula gokula ananda kanda jaya jaya jaladhara syamara anga helana kalpa taru lalita tri bhanga sudha i sudhamaya murali vilasa jaga jana mohana madhurima hasa avani vilambita vani vana bala madhukara jhankaru tatahi rasala taruna aruna ruchi pada aravinda nakha mani nicḣani dasa govinda
IDX.author: govinda dāsa
IDX.verses: jaya jaya jadu-kula-jalanidhi-chandra vraja-kula gokula ānanda-kanda jaya jaya jaladhara śhyāmara aṅga helana kalpa-taru lalita tri-bhaṅga sudha-i sudhāmaya murali-vilāsa jaga-jana-mohana madhurima hāsa avanī vilambita vani vana-bāla madhukara jhaṅkaru tatahi rasāla taruṇa aruṇa ruchi pada aravinda nakha-maṇi nicḣani dāsa-govinda
IDX.en_translation:
All glories, all glories to the Moon of the Yadu dynasty, the very root of joy for the residents of Vraja and Gokula! 

All glories, all glories to Him whose body is dark like a cloud, who effortlessly surpasses the wish-fulfilling tree, and who stands in a charming threefold bending posture! 

Nectarean are His pastimes with the flute, and His sweet smile enchants everyone in the world. 

His forest garland sways low to the earth, and the bees hum there, attracted by the sweet aroma. 

Govinda Dāsa offers his adoration to the jewel-like nails of His lotus feet, which are as radiant as the rising sun.

IDX.search: jaya jaya jaga jana lochana fanda radha ramana vrndavana chanda abhinava nila jalada tanu dhala dhala pincḣa mukuta sire sajani re kanchana vasanaratanamaya abharana nupura ranarani bajani re indivara yuga subhaga vilochana anchala chanchala kusuma sare avichala kula ramani gana manasa jara jara antare madana bhare vani vana maloajanu lambita parimale ali kula mati rahu bimbadhara pare mohana murali ga ota govinda dasa pahu

IDX.verses: jaya jaya jaga-jana-lochana-fānda rādhā-ramaṇa vṛndāvana-chānda abhinava nīla jalada tanu ḍhala ḍhala piñcḣa mukuṭa śhire sājani re kāñchana vasanaratanamaya ābharaṇa nūpura raṇaraṇi bājanī re indīvara-yuga subhaga vilochana añchala chañchala kusuma-śhare avichala kula ramaṇī-gaṇa mānasa jara jara antare madana-bhare vani vana-māloājānu-lambita parimale ali-kula māti rahu bimbādhara pare mohana muralī gā-ota govinda-dāsa-pahu
IDX.en_translation:
All glories, all glories to the moon of Vṛndāvana, Rādhā-ramaṇa, who captivates the eyes of all the people in the world! 

His fresh, blue body is dazzling like a cloud, and a peacock-feather crown adorns His head. He wears golden garments and jeweled ornaments, and His anklets make a jingling sound. 

His beautiful lotus-like eyes dart restless glances like Cupid’s flower-arrows. The hearts of all the ladies of Vraja are overwhelmed with love by His glances. 

A forest garland hangs down to His knees, and its fragrance intoxicates the bees. Upon His red lips, an enchanting flute sings—so says the Master of Govinda Dāsa.

IDX.search: jaya jaya jagannatha sachira nandana tri bhuvana kare janra charana vandana nilachale sankha chakra gada padma dhara nadiya nagare danda kamandalu kara keha bale puravete ravana vadhila golokera vaibhava lila prakasa karila sri radhara bhave ebe gora avatara hare krsna nama gaura karila prachara vasudeva ghosa bale kari joda hata jei gaura sei krsna sei jagannatha
IDX.author: vasudeva ghoṣa
IDX.verses: jaya jaya jagannātha śhachīra nandana tri-bhuvana kare jāṅ’ra charaṇa vandana nīlāchale śhaṅkha-chakra-gadā-padma-dhara nadīyā nagare daṇḍa-kamaṇḍalu-kara keha bale, — ‘pūravete rāvaṇa vadhilā’ golokera vaibhava līlā prakāśha karilā śhrī-rādhāra bhāve ebe gorā avatāra ‘hare kṛṣṇa’-nāma gaura karilā prachāra vāsudeva ghoṣa bale kari’ joḍa hāta jei gaura, sei kṛṣṇa, sei jagannātha
IDX.en_translation:
All glories to Jagannātha, the Son of Śacī! The three worlds worship His feet. 

In Nīlācala, He is the Holder of conch, disc, club, and lotus; in the town of Nadīyā, He is the Holder of the staff and water-pot. 

Someone says, “Previously He killed Rāvaṇa.” He manifested the opulent pastimes of Goloka. 

Now, in the mood of Śrī Rādhā, He is the Golden Avatar; Gaura preached the Name “Hare Kṛṣṇa”. 

Vāsudeva Ghoṣa says with folded hands: He who is Gaura is Kṛṣṇa, is Jagannātha.
IDX.es_translation:
Toda gloria al amado hijo de Jagannātha Miśhra y Śhachī-devī. Sus pies de loto son adorados por los tres mundos. 

En Nīlāchala Él lleva una concha, un disco, una maza y una flor de loto, y en Nadīyā el bastón de renunciante y un recipiente de agua. 

Algunos dicen que en una era anterior mató al demonio Rāvaṇa. Luego (como el Señor Kṛṣṇa) reveló los gloriosos pasatiempos de Goloka. 

Ahora, aceptando el bhāva de Śhrī Rādhā, ha descendido como el avatar dorado. El Señor Gaura predica el (canto del) mahā-mantra Hare Kṛṣṇa. 

Con las manos unidas, Vāsudeva Ghoṣa dice: “Ese Gaura es Kṛṣṇa y también Jagannātha.”

IDX.verses: jaya jaya mahāprabhu jaya gaura-chandra aya viśhvambhara jaya karuṇāra sindhu jaya śhachīsūta jaya paṇḍita nimāñi jaya miśhra purandara jaya śhachī āi jaya jaya navadvīpa jaya suradhunī jaya lakṣmī viṣṇupriyā prabhura gṛhiṇī jaya jaya navadvīpavāsī-bhaktagaṇa jaya jaya nityānanda advaita-charaṇa nityānanda pada dvandva sadā kari āśha nāma saṁkīrtana gāila kṛṣṇa-dāsa
IDX.en_translation:
All glories to Mahāprabhu! All glories to Gaura-candra! All glories to Viśvambhara, the maintainer of the universe and the ocean of mercy! 

All glories to the Son of Mother Śacī, the learned Paṇḍita Nimāi! All glories to Jagannātha Miśra and Mother Śacī! 

All glories to Navadvīpa and the River Ganges! All glories to Lakṣmī-devī and Viṣṇupriyā-devī, the wives of the Lord. 

All glories to the residents of Navadvīpa and all the devotees! All glories to the lotus feet of Lord Nityānanda and Advaita Āchārya! 

I always desire the twin lotus feet of Lord Nityānanda. Kṛṣṇa-dāsa sings this congregational chanting of the Holy Name.

jaya jaya guṇanidhi, jaya dayāmaya 
jaya jaya bhakatavatsala rasamaya

jaya jaya parachaṇḍa, pāṣaṇḍa-mardana 

jaya jaya asura-kuñjara-mahāsiṁha 
jaya jaya vrajavadhu-mukhapadma-bhṛṅga 

jaya jaya jogendra-mānasa-paramahaṁsa 
jaya bhakta-bhavapatha-parikrama-dhvaṁsa 

jaya jaya jagatamaṅgala guṇadhāma 
jaya jaya śhrutivāṇī-agochara nāma 

jaya pūrṇabrahma kṛṣṇa vichitra-vihāra

IDX.en_translation:
All glories to the Son of Nanda, the Master of the family of Vraja! All glories to the Lord of the Yadus, the ultimate destination of the three worlds! 

All glories to the Abode of the universe, the Master of the senses! All glories to Him who is like the sun for the lotus-like devotees! 

All glories to Him whose lotus feet are caressed by the Goddess of Fortune! All glories to the blissful joy of the minds of the great sages! 

All glories to the Ocean of good qualities! All glories to the Merciful One! All glories to Him who is affectionate to His devotees and full of divine mellows! 

All glories to the Destroyer of great fear and sin! All glories to the fierce Subduer of atheists! 

All glories to the great Lion who defeats the elephant-like demons! All glories to the Honeybee for the lotus-like faces of the gopīs! 

All glories to the Swan in the minds of the great yogīs! All glories to the Destroyer of the cycle of material existence for the devotees! 

All glories to the Auspiciousness of the universe, the Abode of all good qualities! All glories to Him whose Name is beyond the reach of the Vedas! 

All glories to the complete Absolute Truth, Lord Kṛṣṇa, who performs wonderful pastimes! All glories to Lord Jagannātha, the incarnation of Nīlācala! 

All glories to Śrī Gaurāṅga, the personification of consciousness! He is the Bestower of loving devotion and the only shelter of the devotees.
