IDX.verses:
kṛṣṇa haite chatur-mukha, haya kṛṣṇa-sevonmukha, 
brahmā haite nāradera mati 
nārada hoite vyāsa, madhva kahe vyāsa-dāsa, 
pūrṇaprajña padmanābha-gati 

nṛhari-mādhava-vaṁśhe, akṣobhya-paramahaṁse, 
śhiṣya bali’ aṅgīkāra kare 
akṣobhyera śhiṣya ‘jaya-tīrtha’ nāme parichaya, 
tāṅ’ra dāsye jñānasindhu tare 

tāṅhā haite dayānidhi, tāṅ’ra dāsa vidyānidhi, 
rājendra hoila tāṅhā ha’te 
tāṅhāra kiṅkara ‘jaya-dharma’ nāme parichaya, 
paramparā jāna bhāla-mate 

jaya-dharma-dāsye khyāti, śhrī-puruṣottama-yati, 
tāṅ’ ha’te brahmaṇya-tīrtha-sūri 
vyāsa-tīrtha tāṅ’ra dāsa, lakṣmīpati vyāsa-dāsa, 
tāṅhā ha’te mādhavendra-purī 

mādhavendra-purī-vara-śhiṣya-vara śhrī-īśhvara, 
nityānanda, śhrī-advaita vibhu 
īśhvara purīke dhanya, karilena śhrī-chaitanya, 
jagad-guru gaura mahāprabhu 

mahāprabhu śhrī chaitanya, rādhā-kṛṣṇa nahe anya, 
rūpānuga-janera jīvana 
viśhvambhara-priyaṅkara, śhrī svarūpa-dāmodara, 
śhrī gosvāmī rūpa, sanātana 

rūpa-priya mahājana, jīva, raghunātha hana, 
tāṅ’ra priya kavi kṛṣṇadāsa 
kṛṣṇadāsa priya-vara, narottama sevā-para, 
jāṅ’ra pada viśhvanātha-āśha 

viśhvanātha bhakta-sātha, baladeva, jagannātha, 
tāṅ’ra priya śhrī bhaktivinoda 
mahā-bhāgavata-vara, śhrī gaurakiśhora-vara, 
hari-bhajanete jāṅ’ra moda 

(‘śhrī-vārṣabhānavī’-varā, sadā sevya-sevā-parā, 
tāṅhāra ‘dayita-dāsa’ nāma) 

(prabhupāda-antaraṅga, śhrī-svarūpa-rūpānuga, 
śhrī-keśhava bhakati-prajñāna) 

(gauḍīya-vedānta-vettā, māyāvāda-tamohantā, 
gauravāṇī-prachārāchāra-dhāma) 

(prachārila gaurāvāṇī, bhakativedānta svāmī, 
pūrāila prabhupāder kāma) 

(keśhav priya-mahājana, vāmana nārāyaṇa hana 
gaurāvāṇī tāṅder prāṇa-dhana) 

(ei saba harijana, gaurāṅgera nija-jana, 
tāṅ’dera uccḣiṣṭe mora kāma)
IDX.en_translation:
From Kṛṣṇa came the four-faced Brahmā, who is inclined to the service of Kṛṣṇa. From Brahmā came the intelligence of Nārada. From Nārada came Vyāsa; Madhva calls himself the servant of Vyāsa. Pūrṇaprajña (Madhva) is the destination of Padmanābha. 

In the lineage of Nṛhari and Mādhava, Akṣobhya accepted Paramahaṁsa as his disciple. Akṣobhya’s disciple is known by the name “Jaya Tīrtha”. His servant was Jñānasindhu. 

From him came Dayānidhi, and his servant is Vidyānidhi. Rājendra came from him. His servant is known by the name “Jaya Dharma”. Know this disciplic succession well. 

Renowned in the service of Jayadharma was Śrī Puruṣottama Yati. From him came the learned Brahmaṇya Tīrtha. Vyāsa Tīrtha was his servant. Lakṣmīpati was the servant of Vyāsa. From him came Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī. 

The best disciple of Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī was Śrī Īśvara Purī, and also Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu and the powerful Śrī Advaita Āchārya. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the spiritual master of the universe, the great Golden Lord, made Śrī Īśvara Purī glorious. 

Mahāprabhu Śrī Caitanya is none other than Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, the life of the followers of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī. The dearmost of Viśvambhara was Śrīla Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, and the Gosvāmīs Śrīla Rūpa and Śrīla Sanātana. 

Dear to Rūpa were the great souls Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī and Śrīla Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī. Their dear poet was Śrīla Kṛṣṇa-dāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī. Kṛṣṇa-dāsa’s dearmost was Śrīla Narottama Dāsa Ṭhākura, dedicated to service, whose feet were the hope of Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura. 

Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura, along with the devotees Śrīla Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa and Śrīla Jagannātha Dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja; their dear Śrīla Saccidānanda Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura. The great mahā-bhāgavata, the excellent Śrīla Gaura-kiśora Dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja, whose delight was in the worship of Hari. 

[Composed by his disciples] The excellent “Śrī Vārṣabhānavī”, always intent on the service of the Object of service—his name is “Dayita-dāsa” (Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura Prabhupāda). 

The intimate associate of Prabhupāda, the follower of Svarūpa and Rūpa, is Śrīla Bhaktiprajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja. 

Knower of Gauḍīya Vedānta, destroyer of the darkness of Māyāvāda, the abode of the practice and preaching of Gaura’s message. 

Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Svāmī Prabhupāda preached the message of Gaura, fulfilling the desire of Prabhupāda. 

The great souls dear to Keśava are Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Vāmana Gosvāmī Mahārāja and Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja. 

The message of Gaura is the treasure of their lives. All these devotees of Hari are Gaurāṅga’s own; my desire is for their remnants.
IDX.es_translation:
Al comienzo de la creación, Śrī Kṛṣṇa impartió la ciencia del servicio devocional al Señor Brahmā. Este transmitió esas enseñanzas a Śrī Nārada Muni, el cual aceptó a Śrī Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana Vyāsadeva como su discípulo. Śhrī Vyāsa transmitió este conocimiento a Śhrī Madhvāchārya, conocido también como Pūrṇaprajña Tīrtha, el único refugio para su discípulo Śrī Padmanābha Tīrtha. 

Nṛhari Tīrtha y Śrī Mādhava Tīrtha siguieron la línea de Śrī Madhvāchārya, y luego también el gran paramahaṁsa Śrī Akṣobhyatīrtha. El principal discípulo de Śrī Akṣobhyatīrtha fue Jayatīrtha, y Sri Jñānasindhu fue su sirviente. 

El paramparā continuó con Śrī Dayānidhi, luego con su discípulo Śrī Vidyānidhi y luego con Śrī Rājendra Tīrtha, cuyo sirviente fue Śrī Jayadharma, también conocido como Śrī Vijayadhvaja Tīrtha. El guru paramparā debe ser entendido apropiadamente de esta manera. 

El sannyāsī Śrī Puruṣottama Tīrtha era un famoso discípulo al servicio de Śrī Jayadharma; fue sucedido por el erudito Śrī Brahmaṇya Tīrtha y posteriormente por Śrī Vyāsa Tīrtha. Este fue sucedido por Śrī Lakṣmīpati, que transfirió la línea a Śrī Mādhavendra Purī. 

Los discípulos más prominentes de Śrī Mādhavendra Purī fueron Śrī Īśvara Purī y los avatāras Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu y Śrī Advaita Āchārya. Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu, el Señor Dorado y preceptor espiritual de todos los mundos, hizo que Īśvara Purī fuese sumamente afortunado al aceptarlo como Su dīkṣā guru. 

Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu, que es Rādhā y Kṛṣṇa combinados, es la vida misma de los vaiṣṇavas rūpānuga (los que siguen a Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī). Śrī Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, Śrī Rūpa y Śrī Sanātana Gosvāmīs eran los sirvientes más queridos del Señor Viśvambhara (Śrī Chaitanya). 

Muy queridos por Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī fueron las grandes y santas personalidades Śrī Jīva Gosvāmī y Śrī Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī, cuyo íntimo discípulo fue el gran poeta Śrī Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja. El discípulo más querido de Kṛṣṇadāsa era Śrīla Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura, que estaba siempre dedicado al guru sevā. Sus pies de loto eran la única esperanza y aspiración de Śrī Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura. 

Uno de los principales asociados de Śrī Viśvanātha Chakravartī Ṭhākura fue Śrī Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa. Tras él, la línea descendió a Śrīla Jagannātha dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja, que era el amado śikṣā- guru de Śrī Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura. Bhaktivinoda era el amigo íntimo del gran mahā-bhāgavata Śrīla Gaura-kiśora dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja, cuya única satisfacción era el hari-bhajana. 

<highlight>[Compuesto por sus discípulos]</highlight> Śrī Vārṣabhānavī, la hija de Śrī Vṛṣabhānu Mahārāja, es la mejor entre las amadas de Śrī Kṛṣṇa, pues está siempre dedicada al servicio amoroso de Su venerable Señor. Śrī Vārṣabhānavī-dayita dāsa, el sirviente (dāsa) de Su amado (dayita) es el nombre de Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura Prabhupāda. 

Un discípulo confidencial de Śrīla Prabhupāda, Śrīla Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja, fue el fiel seguidor Śrī Svarūpa Dāmodara y Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī. 

Mediante su conocimiento del Gauḍīya Vedānta, él acabó con la oscuridad de la ignorancia expandida por la doctrina māyāvāda. Él ejemplificó en su vida la prédica y la práctica de las enseñanzas de Śrī Gaurāṅga (gauravāṇī). 

Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Svāmī Mahārāja predicó extensamente este gauravāṇī y de ese modo satisfizo por completo el deseo íntimo de Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Prabhupāda. 

Las santas personalidades Śrī Bhaktivedānta Vāmana Gosvāmī y Śrī Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī, cuya vida misma es gauravāṇī, le son muy queridos a Śrī Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī. 

Todos estos devotos son asociados personales de Śrī Gaurāṅga. Yo deseo honrar su ucchiṣṭa (los remanentes de sus labios en forma de su mahā-prasāda y sus instrucciones).

kṛṣṇa-kṛṣṇabhakta-gata, ‘guṇa’ ‘nāma’ ‘sucharita’, 
‘maṇḍana’ ‘sambandhi’ ‘taṭastha’ ādi 
bhāva jata agaṇana, ai rasera uddīpana, 
‘hetu’ bali’ bale rasavedī 

mānasa vāchika punaḥ, kāyikete tina ‘guṇa’, 
‘nāma’-kṛṣṇa, śhrī-rādhā-mādhava 
nṛtya vaṁśhī-gāna gati, go-dohana go-āhuti, 
agoddhāra goṣṭhete tāṇḍava 

mālyānulepana āra, vāsa bhūṣā ei chāra-, 
prakāra ‘maṇḍana’ śhobhākara 
vaṁśhī-śhṛṅga-vīṇā-raba, gīta śhilpa susaurabha, 
padāṅka bhūṣaṇa-vādyasvara 

śhikhi-puccḣa gābhī jaṣṭi, veṇu śhṛṅga preṣṭha-dṛṣṭi, 
adridhātu nirmālya godhūli 
vṛndāvana tadāśhrita, govardhana ravi-sutā, 
rāsa-ādi jata līlāsthalī 

khaga bhṛṅga mṛga kuñja, tulasikā latā-puñja, 
karṇikāra kadambādi taru 
śhrī-kṛṣṇa- ‘sambandhi’ saba, vṛndāraṇya su-vaibhava, 
uddīpana kare rasa chāru 

jyotsnā ghana saudāminī, śharat pūrṇaniśhāmaṇi,

‘taṭastha’ ākhya uddīpana, rasāsvāda-vibhāvana,

IDX.en_translation:
The qualities, names, and pastimes associated with Kṛṣṇa and His devotees; all the innumerable emotions like adornments, relationships, and neutral factors—these are what the experts call the stimulants that awaken the divine mellows. 

The three qualities are mental, verbal, and bodily. The names include Kṛṣṇa and Śrī Rādhā-Mādhava. His dancing, flute playing, and movements; His milking of cows, cow worship, and His vigorous dance in the cowherd village for cow protection. 

Garlands, anointments, garments, and ornaments—these four types are the adornments that enhance beauty. The sounds of the flute, horn, and vīṇā, sweet songs, art, and pleasant fragrances, His footprints, ornaments, and musical sounds. 

The peacock feather, cows, shepherd’s staff, flute, horn, and loving glances; minerals from the mountains, remnants, and cow-dust at twilight. Vṛndāvana and all its dependent places, Govardhana, the Yamunā River, and all the places of divine pastimes such as the Rāsa dance. 

Birds, bees, deer, groves, Tulasi plants, clusters of creepers, Karnikara and Kadamba trees, and other trees. All these are related to Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the great opulence of the forest of Vṛndāvana, and they stimulate the charming mellow. 

Moonlight, dense clouds, lightning, the autumn season, the full moon, the fragrant breeze, and flocks of birds. These are called neutral stimulants, all mercifully creating the experience of the divine mellow.

kṛṣṇa-prasādena samasta-śhaila- 
sāmrājyam āpnoti cha vairiṇo ‘pi 
śhakrasya jaḥ prāpa baliṁ sa sākṣād 
govardhano me diśhatām abhīṣṭam 

sva-preṣṭha-hastāmbuja-saukumārya- 
sukhānubhūter ati-bhūmi vṛtteḥ 
mahendra-vajrāhatim apy ajānan 
govardhano me diṣatām abhīṣṭam 

jatraiva kṛṣṇo vṛṣabhānu-putryā 
dānaṁ gṛhītuṁ kalahaṁ vitene 
śhruteḥ spṛhā jatra mahaty ataḥ śhrī- 
govardhano me diṣatām abhiṣṭam 

snātvā saraḥ svaśhu samīra-hastī 
jatraiva nīpādi-parāga-dhūliḥ 
ālolayan khelati chāru sa śhrī- 
govardhano me diṣatām abhīṣṭam 

kastūrikābhiḥ śhayitaṁ kim atrety 
ūhaṁ prabhoḥ svasya muhur vitanvan 
naisargika-svīya-śhilā-sugandhair 
govardhano me diṣatām abhīṣṭam 

vaṁśha-pratidhvany-anusāra-vartma 
didṛkṣavo jatra hariṁ hariṇyaḥ 
jāntyo labhante na hi vismitāḥ sa 
govardhano me diṣatām abhīṣṭam 

jatraiva gaṅgām anu nāvi rādhām 
ārohya madhye tu nimagna-naukaḥ 
kṛṣṇo hi rādhānugalo babhau sa 
govardhano me diṣatām abhīṣṭam 

vinā bhavet kiṁ hari-dāsa-varya- 
padāśhrayaṁ bhaktir ataḥ śhrayāmi 
jam eva saprema nijeśhayoḥ śhrī- 
govardhano me diṣatām abhīṣṭam 

etat paṭhed jo hari-dāsa-varya- 
mahānubhāvāṣṭakam ārdra-chetāḥ 
śhrī-rādhikā-mādhavayoḥ padābja- 
dāsyaṁ sa vinded achireṇa sākṣāta
IDX.en_translation:
By Lord Kṛṣṇa’s mercy, Govardhana Hill attained sovereignty over all mountains and received tribute even from His enemy Indra. May He grant the desire of my heart. 

Govardhana Hill, who, due to the abundant joy experienced from the exquisite touch of Lord Kṛṣṇa’s lotus-like hands, did not even feel the strike of Indra’s thunderbolt—may He grant the desire of my heart. 

May Śrī Govardhana, where Lord Kṛṣṇa engaged in a playful dispute with the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu to collect a toll, and where the desire to hear of these pastimes is great—may He grant the desire of my heart. 

May that Śrī Govardhana, where the elephant-like wind, having bathed in the nearby lakes, beautifully plays by stirring the pollen of the Kadamba and other trees—may He grant the desire of my heart. 

Govardhana Hill, which, by the natural fragrance of its own stones, repeatedly causes one to wonder: “Did my Lord sleep here with musk?”—may He grant the desire of my heart. 

May that Govardhana Hill, where the deer, desiring to see Lord Hari, follow the path guided by the echo of His flute, grant the desire of my heart. 

May that Govardhana Hill, where Lord Kṛṣṇa, having seated Rādhā in a boat along the Mānasa-gaṅgā, and the boat having playfully submerged in the middle, shone beautifully as He embraced Her—may He grant the desire of my heart. 

Without the shelter of the feet of the best of Kṛṣṇa’s servants, Govardhana Hill, what would devotion be? Therefore, I take shelter of Śrī Govardhana, who lovingly serves His own Lords, Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. May He grant the desire of my heart. 

Whoever reads these eight verses describing the great glories of the best of Kṛṣṇa’s servants with a softened heart, he directly attains, without delay, servitude at the lotus feet of Śrīmati Rādhikā and Lord Mādhava.

kṛṣṇa tava puṇya habe bhāi! 
e puṇya karibe jabe, rādhā-rāṇī khuśhi habe, 
dhruva ati bali tomā tāi 

śhrī siddhānta sarasvatī, śhachī-suta priya ati, 
kṛṣṇa-sevāya jāṅra tulya nāi 
sei se mohānta-guru, jagatera madhye ūru, 
kṛṣṇa-bhakti deya ṭhāṅi ṭhāṅi 

tāṅra iccḣā balavāna, pāśhchātyete thāna thāna, 
haya jāte gaurāṅgera nāma 
pṛthivīte nagarādi, āsamudra nada-nadī, 
sakalei laya kṛṣṇa-nāma 

tāhale ānanda haya, tabe haya digvijaya, 
chaitanyera kṛpā atiśhaya 
māyāduṣṭa jata duḥkhī, jagate sabāi sukhī, 
vaiṣṇavera iccḣā pūrṇa haya 

se kārya je karibāre, ājñā jadi dile more, 
jogya nahi ati dīna hīna 
tāi se tomāra kṛpā, māgitecḣi anurūpā, 
āji tumi sabāra pravīṇa 

tomāra se śhakti pele, guru-sevā vastu mile, 
jīvana sārthaka jadi haya 
sei se sevā pele, tāhale sukhī hale, 
tava saṅga bhāgyate milaya 

evaṁ janaṁ nipatitaṁ prabhavāhikūpe 
kāmābhikāmam anu jaḥ prapatana prasaṅgāta 
kṛtvātmasāt surarṣiṇā bhagavan gṛhītaḥ 
so‛haṁ kathaṁ nu visṛje tava bhṛtya-sevām 

tumi mora chira-sāthī, bhuliyā māyāra lāthi, 
khāiyācḣi janma-janmāntare 
āji punaḥ e suyoga, jadi haya jogāyoga, 
tabe pāri tuhe milibāre 

tomāra milane bhāi, ābāra se sukha pāi, 
gochāraṇe ghuri dina bhora 
kata vane cḣuṭācḣuṭi, vane khāi luṭāpuṭi, 
sei dina kabe habe mora 

(āji se subidhā-ne tomāra smaraṇa bhela 
baḍa āśhā ḍākilāma tāi 
āmi tomāra nitya-dāsa tāi kari eta āśha 
tumi binā anya gati nāi)
IDX.en_translation:
Kṛṣṇa! You will accrue merit, brother! When you perform this pious act, Rādhā-rāṇī will be pleased; I tell you this as a certainty. 

Śrī Siddhānta Sarasvatī is very dear to the Son of Śacī; there is no one equal to him in the service of Kṛṣṇa. That great Guru, the best in the world, distributes Kṛṣṇa-bhakti in place after place. 

His desire is powerful—that the name of Gaurāṅga should spread in the West. In all the cities of the earth, from the ocean to the rivers, may everyone take the name of Kṛṣṇa. 

Then there will be joy, then there will be victory in all directions, by the great mercy of Caitanya. All the miserable people polluted by Māyā in the world will be happy, and the desire of the Vaiṣṇava will be fulfilled. 

To perform that task, if you give me the order—although I am unworthy, very low and fallen—I beg for your suitable mercy; today you are the authority for everyone. 

If I get your strength, the object of Guru-sevā is obtained, and my life becomes successful. If I get that service, then I will be happy; by good fortune, your association is obtained. 

“O Lord, I am a person fallen into the blind well of material existence, constantly engaged in lust. I was accepted by the celestial sage (Nārada) and made his own. How can I give up the service of Your servant?” 

You are my eternal companion; forgetting You, I have suffered the kicks of Māyā birth after birth. Today, again, if this opportunity arises—if there is a connection—then I can meet You. 

In meeting You, brother, I again find that happiness, wandering all day grazing the cows. Running in so many forests, rolling on the ground in the forest—when will that day be mine? 

(Today, in that opportunity, I remembered You. With great hope, I called out. I am Your eternal servant, so I have so much hope. Without You, I have no other shelter.)

IDX.search: krsna vamsi gita suni dekhi chitra patakhani lokamukhe guna sravaniya purvaragakranta chita unmada laksananvita sakhisange chalila dhaiya nikunjakanane karila abhisara na manila nivarana grhakarya aganana dharmadharma na karila vichara yamunapuline giya sakhigane sambodhiya jijnasila priyera uddesa cḣadila pranera bhaya vanete pravesa haya vamsidhvani kariya nirdesa nadi jatha sindhu prati dhaya ati vegavati seirupa rasavati sati ati vege kunjavane giya krsna sannidhane atmanivedane kaila mati kena mora durbala lekhani nahi sare abhisara aramtiya sakampa antare milana sambhoga vipralambhadi varnana prakasa karite nahi sare mama mana durbhaga na bujhe rasalila tattvasara sukara jemana nahi chine muktahara adhikarahina jana mangala chintiya kirtana karinu sesa kala vichariya
IDX.author: sacchidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
kṛṣṇa-vaṁśhī-gīta śhuni’, dekhi’ chitra-paṭakhāni, 
lokamukhe guṇa śhravaṇiyā 
pūrvarāgākrānta chita, unmāda-lakṣaṇānvita, 
sakhīsaṅge chalilā dhāiyā 

nikuñjakānane karila abhisāra 
nā mānila nivāraṇa, gṛhakārya agaṇana, 
dharmādharma nā karila vichāra 

yamunāpuline giyā, sakhīgaṇe sambodhiyā, 
jijñāsila priyera uddeśha 
cḣāḍila prāṇera bhaya, vanete praveśha haya, 
vaṁśhīdhvani kariyā nirdeśha 

nadī jathā sindhu-prati, dhāya ati vegavatī, 
seirūpa rasavatī satī 
ati vege kuñjavane, giyā kṛṣṇa-sannidhāne, 
ātmanivedane kaila mati 

kena mora durbalā lekhanī nāhi sare 
abhisāra āramtiyā sakampa antare 

milana, sambhoga, vipralambhādi-varṇana 
prakāśha karite nāhi sare mama mana 

durbhāgā nā bujhe rāsalīlā-tattvasāra 
śhūkara jemana nāhi chine muktāhāra 

adhikārahīna-jana-maṅgala chintiyā 
kīrtana karinu śheṣa, kāla vichāriyā
IDX.en_translation:
Hearing Kṛṣṇa’s flute song, seeing His beautiful form in a painting, and hearing of His qualities, her heart was afflicted by initial attraction; showing symptoms of madness, she ran swiftly with her companions. 

She made her tryst toward the forest bower. She heeded no prevention, nor her countless household duties, nor did she consider right or wrong. 

Going to the bank of the Yamunā and addressing her companions, she inquired about the whereabouts of her beloved. Abandoning all fear for her life, she entered the forest, guided by the sound of the flute. 

Just as a river swiftly rushes toward the ocean, that chaste woman, full of mellows, went with great speed to the forest grove near Kṛṣṇa; with a mood of self-surrender, she gave herself to Him. 

Why does my feeble pen not move, as I begin to describe the tryst with a trembling heart? 

My mind does not move to reveal the meeting, the enjoyment, the separation, and other such topics. 

An unfortunate person cannot understand the essence of the divine rāsa dance, just as a hog cannot recognize a pearl necklace. 

Thinking of the welfare of those who are not yet qualified, I conclude this narration here, considering the time.

Without topics concerning Lord Kṛṣṇa, know all other talk to be “unreal talk.” Such talk is like a very dreadful prostitute. Devotion concerning Lord Kṛṣṇa is extremely rare for the soul, and that prostitute steals away that devotion. 

Listen, O my mind, I tell you: if one listens to the tigress named “liberation,” she swallows all his spiritual wealth. 

Abandon both sense gratification and liberation, and give up talk of impersonal liberation. Keep devotion for Lord Nārāyaṇa far away. If that devotion becomes strong, it throws one into the spiritual sky of Vaikuṇṭha, but does not grant residence in Vraja. 

Devotion for Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in Vraja is an extremely priceless bestower of wealth. Therefore, you should always worship that. At the feet of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī and Śrīla Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī, praying for that devotion, this Bhaktivinoda is poor and humble.

Engaged in the congregational chanting of Kṛṣṇa’s names, singing and dancing—they are oceans of the nectar of divine love. Dear to both the sober and the restless, they are doers of good, free from envy, and revered. Full of the mercy of Lord Caitanya and relieving the earth of its burden—I offer my obeisances to Rūpa, Sanātana, Raghunātha dāsa, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa, Jīva, and Gopāla Bhaṭṭa. 

Expert in deliberating on various scriptures and establishers of true religious principles, they are benefactors of humanity, respected in the three worlds, and abodes of refuge. Like intoxicated bees relishing the bliss of worshiping the lotus feet of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa—I offer my obeisances to Rūpa, Sanātana, Raghunātha dāsa, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa, Jīva, and Gopāla Bhaṭṭa. 

Endowed with abundant faith in the process of describing Lord Caitanya’s qualities, they are the cutters of the miseries and sins of embodied beings through the nectar of the Lord’s glories. Expert in increasing the ocean of bliss and delivering others from impersonal liberation—I offer my obeisances to Rūpa, Sanātana, Raghunātha dāsa, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa, Jīva, and Gopāla Bhaṭṭa. 

Having quickly given up all ranks of powerful leaders and always considering them insignificant, out of compassion they became the masters of the humble and poor. Taking shelter of simple loincloths and patched coverings, they are constantly immersed in the waves and surges of the nectar-ocean of the mood of the gopīs—I offer my obeisances to Rūpa, Sanātana, Raghunātha dāsa, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa, Jīva, and Gopāla Bhaṭṭa. 

In Vṛndāvana, which is filled with cooing cuckoos, swans, and cranes, crowded with peacocks, and adorned with trees whose roots are bound with jewels—they worship Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa day and night and joyfully bestow the ultimate benefit upon all souls. I offer my obeisances to Rūpa, Sanātana, Raghunātha dāsa, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa, Jīva, and Gopāla Bhaṭṭa. 

They utilized their time by chanting the Holy Names a fixed number of times and by offering obeisances. They conquered sleep, eating, and recreation, and were extremely humble. Enchanted by the sweet bliss of remembering the qualities of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa—I offer my obeisances to Rūpa, Sanātana, Raghunātha dāsa, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa, Jīva, and Gopāla Bhaṭṭa. 

On the bank of Rādhā-kuṇḍa, on the bank of the Yamunā, and at the Vaṁśīvaṭa tree, they were always overwhelmed by the madness of divine love, affected by various stages of ecstasy and always intoxicated. Sometimes they were joyfully overwhelmed by transcendental emotions while singing the excellent qualities of the Lord. I offer my obeisances to Rūpa, Sanātana, Raghunātha dāsa, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa, Jīva, and Gopāla Bhaṭṭa. 

“O Rādhā! O Goddess of Vraja! O Lalitā! O Son of Nanda! Where are You? Are You under the wish-fulfilling trees of Govardhana, or in the forest along the Yamunā?” Shouting in this way everywhere in Vraja and greatly agitated by the distress of separation—I offer my obeisances to Rūpa, Sanātana, Raghunātha dāsa, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa, Jīva, and Gopāla Bhaṭṭa.
IDX.es_translation:
Siempre dedicados a cantar las glorias [del nombre, la forma, las cualidades, los pasatiempos, los asociados y la morada] de Śhrī Kṛṣṇa, los seis Gosvāmīs son la personificación del océano de néctar del amor divino. Amados y adorados por caballeros y rufianes, no hay en ellos ni un atisbo de envidia y sus actividades complacen siempre a todos. Śhrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu les ha bendecido plenamente con Su misericordia, por lo que eliminan la carga de la tierra. Yo adoro a Śhrī Rūpa, Śhrī Sanātana, Śhrī Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa, Śhrī Raghunātha dāsa, Śhrī Jīva y Śhrī Gopāla Bhaṭṭa [los seis Gosvāmīs]. 

Ellos son sumamente expertos en extraer la esencia de todas las escrituras reveladas, y establecen la ocupación suprema del alma (bhagavad-bhakti). Son los verdaderos benefactores de la gente, adorados por los tres mundos, y afectuosos con quienes se refugian en ellos. Debido al éxtasis del bhajana por los pies de loto de Śhrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, se han vuelto como abejas embriagadas. Yo adoro a los Gosvāmīs Śhrī Rūpa, Sanātana, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa, dāsa, Jīva y Gopāla Bhaṭṭa. 

Por su profunda fe en el proceso de describir las diversas cualidades de Śhrī Gaurāṅga, ellos anulan el gran pesar generado por las actividades pecaminosas de los seres encarnados derramando sobre ellos nectáreas canciones acerca de Govinda. Son especialmente expertos difundiendo el océano de la bienaventuranza y rescatando a todos del impersonalismo. Yo adoro a los Gosvāmīs Śhrī Rūpa, Sanātana, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa, Raghunātha dāsa, Jīva y Gopāla Bhaṭṭa. 

Ellos abandonaron inmediata y completamente la asociación con la aristocracia real —por considerarla insignificante— y, movidos por su compasión, se volvieron pobres y aceptaron únicamente kaupins y harapos. A partir de entonces se hallaban siempre inmersos en las gozosas e inmensas olas del nectáreo océano de rasa: los bhāvas que experimentan las gopīs. Yo adoro a los Gosvāmīs Śhrī Rūpa, Sanātana, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa, Raghunātha dāsa, Jīva y Gopāla Bhaṭṭa. 

Vṛndāvana, que reluce esplendorosa con árboles de joyas trascendentales incrustadas bajo sus raíces, está llena de cuclillos, cisnes, garzas y pavos reales que entonan dulces sonidos. Allí los Gosvāmīs adoran intensamente a Śhrī Śhrī Rādhā y Kṛṣṇa, y al hacerlo otorgan a todas las jīvas el beneficio máximo de la vida. Yo adoro a los Gosvāmīs Śhrī Rūpa, Sanātana, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa, Raghunātha dāsa, Jīva y Gopāla Bhaṭṭa. 

Ellos dedicaban su tiempo a cumplir diariamente con su voto de recitar un número determinado de santos nombres, cantar unas canciones concretas y ofrecer reverencias [a los santos, las deidades y los lugares de pasatiempos del Señor], y de ese modo dominaron todos los impulsos, como el hambre y el sueño. Considerándose siempre sumamente bajos e insignificantes, ellos estaban siempre absortos en la bienaventuranza suprema del recuerdo de Śhrī Śhrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa. Yo adoro a los Gosvāmīs Śhrī Rūpa, Sanātana, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa, Raghunātha dāsa, Jīva y Gopāla Bhaṭṭa. 

Ellos paseaban por las riberas del Rādhā-kuṇḍa o el Yamunā sobrecogidos por ilimitados éxtasis trascendentales e intoxicados por la locura absoluta del prema, y cantaban jubilosamente las cualidades supremas de Śhrī Hari saturados de dicha. Yo adoro a los Gosvāmīs Śhrī Rūpa, Sanātana, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa, Raghunātha dāsa, Jīva y Gopāla Bhaṭṭa. 

“¡Oh Rādhā, Reina de Vṛndāvana! ¡Oh, Lalitā! ¡Oh, hijo de Nanda Mahārāja! ¿Dónde están? ¿Están sentados bajo los árboles kalpa-vṛkṣa de Śhrī Govardhana? ¿Están deambulando por los bosques a orillas del Kālindī?”. Ellos se lamentaban continuamente con sentimientos de gran separación mientras vagaban por toda Vraja-maṇḍala. Yo adoro a los Gosvāmīs Śhrī Rūpa, Sanātana, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa, Raghunātha dāsa, Jīva y Gopāla Bhaṭṭa.

IDX.en_translation:
The groves, the ponds, the lakes, Govardhana Hill, the trees and creepers, the River Yamunā—all of Vṛndāvana. 

Everything there is made of spiritual jewels and gems; there is not even a trace of material illusion there. 

The soul who becomes perfect by the grace of the gopīs sees everything with eyes cleansed by pure love and with great eagerness. 

An externally oriented person, with material vision, sees only a covering of illusion. 

There is no material place or time there; rather, the spiritual dimension of place and time is beautifully manifest. 

The supremely merciful Lord Kṛṣṇa, showing mercy to the living entities, manifested everything Himself by His descent. 

The soul bound by illusion goes there constantly, but without the Lord’s mercy, he cannot see anything. 

The soul whose past actions are exhausted obtains the association of the saintly. Only such a person can truly see the forest of Vraja. 

An externally oriented soul cannot remain there; the material illusion quickly pulls them away. 

That soul who goes to the holy land of Vraja even once gradually accumulates strong spiritual merit. 

When such merit becomes strong, the association of the saintly occurs. All the scriptures declare that the attainment of Vraja comes through the association of the saintly.

IDX.en_translation:
Anointed with vermilion, She whose golden lotus-like beauty defeats all pride. She whose fragrance, surpassing the scent of a blossoming lotus, proclaims Her fame. She who fulfills all the desires of the son of the king of the cowherds. May that Rādhā, the beloved of Kṛṣṇa, grant me service to Her lotus feet. 

She whose colorful silken garments defeat the luster of sapphire. She is a garden of blossoming flowers for Kṛṣṇa, the maddened bee, to sport in. Rādhā, who is like the sun for the eternal union with Kṛṣṇa. May She grant me service to Her lotus feet. 

Her tenderness surpasses the beauty of young sprouts. She whose cool form is served by the moon, sandalwood, lotus, and camphor. She who relieves the fever of the Lord of the cowherds by Her touch. May She grant me service to Her lotus feet. 

Even the goddess of fortune, who is worshiped by all the worlds, is not equal to Her in the wealth of beauty, youth, and other qualities. In character, affection, and pastimes, She is supreme. May She grant me service to Her lotus feet. 

She is skilled in all the excellent arts of the rāsa dance, singing, and joking. Adorned with the charming beauty of love, attire, and all good qualities. She who is superior even to all the young gopīs of the world. May She grant me service to Her lotus feet. 

Always endowed with the wealth of ever-new beauty, sports, and Kṛṣṇa’s moods, She makes the young gopīs tremble in their bond of love for Him. She is perfectly absorbed in the form, attire, and pastimes of Kṛṣṇa. May She grant me service to Her lotus feet. 

Filled with emotions like perspiration, trembling, thrills of ecstasy, and a choked voice, She is adorned with the ornaments of various moods like indignation, joy, and charm. She bestows a multitude of jeweled ornaments that please Kṛṣṇa’s eyes. May She grant me service to Her lotus feet. 

She who is pleased by the multitude of emotions like extreme humility and restlessness, which arise from even a half-moment’s separation from Kṛṣṇa. She who becomes entirely perfect upon obtaining Kṛṣṇa’s company. May She grant me service to Her lotus feet. 

He who praises the beloved of Kṛṣṇa with these eight verses—She who is difficult for even the greatest goddesses to behold—is quickly made a recipient of the nectar of service to Her feet by Her, making all Her companions joyful.

El color de Su cuerpo destruye el orgullo de una flor de loto dorada teñida con kuṅkuma. Su fragancia corporal agravia la fama de un aromático loto mezclado con azafrán. Ella satisface todos los deseos del pastorcillo príncipe de Vraja. Que esa Śhrīmatī Rādhikā me bendiga siempre con el servicio de Sus pies de loto. 

Su colorido sari de seda derrota el esplendor del coral. Ella es un jardín radiante de flores para el lúdico placer del enloquecido abejorro Śhrī Kṛṣṇa. Adora al dios del sol para obtener eternamente la asociación de Śhrī Kṛṣṇa. Que esa Śhrīmatī Rādhikā me bendiga siempre con el servicio de Sus pies de loto. 

La inigualable suavidad de Su cuerpo humilla la fama de un ramillete de delicadas flores. La frescura de Su cuerpo es adorada por la luna, la pasta de sándalo y el alcanfor. Su contacto disipa el calor de los deseos amorosos de gopī-jana-vallabha Śhrī Kṛṣṇa. Que esa Śhrīmatī Rādhikā me bendiga siempre con el servicio de Sus pies de loto. 

Es experta en todas las hermosas artes del rāsa-līlā, como danzar, cantar y bromear; está decorada con todas las virtudes divinas, como un prema sobrenatural, una belleza encantadora y un maravilloso atuendo. Es superior a todas las demás pastorcillas de Vraja. Que esa Śhrīmatī Rādhikā me bendiga siempre con el servicio de Sus pies de loto. 

Es experta en todas las hermosas artes del rāsa-līlā, como danzar, cantar y bromear; está decorada con todas las virtudes divinas, como un prema sobrenatural, una belleza encantadora y un maravilloso atuendo. Es superior a todas las demás pastorcillas de Vraja. Que esa Śhrīmatī Rādhikā me bendiga siempre con el servicio de Sus pies de loto. 

Con Su lozana belleza, Su jovialidad y Sus sentimientos por Kṛṣṇa, Ella hace que todas las jóvenes doncellas, que están cautivadas por anurāga por Kṛṣṇa, tiemblen. Ella está inmersa en perpetuo trance en la belleza, el atuendo y los gozosos pasatiempos de Śhrī Kṛṣṇa. Que esa Śhrīmatī Rādhikā me bendiga siempre con el servicio de Sus pies de loto. 

Está adornada con [sāttvika-bhāvas como] transpiración, temblor, erizamiento de los vellos, lágrimas y voz trémula, y decorada con bhāvas como indignación, dicha y contrariedad, y lleva espléndidos ornamentos de joyas que deleitan los ojos de Śhrī Kṛṣṇa. Que esa Śhrīmatī Rādhikā me bendiga siempre con el servicio de Sus pies de loto. 

Cuando está separada de Śhrī Kṛṣṇa aunque sea por un instante, se siente mortificada por un creciente sentimiento de humildad y una terrible ansiedad, pero al encontrarse con Kṛṣṇa gracias a los intensos esfuerzos de alguno de Sus mensajeros, toda Su angustia mental desaparece. Que esa Śhrīmatī Rādhikā me bendiga siempre con el servicio de Sus pies de loto. 

Śhrīmatī Rādhikā, cuyo darśhana raramente obtienen ni siquiera Pārvatī-devī y otras diosas, proporciona un gran placer a Sus sakhīs. Ella misma se llena de euforia al reunirse con Śhrī Kṛṣṇa, para quien es la amante más querida. Ella hace que la persona que Le ora cantando este aṣṭaka se vuelva rápidamente destinataria del néctar de Su servicio.

Kuvera Paṇḍita was greatly delighted to see the face of his son. He performed the birth rituals as prescribed by religious duty, and his happiness increased manifold. 

The child was endowed with all auspicious markings and a golden complexion. He had the beauty of a lotus, and His graceful arms reached down to His knees, captivating the minds of all people. 

He had a deep navel, was supremely beautiful, and His eyes surpassed the beauty of lotus flowers. His feet were reddish, and His toenails were like mirrors, conquering the luster of millions of moons and jewels. 

Everyone was astonished to see these charming signs of a Great Personality, and they felt that through Him, the world would be delivered. 

All the women of the town, beholding the child’s face, floated in an ocean of bliss. Their hearts could not contain their joy, and they went again and again to gaze at Him without blinking. 

They jokingly said to His mother, “Who can describe the limit of the fortune of one who has such a son? Who in the world is equal to her?” 

All the women spoke with voices choked with emotion, understanding the reason for the world’s deliverance. This is the hope of Vaiṣṇava Dāsa.

O Mādhava, I have one great plea! Offering sacred Tulasi leaves and sesame seeds, I have surrendered my body. Knowing my surrender, please do not abandon me. 

When You consider my faults, You will not find a trace of good quality. You are the Lord of the universe and are known as its Lord. I, though insignificant, am not outside this world. 

Whether I am born as a human, animal, bird, insect, or worm, due to the consequences of my actions—coming and going again and again—may my mind always remain in Your association. 

Vidyāpati says: I am extremely distressed to cross this ocean of material existence. Taking shelter of Your lotus feet, please grant me Your protection for a moment, O friend of the distressed.

Cuando consideres mi petición, no hallarás más que faltas y ni una sola buena cualidad. Eres famoso en el mundo entero como Jagannātha (el Señor del Universo); por consiguiente, incluso alguien tan despreciable como yo no está fuera de Tu consideración. 

Impelido por mi karma, tal vez nazca como humano, ave, gusano, insecto o cualquier otro animal. Cosechando una y otra vez las consecuencias de mis actos, voy rodando de un destino a otro. Sea como sea, que permanezca siempre absorto en Ti. 

Completamente abatido, Vidyāpati suplica: “En mi travesía por este océano de la existencia material, las tiernas hojas de Tus pies son mi único refugio. Concédeme una partícula de Tu gracia, oh amigo de los caídos”.

IDX.en_translation:
The permanent sentiment of conjugal love finds its manifestation in what I will now describe; listen attentively: complaint, the object of desire, the two aspects of the sense of relationship, His specific qualities, and similes. 

Taking refuge in one’s inherent nature, love descends into the heart, nurturing the conjugal sentiment. For others, these six factors become the cause of their love, but the cowherd girls of Vraja do not view it this way. 

Their spontaneous love, along with Their sense of relationship, always keeps them capable of selfless service. For them, there is no other endeavor except the service of Kṛṣṇa; there is never any attempt for Their own happiness. 

That love matures and attains the stage of the highest ecstatic love, to which there is no equal attainment. Such a desire for union, which is entirely wonderful and astonishing, I find no words to describe.

For those with little piety, faith in mahā-prasāda, Govinda, nāma-brahma, or a Vaiṣṇava never arises. 

O brother! 

The body is a net of ignorance, and the material senses within it are like a deadly snake, throwing the soul into the ocean of material enjoyment. Among them, the tongue is most greedy and wicked-minded; conquering it is very difficult in this material world. 

Kṛṣṇa is very merciful; to help us conquer the tongue, O brother, He has given us His own prasāda. Accept that nectar-like food, sing the glories of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, and with love, call out Caitanya-Nitāi.

Este cuerpo material es una red de ignorancia y sus sentidos inertes son la causa de su perdición, pues arrojan al alma al océano del disfrute material. De todos los sentidos, la lengua es el más tortuoso y voraz; es muy difícil conquistarla en este mundo. 

Kṛṣṇa es tan misericordioso, que nos da los remanentes de Su propia comida para ayudarnos a conquistar la lengua. ¡Oh, hermanos! Honren estos alimentos llenos de néctar, canten las glorias de Rādhā y Kṛṣṇa, e invoquen con prema: “¡Chaitanya! ¡Nitāi!” 

¡Invoca con el corazón lleno de amor! Al misericordioso Nitāi y al compasivo Chaitanya. ¡Invócalos con el corazón lleno de amor! Y canta: hare kṛṣṇa hare kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa hare hare, hare rāma hare rāma rāma rāma hare hare.

She is a jewel of the highest ecstatic love, whose transcendental form is manifested, glorious, and adorned as the chief of the companions. She is a stream of nectar of compassion, youth, and beauty, in which she—the chaste lady who conquers the goddess of fortune—is bathed. 

Her silken garment is shyness, her beauty is the essence of saffron, and her body is adorned with musk. Trembling, tears, thrills of ecstasy, paralysis, perspiration, a faltering voice, and madness are her nine jewels. 

Adorned with a beautiful flower garland of twenty-five qualities, her silken dress is a mood of both patience and impatience. Her braided hair conceals her pique, she shines with the mark of good fortune, and the glory of Kṛṣṇa’s names is the delight of her ears. 

Her lips are red with the betel of attachment, her clear eyeliner is her charming crookedness, and she is playful, perfumed with the camphor of smiles. In the inner chambers of fame and glory, she shines upon the throne of pride, wearing the swaying garland of the uniqueness of love. 

Her blouse of loving anger covers her breasts; she conquers the moon and is the melody of the lute. Playfully placing her lotus hands on the shoulders of two companions, she distributes the nectar of Kṛṣṇa. 

Such feet of Rādhikā are your great wealth; with a blade of grass in my teeth, I beg at your feet. This humble Bhaktivinoda asks for a particle of the nectar of service to Rādhā. O Rūpa, O Raghunātha! Please give it to him.

O my mind! Remain conscious and do not forget the wealth of pure and simple truth. Otherwise, under the sway of illusion, you will eventually have to weep eternally. 

In a pure soul there is no materialism, brother; understand this clearly. The pure soul is naturally happy in Vṛndāvana. When he worships Kṛṣṇa-candra, he drowns in joy and relishes sweet mellows at every moment. 

Within his material body he practices devotion and detachment from worldly knowledge; the journey of his body is conducted in a religious mood. Whether he lives at home or in the forest, he calls out “Kṛṣṇa!” with a single mind. 

This indeed is called simple worship—with a pure mind, the one way to attain Kṛṣṇa. Whoever abandons this and imposes something artificial only perishes; he performs no true worship. 

This is the belief of Cānd Bāula. Choṭa Haridāsa went but a little astray, yet by the decree of the Lord, he became distant and could no longer attain His feet.

O mind! Speak the topics of Gaura. Gaura’s Name is the abode of nectar, the giver of the form of love. 

Gaura in sleep, Gaura in dreams, Gaura is the star of the eye. Gaura in life, Gaura in death, Gaura is the necklace of the neck. 

Keeping Gaurāṅga within my heart, I will remain sitting in solitude. With the desire of the mind, I will place that Moon of Beauty eye to eye. 

Without Gaura, I do not survive in life; I have made Gaura the essence. Let life go saying “Gaura”; I will not want anything else. 

Gaura’s gait, Gaura’s form, the smile on Gaura’s face; Gaura’s love, Gaura’s form—remained entered in my heart. 

Gaura is Dharma, Gaura is Karma, Gaura is the essence of the Vedas. At Gaura’s feet I have offered my life; Gaura will take me across. 

He in whose heart the Sound of Gaura and the Wealth of Gaura awaken—Narahari Dāsa, the servant of His servant’s servant, begs for shelter at the feet.
IDX.es_translation:
¡Oh, mente! Habla solo de Gaura. El nombre de Gaura es la morada del néctar. Ese nombre personifica y otorga amor divino. 

Cuando duermo, Gaura y cuando sueño, Gaura. Gaura es la estrella de mis ojos. En la vida, Gaura y en el momento de la muerte, Gaura. Gaura es un collar sumamente valioso. 

Llevando a Gaura en el corazón, me sentaré en un lugar apartado y contemplaré fijamente Su forma de luna, satisfaciendo así mi deseo interno. 

Sin Gaura no puedo vivir. Él es ahora la esencia de mi existencia. Que mi vida transcurra cantando el nombre de Gaura. No deseo ninguna otra cosa. 

El movimiento de Gaura, la presencia de Gaura, el sonriente rostro de Gaura, el amor de Gaura y la forma de Gaura ―que todo ello penetre en mi corazón. 

Gaura es mi dharma, Gaura es (el objeto de) mi karma y Gaura es la esencia de los Vedas. Entrego mi vida a los pies de loto de Gaura. Gaura me conducirá al otro lado (del océano de la existencia material). 

Narahari suplica que se le conceda el refugio de los pies del sirviente del sirviente de la persona en cuyo corazón se ha manifestado el sonido ‘Gaura’ y el teroso de Gaura.

IDX.verses: maṅgala śhrī guru-gaura maṅgala mūrati maṅgala śhrī rādhā-kṛṣṇa-yugala-pirīti maṅgala niśhānta-līlā maṅgala udaye aṅgala ārati jāge bhakata-hṛdaye tomāra nidrāya jīva nidrita dharāya tava jāgaraṇe viśhva jāgarita haya śhubha dṛṣṭi karo ebe (prabhu) jagatera prati jāguka hṛdaye sumaṅgalā rati mayūra-śhukādi sāri kato pikarāja maṅgala jāgara-hetu koricḣe virāja sumadhura dhvani kare yato śhākhī-gaṇa maṅgala śhravaṇe bāje madhura kūjana kusumita sarovare kamala-hillola maṅgala saurabha bahe pavana-kallola jhāṅjhara kāṅsara ghaṇṭā śhaṅkha karatāla maṅgala mṛdaṅga bāje parama rasāla maṅgala ārati kare bhakatera gaṇa abhāgā keśhava kare nāma-saṅkīrtana (śhrī keśhava dāsa kare nāma-saṅkīrtana)
IDX.en_translation:
Glories to the auspicious forms of Śrī Guru and Gaura, and all glories to Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa’s auspicious amorous love.

All glories to Their auspicious niśānta-līlā which heralds the end of night and Their auspicious awakening, bringing auspiciousness to all! Glories to maṅgala-ārati, which awakens a sfūrti of that niśānta-līlā within the devotees’ hearts!

While You sleep, the jīvas lie sleeping deep in their ignorance, but upon Your rising, the whole world awakens! <highlight>[Meaning, if You manifest in their hearts, then all tattva and all siddhānta will be revealed to them.]</highlight>

(Prabhu!) Shower Your kind glance upon the world now. Awaken in my heart that most auspicious rati.

The peacocks, parrots, śuka, sāri, and cuckoos (by Vṛndā-devī’s order) are singing the reasons for Your auspicious awakening.

Sitting on the branches of the trees, all the birds sing their supremely sweet morning melodies which resound throughout the forest. Those sweet, soft, auspicious sounds come and grace everyone!

In the pond, which is filled with many varieties of flowers, the lotuses sway in the center. The breezes spread their auspicious aromas in all directions, bringing pure delight and joy to all.

Large cymbals, gongs, bells, conches, karatālas and auspicious mṛdaṅgas play the supreme rasa.

Performing maṅgala ārati within the company of devotees, the unfortunate Keśava (the servants of Srī Keśava) sings nāma-saṅkīrtana.
IDX.es_translation:
Toda gloria a las auspiciosas formas de śhrī guru y Śhrī Gaura. Toda gloria al divino amor conyugal de Śhrī Śhrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa. 

Toda gloria a Su niśhānta-līlā, que hace surgir todo lo auspicioso. Toda gloria a Su ceremonia de arati, que se despierta en el corazón de los devotos. 

Mientras Ustedes duermen, las jīvas permanecen dormidas en este mundo, pero cuando se levantan, el mundo entero despierta. 

[¡Oh, Señor!] Dirige Tu misericordiosa mirada al mundo ahora. Que este auspicioso rati se despierte en mi corazón. 

Multitud de pavos reales, loros, cuclillos y otras aves se hallan presentes para anunciar Su auspicioso despertar. 

Los pájaros en las ramas entonan dulcísimas melodías. Su dulce piar resuena de un modo muy auspicioso. 

En un estanque repleto de una gran variedad de flores, los lotos se balancean de un lado a otro, y suaves y ondeantes brisas esparcen su auspiciosa fragancia por doquier. 

Grandes címbalos, gongs, campanas, caracolas, karatālas y auspiciosas mṛdaṅgas resuenan dulcemente. 

Mientras los devotos realizan maṅgala-ārati, este desafortunado Keśhava (el sirviente de Śhrī Keśhava) canta nāma-saṅkīrtana.

IDX.translation_intro: extended prayers 2
IDX.en_translation:
I offer my obeisances to the lotus feet of my Spiritual Master, to the preceptors, and to the Vaiṣṇavas; to Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī with his elder brother (Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī), to Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī, along with Śrīla Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī and his associates. 

I offer obeisances to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Deva, along with Śrī Advaita Āchārya, Śrī Nityānanda Avadhūta, and His associates; and to the lotus feet of Śrī Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, accompanied by Śrīmatī Lalitā-devī, Śrīmatī Viśākhā-devī, and their associates. 

[Samaṣṭigata Praṇāma] 
I offer my obeisances time and again unto Śrī Gurudeva, Śrī Gauracandra, Śrīmatī Rādhikā, Her associates and Her abode Śrī Vṛndāvana-dhāma, to Śrī Kṛṣṇa and His devotees, and to all Vaiṣṇavas. 

[Śrī Guru Praṇāma] 
I offer my respectful obeisances unto my Spiritual Master, who opened my eyes, which were blinded by the darkness of ignorance, with the torchlight of knowledge. 

[Śrīla Nārāyaṇa Praṇāma] 
I offer praṇāma to oṁ viṣṇupāda Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja, who is very dear to Śrīmatī Rādhikā. 

O Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja, you are expert in describing kṛṣṇa-līlā and are fully endowed with the qualities of magnanimity and sweetness. You are the best of all great souls. I bow my head to you. 

Tridaṇḍī-sannyāsī Śrīla Nārāyaṇa Mahārāja, the crown-jewel of devotees, always keeps in his heart the lotus feet of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, especially when Kṛṣṇa serves Śrīmatī Rādhikā. He deeply meditates on Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and the internal reasons for His descent. I bow down to the lotus feet of Śrīla Nārāyaṇa Mahārāja, who possesses innumerable transcendental qualities. 

[Śrī Nārāyaṇa Vandanā] 
I offer obeisances to the best of Gurus, the excellent follower of Rūpa, who is a connoisseur of the mellows of Vraja—to that Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja, who is surrendered. 

I offer obeisances to the lotus feet of the Guru, who is the beloved of the Lord on earth, who bestows Rūpānuga-bhakti, the embodiment of mercy, Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja. 

Who always bestows service in the delightful Seva-kuñja in Vraja, at Govardhana Hill, and at Rādhā-kuṇḍa, which is full of the bliss of rasa. 

I offer obeisances to that Guru named Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja, the beloved of the Lord, by the mere remembrance of whose feet Dāmodara becomes pleased. 

[Śrīla Vāmana Vandanā] 
I offer praṇāma to oṁ viṣṇupāda Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktivedānta Vāmana Gosvāmī Mahārāja, who is most dear to Śrī Keśava (alternately: Śrī Śrīmad Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja) 

Obeisances to the servant of the saintly, the beloved of the saintly on earth, the friend of the devotees, known as “Rādhānātha-vallabha”. 

Most dear to Śrīla Saccidānanda Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, Śrīla Narottama Dāsa Ṭhākura, and Narahari Sarakāra Ṭhākura; the well-wisher of Śrī Vedānta, the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, and the Six Gosvāmīs. 

Dear to the abode of Māyāpura, the servant of the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇavas, more humble than a blade of grass—the beautiful personality, Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Vāmana Gosvāmī Mahārāja. 

[Śrīla Svāmī Vandanā] 
I offer my respectful obeisances unto His Divine Grace A.C. Bhaktivedānta Svāmī Prabhupāda, who is very dear to Lord Kṛṣṇa on this earth, having taken shelter at His lotus feet. 

Our respectful obeisances are unto you, O spiritual master, servant of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Gosvāmī Prabhupāda. You are kindly preaching the message of Lord Caitanyadeva and delivering the Western countries, which are filled with impersonalism and voidism. 

[Śrīla Keśava Vandanā] 
I offer my respectful obeisances unto Viṣṇupāda Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktiprajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī, who is like a lion among the Āchāryas. 

Whose character is superhuman, the protector of those who take shelter of him, always distressed by the suffering of the jīvas, the giver of the Name and Love. 

The embodiment of shelter in Gaura, whose only desire is Kṛṣṇa, the excellent follower of Rūpa, whose form is like Vinoda. 

The intimate associate of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Gosvāmī Prabhupāda, possessor of all good qualities, the destroyer of the darkness of Māyāvāda, the knower of the meaning of Vedānta. 

[Śrīla Prabhupāda Vandanā] 
I offer my respectful obeisances unto His Divine Grace Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Gosvāmī Prabhupāda, who is very dear to Lord Kṛṣṇa on this earth, having taken shelter at His lotus feet. 

I offer my respectful obeisances to Śrī Vārṣabhānavī-devī-dayita Dāsa, who is favored by Śrīmatī Rādhā-rāṇī and who is the ocean of transcendental mercy and the deliverer of the science of Kṛṣṇa. 

I offer my respectful obeisances unto you, the personified energy of Śrī Caitanya’s mercy, who deliver devotional service which is enriched with conjugal love of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, coming exactly in the line of revelation of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī. 

I offer my respectful obeisances unto you, who are the personified teachings of Lord Caitanya. You are the deliverer of the fallen souls. You do not tolerate any statement which is against the teachings of devotional service enunciated by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī. 

[Śrīla Gaura-kiśora Vandanā] 
I offer my respectful obeisances unto Śrīla Gaura-kiśora Dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja, who is renunciation personified and always merged in the ocean of the mellow of separation from Kṛṣṇa. 

[Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Vandanā] 
I offer my respectful obeisances unto Śrīla Saccidānanda Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, who is the personification of the energy of Lord Caitanya and the best of the followers of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī. 

[Śrīla Jagannātha Vandanā] 
Obeisances to you, Śrīla Jagannātha Dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja, the Emperor of the Vaiṣṇavas, dear to the saintly, who indicated the place of Gaura’s appearance. 

Indeed, Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, whose dear friend was Svarūpa Dāmodara, was the exact replica of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, and he was very, very dear to the Lord. Being the embodiment of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu’s ecstatic love, Rūpa Gosvāmī was naturally very beautiful. He very carefully followed the principles enunciated by the Lord, and he was a competent person to explain properly the pastimes of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu expanded His mercy to Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī just so he could render service by writing transcendental literatures. 

[Śrī Vaiṣṇava Vandanā] 
I offer my respectful obeisances unto all the Vaiṣṇava devotees of the Lord. They are just like desire trees who can fulfill the desires of everyone, and they are oceans of mercy and the purifiers of the fallen souls. 

[Śrī Pañca-tattva Praṇāma] 
I offer my obeisances unto the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa, who appears in the form of a devotee (Lord Caitanya), as His expansion (Lord Nityānanda), His incarnation (Advaita Āchārya), His internal potency (Gadādhara), and His marginal potency (Śrīvāsa). 

[Śrī Nityānanda Praṇāma] 
May Śrī Nityānanda Rāma be the object of my constant remembrance. Saṅkarṣaṇa, Śeṣa Nāga and the Viṣṇus who lie on the Kāraṇa Ocean, Garbha Ocean, and ocean of milk are His plenary portions and the portions of His plenary portions. 

I offer praṇāma unto Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu who bestows the bliss of divine love, who eliminates the filth of the age of Kali, and who is the master of Jāhnavā-devī. 

[Śrī Gaurāṅga Praṇāma] 
Obeisances to the most munificent incarnation, who bestows love of Kṛṣṇa—to Kṛṣṇa Himself, who has assumed the name Kṛṣṇa Caitanya and a golden complexion. 

[Śrī Gaura-Nityānanda Vandanā] I worship the incarnations of mercy, Śrī Gaura-Nityānanda, whose arms extend to Their knees, whose complexions are dazzling, who inaugurated the saṅkīrtana movement, whose eyes are large like lotus petals, who nourish the entire universe, who are the best of brāhmaṇas, who protect the yuga-dharma, and who are engaged in performing pleasing activities for the welfare of the world. <highlight>(Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata, Ādi-khaṇḍa 1.1)</highlight> 

[Śrī Śukadeva Praṇāma] 
I offer obeisances to Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmī, who can enter the hearts of all living entities. When he left home without undergoing the purificatory processes such as accepting the sacred thread, his father Vyāsa cried out, “Oh my son!” As if they were absorbed in that same feeling of separation, only the trees echoed in response to his call. 

[Śrī Kṛṣṇa Praṇāma] 
O my dear Kṛṣṇa, ocean of mercy, You are the friend of the distressed and the source of creation. You are the master of the cowherd men and the lover of the gopīs, especially Rādhā-rāṇī. I offer my respectful obeisances unto You. 

“Oh Shyāmasundara! Oh You whose head is adorned with peacock feathers! Your face is always graced with a playful smile, Your flute-playing is enchanting, and You are expert in relishing rasa with Śrīmati Rādhika. Because You are an ocean of mercy, I am appealing to You to please make me a kinkari [maidservant] at the lotus feet of Your beloved.” 
(Śrī Rādhā Prārthanā 2—Śrī Vitthalacharya) 

[Śrī Rādhā Praṇāma] 
Reverential obeisances unto you, O Rādhā, whose complexion is like molten gold and who are the Queen of Vṛndāvana. You are the daughter of King Vṛṣabhānu, and You are very dear to Lord Kṛṣṇa. 

O Svāminī Śrī Rādhe, I am Yours, I am Yours! I cannot live without You! Knowing this, please bestow the shelter of Your lotus feet. 

[Sambandha-adhideva Praṇāma] 
Glory to the all-merciful Rādhā and Madana-mohana! They are the only shelter of my depraved and crippled intelligence. Their lotus feet are my everything. 

[Abhidheya-adhideva Praṇāma] 
In a temple of jewels in Vṛndāvana, underneath a desire tree, Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Govinda, served by Their most confidential associates, sit upon an effulgent throne. I offer my humble obeisances unto Them. 

[Prayojana-adhideva Praṇāma] 
Śrī Śrīla Gopīnātha, who originated the transcendental mellow of the rāsa dance, stands on the shore in Vaṁśīvaṭa and attracts the attention of the cowherd damsels with the sound of His celebrated flute. May they all confer upon us their benediction. 

[Śrī Tulasī Praṇāma] 
I offer my repeated obeisances unto Vṛndā, Tulasī-devī, who is very dear to Lord Keśava. O goddess, you bestow devotional service to Kṛṣṇa and you possess the highest truth. 

[Śrī Vṛndā-devī] Devoid of devotion and guilty of committing unlimited offences, I am being tossed about in the ocean of material existence by the turbulent waves of lust, anger, greed and so forth. Therefore, O merciful Vṛndā-devī, I take shelter of you and offer obeisances unto your lotus feet. 

[Śrī Paurṇamāsī] Śrī Paurṇamāsī is completely adept at arranging the most elevated varieties of enjoyment for the master of Śrī Rādhā. Her lotus feet are worshiped by the Vrajavāsīs. Due to possessing all good qualities, beginning with kindness, she is worshipful for the entire universe. I bow my head and offer praṇāma unto that Śrī Paurṇamāsī-devī. 

[Śrī Gopīśvara-mahādeva] O protector of the land of Vṛndāvana, O husband of Umā, O Somamauli, you who carry the moon on your head! O you who are worshiped by Sanandana, Sanātana, and Nārada! O Gopeśvara, please bestow upon me unconditional prema for the lotus feet of Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, who perform loving pastimes in Vraja. 

[Śrī Yamunā-devī] Yamunā-devī is a reservoir of prema for Śrī Nanda-nandana, and the sun of spiritual bliss. Her body is made of liquid transcendence, she destroys all sins, and brings auspiciousness to the world. May that Yamunā-devī, daughter of the Sun-god, purify our bodies. 

[Śrī Pañca-tattva] 
Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, Prabhu Nityānanda, Śrī Advaita, Gadādhara, Śrīvāsa and all the devotees of Lord Gaura. 

[Mahā-mantra] 
Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa, Hare Hare; Hare Rāma, Hare Rāma, Rāma Rāma, Hare Hare.

Ofrezco praṇāma a los pies de loto de mis gurus (tanto el śhrī dīksā-guru como el śhikṣā-guru), al guru-varga (nuestra sucesión discipular) y a todos los demás vaiṣṇavas, a Śhrī Rūpa Gosvāmī, a su hermano mayor Śhrī Sanātana Gosvāmī, a Śhrī Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī, a Jīva Gosvāmī. 

 Y sus asociados, a Śhrī Advaita Āchārya, al avadhūta Nityānanda Prabhu, a Śhrī Kṛṣṇa Chaitanya Mahāprabhu y Sus asociados, y a los pies de loto de Śhrī Rādhā y Kṛṣṇa acompañados por Śhrī Lalitā y Viśhākhā y a todas las demás sakhīs. 

[Samaṣṭigata Praṇāma] 
Ofrezco mis reverencias una y otra vez a Śhrī Gurudeva, a Śhrī Gaurachandra, a Śhrīmatī Rādhikā, a Sus compañeras y a Su morada, Śhrī Vṛndāvana-dhāma, a Śhrī Kṛṣṇa y a Sus devotos, y a todos los vaiṣṇavas. 

[Śhrī Guru Praṇāma] 
Estoy cegado por la oscuridad de la ignorancia, pero śhrī guru me abrió misericordiosamente los ojos untándolos con el bálsamo del conocimiento divino. Yo ofrezco praṇāma a śhrī gurudeva. 

[Śhrīla Nārāyaṇa Praṇāma] 
Ofrezco praṇāma a oṁ viṣṇupāda Śhrī Śhrīmad Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Mahārāja, que Le es muy querido a Śhrīmatī Rādhikā. 

¡Oh, Śhrīla Nārāyaṇa Mahārāja! Tú es experto describiendo el kṛṣṇa-līlā, estás dotado con las cualidades de la magnanimidad y la dulzura, y eres el mejor entre las grandes almas. Yo inclino mi cabeza ante ti. 

Ese tridaṇḍī-sannyāsī, el mejor entre todos los bhaktas, atesora en su corazón los pies de loto de Rādhā y Kṛṣṇa y está siempre meditando en la esencia de los nectáreos līlās de Śhrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu. ¡Oh Śhrīla Nārāyaṇa Mahārāja!, yo me refugio en tus pies de loto. 

[Śhrī Nārāyaṇa Vandanā] 
Ofrezco mis reverencias al mejor de los Gurus, el excelente discípulo de Rūpa, conocedor de las dulzuras de Vraja: a ese Śhrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja, quien se ha entregado por completo. 

Ofrezco mis reverencias a los pies de loto de Guru, quien es el amado del Señor en la Tierra, quien otorga la Rūpānuga-bhakti, la encarnación de la misericordia, Śhrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja. 

Quien siempre presta servicio en el encantador Seva-kuñja de Vraja, en la colina de Govardhana y en Rādhā-kuṇḍa, que está lleno de la dicha del rasa. 

Ofrezco mis reverencias a ese Guru llamado Śhrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja, el amado del Señor, cuyo mero recuerdo de sus pies complace a Dāmodara. 

[Śhrīla Vāmana Vandanā] 
Le ofrezco mi praṇāma a oṁ viṣṇupāda Śhrī Śhrīmad Bhaktivedānta Vāmana Gosvāmī Mahārāja, quien es muy querido por Śhrī Keśhava (alternativamente: Śhrī Śhrīmad Bhakti Prajñāna Keśhava Gosvāmī Mahārāja) 

Reverencias al servidor de los santos, al amado de los santos en la tierra, al amigo de los devotos, conocido como “Rādhānātha-vallabha”. 

El más querido por Śhrīla Saccidānanda Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, Śhrīla Narottama Dāsa Ṭhākura y Narahari Sarakāra Ṭhākura; el benefactor del Śhrī Vedānta, el Śhrīmad-Bhāgavatam y los Seis Gosvāmīs. 

Querido en la morada de Māyāpura, el servidor de los Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇavas, más humilde que una brizna de hierba: la hermosa personalidad, Śhrīla Bhaktivedānta Vāmana Gosvāmī Mahārāja. 

[Śhrīla Svāmī Vandanā] 
Ofrezco praṇāma a oṁ viṣṇupāda Śhrī Śhrīmad Bhaktivedānta Svāmī Mahārāja (Śhrīla Prabhupāda), que Le es muy querido a Kṛṣṇa en este mundo. 

Mis respetuosas reverencias a ti, oh sirviente de Sarasvatī Gosvāmī. Tú predicas el mensaje de Śhrī Gaurāṅga y de ese modo liberas a los países occidentales que están llenos de impersonalismo y nihilismo. 

[Śhrīla Keśhava Vandanā] 
Yo ofrezco praṇāma al āchārya semejante a un león, oṁ viṣṇupāda Śhrī Śhrīmad Bhakti Prajñāna Keśhava Gosvāmī Mahārāja. 

Su carácter y actividades son trascendentales a las modalidades de la naturaleza, y nutre y protege a quienes se refugian en él. Él está siempre afligido al ver el sufrimiento de las entidades vivientes, y otorga amor por śhrī nāma. 

La encarnación del refugio en Gaura, cuyo único deseo es Kṛṣṇa, el excelente discípulo de Rūpa, cuya forma es como la de Vinoda. 

El asociado íntimo de Śhrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Gosvāmī Prabhupāda, poseedor de todas las buenas cualidades, el destructor de la oscuridad del Māyāvāda, el conocedor del significado del Vedānta. 

[Śhrīla Prabhupāda Vandanā] 
Ofrezco praṇāma a oṁ viṣṇupāda Śhrī Śhrīmad Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Gosvāmī Ṭhākura Prabhupāda, que Le es sumamente querido a Kṛṣṇa en este mundo. 

Ofezco praṇāma a Śhrī Vārṣabhānavī-dayita dāsa, que es la manifestación de un océano de miseriordia y que otorga el conocimiento de nuestra relación eterna con Śhrī Kṛṣṇa. 

¡Oh, Śhrīla Sarasvatī Ṭhākura! Tú otorgas śhrī rūpānuga- bhakti enriquecido con ujjvala-mādhurya-prema. Tú eres la personificación de la misericordia de Śhrī Gaurāṅga. Yo te ofrezco praṇāma. 

Mis reverencias a ti, que eres la personificación de las enseñanzas de Śhrī Gaurāṅga. Tú liberas a las almas caídas y aniquilas la oscuridad que surge de los conceptos erróneos que se oponen a los preceptos enunciados por Śhrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī. 

[Śhrīla Gaura-kiśhora Vandanā] 
Ofrezco praṇāma a Śhrī Gaura-kiśhora dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja, que es la personificación de la renuncia y un océano de vipralambha-rasa. 

[Śhrīla Bhaktivinoda Vandanā] 
Yo te ofrezco praṇāma, Śhrīla Sacchidānanda Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, el rūpānuga supremo y la personificación de la śhakti de Śhrī Gaurāṅga (Gadādhara Paṇḍita). 

[Śhrīla Jagannātha Vandanā] 
Tú indicaste el lugar de aparición de Śhrī Gaurāṅga y le eres muy querido a todos los devotos santos. ¡Oh, Śhrīla Jagannātha dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja, líder de los vaiṣṇavas, yo te ofrezco praṇāma. 

De hecho, Śhrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, cuyo querido amigo era Svarūpa Dāmodara, era la réplica exacta de Śhrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu, y era muy, muy querido por el Señor. Al ser la encarnación del amor extático de Śhrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu, Rūpa Gosvāmī era, naturalmente, muy hermoso. Seguía con mucho cuidado los principios enunciados por el Señor, y era una persona competente para explicar adecuadamente los pasatiempos del Señor Kṛṣṇa. Śhrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu extendió Su misericordia a Śhrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī precisamente para que pudiera prestar servicio escribiendo obras literarias trascendentales. 

[Śhrī Vaiṣṇava Vandanā] 
Ofrezco praṇāma una y otra vez a los vaiṣṇavas, que son los salvadores de los caídos. Ellos son como árboles de los deseos y océanos de misericordia. 

[Śhrī Pañcha-tattva Praṇāma] 
Ofrezco mis reverencias al Señor Supremo Kṛṣṇa, quien se manifiesta en la forma de un devoto (el Señor Chaitanya), como Su expansión (el Señor Nityānanda), Su encarnación (Advaita Āchārya), Su potencia interna (Gadādhara) y Su potencia marginal (Śhrīvāsa). 

[Śhrī Nityānanda Praṇāma] 
Que Śhrī Nityānanda Rāma sea el objeto de mi recuerdo constante. Saṅkarṣaṇa, Śheṣa Nāga y los Viṣṇus que yacen en el Océano Kāraṇa, el Océano Garbha y el océano de leche son Sus partes plenarias y las partes de Sus partes plenarias. 

Ofrezco mi praṇāma a Śhrī Nityānanda Prabhu, quien otorga la dicha del amor divino, quien elimina la inmundicia de la era de Kali y quien es el maestro de Jāhnavā-devī. 

[Śhrī Gaurāṅga Praṇāma] 
Ofrezco praṇāma al supremamente magnánimo Señor que otorga kṛṣṇa-prema. Él es el propio Kṛṣṇa que adoptó una tez dorada y aceptó el nombre de Śhrī Kṛṣṇa Chaitanya. 

[Śhrī Gaura-Nityānanda Vandanā] Adoro a las encarnaciones de la misericordia, Śhrī Gaura-Nityānanda, cuyos brazos llegan hasta Sus rodillas, cuya tez es deslumbrante, quienes inauguraron el movimiento del saṅkīrtana, cuyos ojos son grandes como pétalos de loto, quienes nutren a todo el universo, quienes son los mejores entre los brāhmaṇas, quienes protegen el yuga-dharma y quienes Se dedican a realizar actividades agradables para el bienestar del mundo. 
<highlight>(Śhrī Chaitanya-bhāgavata, Ādi-khaṇḍa 1.1)</highlight> 

[Śhrī Śhukadeva Praṇāma] 
Ofrezco mis reverencias a Śhrī Śhukadeva Gosvāmī, quien puede penetrar en los corazones de todas las entidades vivientes. Cuando abandonó su hogar sin someterse a los procesos purificatorios, como aceptar el cordón sagrado, su padre, Vyāsa, exclamó: “¡Oh, hijo mío!”. Como si estuvieran absortos en ese mismo sentimiento de separación, solo los árboles le hicieron eco en respuesta a su llamada. 

[Śhrī Kṛṣṇa Praṇāma] 
¡Oh, Śhrī Kṛṣṇa! Tú eres un océano de misericordia, el amigo de los caídos, el Señor del universo, el amo de los pastores, el amado de las gopīs y (sobre todo) el amado de Śhrī Rādhā. Yo Te ofrezco praṇāma. 

###“Oh Shyāmasundara! Oh You whose head is adorned with peacock feathers! Your face is always graced with a playful smile, Your flute-playing is enchanting, and You are expert in relishing rasa with Śhrīmati Rādhika. Because You are an ocean of mercy, I am appealing to You to please make me a kinkari [maidservant] at the lotus feet of Your beloved.” 
(Śhrī Rādhā Prārthanā 2—Śhrī Vitthalacharya) 

[Śhrī Rādhā Praṇāma] 
¡Oh, Śhrī Rādhā! ¡Oh, Gaurāṅgi! Tu tez es como el oro fundido, Tú eres la reina de Vṛndāvana, la hija de Vṛṣabhānu, y la amada predilecta de Śhrī Hari. Yo Te ofrezco praṇāma. 

###O Svāminī Śhrī Rādhe, I am Yours, I am Yours! I cannot live without You! Knowing this, please bestow the shelter of Your lotus feet. 

[Sambandha-adhideva Praṇāma] 
¡Toda gloria a los supremamente misericordiosos Śhrī Śhrī Rādhā-Madana-mohana! Aunque soy indigno y carezco de inteligencia, Ellos son mi único refugio. Sus pies de loto lo son todo para mí. 

[Abhidheya-adhideva Praṇāma] 
En la resplandeciente tierra de Śhrī Vṛndāvana, en un templo hecho de joyas, Śhrī Śhrī Rādhā-Govinda están sentados en un refulgente trono bajo un árbol kalpa-vṛkṣa aceptando el servicio de Sus amadas sakhīs. Yo medito en Ellos. 

[Prayojana-adhideva Praṇāma] 
Situado a orillas del río en Vaṁśhīvaṭa, Śhrī Gopīnātha, que originó la melosidad trascendental de la danza rāsa, atrae a todas las gopīs con el sonido de Su flauta. Que Él nos conceda todo lo auspicioso. 

[Śhrī Tulasī Praṇāma] 
Ofrezco praṇāma una y otra vez a Śhrīmatī Tulasī-devī, que Le es sumamente querida a Śhrī Keśhava y que es también famosa con los nombres de Vṛndā-devī y Satyavatī. ¡Oh, Devī, tú otorgas kṛṣṇa-bhakti! 

[Śhrī Vṛndā-devī] 
Carente de devoción y culpable de cometer infinidad de ofensas, soy arrastrado por el océano de la existencia material por las turbulentas olas de la lujuria, la ira, la codicia y demás. Por lo tanto, oh misericordiosa Vṛndā-devī, me refugio en ti y ofrezco mis reverencias ante tus pies de loto. 

[Śhrī Paurṇamāsī] 
Śhrī Paurṇamāsī es sumamente hábil para organizar las formas más elevadas de disfrute para el señor de Śhrī Rādhā. Sus pies de loto son adorados por los Vrajavāsīs. Debido a que posee todas las buenas cualidades, empezando por la bondad, ella es objeto de adoración para todo el universo. Inclino mi cabeza y ofrezco praṇāma a esa Śhrī Paurṇamāsī-devī. 

[Śhrī Gopīśhvara-mahādeva] 
¡Oh, protector de la tierra de Vṛndāvana! ¡Oh esposo de Umā, oh Somamauli que llevas la luna en la cabeza! Tú eres adorado por Sanandana, Sanātana y Nārada. ¡Oh, Gopeśvara! Te suplico que me concedas prema incondicional por los pies de loto de Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, que realizan gozosos pasatiempos en Vraja. 

[Śhrī Yamunā-devī] 
Yamunā-devī es el manantial de prema por Śrī Nanda-nandana y el sol de la bienaventuranza espiritual. Su cuerpo hecho trascendencia líquida destruye todos los pecados y otorga todo lo auspicioso al mundo. Que Yamunā-devī, la hija del rey Sol, purifique nuestros cuerpos. 

[Śhrī Pañcha-tattva] 
Ofrezco praṇāma a Śhrī Kṛṣṇa Chaitanya Mahāprabhu en sus cinco aspectos como bhakta-rūpa (Mahāprabhu), bhakta-svarūpa (Nityānanda Prabhu), bhakta-avatāra (Advaita Āchārya), bhakta (Śhrīvāsa Ṭhākura) y bhakta-śhakti (Gadādhara Paṇḍita). 

[Mahā-mantra] 
Hare Kṛṣṇa, Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa, Hare Hare; Hare Rāma, Hare Rāma, Rāma Rāma, Hare Hare.

śhrī-nārāyaṇa-vandanā (2) vande ’haṁ śhrī-guru-varam śhrī-rūpānuga-pravaram vraja-rasa-rasikaṁ cha nārāyaṇam taṁ prapannam śhrī-guru-charaṇaṁ vande ramaṇa-preṣṭhāya bhūtale, rūpānuga-bhaktidaṁ cha IDX.translation_intro: maṅgalācaraṇa 1
IDX.en_translation:
I offer my obeisances to the lotus feet of my Spiritual Master, to the preceptors, and to the Vaiṣṇavas; to Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī with his elder brother (Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī), to Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī, along with Śrīla Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī and his associates. 

I offer obeisances to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Deva, along with Śrī Advaita Āchārya, Śrī Nityānanda Avadhūta, and His associates; and to the lotus feet of Śrī Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, accompanied by Śrīmatī Lalitā-devī, Śrīmatī Viśākhā-devī, and their associates. 

[Śrī Guru Praṇāma] 
I offer my respectful obeisances unto my Spiritual Master, who opened my eyes, which were blinded by the darkness of ignorance, with the torchlight of knowledge. 

[Śrīla Nārāyaṇa Praṇāma] 
I offer praṇāma to oṁ viṣṇupāda Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja, who is very dear to Śrīmatī Rādhikā. 

O Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja, you are expert in describing kṛṣṇa-līlā and are fully endowed with the qualities of magnanimity and sweetness. You are the best of all great souls. I bow my head to you. 

Tridaṇḍī-sannyāsī Śrīla Nārāyaṇa Mahārāja, the crown-jewel of devotees, always keeps in his heart the lotus feet of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, especially when Kṛṣṇa serves Śrīmatī Rādhikā. He deeply meditates on Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and the internal reasons for His descent. I bow down to the lotus feet of Śrīla Nārāyaṇa Mahārāja, who possesses innumerable transcendental qualities. 

[Śrī Nārāyaṇa Vandanā] 
I offer obeisances to the best of Gurus, the excellent follower of Rūpa, who is a connoisseur of the mellows of Vraja—to that Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja, who is surrendered. 

I offer obeisances to the lotus feet of the Guru, who is the beloved of the Lord on earth, who bestows Rūpānuga-bhakti, the embodiment of mercy, Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja. 

Who always bestows service in the delightful Seva-kuñja in Vraja, at Govardhana Hill, and at Rādhā-kuṇḍa, which is full of the bliss of rasa. 

I offer obeisances to that Guru named Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja, the beloved of the Lord, by the mere remembrance of whose feet Dāmodara becomes pleased. 

[Śrīla Vāmana Vandanā] 
I offer praṇāma to oṁ viṣṇupāda Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktivedānta Vāmana Gosvāmī Mahārāja, who is most dear to Śrī Keśava (alternately: Śrī Śrīmad Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja) 

Obeisances to the servant of the saintly, the beloved of the saintly on earth, the friend of the devotees, known as “Rādhānātha-vallabha”. 

Most dear to Śrīla Saccidānanda Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, Śrīla Narottama Dāsa Ṭhākura, and Narahari Sarakāra Ṭhākura; the well-wisher of Śrī Vedānta, the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam, and the Six Gosvāmīs. 

Dear to the abode of Māyāpura, the servant of the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇavas, more humble than a blade of grass—the beautiful personality, Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Vāmana Gosvāmī Mahārāja. 

[Śrīla Svāmī Vandanā] 
I offer my respectful obeisances unto His Divine Grace A.C. Bhaktivedānta Svāmī Prabhupāda, who is very dear to Lord Kṛṣṇa on this earth, having taken shelter at His lotus feet. 

Our respectful obeisances are unto you, O spiritual master, servant of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Gosvāmī Prabhupāda. You are kindly preaching the message of Lord Caitanyadeva and delivering the Western countries, which are filled with impersonalism and voidism. 

[Śrīla Keśava Vandanā] 
I offer my respectful obeisances unto Viṣṇupāda Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktiprajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī, who is like a lion among the Āchāryas. 

Whose character is superhuman, the protector of those who take shelter of him, always distressed by the suffering of the jīvas, the giver of the Name and Love. 

The embodiment of shelter in Gaura, whose only desire is Kṛṣṇa, the excellent follower of Rūpa, whose form is like Vinoda. 

The intimate associate of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Gosvāmī Prabhupāda, possessor of all good qualities, the destroyer of the darkness of Māyāvāda, the knower of the meaning of Vedānta. 

[Śrīla Prabhupāda Vandanā] 
I offer my respectful obeisances unto His Divine Grace Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Gosvāmī Prabhupāda, who is very dear to Lord Kṛṣṇa on this earth, having taken shelter at His lotus feet. 

I offer my respectful obeisances to Śrī Vārṣabhānavī-devī-dayita Dāsa, who is favored by Śrīmatī Rādhā-rāṇī and who is the ocean of transcendental mercy and the deliverer of the science of Kṛṣṇa. 

I offer my respectful obeisances unto you, the personified energy of Śrī Caitanya’s mercy, who deliver devotional service which is enriched with conjugal love of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, coming exactly in the line of revelation of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī. 

I offer my respectful obeisances unto you, who are the personified teachings of Lord Caitanya. You are the deliverer of the fallen souls. You do not tolerate any statement which is against the teachings of devotional service enunciated by Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī. 

[Śrīla Gaura-kiśora Vandanā] 
I offer my respectful obeisances unto Śrīla Gaura-kiśora Dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja, who is renunciation personified and always merged in the ocean of the mellow of separation from Kṛṣṇa. 

[Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Vandanā] 
I offer my respectful obeisances unto Śrīla Saccidānanda Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, who is the personification of the energy of Lord Caitanya and the best of the followers of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī. 

[Śrīla Jagannātha Vandanā] 
Obeisances to you, Śrīla Jagannātha Dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja, the Emperor of the Vaiṣṇavas, dear to the saintly, who indicated the place of Gaura’s appearance. 

[Śrī Vaiṣṇava Vandanā] 
I offer my respectful obeisances unto all the Vaiṣṇava devotees of the Lord. They are just like desire trees who can fulfill the desires of everyone, and they are oceans of mercy and the purifiers of the fallen souls. 

[Śrī Pañca-tattva Praṇāma] 
I offer my obeisances unto the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa, who appears in the form of a devotee (Lord Caitanya), as His expansion (Lord Nityānanda), His incarnation (Advaita Āchārya), His internal potency (Gadādhara), and His marginal potency (Śrīvāsa). 

[Śrī Nityānanda Praṇāma] 
May Śrī Nityānanda Rāma be the object of my constant remembrance. Saṅkarṣaṇa, Śeṣa Nāga and the Viṣṇus who lie on the Kāraṇa Ocean, Garbha Ocean, and ocean of milk are His plenary portions and the portions of His plenary portions. 

[Śrī Gaurāṅga Praṇāma] 
Obeisances to the most munificent incarnation, who bestows love of Kṛṣṇa—to Kṛṣṇa Himself, who has assumed the name Kṛṣṇa Caitanya and a golden complexion. 

[Śrī Kṛṣṇa Praṇāma] 
O my dear Kṛṣṇa, ocean of mercy, You are the friend of the distressed and the source of creation. You are the master of the cowherd men and the lover of the gopīs, especially Rādhā-rāṇī. I offer my respectful obeisances unto You. 

[Śrī Rādhā Praṇāma] 
Reverential obeisances unto you, O Rādhā, whose complexion is like molten gold and who are the Queen of Vṛndāvana. You are the daughter of King Vṛṣabhānu, and You are very dear to Lord Kṛṣṇa. 

[Sambandha-adhideva Praṇāma] 
Glory to the all-merciful Rādhā and Madana-mohana! They are the only shelter of my depraved and crippled intelligence. Their lotus feet are my everything. 

[Abhidheya-adhideva Praṇāma] 
In a temple of jewels in Vṛndāvana, underneath a desire tree, Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Govinda, served by Their most confidential associates, sit upon an effulgent throne. I offer my humble obeisances unto Them.

He is the original teacher of captivating and skillful deeds, awakened in the entire world, and the resting place of supreme strength. He is the friend who delights everyone with His incomparable qualities; may the youthful prince of Vraja fulfill my desires. 

By the twitching of His bow-like eyebrows, He creates waves of agitation in young women that are difficult even for Cupid with his countless arrows. He is the ocean for the fish-like lives of His dear companions; may the youthful prince of Vraja fulfill my desires.

One who diligently studies these eight verses of the youthful prince of Vraja—which are full of excellent pastimes—will have his name recorded in the list of Her intimate associates by the Queen of Vṛndāvana, who is an expert in divine mellows.

kiṁ te kṛtaṁ hantatapaḥ kṣitīti

mamāstu vṛndāvana eva vāsaḥ 

jasmin mahā-rāsa-vilāsa-līlā 
na prāpa jāṁ śhrī-rapi sā tapobhiḥ 
tatrollasanmañju-nikuñja-puñje 
mamāstu vṛndāvana eva vāsaḥ 

sadā rurunyaṅkumukhā viśhaṅkaṁ 
khelanti kūjanti pikāli-kīrāḥ 
śhikhaṇḍino jatra naṭanti tasmin 
mamāstu vṛndāvana eva vāsaḥ 

vṛndāvanasyāṣṭakametaduccḣaiḥ
