IDX.en_translation:
I have no desire for yogic perfections or liberation. Nor do I desire to be an associate in the spiritual world. Even if I do not attain divine love, may my residence certainly be in Vṛndāvana. 

Where Lord Brahmā prayed to be born even as a blade of grass, and Uddhava, the crest-jewel of pure devotees, also prayed, seeing its supreme sweetness—in that place, may my residence certainly be in Vṛndāvana. 

“What austerities have you performed, O Earth?” Even the gopīs glorified the Earth, saying: “Because the marks of Lord Kṛṣṇa’s lotus feet are imprinted upon you.” In that place, may my residence certainly be in Vṛndāvana. 

Where the attachment to the gopīs alone reaches its complete perfection, and because of which the Vedas declare “He is the personification of all mellows”—therefore, may my residence certainly be in Vṛndāvana. 

Bounded by Bhaṇḍīravana, Govardhana, and the site of the Rāsa dance, marked by these three boundaries within a radius of forty miles—though measured, it is immeasurable in its glories. In that place, may my residence certainly be in Vṛndāvana. 

Where the sovereignty belongs to the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu, by whom the joy of divine love arises in people, and in which my hope is very strong—therefore in that place, may my residence certainly be in Vṛndāvana. 

Where the pastimes of the great Rāsa dance take place, which even the Goddess of Fortune could not attain through many austerities—in that place, filled with splendid and beautiful groves, may my residence certainly be in Vṛndāvana. 

Where deer and antelopes always play fearlessly, cuckoos and parrots chirp sweetly, and peacocks dance—in that place, may my residence certainly be in Vṛndāvana. 

Those who loudly recite these eight verses of Vṛndāvanāṣṭakam with steadfast intelligence will directly attain service to the lotus feet of the Mistress of Vṛndāvana at the end of their lives.

nāche śhachī-nandana, bhakatajīvana dhana, 
saṅge nāche priya nityānanda 
advaita śhrīnivāsa, āra nāche haridāsa, 
vāsughoṣa rāya rāmānanda 

nityānanda mukha heri, bole pahuṅ hari hari, 
premāya dharaṇī gaḍi jāya 
priya gadādhara āsi, prabhura bāma pāśhe basi, 
ghana naraharimukha chāya 

pahuṅ nāhi mele āṅkhi, kahe mora kāhāṅ sakhī, 
kāhāṅ pāba rāi daraśhana 
kaha kaha narahari, āra sambarite nāri, 
ihā bali bhela achetana 

ekhani ācḣalū tathā, ke more ānila ethā, 
rāsa-rase nikuñja-bhavana 
gela sukhasampada, ebe bhela vipada, 
viṣādaye e dāsa lochana
IDX.en_translation:
Śacī-nandana, the treasure and life of the devotees, dances. With Him dances dear Nityānanda. Advaita, Śrīnivāsa, and Haridāsa also dance. Vāsughoṣa and Rāya Rāmānanda likewise dance. 

Seeing Nityānanda’s face, the Lord chants “Hari! Hari!” and rolls on the earth in divine love. Dear Gadādhara comes and sits on the Lord’s left side, frequently looking at Narahari’s face. 

The Lord does not open His eyes, saying, “Where is my sakhī? Where will I get the audience of Rādhā?” “Tell me, tell me, Narahari, I can no longer control myself,” Saying this, He became unconscious. 

“Just now I was there, who brought me here? In the forest grove with the mellows of the Rāsa dance.” All happiness and opulence is gone, now there is only calamity— thus the servant Locana Dāsa laments.

nadīyā-nagare gorā-charita-amṛta

gorā-śhikṣā-mate kṛṣṇa bhaja anivāra 

gorāra charaṇa dhari’ jei bhāgyavān 
vraje rādhā-kṛṣṇa bhaje, sei mora prāṇa 

‘rādhā-kṛṣṇa-gorāchāṅda’, ‘nade-vṛndāvana’ 
eimātra kara sāra pā’be nityadhana 

vidyā-buddhihīna dīna akiñchana cḣāra 
karmajñāna-śhūnya āmi śhūnya-sadāchāra 

śhrī-guru-vaiṣṇava more dilena upādhi 
bhakti-hīne upādhi hoila ebe vyādhi 

jatana kariyā sei vyādhi-nivāraṇe 
śharaṇa loinu āmi vaiṣṇava-charaṇe

IDX.en_translation:
In Nadiyā, drink the nectar of Gorā’s pastimes. Drink it, give up sorrow and fear, and steady your mind. 

This temporary world, O brother, only Kṛṣṇa is the essence. According to Gorā’s teachings, worship Kṛṣṇa constantly. 

Whoever is fortunate to grasp the lotus feet of Gorā and worships Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa in Vraja, that person is my life. 

“Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa-Gorācānd” and “Nadiyā-Vṛndāvana”- just make this the essence, and you will attain eternal wealth. 

I am devoid of knowledge and intelligence, fallen, insignificant, and contemptible. I am without fruitive action or knowledge, and without good conduct. 

My Guru and the Vaiṣṇavas gave me titles. But for one devoid of devotion, these titles have now become a disease. 

Striving to remove that disease, I have taken shelter of the lotus feet of the Vaiṣṇavas. 

Holding the dust of the lotus feet of the Vaiṣṇavas on my head, Bhaktivinoda sings this song, “The Slayer of Sorrow”.

nadīyā-udayagiri, pūrṇa-chandra gaura-hari, 
kṛpā kari’ hoila udaya 
pāpa-tamo haila nāśha, trijagatera ullāsa, 
jagabhari’ hari-dhvani haya 

seikāle nijālaya, uṭhiyā advaita rāya, 
nṛtya kare ānandita-mane 
hari-dāse lañā saṅge, huṅkāra-kīrtana-raṅge, 
kene nāche keha nāhi jāne 

dekhi’ uparāga hāsi, śhīghra gaṅgā-ghāṭe āsi’, 
ānande karila gaṅgāsnāna 
pāñā uparāga-cḣale, āpanāra manobale, 
brāhmaṇere dila nānā dāna 

jagat ānandamaya, dekhi’ mane savismaya, 
ṭhāre-ṭhore kahe haridāsa 
‘tomāra aicḣana raṅga, mora mana parasanna, 
dekhi-kicḣu kārye ācḣe bhāsa’ 

āchārya-ratna, śhrīvāsa, haila mane sukhollāsa, 
jāi’ snāna kaila gaṅgājale 
ānande vihvala mana, kare hari saṁkīrtana, 
nānā dāna kaila manobale 

ei mata bhakta-yati, jāṅ’ra jei deśhe sthiti, 
tāhāṅ tāhāṅ pāñā manobale 
nāche kare saṅkīrtana, ānande vihvala mana, 
dāna kare grahaṇera cḣale 

brāhmaṇa-sajjana-nārī, nānā dravye thāli bhari’, 
āilā sabe jautuka loiyā 
jena kāṅchāsonā-dyuti, dekhi’ bālakera mūrti, 
āśhīrvāda kare sukha pāñā 

sāvitrī, gaurī, sarasvatī, śhachī, rambhā, arundhatī, 
āra jata deva-nārīgaṇa 
nānā dravye pātra bhari’, brāhmaṇīra veśha dhari’, 
āsi’ sabe karena daraśhana 

antarīkṣe devagaṇa, gandharva, siddha, chāraṇa, 
stuti-nṛtya kare vādya-gīta 
nartaka, vādaka, bhāṭa, navadvīpe jā’ra nāṭa, 
sabe āsi’ nāche pāñā prīta 

kebā āse kebā jāya, kebā nāche kebā gāya, 
sambhālite nāre kāra bola 
khaṇḍileka duḥkha-śhoka, pramoda-pūrita loka, 
miśhra hailā ānande vihvala 

āchāryaratna, śhrīvāsa, jagannāthamiśhra-pāśha, 
āsi’ tāṅre kare sāvadhāna 
karāila jāta-karma, je ācḣila vidhi-dharma, 
tabe miśhra kare nānā dāna 

jautuka pāila jata, ghare vā ācḣila kata, 
saba dhana vipre dila dāna 
jata nartaka, gāyana, bhāṭa, akiñchana jana, 
dhana diyā kailā sabāra māna 

śhrīvāsera brāhmaṇī, nāma tāṅ’ra ‘mālinī’, 
āchāryaratnera patnī-saṅge 
sindura, haridrā, taila, khoi, kalā, nānā fala, 
diyā pūje nārīgaṇa raṅge 

advaita āchārya-bhāryā, jagat-pūjitā āryā, 
nāma tāṅ’ra ‘sītā ṭhākurāṇī’ 
āchāryera ājñā pāñā, gelā upahāra lañā, 
dekhite bālaka-śhiromaṇi 

suvarṇera kaḍi-bouli, rajatamudrā-pāśhuli, 
suvarṇera aṅgada, kaṅkaṇa 
du-bāhute divya śhaṅkha, rajatera malabaṅka, 
svarṇamudrāra nānā hāra-gaṇa 

vyāghra-nakha hemajaḍi, kaṭi-paṭṭasūtra-ḍorī, 
hasta-padera jata ābharaṇa 
chitravarṇa paṭṭaśhāḍī, buni foto paṭṭapāḍī, 
svarṇa-raupya-mudrā bahu-dhana 

durvā, dhānya, gorochana, haridrā, kuṅkuma, chandana, 
maṅgala-dravya pātra bhariyā 
vastra-gupta dolā chaḍi’, saṅge lañā dāsī cheḍī, 
vastrālaṅkāra peṭāri bhariyā 

bhakṣya, bhojya, upahāra, saṅge loila bahu bhāra, 
śhachīgṛhe haila upanīta 
dekhiyā bālaka-ṭhāma, sākṣāt gokula-kāna, 
varṇamātra dekhi viparīta 

sarva aṅga-sunirmāṇa, suvarṇa-pratimā-bhāna, 
sarva aṅga-sulakṣaṇamaya 
bālakera divya-jyoti, dekhi’ pāila bahuprīti, 
vātsalyete dravila hṛdaya 

durvā, dhānya dila śhīrṣe, kaila bahu āśhīṣe, 
chirajīvi hoo dui bhāi 
ḍākinī-śhāṅkhinī haite, śhaṅkā upajila chite, 
ḍare nāma thuila ‘nimāi’ 

putramātā-snāna-dine, dila vastra-vibhūṣaṇe, 
putra-saha miśhrere sammāni’ 
śhachī-miśhrera pūjā lañā, manete hariṣa hañā, 
ghare āilā sītā-ṭhākurāṇī 

aicḣe śhachī-jagannātha, putra pāñā lakṣmī-nātha, 
pūrṇa hoila sakala vāñcḣita 
dhana-dhānye bhare ghara, lokamānya kalevara, 
dine dine haya ānandita 

miśhra-vaiṣṇava, śhānta, alampaṭa, śhuddha, dānta, 
dhanabhoge nāhi abhimāna 
putrera prabhāve jata, dhana āsi’ mile tata, 
viṣṇu-prīte dvije dena dāna 

lagna gaṇi’ harṣamati, nīlāmbara chakravartī, 
gupte kicḣu kahila miśhrere 
‘mahā-puruṣera chihna, lagne aṅge bhinna bhinna, 
dekhi’,-ei tāribe saṁsāre’ 

aicḣe prabhu śhachī-ghare, kṛpāya kaila avatāre, 
jei ihā karaye śhravaṇa 
gaura-prabhu dayā-maya, tāṅ’re hayena sadaya, 
sei pāya tāṅhāra charaṇa 

pāiyā mānuṣa-janma, je nā śhune gaura-guṇa, 
hena janma tā’ra vyartha haila 
pāiyā amṛtadhunī, piye viṣagarta-pāni, 
janmiyā se kene nāhi maila 

śhrī-chaitanya-nityānanda, āchārya-advaitachandra, 
svarūpa-rūpa-raghunāthadāsa 
īṅhā sabāra śhrī-charaṇa, śhire vandi nijadhana, 
janmalīlā gāila kṛṣṇa-dāsa
IDX.en_translation:
From the rising mountain of Nadīyā, the full moon of Lord Gaura-hari mercifully arose. The darkness of sin was destroyed, the three worlds rejoiced, and the whole world was filled with the sound of Lord Hari’s Name. 

At that time, Advaita Āchārya rose up in his own home and danced with a joyful heart. Taking Haridāsa Ṭhākura with him, he danced in the joy of congregational chanting, though no one knew why. 

Seeing the eclipse, he smiled and quickly came to the bank of the Ganges to bathe. Taking the eclipse as a pretext, he gave various gifts to the brāhmaṇas with strong conviction. 

Seeing the world filled with joy, Haridāsa Ṭhākura hinted: “Seeing your wonderful mood, my mind is very pleased. I see that some great event is about to manifest.” 

Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita was filled with great joy and went to bathe in the Ganges. His mind overwhelmed with joy, he performed congregational chanting and gave various donations. 

In this way, devotees and renunciants wherever they resided received great strength. They danced and performed congregational chanting, their minds overwhelmed with joy, and gave donations on the pretext of the eclipse. 

The women of the village, filling plates with various gifts, all came to see. Seeing the form of the child who glowed like raw gold, they gave their blessings, experiencing great happiness. 

The celestial women, assuming the guise of village women, also came to see, filling their vessels with various articles. 

In the sky, the demigods and celestial musicians danced and sang praises with their instruments. Dancers and musicians from all of Navadvīpa also came and danced with great joy. 

Who was coming and who was going, who was dancing and who was singing—no one could keep track. Sorrow and lamentation were dispelled, the people were filled with delight, and Jagannātha Miśra became overwhelmed with joy. 

Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita and other devotees came to Jagannātha Miśra and reminded him of his duties. He had the birth ceremony performed according to scriptural injunctions and then gave various donations. 

All the gifts he received, and whatever he had in his house, he gave in charity to the priests. He honored all the dancers, singers, and poor people by giving them wealth. 

Mālinī-devī, the wife of Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita, along with the wives of other devotees, joyfully offered worship with vermillion, turmeric, oil, and various fruits. 

Sītā-Ṭhākurāṇī, the venerable wife of Advaita Āchārya, receiving her husband’s order, went with gifts to see the crest-jewel of children. 

She brought golden ornaments, silver coins, bangles, divine conch-shells, and various necklaces of gold coins. 

She brought tiger-claw pendants set in gold, silk waist-threads, and all manner of ornaments for the hands and feet. She also brought multi-colored silk saris and much wealth in gold and silver coins. 

Filling vessels with auspicious articles like grass, turmeric, saffron, and sandalwood, she rode in a covered palanquin with her attendants and baskets full of clothes and ornaments. 

She arrived at the house of Mother Śacī with many gifts of food and clothing. Seeing the child’s form, she saw directly the Lord of Gokula, only the complexion was different. 

All His limbs were perfectly formed, appearing like a golden Deity and endowed with all auspicious marks. Seeing the child’s divine effulgence, her heart melted with parental love. 

She placed grass and paddy on His head and gave many blessings, saying: “May You two brothers live long.” Fearing that witches might cast an evil eye, she named Him “Nimāi.” 

On the day of the mother and son’s first bath, she gave them clothes and ornaments, honoring Jagannātha Miśra as well. Having accepted the hospitality of Mother Śacī and Jagannātha Miśra, Sītā-Ṭhākurāṇī returned home with a joyful heart. 

Thus, Mother Śacī and Jagannātha Miśra, having received their Son, had all their desires fulfilled. Their house was filled with wealth and grain, and they became more joyful day by day. 

Jagannātha Miśra was a peaceful and pure devotee; he had no pride in his wealth. By the influence of his Son, much wealth came to them, and he gave it all in charity to the priests for the pleasure of the Lord. 

Calculating the astrological moment with joy, the grandfather of the Lord secretly told Jagannātha Miśra: “I see the marks of a great personality upon His limbs; He will surely deliver the entire world.” 

Thus the Lord mercifully made His advent in Mother Śacī’s house. Whoever hears this narrative will receive the mercy of Lord Gaura and eventually attain His lotus feet. 

Having attained a human birth, one who does not hear the glories of Lord Gaura makes such a birth useless. Having found a river of nectar, if one chooses to drink from a poisonous pit, why did they not simply die after taking birth? 

I worship the lotus feet of Śrī Caitanya, Nityānanda, Advaita Āchārya, Svarūpa Dāmodara, Rūpa Gosvāmī, and Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī. Kṛṣṇa-dāsa Kavirāja has thus sung the pastimes of the Lord’s birth.

IDX.en_translation:
What is the state of mind of the very virtuous and devoted wives of Nadīyā? Their minds are not with their own sons for even a moment, as they praise the character and pastimes of the Son of Śacī. 

Seeing the end of the night, forsaking their beds, they cannot hold patience for even half a moment. Filling plates with various items, row after row, they set off to offer them to the Moon of Nadīyā. 

As they enter Śacī-mātā’s house, a sea of joy overflows in their hearts. Everyone sees, in the lap of His mother, Gorā, the Moon of Gokula, playing. 

Their eyes are soothed, and holding Him in their laps, the women forget their own bodies. Narahari says, “Oh, wonderful! Oh, wonderful! Who has created such a loving sentiment?”

I offer my obeisances unto Viṣṇupāda Śrī Śrīmad Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī, who is like a lion among the āchāryas. 

He perfectly fulfills the desire of Śrī Sarasvatī in every way; he is non-different from Śrī Sarasvatī and is the deliverer of the fallen. 

He is harder than a thunderbolt in destroying conclusions opposed to bhakti; he is fearless for the sake of truth and causes one to reject bad association. 

His character is superhuman, and he protects those who take shelter of him; he is always distressed by the suffering of the jīvas and bestows love for the Holy Name. 

He is the manifestation of Viṣṇupāda, and his only desire is to serve Kṛṣṇa; he is immersed in thoughts of Gaura and holds Śrī Guru in his heart. 

He possesses affectionate vision, seeing the whole universe as pervaded by Viṣṇu; I offer obeisances to you, Gurudeva, who are the embodiment of Kṛṣṇa’s opulence. 

He is the founder of the Śrī Gauḍīya Vedānta Samiti and the one who brought about the prosperity of service in Śrī Māyāpura Dhāma. 

He always protected the Navadvīpa Parikramā; I offer my obeisances to that Śrī Guru who is merciful to the fallen. 

Please give me your strength; this is the earnest prayer of this fallen soul. May my mind run rapidly toward your lotus feet.
IDX.es_translation:
Yo ofrezco praṇāma al āchārya oṁ viṣṇupāda Śhrī Śhrīmad Bhakti Prajñāna Keśhava Gosvāmī Mahārāja, que es como un león. 

Él protege con firmeza y en todos los aspectos la misión de satisfacer el deseo íntimo de Śhrīla Sarasvatī Prabhupāda. Él no es diferente de Śhrīla Sarasvatī Ṭhākura, y por ello es la causa de la liberación de todas las almas caídas. 

Él es más devastador que un rayo a la hora de erradicar las conclusiones filosóficas erróneas, es intrépido cuando se trata de establecer la verdad, y elimina la asociación perjudicial.. 

Él es una personalidad completamente trascendental y nutre con gran afecto a quienes se han refugiado en él. Se entristece siempre al ver el sufrimiento de las jīvas condicionadas, y otorga prema por el glorioso santo nombre. 

Él es una manifestación directa de los pies de loto de Śhrī Viṣṇu y está perpetuamente dedicado a satisfacer los deseos de Śhrī Kṛṣṇa. Siempre inmerso en la meditación de Śhrī Gaurāṅga, él lleva constantemente a su guru en su corazón. 

Mediante su amorosa visión, él percibe la presencia de Viṣṇu en todas partes. Yo ofrezco praṇāma a Śhrī Gurudeva, que es la personificación de la excelencia de Śhrī Kṛṣṇa. 

Él estableció el Śhrī Gauḍīya Vedānta Samiti e incrementó el servicio a Śhrī Māyāpura-dhāma. 

Yo ofrezco praṇāma a Śhrīla Gurudeva, que protege permanentemente el parikramā de Śhrī Navadvīpa-dhāma y es siempre misericordioso con las personas caídas. 

¡Oh, Gurudeva! Concede por favor tu misericordia a esta persona desamparada, que siempre la desea en todos los aspectos, para que pueda meditar siempre en tus pies de loto.

IDX.translation_intro: <highlight>Oración que se recita durante el mes de Kārtika</highlight>
IDX.en_translation:
I bow down to that Supreme Controller, whose form is eternal bliss and knowledge, whose ears are adorned with swinging earrings, and who is splendidly manifest in Gokula. He is fleeing from Mother Yaśodā due to fear, being pursued by her to the point of being caught. 

He is crying again and again, rubbing His two eyes with His two lotus-like hands, His eyes filled with fear. His neck, marked with three lines, is trembling due to His frequent breaths, and the garland around His belly is tied by the devotion of Yaśodā. 

To this Lord, who immerses His own people in pools of joy through such pastimes and who reveals that He is conquered by His devotees who possess knowledge of His supremacy, I offer my obeisances again and again with love. 

O Lord! I do not pray for liberation, nor for its ultimate limit, nor any other boon from the bestowers of boons. O Lord! May Your form as a cowherd child always be manifest in my mind. What need is there for anything else? 

O Lord! May Your lotus-like face—encircled by dark-blue, soft, curly hair and repeatedly kissed by Mother Yaśodā, with reddish bimba fruit-like lips—always be manifest in my mind. What is the use of millions of other gains? 

O Lord! I offer my obeisances to You, O Dāmodara! O Ananta! O Viṣṇu! Be pleased, O Master! I am submerged in a network of miseries. O Lord! Please bestow Your merciful glance upon me, who am extremely poor and ignorant. Become visible before my eyes! 

Just as the two sons of Kuvera, though bound in material forms, were liberated by You and made into devotees, similarly, please bestow upon me Your own loving devotion. I have no desire for liberation in this world, O Dāmodara! 

My obeisances to the rope which is a brilliant abode! And to Your belly, which is the abode of the entire universe! My obeisances to Rādhikā, Your beloved! My obeisances to You, O Lord, whose pastimes are endless!
IDX.es_translation:
Yo adoro al Controlador Supremo cuya forma es eterna y está llena de conocimiento y bienaventuranza. Pendientes con forma de makara se balancean sobre Sus mejillas, y reluce de modo esplendoroso en Gokula. Él se aleja del mortero corriendo por temor a Madre Yaśhodā, y es finalmente atrapado por detrás. 

Él llora incesantemente y se frota los ojos con Sus dos manos de loto. Sus ojos están llenos de temor. Sus profundos sollozos hacen que se agiten las perlas y demás ornamentos alrededor de Su cuello, que está marcado con tres atractivas líneas. [Yo ofrezco praṇāma a] ese Dāmodara que es atado por el vātsalya-bhakti de Su madre. 

Mediante pasatiempos como este, Él sumerge a los habitantes de Gokula en ríos de bienaventuranza e informa a quienes son conscientes de Su divinidad que solo puede ser conquistado por Sus devotos. Yo Le ofrezco reverencias cientos de veces con amor. 

¡Oh, Deva! No pido la liberación [de este mundo] ni la liberación suprema [de residir en Vaikuṇṭha]. Tampoco deseo ninguna otra bendición 4 de Ti, el benefactor supremo. ¡Oh, Nātha! Que Tu forma de Bāla-gopāla (pastorcillo) en Vṛndāvana se manifieste siempre en mi corazón. No necesito ninguna otra bendición. 

Tu rostro de loto, enmarcado por suaves rizos de color negro azulado y brillo rojizo, es besado una y otra vez por la gopī Śhrī Yaśhodā. Que ese rostro de loto con labios rojos como la fruta bimba permanezca siempre visible en mi corazón. Millones de otros logros carecen de interés para mí. 

¡Oh, Deva! ¡Oh, Dāmodara! ¡Oh, Ananta! ¡Oh, Viṣṇu! Yo Te ofrezco reverencias. ¡Oh, prabhu! Sé misericordioso. Me estoy hundiendo en un océano de penurias. Estoy sumamente afligido y no sé qué hacer. ¡Oh, Īśha! Derrama Tu misericordiosa mirada sobre mí y ten la bondad de rescatarme manifestándote directamente ante mis ojos. 

4 Na cānyam —también otras— puede referirse a la bendición de ejecutar los seis procesos del bhakti o a alcanzar cualquier otro logro de valor. Igual que liberaste a los dos hijos de Kuvera a pesar de estar atado por la cintura y los volviste merecedores de devoción, otórgame por favor a mí también un inmenso prema-bhakti por Ti [en Tu forma de pastorcillo]. ¡Oh, Dāmodara! Este es mi único anhelo; no deseo ningún otro tipo de liberación. 

¡Oh, Dāmodara! Ofrezco praṇāma a la cuerda que ata Tu cintura que es morada de brillante refulgencia. Ofrezco praṇāma a Tu abdomen, que es el sostén del universo entero. Ofrezco praṇāma una y otra vez a Śhrīmatī Rādhikā, que Te es supremamente querida. Y Te ofrezco praṇāma a Ti, mi Divino Señor, que ejecutas ilimitados pasatiempos trascendentales.

IDX.en_translation:
I offer my obeisances unto You, the son of Jagannātha Miśra, who are the Absolute Truth in the past, present, and future. I offer my respectful obeisances unto You, along with Your servants, Your followers, and Your associates. 

I worship Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, who is very eager to bestow mercy upon His devotees. He is satisfied by anything whatsoever offered by a devotee with faith. 

I worship Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, an ocean of mercy, who descended in Bengal for the purpose of bestowing loving devotion. 

Repeated obeisances to the maintainer of the universe, the golden Lord, the Supreme Soul, the son of Śacī, and the husband of the goddess of fortune. 

O beautiful young moon of Navadvīpa! O Lord Viśvambhara, best among men! O son of Śacī, thief of my thoughts! O Lord of Viṣṇupriyā, please be pleased! 

Repeated obeisances to You, whose form is full of joyful pastimes, who are beautiful with a divine golden luster, and who bestow the great mellow of divine love. 

I surrender to the one ancient Supreme Person, an ocean of mercy, who—for the purpose of teaching renunciation and His own devotional service—assumed the form of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya. 

All glories to the Lord who was born from the womb of Śacī! All glories to Him whose only principle is to give devotional love! All glories to His golden form that rivals Mount Meru! Blessed is the name of Kṛṣṇa Caitanya! 

O Lord Caitanya! I have fallen into the ocean of worldly miseries, swallowed up by the crocodiles and sharks of lust, anger, and greed. I am chained by bad desires and am without shelter. Please give me the support of Your feet. 

May the son of Śacī, Lord Hari—resplendent with a cluster of beautiful golden effulgence—mercifully descend in this age to bestow the opulence of His own devotion in the most elevated and brilliant mellow, which was never given before. May He always manifest in the cave of your heart. 

Rādhā is the transformation of Kṛṣṇa’s love, His internal pleasure potency. Although They are one in nature, They formerly appeared on earth in two separate bodies. Now those two have attained unity as Caitanya. I offer obeisances to that form of Kṛṣṇa, who is covered by the mood and luster of Rādhā. 

Out of a desire to know the glory of Rādhā’s love, the wonderful sweetness She experiences through Me, and the happiness She derives from My experience, the moon-like Lord Hari was born from the womb of Śacī.

I offer my obeisances to Lord Narasimha, who gives joy to Prahlada Maharaja and whose nails are like chisels on the stonelike chest of the demon Hiranyakasipu. 

Lord Nrsimhadeva is here, and He is also there on the opposite side. Wherever I go, there I see Lord Nrsimhadeva. He is outside and within my heart. Therefore I take shelter of Lord Nrsimhadeva, the original Supreme Personality of Godhead. 

O Kesava! O Lord of the universe! O Lord Hari, who have assumed the form of half-man, half-lion! All glories to You! Just as one can easily crush a wasp between one’s fingernails, so in the same way the body of the wasp-like demon Hiranyakasipu has been ripped apart by the wonderful pointed nails on Your beautiful lotus hands. 

All glories to Nrsimhadeva! All glories to Nrsimhadeva! All glories to Nrsimhadeva! All glories to the Lord of Prahlada, the bee who sits on the lotus face of the Goddess of Fortune. 

I worship Lord Nrsimha, within whose mouth resides the Goddess of Learning, on whose chest resides the Goddess of Fortune, and within whose heart resides the Divine Will. 

I offer my obeisances to Lord Hari, who has the face of a lion, whose effulgence is like that of the autumn moon, who destroys the ignorance of His devotees, and who gives pleasure to the heart of Prahlada. 

Although very ferocious, the lioness is very kind to her cubs. Similarly, although very ferocious to non-devotees like Hiranyakasipu, Lord Nrsimhadeva is very soft and kind to devotees like Prahlada Maharaja.

This humble soul's desire is that you please grant me residence in the holy land of Navadvīpa; I will always smear the dust of that sacred place upon my body. 

For your worship, I offer incense, lamps, and flowers. I now extol your glories; please be pleased with me.

“I have won! I have won!” he said repeatedly. “To deliver the living entities, Lord Gaura must now incarnate.” 

Hearing these words, the saintly Haridāsa Ṭhākura danced in joy. Locana Dāsa says: “The noose of illusion around the souls was thus cut.”

I offer my obeisances to the excellent Golden Lord, the son of Śacī, who is eternally fresh and golden, whose arrows are fresh flowers, who embodies new emotions, and who is engrossed in new playful dancing, bringing forth new laughter. 

I offer my obeisances to the son of Śacī, who is filled with fresh love, whose purity is like fresh butter, and who is adorned with new attire—the very essence of love, shining in nine ways with auspicious, loving emotions. 

I offer my obeisances to the son of Śacī, who is devoted to the Lord and bears His name, whose hands are engaged in chanting on beads, and whose eyes always stream with tears of love. 

I offer my obeisances to the son of Śacī, who constantly removes the miseries of material existence for the people, who is the refuge for those devoted to the ultimate spiritual goal, and who bestows new attachments and removes the world’s afflictions. 

I offer my obeisances to the son of Śacī, who bestows His own devotion, who is supremely charming, and who is the king among expert performers, captivating the minds of chaste women with His playful dancing. 

I offer my obeisances to the son of Śacī, whose hands hold cymbals, whose voice is sweet like a cuckoo, and who sweetly plays the vīṇā, performing dances imbued with the qualities of His own devotion. 

I offer my obeisances to the son of Śacī, who embodies the religious principles for this age, who is the son of Nanda Himself, whose beautiful form on earth is appropriate for the emotions of love, and whose mind is absorbed in meditation. 

I offer my obeisances to the son of Śacī, whose eyes are reddish, whose feet are adorned, and whose garments are beautiful—the Lord whose own name is uttered falteringly from His mouth, bestowing supreme nectar to the world.

The branches are adorned with fresh new sprouts. Parrots and cuckoos sing melodiously.

The young women of Vraja give the swing a push. Thinking She might fall, the beautiful Rādhā embraces Her Lord. 

Many kinds of divine mellows arise from Their association. Govinda Dāsa witnesses that joyful play.

Worship Kṛṣṇa, the treasure and son of Vraja-rāja, whose bodily luster shames a fresh cloud, who is the best of clever kings of divine mellows, and whose auspicious, graceful, and beautiful peacock feather crest shines. 

Worship Kṛṣṇa, the treasure and son of Vraja-rāja, whose arched eyebrows mock the rainbow, whose moon-like face condemns millions of moons, and who is endowed with a gentle, sweet smile and pleasing speech. 

Worship Kṛṣṇa, the treasure and son of Vraja-rāja, whose beautiful limbs make Cupid himself tremble, who captivates the minds of the residents of Vraja with His attire, and whose eyes intensely shame the blue lotuses. 

Worship Kṛṣṇa, the treasure and son of Vraja-rāja, whose forehead is adorned with locks of hair, whose shark-shaped earrings swing by His ears, and whose waist is encircled by a well-fitting yellow garment. 

Worship Kṛṣṇa, the treasure and son of Vraja-rāja, whose beautiful feet are graced with tinkling ankle bells, whose jewel-decorated feet mock the pride of bees, and whose feet bear the marks of a flag, a thunderbolt, and a fish. 

Worship Kṛṣṇa, the treasure and son of Vraja-rāja, whose beautiful body is smeared with sandalwood, whose Kaustubha gem shames the radiance of the sun, and who has assumed the form of the crest-jewel of the youth of Vraja. 

Worship Kṛṣṇa, the treasure and son of Vraja-rāja, who is worshiped by hosts of demigods, and who is the crest-jewel of their lords and the guru of all—the supreme Giridhārī, Murāri, and Purāri.

Tan solo adora al tesoro de Śhrī Kṛṣṇa, el hijo del rey de Vraja.

Su frente está rodeada de hileras de rizos, en Sus orejas se columpian pendientes con forma de mākara, y Su cintura está graciosamente embellecida con una tela de seda amarilla. Tan solo adora al tesoro de Śhrī Kṛṣṇa, el hijo del rey de Vraja.

Su hermoso cuerpo está generosamente untado con pasta de sándalo. La luz que emana de Su joya Kaustubha eclipsa al sol. Él ha aparecido como la joya cumbre de los jóvenes de Vraja. Tan solo adora al tesoro de Śhrī Kṛṣṇa, el hijo del rey de Vraja.

Él levantó Giri-Govardhana, exterminó al demonio Mura y es el amo del Señor Śhiva. Tan solo adora al tesoro de Śhrī Kṛṣṇa, el hijo del rey de Vraja. 

Está inmerso en dulces y amorosos juegos con la hija de Vṛṣabhānu Mahārāja. Su atuendo es como el de rasa-rāja-śhiromaṇi, la joya cumbre de los emperadores que saborean melosidades trascendentales. Él es amo de la manifestación cósmica, el Controlador Supremo y el mejor entre todos aquellos dignos de ser adorados. Tan solo adora al tesoro de Śhrī Kṛṣṇa, el hijo del rey de Vraja.

O Govardhana! With great delight, You allow my Beloved to play with Balarāma and His friends amidst Your incomparable jeweled altars, gem-studded thrones, trees, waterfalls, caves, peaks, and valleys. Please grant me residence near you. 

O Govardhana! You make manifest the beautiful and fragrant dark altar, which is a witness to the tax-collecting pastime of the ocean of divine mellows—the youthful Divine Couple—thus bringing joy to the most discerning devotees. Please grant me residence near you. 

O Govardhana! You secretly embrace Rādhā-kuṇḍa—the unique and most beloved friend of Hari—and thus confidentially witness the pastimes of the divine youthful couple there. Please grant me residence near you. 

O Govardhana! You constantly nourish the cows with your fresh grass, pure water, and the shade of your trees at every step, thus making your name meaningful throughout the three worlds. Please grant me residence near you. 

O Govardhana! By providing refuge in your form as a new home, you protected the cowherd village from the prolonged wrath of Indra, and thus received great honor from Kṛṣṇa, the enemy of Agha and Baka. Please grant me residence near you. 

O King of Mountains! The nectar of your name—“the best among the servants of Hari”—emanated from the moon-like face of Śrī Rādhā, and the Vedas clearly declare you to be the ornament of Vraja. Please grant me residence near you. 

O Govardhana! You are the sole bestower of happiness upon the cowherd men, animals, and birds of Vraja, who are saturated with the mellow of friendship with Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa and Their associates. Due to your boundless compassion, please accept me and grant me residence near you. 

O Govardhana! By the causelessly merciful son of Śacī, who is most dear to you, I—who am deceitful and wicked—have been offered to you. Therefore, disregarding my fitness or unfitness, please grant me residence near you. 

One who diligently recites these ten verses—which bestow divine mellows in praise of Śrīla Govardhana, the chief of all mountains—will quickly attain residence in this blissful place and directly achieve the jewel of service to the auspicious Divine Couple.

IDX.en_translation:
O Hari Nama! the Tips of Thy Lotus Feet have eternally been adored by the glowing radiance diffused from the gemmed chaplets of the Upanishads, the crest jewels of the Vedas. Thou art eternally worshipped by the liberated souls. O Hari Nama! clearing myself of all offences, I entirely take shelter in Thee. 

O Holy Name! all glory to Thee who art eternally chanted by the saints. To confer eternal bliss upon the people Thou hast appeared before them as the Transcendental Word. Thou killest all sorts of terrible sufferings of him who happens to chant even Thy dimly reflected Name known as Namabhasa. 

O Sun of Blessed Name! even the slightest reflection of Thy Radiant Self is suficient to dispel the gloom of ignorance from the minds of those who are steeped in the foul sink of worldliness, and confer spiritual vision of pure devotion on those who are blind of the inner sight. Who is there so expert in the world that can sing the glories of Thy Name to finish? 

O Holy Name! the seed of deeds, which necessitates rebirth for their fruition, is not totally destroyed despite veritable at-one-ment with Brahman by dint of constant meditation. But O Name! no sooner dost Thou gain a free scope on the tongue of Thy chanter than all the seeds of deeds of his prenatal existence are destroyed. Such the Vedas loudly declare. 

O Killer of the demon Agha! O Son of Yashoda! O Son of Nanda! O Lotus-Eyed! O Moon of the Gopees! O Lord of Brindaban! O Merciful to the bowed! O Kṛṣṇa! Thou hast manifested Thy self in such various Forms out of Thy infinite mercy. Let my ardour of love go on increasing, in a great measure, for Thee. 

O Holy Name! Thou hast a double Form, viz., Vachya (Signified) i.e., the Transcendental Personality, and Vachaka (Significant) i. e., the Transcendental Word or Name- such Kṛṣṇa, Govinda, etc., -identical with the Vachya. To us the latter Vachaka is more compassionate than the former Vachya against whom we fallen souls as have sinned. Because as soon as we chant the Vachaka, i.e., Thy Holy Name, keeping clear of offences against the Name, we are at once immersed the blissful ocean of Divine Love. 

O Holy Name! O Kṛṣṇa! Thou killest the offences of Thy devotees who have taken shelter in Thy Lotus Feet. Thou art veritable Living Entity of the most Beautiful self conscious concentrated Bliss. Thou art, O Name! the Entity of the great Rejoicings of Gokula. O Kṛṣṇa! I offer my humble greetings, time and again, to Thee- the Divine Form of all Exquisiteness in the fullest degree. 

O Holy Name of Kṛṣṇa! Thou art the very life of Narada’s guitar and the Elixir of the ambrosial ripples of the ocean surcharged with Divine mellowness. I beseech Thee, O Holy Name! do Thou ever find a full scope in my tongue with all the ardour of Divine Love.

I offer my obeisances to the sacred feet of Keśava, which are the desired treasure of the eternally liberated souls, the wish-fulfilling tree worshiped by the giver of wealth (Kuvera), and which wander in the spiritual abode adorned with trees. 

I offer my obeisances to the sacred feet of Keśava, which revealed the excellent abode of Kuliyā (Navadvīpa) like the boar incarnation, and which destroyed the darkness of the mass of accumulated sins. 

I offer my obeisances to the sacred feet of Keśava, which are beautiful with the art of loving emotions fond of dancing, which are the eternal Lord shining in the eternal abode, and which are the jewel of accomplishment in the ocean of Prabhupāda's mellows. 

I offer my obeisances to the sacred feet of Keśava, which are devoted to renunciation like Raghunātha Dāsa, which are the divine form of the supreme blazing attachment (ujjvala-rāga), and which are the best of gods, pleasing and satisfying the surfactant gods. 

I offer my obeisances to the sacred feet of Keśava, which hold the internal mood of Prabhupāda, which are a human form devoid of the dull enjoyments of the earth, and which are full of the ecstatic emotions of the pastimes of the human-like form. 

I offer my obeisances to the sacred feet of Keśava, whose feet are a holy place giving fearlessness to the surrendered, which deliver the fallen souls who have taken shelter of them, and which remove the material existence of the living entities eager to cross over. 

I offer my obeisances to the sacred feet of Keśava, who is the shelter of the disciples devoted to the mood of their father (guru), who is the best of the peaceful, arranging for their destination and liberation, and whose feet are the auspicious destination for the wicked who have surrendered. 

I offer my obeisances to the sacred feet of Keśava, who holds new fame in the assembly of vedanta, who is devoted to Lord Gaura, the deliverer of the people of the earth. I bow to the dust of his lotus feet, which are worshipable by others.

Cuando regresa del bosque de Vraja, Él lleva pendientes de flores priyaka, una corona de mālatī en flor y un cordón brahmánico hecho de pequeños y encantadores jazmines. Yo adoro al Señor Keśhava. 

Cuando regresa del bosque de Vraja, Él llama alegremente a Sus vacas surabhi extraviadas: “¡Piśhāṅgī! ¡Maṇikastanī! ¡Praṇataśhṛṅgī! ¡Piṅgekṣaṇā! ¡Mṛdaṅgamukhī! ¡Dhūmalā! ¡Śhabalī! ¡Haṁsī! ¡Vaṁsī! ¡Priyā!”. Yo adoro al Señor Keśhava. 

Cuando regresa del bosque por los senderos de Vraja, con palabras sublimes hace sonreír y reír a Sus afectuosos amigos, los cuales están espléndidamente ataviados y son expertos en el arte de las placenteras bromas y ocurrencias. 

Cuando regresa del bosque de Vraja, Sus mejillas son lamidas por regueros de transpiración, está decorado con pinturas dibujadas con minerales de colores procedentes de la colina, y Sus rizos eclipsan el esplendor de un enjambre de abejorros negros. Yo adoro al Señor Keśhava. 

Cuando regresa del bosque de Vraja, con el dulce sonido de Su flauta llama a las vacas surabhi, las cuales, en su ansiedad por ver a sus terneros, desgarran la tierra con sus pesadas y danzantes pezuñas. Yo adoro al Señor Keśhava. 

Cuando regresa del bosque de Vraja, Él embellece el camino con Sus huellas. Lleva una guirnalda de polvo levantada por las vacas, y Sus ropas y Su pluma de pavo real se mecen con las ondas del viento. Yo adoro al Señor Keśhava. 

A Su regreso del bosque, Él deleita los corazones de las reinas de Vraja y satura de dicha a todas las gopīs en sus casas con la juguetona y dulce música de Su flauta. Él hace que sus vellos se ericen de felicidad. Yo adoro al Señor Keśhava. 

Cuando regresa del bosque de Vraja, Él es adorado por las gopīs, las cuales están subidas en las terrazas de sus palacios y se encuentran con Él en el camino mediante cientos de modos de lanzar miradas y suaves sonrisas. Como grandes abejorros negros, los rabillos de Sus ojos revolotean alrededor de los pechos de las gopīs. Yo adoro al Señor Keśhava. 

Que Kṛṣṇa, el amigo de Viśhākhā, proporcione felicidad trascendental y amor incondicional por Sus pies de loto a la persona sumamente inteligente que lea con atención estos ocho versos, los cuales constituyen un glorioso festival para todas las gopīs.

Whatever you have understood as good, spend your time with that. Without devotion, there is no fruit; you cannot know the essence through argument.

Worshiping Kṛṣṇa by taking shelter of His form, if I become absorbed in love for God—then, O brother, tell me, what will remain unattainable?

Detachment, dejection, pride, humility, weariness, and the madness of exertion; arrogance, fear, apprehension, and forgetfulness; agitation, laziness, and sickness; delusion, death, and inertia; bashfulness, dissimulation, and memory. 

Deliberation, mental fickleness, anxiety, joy, and steadfastness; fierceness, envy, sleepiness, and deep slumber—know all these groups of emotions, thirty-three in total, are recognized as transitory states. 

In the unparalleled sweet mellow, fierceness and laziness do not appear; all other emotions remain as they should. Arising in the bliss of emotional absorption, they are especially eager to move toward the permanent sentiment. 

Through the support of speech, body, and goodness, they convey the union of the mellow, like the enduring waves of an ocean. Quickly fulfilling their own purpose and making the ocean full, they then subside and are seen no more.

Seeing that the night has ended, Vṛndā-sakhī becomes anxious and devises many plans to awaken the Divine Youthful Couple. She makes various sounds, and the parrots and mynahs sing in diverse meters.

IDX.en_translation:
I shall now speak the Nṛsiṁha-kavaca, which was spoken by Prahlāda in ancient times. It gives all protection, is pious, and destroys all disturbances. 

It bestows all opulence and grants heaven and liberation. Having meditated on Nṛsiṁha, the Lord of gods, seated on a golden throne. 

With open mouth, three eyes, and luster like the autumn moon; embraced by Lakṣmī on His left side, and surrounded by opulences. 

Four-armed, with soft limbs, adorned with golden earrings; with a chest beautified by a lotus, and marked with jeweled armlets. 

Resembling molten gold, wearing yellow, spotless garments; the crest-jewel of Indra and the gods, with the brilliance of shining rubies. 

His two feet shine with weapons like the conch and disc; He is praised by Garuḍa with humility and joy. 

Having placed Him in the lotus of one’s own heart, one should recite the Kavaca. May Nṛsiṁha, who appeared for the protection of the world, protect my head. 

May He who is all-pervading and resides in the pillar protect the fruit of my words. May Nṛsiṁha, whose eyes are the moon, sun, and fire, protect my eyes. 

May Nṛhari, who is dear to the prayers of the best of sages, protect my memory. May Siṁha-nāsa protect my nose, and He who is dear to the face of Lakṣmī protect my face. 

May the Lord of all knowledge, Nṛsiṁha, protect my tongue. May He whose face is like the moon and who is always worshiped by Prahlāda protect my mouth. 

May Nṛsiṁha protect my neck, and the Sustainer of the earth and Maker of Ananta protect my shoulders. May Nṛsiṁha, whose arms are adorned with divine weapons, protect my arms. 

May Nṛsiṁha, the bestower of boons to the gods, protect my hands from all sides. May Hari, who is attainable by yogīs, protect my heart, His residence. 

May He who tore open the chest and abdomen of Hiraṇyākṣa protect my middle. May Nṛhari protect my navel, He who is praised by Brahmā who sits on His own navel. 

May He in whose hips are millions of universes protect my hips. May He who sees the secret form of the secret mantras protect my private parts. 

May Manobhava protect my thighs, and He who appears in a human form protect my knees. May the Man-Lion, who removes the burden of the earth, protect my calves. 

May the Lord Nṛhari, the giver of the kingdom of the gods, protect my feet. May the Thousand-headed Person protect my body entirely. 

May the Ferocious One protect me from the East, and the Elder Brother of the Great Hero (Maha-vīra-agraja) from the Southeast (Agni). May Mahā-viṣṇu protect me from the South, and the Greatly Blazing One from the Southwest. 

May the Lord of all protect me from the West, He whose faces are in all directions. May Nṛsiṁha protect me from the Northwest, and the Ornamented Form from the North. 

May the Auspicious One, the giver of all auspiciousness, protect me from the Northeast. May the Man-Lion, the Death of death, protect me from the fear of material existence. 

This Nṛsiṁha-kavaca is adorned by the mouth of Prahlāda. One who reads it daily with devotion is freed from all sins. 

He becomes wealthy and has sons in this world, and lives a long life. Whatever desire he wishes for, he undoubtedly obtains it. 

He attains victory everywhere; he becomes victorious everywhere. It is the preventer of the influence of earthly, aerial, and celestial planets. 

It is the supreme remover of poison born of scorpions and snakes. It is the cause of driving away Brahma-rākṣasas and Yakṣas. 

Whether written on the arm or on a palm leaf, this auspicious Kavaca—if one wears it on the wrist, all his activities are perfected. 

One attains victory over one’s own self among gods, demons, and humans. A man who recites it with regulation at one sandhyā or three sandhyās (junctions of the day). 

He finds all-auspiciousness, enjoyment, and liberation. Reading thirty-two thousand times for pure souls. 

The perfection of the mantra of this Kavaca is born. By this King of Mantras, having made ashes (bhasma) with the mantras. 

One who applies the tilaka removes the fear of planets. Chanting three times and enchanting water given. 

The man who drinks the mantra and practices meditation on Nṛsiṁha—his diseases are destroyed, even those born in the abdomen. 

Roaring and making others roar, cracking the surface of the earth with His own arms, killing, ripping, and heating. Throwing and casting down the sons of Diti in heaven and on earth. Crying and causing anger, constantly destroying and filling in every direction. Seeing and filling—I bow to the Divine Lion with hundreds of multitudes of hands. 

Thus ends the Śrī Nṛsiṁha-kavaca spoken by Prahlāda in the Śrī Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa.

IDX.en_translation:
O my most merciful Śrīla Narottama Dāsa Ṭhākura! He is the very personification of divine love. How tender is his form, like a śiriṣa blossom, surpassing even the golden luster of a physical body. 

In his youth, no worldly pleasure appealed to him. Hearing the qualities of Lord Gaura, he always wept. Abandoning kingly enjoyments and with great longing, he journeyed to Vraja. 

Entering Vṛndāvana with a joyful mind, he surrendered himself to Śrīla Lokanātha Dāsa Gosvāmī. Lokanātha Dāsa, being merciful, accepted him as his own and initiated him with the Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa mantra. 

Seeing Narottama’s endeavor, everyone in Vṛndāvana was happy and showered him with affection as if he were their very life. He and Śrīnivāsa Āchārya had such a deep connection—their lives were one, and only their bodies were distinct. 

Seeing the Deity of Śrī Rādhā-vinoda, his eyes were always soothed, as Lord Lokanātha was engaged in His service. Through the study of devotional scriptures, great joy increased in his mind, and all his desires were fulfilled. 

By his Guru’s permission, he left Vraja and entered the land of Gauḍa. By the grace of his Master, he traveled to the homes of devotees in Navadvīpa and Jagannātha Purī. 

What a sweet tradition he established in the village of Khetari! He served Lord Gaura, Rādhā-ramaṇa, Śrī Vallabhīkānta, Rādhākānta, Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, and Śrī Vrajamohana. 

These six Deities seemed to be directly performing Their pastimes. Who would not be enchanted by such beauty? With his dear companion Rāmacandra, Narottama floats in the waves of the mellows of divine love. 

O Lord Gaurāṅga! O Vallabhīkānta! O Lord Kṛṣṇa! O Vrajamohana! O Rādhā-ramaṇa! O Rādhā! O Rādhākānta! I offer my obeisances unto You. 

Who can describe all the qualities of Narottama? His congregational chanting is like a shower of divine love. Advaita Āchārya, Lord Nityānanda, and Lord Gaura-candra with Their associates all dance in his kīrtana—the fortunate ones witnessed this. 

Narottama is supremely dear to the associates of Lord Gaura and is of great wisdom. His fame resounds in the service of the devotees. What an astonishingly merciful soul! To whom does he not give the spotless jewel of pure devotion? 

Even the atheistic and demoniac persons he intoxicated with the qualities of Lord Gaura, overwhelmed with ecstatic love. His supernatural activities are unique; his fame is proclaimed in every land. 

The lowly Narahari says: “Will such a day ever come when I will be completely surrendered at the feet of Narottama? Raising both arms repeatedly and crying out “O Master Narottama!”, will I weep and roll in the dust?”

nāma-aparādhāvadhi nāśhaha tāhāra

IDX.en_translation:
O Holy Name, Your glories are boundless. I repeatedly offer my obeisances at Your feet. 

You are the great festival and the ocean of bliss for Gokula. I fall at Your feet, full of longing. 

You are Kṛṣṇa in Your complete form, the source of all spiritual mellows. Falling at Your feet, I sing Your qualities. 

Whoever takes exclusive shelter at Your feet, You certainly destroy their many miseries. 

You destroy all their offenses, and You even eradicate offenses to the Holy Name. 

Washing away all faults from their heart, You sit on the throne of their heart, O supreme refuge. 

You are supremely enchanting, the embodied form of concentrated spiritual bliss. The Vedas sing Your praises, proclaiming You to be the very essence of rasa. 

Bhaktivinoda, at the feet of Rūpa Gosvāmī, always prays for the clear manifestation of the Holy Name at every moment.

IDX.en_translation:
O Lord of love! O Lord Gaura-candra! How shall I express the anguish of my soul, O Lord? I have lost my very self. 

What more can I say? I have forgotten the very purpose for which You brought me into this world. To speak of it now, after so long, fills me with regret and sorrow. 

No attachment for Your worship has arisen in me; my evil mind is always intoxicated by material illusion. By staying near materialistic people repeatedly, I have become like them. 

Who am I? Why have I come here? I never think about these things. Sometimes enjoying and sometimes renouncing, my mind only dances in deception. 

What will be my fate? I never consider it, nor do I seek the company of Your devotees. All the inauspicious signs of one who is averse to the Lord are present within me. 

By the mercy of my spiritual master, the dream is broken. Now I understand that only You are my own; Your devotees are my only true friends in this prison house of material existence. 

I shall not worship anyone but Your devotees; I take refuge in Your lotus feet. Deliver me, O Lord, from the net of illusion by grabbing this servant by the hair! 

Do You not show mercy even to sinners? Jagāi and Mādhāi were great sinners, yet I have learned that You, the Lord of love, deliver even such as them. 

I am devoid of devotion, fallen and insignificant. Please place Your two feet on the head of this offender. At Your fearless feet I take refuge forever.
IDX.es_translation:
¡Oh Gaura, Señor del prema! ¿Qué Te puedo decir de mis penas y mis sufrimientos? He olvidado mi verdadera identidad. 

¿Qué más puedo decir? Oh, mi Señor! Después de tanto tiempo hablando sobre el propósito por el cual me trajiste al mundo, estoy cansando y siento un gran pesar. 

No se ha despertado en mí atracción por el bhajana, estoy intoxicado por lo mundano e ilusorio, y mi inteligencia es siempre perversa. Por estar siempre con disfrutadores sensuales, me he vuelto igual que ellos. 

¿Quién soy? ¿Por qué estoy aquí? Mi mente nunca se hace estas preguntas. Unas veces disfrutando y otras renunciando, mi mente solo danza en el desconcierto. 

Nunca me paré a pensar cuál iba a ser mi final. Ni siquiera me acerco a los devotos de Hari. Poseo todos los malos signos de alguien hostil a Hari. 

Ahora, por la gracia de śhrī guru, he despertado del sueño ilusorio. Ahora comprendo que solo Te tengo a Ti, y que Tus asociados son mis mejores amigos en esta prisión de la existencia material. 

No adoraré a ninguna otra cosa aparte de los pies de Tus devotos. Me he refugiado en las plantas carmesí de Tus pies de loto. ¡Oh Señor!, agarra a este sirviente por el cabello y rescátalo del enredo de māyā. 

Jagāi y Mādhāi eran grandes pecadores y, aun así, los liberaste. Eso me hizo comprender, oh Señor del prema, que también liberas a los pecadores. 

Carezco de bhakti, y soy vil y desposeído. Coloca Tus pies de loto sobre la cabeza de este ofensor. Yo me refugio eternamente en Tus hermosos pies que vuelven a uno audaz.

IDX.search: ohe vaisnava thakura doyara sagara e dase koruna kori diya pada cḣaya sodho he amaya tomara charana dhori cḣaya vega domi cḣaya dosa sodhi cḣaya guna deho dase cḣaya sat sanga deho he amare bosecḣi sangera ase ekaki amara nahi paya bala hari nama sankirtane tumi krpa kori sraddha bindu diya deho krsna nama dhane krsna se tomara krsna dite paro tomara sakati acḣe ami to kangala krsna krsna boli dhai tava pacḣe pacḣe
IDX.author: sacchidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
ohe! 
vaiṣṇava ṭhākura, doyāra sāgara, 
e dāse korunā kori’ 
diyā pada-cḣāyā, śhodho he āmāya, 
tomāra charaṇa dhori 

cḣaya vega domi’, cḣaya doṣa śhodhi’, 
cḣaya guna deho’ dāse 
cḣaya sat-saṅga, deho’ he āmāre, 
bosecḣi saṅgera āśhe 

ekakī āmāra, nāhi pāya bala, 
hari-nāma-saṅkīrtane 
tumi kṛpā kori’, śhraddhā-bindu diyā, 
deho’ kṛṣṇa-nāma-dhane 

kṛṣṇa se tomāra, kṛṣṇa dite pāro, 
tomāra śhakati ācḣe 
āmi to’ kāṅgāla, “kṛṣṇa” “kṛṣṇa” boli’, 
dhāi tava pācḣe pācḣe
IDX.en_translation:
O revered Vaiṣnava Ṭhākura! O ocean of mercy! Please be merciful to me, your humble servant. Purify me by giving the shade of your lotus feet. Your feet I clasp submissively. 

Please help me to control the six urges <footnote>(speech, mind, anger, tongue, belly, and genitals)</footnote>, purify me of the six faults <footnote>(overeating or collecting more funds than required, over-endeavoring for material objectives, unnecessarily talking of mundane affairs, being too attached or too neglectful of scriptural rules and regulations, associating with worldly minded people, and lusting after mundane achievements)</footnote>, and please instill in your servant the six good qualities <footnote>(enthusiasm, patience, confidence, determination to perform activities favorable to devotional service, the resolution to abandon the association of non-devotees, and the discipline required to always follow in the footsteps of predecessor āchāryas)</footnote>. Oh, bestow upon me the six kinds of holy association! <footnote>(giving and receiving gifts, accepting and offering spiritual food, revealing one’s inner thoughts, and posing confidential questions regarding devotional service)</footnote> I am seated here in the hope of having your company. 

On my own, I find I have no strength to chant the holy name of Lord Hari. Please be merciful by awarding me with a particle of faith and giving me the great treasure of the holy name of Kṛṣṇa. 

Kṛṣṇa is yours, therefore you are able to give Him to others. This is certainly within your power. I am indeed wretched and fallen, simply running after you crying “Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa!”
IDX.es_translation:
¡Oh, Vaiṣṇava Ṭhākura! Tú eres un océano de misericordia. Muestra tu compasión a este sirviente y purifícame otorgándome la sombra de tus pies, a los cuales me aferro. 

Ayúdame a vencer los seis impulsos <footnote>(la palabra, la mente, la ira, la lengua, el estómago y los genitales)</footnote>, purifica mis seis defectos <footnote>(comer en exceso o acumular más fondos de los necesarios, esforzarme en exceso por objetivos materiales, hablar innecesariamente sobre asuntos mundanos, estar demasiado apegado o ser demasiado negligente con las reglas y regulaciones de las escrituras, asociarme con personas de mentalidad mundana y codiciar logros mundanos)</footnote>, concédeme por favor las seis cualidades de un devoto <footnote>(entusiasmo, paciencia, confianza, determinación para realizar actividades favorables al servicio devocional, la resolución de abandonar la compañía de los no devotos y la disciplina necesaria para seguir siempre los pasos de los āchāryas predecesores)</footnote>, concédeme por favor las seis cualidades de un devoto <footnote>(dar y recibir regalos, aceptar y ofrecer alimento consagrado, revelar los pensamientos íntimos y plantear preguntas confidenciales sobre el servicio devocional)</footnote> Estoy esperando con la confianza de poder obtener tu asociación. 

Solo no poseo la fuerza para hacer harināma-saṅkīrtana. Sé bondadoso y dame una gota de fe; concédeme el inestimable tesoro del kṛṣṇa-nāma. 

Kṛṣṇa es tuyo, de modo que tienes el poder de dar a Kṛṣṇa. Yo no soy más que un mendigo que corre detrás de ti clamando: “¡Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa!”

IDX.author: śhukadeva gosvāmī
IDX.verses:
oṁ ity uccḣārato moha-nidrā dūraṁ palāyate 
tayā grastaṁ jagannātha! trāhi māṁ madhusūdana 

na gatir-vidyate nātha! tvam-eva śharaṇaṁ mama 
pāpa-paṅke nimagno‛smi trāhi māṁ madhusūdana 

mohito‛jñāna-tamasā putra-dāra gṛhādiṣu 
tṛṣṇayā pīḍyamāno‛smi trāhi māṁ madhusūdana! 

bhakti-hīna dīnañcha duḥkha-śhokāturaṁ prabho! 
anāśhrayamanāthañcha trāhi māṁ madhusūdana! 

gatāgatena śhrānto‛smi dīrgha-saṁsāra-vartmasu 
purnanāgantumiccḣāmi trāhi māṁ madhusūdana! 

vahavo hi mayā dṛṣṭvā joni dvāraḥ pṛthak pṛthak 
garbhavāsa-mahāduḥkhāt trāhi māṁ madhusūdana! 

tena deva! prapanno‛smi trāṇārthastvat-parāyaṇaḥ 
duḥkhārṇava nimagno‛haṁ trāhi māṁ madhusūdana! 

vāchā jaccḣa pratijñātaṁ karmaṇā nopapāditaṁ 
tatpāpāvdhinimagno‛smi trāhi māṁ madhusūdana! 

sukṛtaṁ na kṛtaṁ kiñchidduṣkṛtañcha kṛtaṁ mayā 
saṁsārārṇava-magno‛smi trāhi māṁ madhusūdana! 

dehāntara-sahaśhreṣu prāpitaṁ bhramatā mayā 
tiryaktva mānuṣatvañcha trāhi māṁ madhusūdana! 

vāchayāmi jathonmattaḥ pralapāmi tavāgrataḥ 
jarāmaraṇa-bhīto‛smi trāhi māṁ madhusūdana! 

jatra jatra cha jāto‛smi strīṣu vā puruṣeṣu vā 
dehi tatrāchalāṁ bhakti trāhi māṁ madhusūdana! 

gatvā gatvā nivartante chandra-sūryādayo grahāḥ 
kadāpi na nivartante dvādaśhākṣara-chinantakāḥ 

santi stotrāṇi vahavo vāñcḣitārtha pradāni vai 
dvādaśhārṇāt paraṁ nāsti vāsudevena bhāṣitaṁ 

dvādaśhārṇat mahāstotraṁ sarva-kāma-fala-pradaṁ 
garbhavāsa-nirāsāya śhukena paribhāṣitaṁ 

dvādaśhārṇaṁ nirāhāro jaḥ paṭhet harivāsare 
sa gaccḣed vaiṣṇavaṁ dhāma jatra jogeśhvara hariḥ 

iti śhrīla-śhukadeva-gosvāmi-virachitaṁ 
śhrīmadhusūdana-stotraṁ sampūrṇaṁ
IDX.en_translation:
By the utterance of “Om”, the sleep of illusion flees far away. O Lord of the Universe! I am seized by that. Save me, O Madhusūdana! 

There is no other goal, O Lord! You alone are my shelter. I am drowned in the mud of sin. Save me, O Madhusūdana! 

Bewildered by the darkness of ignorance, absorbed in son, wife, home, etc., I am tormented by thirst. Save me, O Madhusūdana! 

Devoid of devotion and destitute, afflicted with misery and grief, O Lord! Shelterless and helpless, save me, O Madhusūdana! 

I am exhausted by coming and going on the long paths of material existence. I do not wish to come again. Save me, O Madhusūdana! 

Many doors of the womb have been seen by me, one by one. From the great misery of residence in the womb, save me, O Madhusūdana! 

Therefore, O God! I am surrendered, devoted to You for the sake of deliverance. I am drowned in the ocean of misery. Save me, O Madhusūdana! 

Whatever was promised by speech was not accomplished by action. I am drowned in that ocean of sin. Save me, O Madhusūdana! 

No pious deed was done by me, but sin was done. I am drowned in the ocean of material existence. Save me, O Madhusūdana! 

Obtained by me wandering in thousands of other bodies—animal-ness and human-ness—save me, O Madhusūdana! 

I speak like a madman, I prattle before You. I am afraid of old age and death. Save me, O Madhusūdana! 

Wherever I have been born, among women or among men, give me unalloyed devotion there. Save me, O Madhusūdana! 

Having gone, having gone, the moon, sun, and other planets return. Those who think of the Twelve Syllables never return. 

There are many Stotras granting desired objects indeed. There is nothing superior to the Twelve Syllables spoken by Vāsudeva. 

The great Stotra of the Twelve Syllables, bestowing the fruit of all desires, was spoken by Śuka for the removal of residence in the womb. 

He who recites the Twelve Syllables without food on the day of Hari goes to the abode of Viṣṇu where Hari, the Lord of Yoga, is. 

Thus ends the Śrī Madhusūdana Stotra composed by Śrīla Śukadeva Gosvāmī.

IDX.search: ore bhai krsna se e tina loka bandhu jiva nija karme bandha mayate padiya andha uddharite karunara sindhu nija sakti gunagana saba name samarpana nyunadhika nahika vichara nama nami bheda nai namera gune nami pai nama kare helaya uddhara nahi kalakala tara suchi ki asuchi ara nama laite nisedha na ithe ki mora durdaiva haya hena se dayalu paya anuraga na janmila tate ore mana paye padi asat prayasa cḣadi krsna krsna kaha anuksana e bada sulabha ati name jadi kara priti tabe premanandera nandana
IDX.author: premānanda-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
ore bhāi! kṛṣṇa se e tina-loka-bandhu 
jīva nija-karme bandha, māyāte paḍiyā andha, 
uddhārite karuṇāra sindhu 

nija-śhakti-guṇagaṇa, saba ‘nāme’ samarpaṇa, 
nyūnādhika nāhika vichāra 
nāma-nāmī bheda nāi, nāmera guṇe nāmī pāi, 
nāma kare helāya uddhāra 

nāhi kālākāla tā’ra, śhuchi ki aśhuchi āra, 
nāma laite niṣedha nā ithe 
ki mora durdaiva hāya, hena se dayālu-pāya, 
anurāga nā janmila tā’te 

ore mana! pāye paḍi, asat prayāsa cḣāḍi’, 
‘kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa’ kaha anukṣaṇa 
e baḍa sulabha ati, nāme jadi kara prīti, 
tabe premānandera nandana
IDX.en_translation:
O brothers! Lord Kṛṣṇa is the only friend of these three worlds. The individual soul is bound by its own past actions and is fallen into illusion and blinded. He is an ocean of mercy to deliver us. 

The Lord has surrendered all His own potencies and qualities to His Name; there is no consideration of more or less. There is no difference between the Name and the Lord Himself; by the qualities of the Name we obtain the Lord, for the Name easily delivers us. 

There is no consideration of time or place for it, nor of purity or impurity; there is no prohibition in chanting the Name. Alas! What is my misfortune! At the feet of such a merciful Lord, no attachment has arisen in me. 

O my mind! I fall at your feet—abandoning all useless endeavors, chant “Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa!” constantly. This is very easily obtained; if you develop love for the Name, then you will experience true divine love and bliss.

IDX.verses:
ore mana! āra ki hoibe hena janma 
nā jāni ki puṇya-fale, mānuṣa-uttama-kule, 
hele jā’ra nā bujhile marma 

dekha āyu-saṁkhyā jata, nidrāte ardheka gata, 
chauṭhi roga-śhoka-apakathā 
chauṭhi vidyā-dhane-māne, kāma-krodha-durvāsane, 
hāsya-kautuke gela vṛthā 

satya-tretā-dvāparete, bahu āyu cḣila tāte, 
vinā saṁkhyā-pūrṇa mṛtyu nāi 
kata kari’ pariśhrama, ācharita juga-dharma, 
dhyāna jajñārchana bhari āi 

ebe kali alpa āi, śhateka vatsara bhāi, 
seha dṛḍha nahe nirūpaṇa 
tā goṅāli micḣā kāje, ki balibi kon lāje, 
jabe tore sudhābe śhamana 

emana sulabha kali, jāte ‘hare kṛṣṇa’ bali, 
hena nāme nā karili rati 
premānanda kahe puni, e chaurāśhīlakṣa joni, 
bhramāibe kateka durgati
IDX.en_translation:
O my mind! Will such a birth ever happen again? I do not know by what great piety you obtained this excellent human birth, but you have negligently failed to understand its true purpose. 

Observe that half of your life is spent in sleep, and a fourth is lost to disease, sorrow, and useless talk. Another fourth is consumed by the pursuit of learning, wealth, and honor, or lost to lust, anger, and evil desires. Thus, it passes in vain. 

In previous ages, life was very long and death did not come prematurely. Much effort was made then to perform the duties of the age through meditation, sacrifice, and worship. 

But in the Age of Kali, life is short—perhaps a hundred years, and even that is not certain. Still, you waste it in useless activities. What will you say, and with what shame, when the God of Death questions you? 

This Age of Kali is so beneficial because one can simply chant “Hare Kṛṣṇa!” yet you have not developed love for such a Name. Premānanda says: “The cycle of eight million four hundred thousand species will make you wander through endless misfortune.”

IDX.first_line: ore mana bhāviyā nā bujha āpanāke
IDX.search: ore mana bhaviya na bujha apanake jara lagi duhkha kara svadese videse fira se jana ki sukha dibe toke javat samarthya acḣe tavat tomara kacḣe javat aniya deha artha jakhana se gandha nai dakile na sune bhai na pucḣe dekhile asamartha avastha dekhiya hase bhala katha manda vase banka mukhe o naka tolai ksudhaya na deya bhata tate ara katu vata kahe eki hoila balai dine dine khata rati kise ara pita pati parijane na kara badai jeba age joda hate tara sunaya nirghate e samaye bandhu ke re bhai parake apana kari bhebe mali janma bhari ke tumi tomara acḣe keba premananda kahe mati krsna vina nahi gati kaha krsna e duhkha tariba
IDX.author: premānanda-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
ore mana! bhāviyā nā bujha āpanāke 
jā’ra lāgi’ duḥkha kara, svadeśhe videśhe fira, 
se-jana ki sukha dibe toke 

jāvat sāmarthya ācḣe, tāvat tomāra kācḣe, 
jāvat āniyā deha artha 
jakhana se gandha nāi, ḍākile nā śhune bhāi, 
nā pucḣe, dekhile asamartha 

avasthā dekhiyā hāse, bhāla kathā manda vāse, 
bāṅkā-mukhe o nāka-tolāi 
kṣudhāya nā deya bhāta, tā’te āra kaṭu vāta, 
kahe eki hoila bālāi 

dine dine khāṭa rati, kise āra pitā pati, 
parijane nā kara baḍāi 
jebā āge joḍa-hāte, tā’rā śhunāya nirghāte, 
e samaye bandhu ke re bhāi 

parake āpana kari, bhebe mali janma bhari, 
ke tumi, tomāra ācḣe kebā? 
premānanda kahe mati, ‘kṛṣṇa’ vinā nāhi gati, 
kaha ‘kṛṣṇa’-e duḥkha taribā
IDX.en_translation:
O my mind! Reflect deeply and understand your situation. The ones for whom you grieve, wandering everywhere—how will those people ever give you true happiness? 

As long as you have strength and provide wealth, they are with you. But when that usefulness is gone, if you call, they won’t even listen, brother; they won’t even inquire about you when they see you are helpless. 

Seeing your plight, they will laugh, and your good words will seem bitter to them. With a crooked face and an upturned nose, they won’t even give you food when you are hungry, and they will add harsh words, saying: “What a nuisance this person has become!” 

Day by day, their affection for you will wane. What good are family members then? Do not rely on them. Those who once stood with folded hands will now speak harshly, saying: “Who is your friend at this time, O brother?” 

Treating others as your own, you have wasted your entire life. Who are you, and who truly belongs to you? Premānanda says: “Without Lord Kṛṣṇa, there is no refuge. Say “Kṛṣṇa!” and you will overcome this sorrow.”

IDX.search: ore mana dhana jana jivana yauvana ei acḣe ei nai chakse kina dekha tai tumi kise balicḣa apana nisira svapana jena e dhana sampada tena tileke sakali bhai micḣe dekhiya na dekha kene suniya na suna kane ki lagi cḣadite nara iccḣe kanya putra jata ithi marile se jaya kathi ki jani kothaya tumi jao mithya mora mora kara ratridina bhavi mara para lagi apana harao kiba ara anya para apana e kalevara se nahi tomara sange jaya pacḣu nahi dekha eva tora lagi kande keba kara lagi kara haya haya jeba hoiyacḣe ayu se matra nasara vayu sariya padile ara nai kiba vrddha kiba vala nahi tara kalakala kotha thake jauvana badai e sakala janra maya tanre kena bhula bhaya janra name tribhuvana tare premananda kahe jadi krsna kaha niravadhi tabe ki e jana ara mare
IDX.author: premānanda-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
ore mana! dhana-jana-jīvana-yauvana 
ei ācḣe ei nāi, chakṣe kinā dekha tāi, 
tumi kise balicḣa āpana 

niśhira svapana jena, e dhana-sampada tena, 
tileke sakali bhāi micḣe 
dekhiyā nā dekha kene, śhuniyā nā śhuna kāṇe, 
ki lāgi cḣāḍite nāra iccḣe 

kanyā putra jata ithi, marile se jāya kathi, 
ki jāni kothāy tumi jāo 
mithyā ‘mora mora’ kara, rātridina bhāvi’ mara, 
para lāgi’ āpanā hārāo 

kibā āra anya para, āpanā e kalevara, 
se nāhi tomāra saṅge jāya 
pācḣu nāhi dekha evā, tora lāgi kānde kebā, 
kāra lāgi kara hāya hāya 

jebā hoiyācḣe āyu, se mātra nāsāra vāyu, 
sariyā paḍile āra nāi 
kibā vṛddha kibā vāla, nāhi tāra kālākāla, 
kothā thāke jauvana-baḍāi 

e-sakala jāṅra māyā, tāṅre kena bhula bhāyā, 
jāṅra nāme tribhuvana tare 
premānanda kahe jadi, ‘kṛṣṇa’ kaha niravadhi, 
tabe ki e jana āra mare
IDX.en_translation:
O my mind! Wealth, family, life, and youth—they are here one moment and gone the next. Do you not see this with your own eyes? How then can you call them your own? 

These wealth and possessions are just like a dream in the night. In an instant, O brother, it is all revealed to be false. Why do you see yet remain blind? Why do you hear yet remain deaf? For what reason can you not abandon your worldly desires? 

All your children—where will they go when you die? And who knows where you yourself will go? Falsely you say “mine, mine,” and you worry and die in such thoughts. For the sake of others, you lose yourself. 

What to speak of others? Even this very body of yours does not go with you. Do you not see what remains behind? Who will truly cry for you? For whom do you lament so much? 

Whatever life you have is merely the breath in your nostrils. Once it leaves, it is no more. Whether you are old or young, there is no fixed time for death. Where then remains the pride of youth? 

All of this is the illusion of Lord Kṛṣṇa. Why do you forget Him, O brother? By His Name, the three worlds are delivered. Premānanda says: “If you chant the Name of Kṛṣṇa constantly, then how can you ever really die?”

ore mana dhikre tomāya 
pāiyā manuṣya janma, nā chintile kṛṣṇa karma, 
vṛthā janma gelare khelāya 

kateka sukṛti-fale, mānuṣa uttama kule, 
tāhāte bhāratavarṣe janma 
dhanya kaliyuga tā’te, śhrī-kṛṣṇachaitanya jā’te, 
prakāśhilā nāma mātra dharma 

pāye dhari cḣāḍa bhrama, kicḣu nāhi pariśhrama, 
kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kaha avirāma 
kaha lakṣa kathā āna, tāhe nā āsila jñāna, 
ki bhāra ki bojhā kṛṣṇa-nāma 

e jadi nā śhuna bhāi, tabe āra gati nāi, 
hena janma nā hoibe āra

IDX.en_translation:
O my mind! Shame on you! Having received a human birth, you did not think of the service of Lord Kṛṣṇa; your life passed in vain in mere play. 

Due to the results of many pious deeds, you were born as a human in a noble family, and furthermore, you were born in the sacred land of Bhārata. Blessed is this Age of Kali, where Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya revealed the religious practice of only the Holy Name. 

I beg you, give up your illusion—there is no great effort involved. Just constantly chant “Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa!” You speak a million other things, but no knowledge comes from them. What is the burden, what is the weight of Kṛṣṇa’s Name? 

If you do not listen to this, O brother, then there is no other path. Such a birth will not come again. Śrīla Premānanda Dāsa says: “If you do not worship Lord Kṛṣṇa now, then even in millions of cosmic ages there will be no liberation.”

jadi jaya karibe śhamana 
kṛṣṇa-nāma gaḍa kari’, sādhugaṇa-śhūra bhari’, 
tāra mājhe raha anukṣaṇa 

tribhuvane jei ālā, tilaka, tulasī-mālā,

O my mind! Now you will understand the gravity of your situation. The God of Death is angered, and his messengers will bind you to correct your unrighteousness. 

If you heed my words, then save yourself if you wish to conquer death. Make the Name of Lord Kṛṣṇa your fortress, fill yourself with the valor of the saintly, and remain there constantly. 

Hold firmly to the light of the three worlds—the tilaka markings and the necklace of Tulasī beads. Seeing these, the messengers of death will bow their heads and retreat. 

Remain seated with a joyful heart under the canopy of your Spiritual Master’s merciful shade. Proclaiming everywhere that you are the eternal servant of Lord Kṛṣṇa, beat the drum of victory. Premānanda says: “Who then is there to fear?”

IDX.author: premānanda-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
ore mana! ebe tora e kemana rīta 
je karme āili hethā, se-saba rahila kothā, 
ebe je dekhiye viparīta 

kṛṣṇa-karma lāgi’ kara, tāhe kena barbvara, 
se-kare parera vitta hara 
se avaśha nahe kene, ki susāra bahu dāne, 
tāhe āra kara vā nā kara 

mukhe ka’be ‘hṛṣīkeśha’, tāhe jadi sādhu-dveṣa, 
tabe bakramukha kene noo 
agni diyā hena mukha, poḍā’le nā ghuche dukha, 
tāhe ‘kṛṣṇa’ koo vā nā koo 

bhramite kṛṣṇera tīrtha, padera nā ehi kṛtya, 
tāhe jadi para-dāre chala 
ki kāja padera ei, paṅgu kene nahe sei, 
tabe tīrthe gela vā nā gela 

kṛṣṇa-līlā-guṇa-kathā, karṇete śhunibe jathā, 
tāhe jadi ku-kathāya bhora 
jadi āra sādhu-nindā, śhuniyā bāḍaye śhraddhā, 
se kāṇa badhira hou tora 

guru-kṛṣṇa-vaiṣṇava-mūrti, dekhibe kariyā ārti, 
se jadi dekhaye para-dāre 
asantoṣa sādhu dekhi’, kena vidhi hena āṅkhi, 
āśhu andha nā kare tāhāre 

tumi kṛṣṇa-smṛti-kāje, janmilā saṁsāra-mājhe, 
tāhā cḣāḍi’ dhane-jane āśha 
tabe jīye kibā kāja, paḍuka tora muṇḍe bāja, 
kene āra nahe sarvanāśha 

premānanda kahe mana, ‘kṛṣṇa’ kaha anukṣaṇa, 
kene bhula āpanāra prabhu 
mukhe ‘hari hari’ bala, sadāi ānande dola, 
tina-loke duḥkha nahe kabhu
IDX.en_translation:
O my mind! What kind of conduct is this of yours now? The spiritual deeds for which you came here—where have they all gone? Now you show only the opposite. 

You are meant to engage in Lord Kṛṣṇa’s service—why then are you so barbaric? You spend your time stealing the wealth of others. Why are you not subdued? What good is giving much in charity if your heart is not right? 

With your mouth you say “Hṛṣīkeśa,” but if there is hatred for the saintly in your heart, then why is your mouth not crooked? Even if such a mouth is burned with fire, the sorrow does not end, whether you say “Kṛṣṇa” or not. 

To wander to the holy places of Lord Kṛṣṇa is the duty of your feet—but if with them you go to the wife of another, what is the use of those feet? Why are they not lame? Whether they went to holy places or not would then make no difference. 

The pastimes and qualities of Lord Kṛṣṇa should be heard with the ears—but if instead you are engrossed in evil talk, or if by hearing blasphemy of the saintly your faith increases, then may those ears of yours be deaf. 

You should look upon the forms of the Guru, Kṛṣṇa, and the devotees with earnest longing—but if instead your eyes look with lust at the wife of another, or if you look upon a saintly person with dissatisfaction, why does destiny not quickly make you blind? 

You were born into this material world for the purpose of remembering Lord Kṛṣṇa, but leaving that aside, you only desire wealth and people. Then what is the use of living? May thunder strike your head; why is there not total destruction? 

Premānanda says: “O my mind! Chant “Kṛṣṇa!” always. Why do you forget your own Lord? Say “Hari! Hari!” with your mouth and always sway in bliss—then there will never be any sorrow in the three worlds.”

ore mana! kena hena bujha viparīta 
daṇḍe pale āyukṣaya, tāte tora bodha naya, 
āise dina ithe haraṣita 

dine māse avde bāḍha, aicḣe jāniyācḣa daḍha, 
ghāṭe ke, tā bujhite nā pāra 
nāye chaḍi’ chāha kule, dekha jena pṛthvī chale, 
tumi je chalicḣa tā nā hera 

dhana jana āpanāra, se nā bhāviyācḣa sāra, 
se ki tora, jāna nā se kāra 
tileke kāḍiyā laya, jāre iccḣā tāre deya, 
nahe tumi marileo tāra 

vṛthā ahaṅkāre mara, vichāriyā pūrvāpara, 
sādhujana-pathete dāṅḍāo 
manuṣya durlabha janma, kena kara apakarma, 
kare ratna pāiyā felāo 

jāvata sāmarthya ācḣe, jarā nā āsicḣe kācḣe, 
‘kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa’ kaha avirāma 
jarāya bhāṅgibe tanu, sarvendriya habe kṣīṇu, 
tabe ki sfuribe kṛṣṇa-nāma 

nahe vā kakhane jāi, kicḣu nirūpaṇa nāi, 
tile eka nāhika viśhvāsa 
premānanda kahe bhāi, kaha ‘kṛṣṇa’, byāja nāi, 
e jīvana kevala niśhvāsa
IDX.en_translation:
O my mind! Why do you understand things so incorrectly? Moment by moment, your life is declining, but you do not perceive it; instead, you are happy as the days pass by. 

You firmly believe that the days, months, and years are increasing for you, but you do not understand who is truly diminishing. Sitting in a boat, you look at the shore and think the earth is moving, but you do not see that it is actually you who are moving. 

You consider your wealth and family to be your own and essential to you. But are they truly yours? You do not even know to whom they really belong. In a moment they can be taken away and given to someone else; even after you die, they will not belong to you. 

You are dying in vain pride—consider your past and future and stand on the path of the saintly. This human birth is rare; why do you commit sinful acts? It is like throwing away a jewel after finally finding it in your hand. 

As long as you have strength and old age has not yet approached, chant “Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa!” incessantly. In old age, your body will break and all your senses will weaken; will the Name of Kṛṣṇa then appear in your mind? 

No one knows when death will come; there is no certainty at all. There is not a single moment of assurance. Premānanda says: “O brother! Chant “Kṛṣṇa!” without any delay, for this life is merely a single breath.”

ore mana! ki bhaya śhamane kari āra 
jadi kṛṣṇa-pade rati, ki karibe pitṛ-pati, 
ihā kene nā kara vichāra 

je pada bharasā kari’, brahmā sṛṣṭi-adhikārī, 
je-pada vāñcḣaye pañchānana 
je pade gaṅgāra janma, lakṣmī jāne jā’ra marma, 
aharniśhi smare anukṣaṇa 

dhruva-ādi je prasāde, jogīndra dharaye hṛde, 
munigaṇa je-pada dheyāya 
draupadī prahlāda kari, je-pada hṛdaye smari, 
dekha kata saṅkaṭa eḍāya 

jadi kara nija kāja, mitra habe dharmarāja, 
vṛthā chinta asāra-saṁsāra 
kahe dīna premānanda, chinta kṛṣṇa-padadvandva, 
tribhuvane śhatru nahe āra
IDX.en_translation:
O my mind! What further fear do you have of the God of Death? If you have deep attachment for the lotus feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa, what can the Lord of the Dead do to you? Why do you not consider this? 

Relying on those lotus feet, Lord Brahmā became the master of creation. Those same feet are desired by the five-faced Lord Śiva. From those feet the River Ganges was born, and the Goddess of Fortune knows their true essence and remembers them day and night. 

By the grace of those feet, Dhruva Mahārāja and the great kings among the yogīs hold them in their hearts, and all the sages meditate upon them. Consider how many dangers were averted by Draupadī and Prahlāda Mahārāja just by remembering those lotus feet. 

If you perform your true duty of devotion, the King of Death will become your friend. You are worrying uselessly about this worthless material world. The humble Premānanda says: “Meditate upon the twin lotus feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa, and you will have no more enemies in the three worlds.”
