IDX.verses: rāgera bhajana-patha, kahi ebe abhimata, loka veda-sāra ei vāṇī sakhīra anugā hañā, vraje siddhadeha pāñā, ei bhāve juḍābe parāṇī śhrī-rādhikāra sakhī jata, tāhā nā kahiba kata, mukhya sakhī kariyā gaṇana lalitā, viśhākhā tathā, suchitrā, champakalatā, raṅgadevī, sudevī kathana tuṅgavidyā, indurekhā, ei aṣṭasakhī lekhā, ebe kahi narma-sakhīgaṇa iho sevā-sahacharī, ‘priya-preṣṭha’ nāma dhari’ prema-sevā kare anukṣaṇa (samasnehā viṣama snehā, nā kariha dui lehā, kahi mātra adhikasnehāgaṇa nirantara thāke saṅge, kṛṣṇakathā līlāraṅge, narmasakhī ei saba jana ) śhrī-rasamañjarī āra, śhrī-ratimañjarī sāra, lavaṅgamañjarī, mañjunālī lavaṅgamañjarī-saṅge, kastūrikā-ādi raṅge, premasevā kare kutūhalī e-sabāra anugā hañā, premasevā niba chāñā, iṅgite bujhiba saba kāje rūpe guṇe ḍagamagī, sadā haba anurāgī, vasati kariba sakhāmājhe vṛndāvane dui jana, chāridike sakhīgaṇa, samayera sevā-rasa-sukhe sakhīra iṅgita habe, chāmara ḍhulāba tabe, tāmbūla jogāba chāṅda mukhe yugala charaṇa sevi, nirantara ei bhāvi, anurāge thākiba sadāya sādhane bhāviba jāhā, siddha dehe pāba tāhā, rāgapathera ei se upāya sādhane je dhana chāi, siddhadehe tāhā pāi, pakvāpakva mātra se vichāra pākile je premabhakti, apakve ‘sādhana’ khyāti, bhakati-lakṣaṇa-anusāra narottama-dāsa kahe, ei jena mora haye, vrajapure anurāge vāsa sakhīgaṇa-gaṇanāte, āmāre gaṇibe tāte, tavahū pūriba abhilāṣa tathāhi- sakhīnāṁ saṅginīrūpāmātmānaṁ vāsanāmayīm ājñāsevāparāṁ tattat kṛpālaṅkārabhūṣitām kṛṣṇaṁ smaran janañchāsya preṣṭhaṁ nijasamīhitam tattatkathārataśhchāsau kuryādvāsaṁ vraje sadā
IDX.en_translation:
I will now speak my opinion on the path of worship in rāga (spontaneous devotion); this is the essence of the words of the people and the Vedas. Becoming a follower of the sakhīs, attaining a siddha-deha in Vraja—in this way, the life will be soothed. 

How many sakhīs of Śrī Rādhikā are there? I will not say how many. Counting the principal sakhīs: Lalitā, Viśākhā, and Sucitrā, Campakalatā, Raṅgadevī, Sudevī are mentioned. 

Tuṅgavidyā, Indurekhā—these eight sakhīs are written. Now I speak of the narma-sakhīs. They are assistants in service, bearing the name “Priya-preṣṭha”; they perform loving service at every moment. 

(Sama-snehā, Viṣama-snehā—do not make affection for these two; I speak only of the Adhika-snehā group. They remain constantly in company, in Kṛṣṇa-kathā and the joy of pastimes; all these people are narma-sakhīs.) 

Śrī Rūpa-mañjarī, and Śrī Rati-mañjarī—the essence; Lavaṅga-mañjarī, Mañjulālī. Along with Lavaṅga-mañjarī, with musk and so on, they enthusiastically perform loving service in joy. 

Becoming a follower of all of them, I will ask for and take loving service; I will understand all tasks by hints. Overwhelmed by beauty and qualities, I will always be affectionate; I will reside in the midst of the sakhīs. 

The Two Persons in Vṛndāvana, sakhīs on four sides, in the happiness of the rasa of timely service. There will be a hint from the sakhī, then I will wave the whisk; I will supply betel nuts to the moon-faces. 

Serving the lotus feet of the Couple, constantly thinking this, I will always remain in affection. What I think of in sādhana, I will get that in the siddha-deha; this is the method of the path of rāga. 

The wealth I want in sādhana, I get that in the siddha-deha; the consideration is only ripe and unripe. When ripe, it is prema-bhakti; in the unripe state, it is known as “sādhana”, according to the characteristic of bhakti. 

Narottama Dāsa says: May this be mine—residence in Vrajapura in affection. In the counting of the sakhīs, they will count me in that; then my desire will be fulfilled. 

Thus it is said: “One should meditate upon oneself in a form that is a female companion (sakhī) to the Divine Couple—a form born of spiritual desire, dedicated to following their commands and serving them, and adorned with the ornaments of their mercy. While remembering Kṛṣṇa and His beloved associates who are dear to one’s own heart, one should remain constantly absorbed in narrations about them and reside eternally in Vraja.”

rāhu-kavale indu, parakāśha nāma-sindhu, 
kalimardana bāje bāṇā 
pahū bhela parakāśha, bhuvana chaturdaśha, 
jaya jaya paḍila ghoṣaṇā 

dekhite gaurāṅgachandra 
nadīyāra loka-, śhoka saba nāśhala, 
dine dine bāḍala ānanda (<eng>refrain</eng>) 

dundubhi bāje, śhata śhaṅkha gāje, 
bāje veṇu-viṣāṇa 
śhrī-chaitanya-ṭhākura, nityānanda-prabhu, 
vṛndāvana-dāsa gāna
IDX.en_translation:
Just as the moon is swallowed by Rāhu, the ocean of the Name has appeared. The destroyer of Kali sounds His powerful proclamation. The Lord has manifested throughout the fourteen worlds, and a proclamation of “All Glories!” was heard. 

Upon seeing Gaurāṅgacandra, the people of Nadīyā had all their sorrow destroyed, and their joy increased day by day. 

The dundubhi sounds, hundreds of conch shells resound, and the flute and horn play. Vṛndāvana Dāsa sings of Śrī Caitanya Ṭhākura and Nityānanda Prabhu.

IDX.en_translation:
Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa are in the middle of the Yamunā. The boat turns while the water swirls, and they have no shame regarding family honor. 

Crocodiles, alligators, and fish rise up, frequently lifting their faces to see. The Yamunā overflows twofold in joy, enchanted by the beauty of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa. 

Lalitā says, becoming alarmed: “Listen, O talkative old woman! Because of your words, we have boarded this broken boat, and I fear we will lose our lives.” 

The old woman replies: “Whatever the boatman asks for, just give it to him. This broken boat will cross now; why should your lives be lost?” 

Hearing these words, the boatman says to Lalitā: “I am only asking for the touch of your friend.” He laughs upon hearing the sound of His own flute.

IDX.verses: ramaṇī-śhiromaṇi, vṛṣabhānu-nandinī, nīla-vasana-paridhānā cḣinna-puraṭa jini’, varṇa-vikāśhinī, baddha-kavarī hari-prāṇā ābharaṇa-maṇḍitā, hari-rasa-paṇḍitā, tilaka-suśhobhita-bhālā kañchulikāccḣāditā, stana-maṇi-maṇḍitā, kajjala-nayanī rasālā sakala tyajiyā se-rādhā-charaṇe dāsī ha’ye bhaja parama-yatane saundarya kiraṇa dekhiyā jāṅhāra rati-gaurī-līlā-garva-parihāra śhachī-lakṣmī-satyā saubhāgya-balane parājita haya jāṅhāra charaṇe kṛṣṇa-vaśhīkāre chandrāvalī-ādi parājaya māne hoiyā vivādī hari-dayita-rādhā-charaṇa-preyasī bhakativinoda śhrī godruma-vāsī
IDX.en_translation:
The crest-jewel of women, the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu, is dressed in blue garments. Conquering the beauty of pure gold, her complexion blossoms forth; with braided hair, she is the very life of Hari. 

Adorned with ornaments and expert in the mellows of devotion, her forehead is beautifully decorated with a tilaka. Covered by a bodice, her jewel-like breasts adorned, her eyes are beautified with eyeliner and are full of sweetness. 

Abandoning everything, at those feet of Rādhā, become a maidservant and worship with utmost care. 

Seeing the rays of her beauty, the goddess of love and the goddess Pārvatī abandon their pride in their own pastimes. 

Śacī, Lakṣmī, and Satyabhāmā are defeated at her feet by the power of her good fortune. 

In captivating Kṛṣṇa, even Candrāvalī and other rivals accept defeat. 

Bhaktivinoda, a resident of Godruma, aspires for the feet of Rādhā, who is very dear to Hari.
IDX.es_translation:
La amada hija de Vṛṣabhānu Mahārāja es la joya cimera entre todas las doncellas hermosas. Ella viste con ropas azules. Su tez, que brilla de un modo muy atractivo, derrota la belleza del oro. Su cabello está hermosamente trenzado. Ella es la vida y el alma de Hari. 

Está decorada con hermosos ornamentos, es experta en intercambios amorosos con Śhrī Hari, y Su frente está exquisitamente adornada con tilaka. Sus pechos están cubiertos por un corpiño y decorados con joyas, y Sus ojos llenos de rasa están ungidos con colirio negro. 

Renuncia a todo para volverte una sirvienta a los pies de loto de Śhrī Rādhā, adórala y sírvela con sumo cuidado. 

Al contemplar los refulgentes rayos de Su belleza, Rati (la esposa de Kāmadeva), Gaurī (la consorte de Śhiva) y Līlā (la potencia de Nārāyaṇa) abandonan su orgullo. Ante Sus pies de loto, la buena fortuna que se dice que poseen Śhacī (la esposa de Indra), Lakṣmī y Satyābhāma es completamente derrotada. 

En la competición por controlar a Śhrī Kṛṣṇa, Chandrāvalī y todas las otras gopīs aceptan su derrota ante Ella. 

Bhaktivinoda, un residente de Śhrī Godruma, aspira por los pies de loto de Śhrī Rādhā, la más amada por Śhrī Hari.

IDX.verses:
rasa-tattva nitya jaicḣe, vraja-tattva nitya taicḣe, 
līlā-rasa eka kari’ jāna 
kṛṣṇa je sākṣāt rasa, sakaloi kṛṣṇera vaśha, 
veda-bhāgavate kare gāna 

śhrī-kṛṣṇa parama-tattva, tāṅ’ra līlā śhuddha-sattva, 
māyā jāṅ’ra dūrasthitā dāsī 
jīva-prati kṛpā kari’, līlā prakāśhila hari, 
jīvera maṅgala-abhilāṣī 

brahmā, śheṣa, śhiva jāṅra, anveṣiyā bāra bāra, 
tattva nāhi bujhibāre pāre 
brahmera āśhraya jini, paramātmāra aṁśhī tini, 
‘svayaṁ bhagavān’ bali jāṅre 

sei kṛṣṇa dayāmaya, mūla-tattva sarvāśhraya, 
ananta līlāra eka khani 
nirviśheṣa-līlābhare, brahmatā prakāśha kare, 
svīya aṅgakānti guṇa-maṇi 

aṁśhe paramātmā haye, baddha-jīva-gaṇe la’ye, 
karma-chakre līlā kare kata 
deva-loke deva-saha, upendrādi haye teṁha, 
deva-līlā kare śhata śhata 

paravyome nārāyaṇa, haye pāle dāsa-jana, 
deva-deva rāja-rājeśhvara 
sei kṛṣṇa sarvāśhraya, vraje nara-parichaya, 
nara-līlā karila vistāra
IDX.en_translation:
Just as the principle of divine mellows is eternal, the principle of Vraja is similarly eternal. Know the mellows of His pastimes to be one. Kṛṣṇa is the direct embodiment of rasa, and everything is under His control, as sung in the Vedas and scriptures. 

Śrī Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Truth, and His pastimes are of pure goodness. Illusion is His distant maidservant. Showing mercy to all living entities, Kṛṣṇa revealed His pastimes, desiring their welfare. 

Brahmā, Śeṣa, and Śiva—searching repeatedly—cannot understand His truth. He is the shelter of the impersonal Absolute and the complete manifestation of the Supersoul, whom we call the Supreme Lord Himself. 

That merciful Kṛṣṇa is the original truth and the shelter of all—a mine of endless pastimes. By the abundance of His impersonal manifestations, He reveals His nature as the Absolute through the effulgence of His own body, which is a jewel of all qualities. 

As a partial manifestation, becoming the Supersoul, He engages the conditioned souls in the cycle of karma through many pastimes. In the celestial planets He performs hundreds of divine pastimes with the demigods. 

In the spiritual sky He maintains His servants as the God of gods and the King of kings. That same Kṛṣṇa, the shelter of all, assumed a human identity in Vraja and expanded His human-like pastimes.

Rādhikā is the jewel among all beautiful gopīs, the swan upon the lake of Lord Kṛṣṇa’s joyful love, and the sacred vine of the excellent Vṛṣabhānu. When will She immerse me in Her divine service? 

When will Rādhikā, whose hips are illuminated by a glittering red silk garment and gracefully adorned with a beautiful belt, and whose beauty is enhanced by a lustrous pearl necklace, immerse me in Her service? 

When will Rādhikā, whose beauty surpasses the finest lotus and who possesses the essence of blossoming youth, whose adolescent charm is like nectar and whose enchanting smile emanates from Her reddish lips, immerse me in Her service? 

When will Rādhikā, with eyes filled with apprehension upon seeing the restless Prince of Vraja meeting Her in the forest, and who is praised with sweet and gentle words and glances, immerse me in Her service? 

When will Rādhikā, who is the life of all the women of Vraja, who is as dear to Mother Yaśodā as Lord Kṛṣṇa himself, and whose heart blossoms with affection for the charming Lalitā, immerse me in Her service? 

When will the excellent and beloved consort of Lord Kṛṣṇa—who along with Viśākhā is incessantly making a beautiful garland in the forest from the flowers of the trees—immerse me in Her service? 

When will Rādhikā, whose eyes smile as She quickly approaches Lord Hari in a grove, drawn by the sweet sound of His flute, and whose lowered face expresses Her longing for the sound to fill Her ears, immerse me in Her service? 

When will Rādhikā, who delights in the evening in Her own cool pond, refreshed by the breeze touching the pure lotus flowers, and who plays with Lord Kṛṣṇa accompanied by Her companions, immerse me in Her service? 

The pure-hearted person who recites these sweet eight verses in praise of Rādhā, having given up all other desires—the Prince of Nanda Mahārāja, being greatly pleased, will establish him among Rādhikā’s own associates.

He who is the abode of rasa, His heart is a mine of rasa. Within that heart, in specific states, faith, steadfastness, taste, and attachment gradually manifest as spiritual emotion, designated as love by His command. 

Both opposing and non-opposing emotions, above all His own influence, manifest and take control. Becoming the Lord of all, they shine most beautifully and obtain the name “permanent sentiment” in the experience of rasa. 

Its identity is of two types, distinguished as primary and secondary. There are five primary and seven secondary types. Neutrality, servitude, friendship, parental affection, and conjugal love are the essence; these five types of love are known as primary.

The six emotions beginning with sneha are known as “prema” to the common people. Whatever emotion one has for Kṛṣṇa, in that way Kṛṣṇa belongs to him. This mystery is indeed eternal in rasa. 

The sthāyī-bhāva, the king of all emotions, is seated on the throne of the devotee’s heart. The Hlādinī (pleasure-giving potency) is the supreme energy; its essence is pure devotion. It reigns in the form of bhāva. 

Bringing the vibhāvas and other components of emotion under its control, it manifests rasa. Rasa is the truth of eternal bliss, the essence of the eternally perfect reality. It develops in the heart of the jīva.

At the end of the night, Lord Hari leaves the pleasure groves and returns to His own home. In the morning, His pastimes include milking the cows and eating delicious food, and in the forenoon, He goes out to tend the cows. 

At midday, in the forest, He constantly performs pastimes while immersed in the joy of Rādhā’s company. In the afternoon, He brings the cows home, in the evening He milks them again, and at dusk He resides with His friends. 

At night, He again reaches the groves and attains the joy of Rādhā’s company. Such are the eight periods of these divine pastimes. This is the eternal pastime that never ceases; it is full of spiritual bliss and supreme nectar.

Kṛṣṇa Himself is the crown-jewel of lovers, the jewel of all qualities, the eternal abode of virtues, and the Supreme Absolute. Those many devotees who are attached to His mood and are rich in qualities are either perfected or practitioners. 

Things that excite these feelings are called “uddīpana”; these are all objects related to Kṛṣṇa: a smiling face, fragrance, a horn, a flute, a conch, a holy place, a bumblebee, footprints, ankle bells, and sweet sounds. 

The Tulasi plant, a sign of worship, and the sight of devotees are various excitants. For relishing the mellow of devotion, all these causes were described by Rūpa and Sanātana.

One who desires to understand the essence of the truth according to Rūpa Gosvāmī needs knowledge of the transcendental mellows. The spiritual mellow of bliss, to which all truths are subservient, is the indivisible supreme wealth of truth. 

By its mere reflection, the wise people search for merging into the Absolute without understanding the essence of the Vedas. By its mere shadow, the yogis practice discipline; by its mere pretense, the fruitive workers perform their actions. 

The causes of emotion, external manifestations, involuntary ecstatic symptoms, and transitory emotions—these four, in beautiful union with the permanent sentiment, become rasa, which is eternally full of spiritual bliss and constantly supremely relishable. 

That mellow which is material, manifest in worldly poetry, is a distorted reflection of the supreme mellow. A distorted reflection is not eternal; it is a shadow of the ideal, like the appearance of water in a mirage.

I worship the great and powerful Śrīla Jagannātha dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja, the best of the followers of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī. He is perfectly self-controlled, the beloved devotee of Śrī Gaura-candra, and the delight of Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Mādhava. 

I worship the great and powerful Śrīla Jagannātha dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja. He is the best of scholars, compassionate, and resides at Sūrya-kuṇḍa. He shines as the dearest associate of Śrīla Madhusūdana dāsa Bābājī. 

I worship the great and powerful Śrīla Jagannātha dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja. He is the moon amongst the stars of the devotees of Vṛndāvana, and he is the guardian of those who have taken exclusive shelter of the Holy Name. 

I worship the great and powerful Śrīla Jagannātha dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja. He radiates renunciation, wisdom, and devotion to Lord Hari. He is a thunderbolt smashing wickedness and deceit, yet he is full of respect for the faithful. 

I worship the great and powerful Śrīla Jagannātha dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja. Inspired by the moon-like Lord Gaura, he revealed the Lord’s birthplace. Praised by the demigods, he is the emperor of the Vaiṣṇavas. 

I worship the great and powerful Śrīla Jagannātha dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja. By infusing his own power into Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, he caused a flood of the Holy Name to drown the entire world. 

I worship the great and powerful Śrīla Jagannātha dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja. Eager to preach the glories of the Name and the Abode, and submerged in the ocean of divine love, he dances in ecstasy at the Yoga-pīṭha. 

I worship the great and powerful Śrīla Jagannātha dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja. His heart is attached to Māyāpura Dhāma, and he is filled with joy by the revelation of Lord Gaura. Tears pour from his eyes as he sings the Holy Names. 

O Master! O Emperor of Vaiṣṇavas! Your devotion conquers the abode of Indra. I bow again and again to the holy line of Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, which has expanded your divine family.

Considering the pure fortune of a child, You should abandon the delusion and grief that disturb the mind. 

Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of the fourteen worlds, Appeared as Caitanya Mahāprabhu in Nadīyā. 

That very Kṛṣṇa dances in my courtyard, Overwhelmed with bliss, along with His devotees. 

Hearing the chanting of holy names, my child Left his body, utterly absorbed in love for Kṛṣṇa. 

When such fortune comes to me, Then I too will cross over the ocean of material existence. 

Forgetting all this consideration, Why do you cause grief and mental agitation? 

If you are not steady in these instructions, You will eventually be deprived of the divine nectar. 

I will enter the celestial Ganges, Bhaktivinoda sees the danger in that.

IDX.verses: śhachī-suta gaura-hari, navadvīpe avatari, karilena vividha vilāsa saṅge laiyā priya-gaṇa, prakāśhiyā saṅkīrtana, bāḍhāilā sabāra ullāsa kibā se sannyāsa-veśhe, bhrami prabhu deśhe deśhe, nīlāchale āsiyā rahilā rādhikāra preme māti’, nā jāni divārāti, se preme jagat mātāilā nityānanda-balarāma, advaita-guṇera dhāma, gadādhara śhrīvāsādi jata dekhi se adbhuta rīti, keha nā dharaye dhṛti, premāya vihvala avirata devera durlabha ratna, milāilā kari’ jatna, kṛpāra bālāi loiyā mari kailā kali-yuga dhanya, prabhu śhrī-kṛṣṇa-chaitanya, jaśha gāy dāsa narahari
IDX.en_translation:
The son of Śacī, Gaura-hari, descending in Navadvīpa, performed various pastimes. Taking His dear associates with Him, He manifested the saṅkīrtana, increasing everyone’s joy. 

How wonderful in that dress of a sannyāsī! The Lord wandered from land to land and came to reside in Nīlācala (Puri). Maddened by the love of Rādhikā, not knowing day or night, He maddened the world with that love. 

Nityānanda-Balarāma, Advaita—the abode of qualities, Gadādhara, Śrīvāsa, and others; seeing that wonderful manner, no one could maintain patience, being constantly overwhelmed with love. 

He carefully distributed the jewel rare for the gods; I die taking the calamity of His mercy. Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya made the Kali-yuga blessed; the servant Narahari sings His glory.

Holding His mother’s cloth with His restless hands, He dances and moves like a wagtail bird. 

Vāsudeva Ghoṣa says: “What wondrous beauty! Seeing His child-form, the minds of everyone in the world are captivated.”

Lord Gorā, the son of Mother Śacī, with His moon-like face, calls out again and again with delightful sounds to the cows. 

Understanding the flow of His mood, Lord Nityānanda makes a loving sound with a horn. 

From the moon-like face of Lord Nitāi comes a signal of divine love; hearing this, the devotees are overwhelmed with ecstatic love. 

Paṇḍita Gaurīdāsa ran forward, and Abhirāma Ṭhākura followed him, crying out: “O brothers! O brothers!” 

Upon seeing the form of Lord Gaurāṅga, he entered a trance of divine love. The Lord wore an enchanting crown with a peacock feather and was dressed like the best of dancers. 

Ankle bells jingle on His feet, and sandalwood paste covers His entire body. Vaṁśīvadana says: “Let us go to Govardhana Hill.”

IDX.en_translation:
The ordinary and balanced heroines attain a permanent emotional state, with Kubjā and the queens as examples. Only among the cowherd damsels of Vraja, in the manifestation of mahābhāva, are the advanced stages of “rūḍha” and “adhirūḍha” found. 

In that state, there is intolerance of even a blink of an eye, and one is almost distressed by the churning of the heart; a moment feels like an eon, and even in happiness, one is filled with apprehension. Forgetting oneself and considering a moment as an eon are the same in both union and separation. 

Again, listen to the two distinctions in the adhirūḍha stage, known as “modana” and “mādana”. In the state of separation, modana becomes “mohana”, from which divine madness is born. 

Divine madness is of two types: citrajalpa and udghūrṇā. Citrajalpa itself has many kinds. In modana, Śrī Rādhā’s state is the essence of mādana. She attains an emotional state full of eternal pastimes. 

Ordinary love is like smoldering, and balanced love is always glowing. In rūḍha, it is intensely shining. The brilliantly shining love of Śrī Rādhā is like blazing gold; it always appears in emotional states like modana.

IDX.en_translation:
Alas, association with devotees did not happen! Days passed needlessly in earning money; where did spiritual welfare remain? 

Abandoning gold and having an attachment to a trivial clod of earth—this is the sign of the unfortunate. Associating with those not devoted to God and avoiding saintly persons, I spent my life in intoxicated pride. 

Upon seeing the signs of devotion, I would laugh in my mind, calling it madness. That civilization which I considered supreme—by it I lost the wish-fulfilling gem; where did it ultimately remain? 

Due to the glory of knowledge, I neglected the excellent treasure of devotion, forgetting my own true interest. This wicked knowledge based on matter has now disappeared, leaving me in the experience of my actions. 

Now, if saintly persons, out of kindness to this wretched soul, give a drop from the ocean of devotion, then effortlessly, being freed from the noose of material existence, I can cross this ocean of material life.

sureśhānāṁ durgaṁ gatir atiśhayenopaniṣadāṁ 
munīnāṁ sarva-svaṁ praṇata-paṭalīnāṁ madhurimā

Will that glorious Śrī Caitanya, who is always worshiped by demigods like Giriśa (Lord Śiva) and Parameṣṭhi (Lord Brahmā) and others, who assume human bodies out of affection, and who instructs His devotees in the pure method of His own worship, again become visible to my eyes? 

Will that Śrī Caitanya, who is an inaccessible destination for the kings of the demigods, the special goal of the Upaniṣads, the very life of the sages, the sweetness for the multitude of surrendered souls, and the essence of love for all the lotus-eyed gopīs, again become visible to my eyes? 

Will that Śrī Caitanya, who manifests a unique form in the world, the beloved of Advaita Āchārya, the protector of Prapanna Śrīvāsa, the source of supreme bliss and greatness, Hari, the deliverer of the fallen, and who is moved by the outpouring of grace to Gajapati (King Pratāparudra), again become visible to my eyes? 

Will that Śrī Caitanya, who is full of ecstatic rasa, whose brilliant form is as sweet as millions of Cupids, the crest-jewel of ascetics, whose garments shine like sunbeams, and who overcomes the opulence of gold and Lakṣmī with the splendor of His bodily luster, again become visible to my eyes? 

Will that Śrī Caitanya, whose tongue vibrates loudly chanting “Hare Kṛṣṇa,” whose charming hand shines with a beautiful thread (mālā) for counting names, with a series of knots, who has broad eyes, and whose playfully moving arms resemble long bolts, again become visible to my eyes? 

Will that Śrī Caitanya, who, on the shore of the ocean, seeing the shining rows of gardens, becomes repeatedly overwhelmed by love arising from the remembrance of Vṛndāvana, and who sometimes, with a restless tongue repeating Kṛṣṇa’s names, is a connoisseur of devotional rasa, again become visible to my eyes? 

Will that Śrī Caitanya, who, near the Ratha (chariot)-riding Lord of Nīlācala (Jagannātha Purī), becomes overwhelmed by boundless waves of love, manifesting ecstatic dancing, and whose body is surrounded by Vaiṣṇavas joyfully singing, again become visible to my eyes? 

Will that Śrī Caitanya, who sprinkles the earth with streams of tears, whose body is covered all around with dense goosebumps surpassing the fresh pollen of a nīpa flower cluster, whose body is moistened by profuse streams of sweat, and who finds joy in loud chanting, again become visible to my eyes? 

May the waves of love of that fortunate person, whose pure intelligence shines with faith, and who studies this aṣṭakam (eight verse prayer), the supremely auspicious path of remembering Gaurāṅga, spread abundantly and immediately in supreme bliss at His immaculate lotus feet.

What did I see today? The playful Lover beneath the Kadamba tree of pastimes. Gazing at His beauty, the shyness of my eyes melted into tears of joy. 

With a flower garland pulling His hair, He is adorned with a peacock-feather crown. To captivate the restless eyes of the gopīs, He has set an intricate trap. 

His shark-shaped earrings sway, reflecting upon His mirror-like cheeks. On His forehead, Cupid himself is reflected—so Govinda Dāsa surmises.

Like the shark-shaped emblem of Cupid, jeweled earrings sway upon His ears. Seeing this, the fish of the world’s mind is swallowed by His beauty; Govinda Dāsa testifies to this.

Sin su misericordia, eso es inalcanzable. Claramente yo no estoy en absoluto capacitado. 

Ustedes son árboles de los deseos y océanos de compasión. Esta es la única esperanza que alberga mi corazón (que me concedan su gracia). 

No poseo ninguna cualidad y he cometido ilimitadas ofensas. Si me liberan, todo el mundo se hará eco de sus glorias. 

Muestren por favor su gran compasión otorgando gusto por el nāma-saṅkīrtana y el tesoro del prema a este Rādhā-mohana dāsa.

I offer obeisances to the lotus feet of the spiritual master, who is like a dense cloud of mercy appearing to save those who are scorched by the blazing forest fire of material existence. He is an ocean of auspicious qualities. 

I offer obeisances to the lotus feet of the spiritual master, whose mind is maddened by the nectar of the congregational chanting, dancing, singing, and musical instruments of Lord Caitanya. He is always experiencing waves of ecstatic thrills, trembling, and tears. 

I offer obeisances to the lotus feet of the spiritual master, who is engaged in the daily worship of the Deity of the Lord, adorning Them with various ornaments and cleaning Their temple. He also engages the devotees in these services. 

I offer obeisances to the lotus feet of the spiritual master, who is always satisfied by seeing the assemblies of devotees contentedly partaking of the four kinds of delicious food offered to the Supreme Lord. 

I offer obeisances to the lotus feet of the spiritual master, who is ever greedy to relish, moment after moment, the unlimited sweetness of the pastimes, qualities, forms, and names of Śrī Rādhā and Mādhava. 

I offer obeisances to the lotus feet of the spiritual master, who is very expert and dear to the Divine Couple in bringing about the success of Their loving pastimes through whatever arrangements are required by the companions. 

I offer obeisances to the lotus feet of the spiritual master, who is directly the Lord Himself according to all the scriptures and is also considered so by the saintly. However, he is the dearmost beloved of the Lord. 

I offer obeisances to the lotus feet of the spiritual master. By his mercy, one achieves the mercy of the Lord. Without his mercy, there is no progress toward the destination. Therefore, one should meditate upon and glorify his fame three times a day. 

Whoever carefully recites these eight stanzas glorifying the spiritual master loudly during the auspicious hour before dawn will surely attain the direct service of the Lord of Vṛndāvana at the end of this very life.
IDX.es_translation:
Śhrī gurudeva, que es un océano de cualidades auspiciosas, se manifiesta misericordiosamente como una densa nube para liberar a las entidades vivientes que se queman en el ardiente fuergo forestal de la existencia material. Yo adoro los pies de loto de śhrī gurudeva. 

Con el corazón embriagado por el prema-rasa del kīrtana de Śhrīman Mahāprabhu, śhrī guru danza, canta y toca diferentes instrumentos. Ebrio de amor, sus vellos se erizan, su cuerpo tiembla y de sus ojos fluyen torrentes de lágrimas. Yo adoro los pies de loto de śhrī gurudeva. 

Śhrī gurudeva adora y sirve siempre a śhrī vigraha decorándolos con diferentes vestiduras y ornamentos [que estimulan Su śhṛṅgāra-rasa], y ejecutando otros servicios como la limpieza del templo. Él ocupa también a los devotos [bajo su guía] en esos servicios. Yo adoro los pies de loto de śhrī gurudeva. 

Śhrī guru experimenta gran dicha complaciendo a los devotos de Śhrī Hari con las cuatro clases de bhagavat-prasāda ―el que se mastica, se succiona, se lame y se bebe. [Por honrar ese prasāda se destruye la vida material y se obtiene verdadera satisfacción o la dicha del prema.] Yo adoro los pies de loto de śhrī gurudeva. 

Śhrī gurudeva experimenta a cada momento un intenso anhelo en su corazón por saborear la ilimitada dulzura de los santos nombres, las formas, las cualidades y los pasatiempos de Śhrī Śhrī Rādhā-Mādhava. Yo adoro los pies de loto de śhrī gurudeva. 

Porque lleva a cabo magistralmente las disposiciones de las sakhīs para la perfección de Sus pasatiempos amorosos en las arboledas de Vṛndāvana, śhrī gurudeva le es muy querido a Śhrī Śhrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa. Yo adoro los pies de loto de śhrī gurudeva. 

Todas las escrituras proclaman que śhrī guru es sākṣāt hari, directamente Śhrī Hari. Este hecho lo corroboran todas las personas santas. Y no obstante, al mismo tiempo śhrī guru Le es muy querido a Bhagavān. Yo adoro los pies de loto de śhrī gurudeva [que es inconcebiblemente igual y diferente de Bhagavān]. 

Solo por la misericordia de Śhrī Gurudeva se puede recibir la misericordia de Bhagavān; sin su gracia no se puede hacer ningún avance. Medita en śhrī guru y canta sus alabanzas en las tres conjunciones sagradas del día. Yo adoro los pies de loto de śhrī gurudeva. 

La persona que recita atentamente y en voz alta este guruvāṣṭakam durante el brāhma muhūrta, obtendrá sin duda alguna el servicio directo de los pies de loto de Śhrī Kṛṣṇa, la vida y el alma de Vṛndāvana, al final de su vida [al alcanzar su vastu-siddhi o forma espiritual eterna].

madhupāna, vadhūveṣa, kapaṭa-nidrā-āveśha, 
dyūtakrīḍā, vastra-ṭānāṭāni 
chumbāśhleṣa, nakhārpaṇa, bimbādhara-sudhāpāna, 
samprayoga ādi līlā māni 

sambhogaprakāra saba, sambhogera mahotsava, 
līlā haya sadā supeśhala 
sei līlā aparūpa, ujjvala rasera kūpa, 
tāhe jāra haya kautūhala 

chidvilāsa-rasabhare, rati bhāva-daśhā dhare, 
mahābhāva paryanta bāḍaya 
je jīva saubhāgyavān, līlā-yoge su-sandhāna, 
vraje vasi’ satata karaya
IDX.en_translation:
Sandarśana, saṁsparśana, jalpa, vartmanirodhana, the rāsa, and the abundant pastimes of Vṛndāvana—water sports in the Yamunā, boat playing, stealing, pastimes on the river bank, and hide-and-seek in the groves. 

Madhupāna, vadhūveṣa, feigned sleep, gambling, pulling at clothes, kissing and embracing, nail marks, and drinking the nectar of bimba-like lips—I consider these and other intimate pastimes. 

All types of union and the great festival of enjoyment, the pastimes are always delightful. Those unique pastimes are a well of brilliant rasa; for one who has a keen interest in them, 

filled with the mellow of spiritual enjoyment, rati attains the stage of bhāva and increases up to mahābhāva. That fortunate soul, through connection with these pastimes, constantly resides in Vraja and performs them.

IDX.verses: saptadvīpa dīpta kari’, śhobhe navadvīpa-purī, jāhe viśhvambhara devarāja tāhe tāṅ’ra bhakta jata, tāhāte śhrīvāsa khyāta, śhrī-kṛṣṇa-kīrtana jāṅ’ra kāja jaya jaya ṭhākura paṇḍita jāṅ’ra kṛpā-leśha mātra, haiyā gaura-premapātra, anupama sakala charita gaurāṅgera sevā vine, deva-devī nāhi jāne, chāri bhāi dāsa-dāsī laiyā satata kīrtana-raṅge, gaura-gaurabhakta-saṅge, aharniśhi prema-matta haiyā jāṅ’ra bhāryā śhrī-mālinī, pativratā-śhiromaṇi, jāṅ’re prabhu kahaye jananī nityānanda rahe ghare, putra-sama sneha kare, stana jhare, netre vahe pānī kabhu vā īśhvara-jñāne, nati kare śhrī-charaṇe, kabhu kole karaye lālana prabhura nṛtya-bhaṅga lāgi, mṛta putraśhoka-tyāgī, śhuni’ prabhu karaye rodana bhrātṛsutā nārāyaṇī, vaiṣṇava-maṇḍale dhvani, jāṅ’ra putra vṛndāvana-dāsa varṇiyā chaitanya-līlā, tribhuvana uddhārilā, premadāsa kare jāṅ’ra āśha
IDX.en_translation:
Navadvīpa-purī is resplendent, making the seven islands of the world shine. There, Viśvambhara reigns as the King of the Gods. Among all His devotees, Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita is famous, and his only work is the congregational chanting of the Holy Names of Lord Kṛṣṇa. 

All glories, all glories to Śrīla Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita! By even a drop of his mercy, one becomes a recipient of Lord Gaura’s love. All his deeds are incomparable. 

Except for the service of Lord Gaurāṅga, he knows no other gods or goddesses. Together with his four brothers and his servants, he is constantly immersed in the joy of kīrtana. In the association of Lord Gaura and His devotees, he remains intoxicated with divine love day and night. 

His wife is Śrīmati Mālinī-devī, the crest jewel of chaste wives, whom the Lord calls “Mother.” Lord Nityānanda stays in their house and she shows Him affection just like a son. Milk flows from her breasts and tears flow from her eyes out of motherly love. 

Sometimes, knowing Him to be the Supreme Lord, she bows at His lotus feet. At other times, she nurtures Him on her lap. For the sake of the Lord’s ecstatic dancing, she even abandoned the grief for her dead son. Hearing of this, the Lord wept. 

His brother’s daughter is Nārāyaṇī, who is renowned throughout the Vaiṣṇava community. Her son is Śrīla Vṛndāvana Dāsa Ṭhākura. By describing the pastimes of Lord Caitanya, he delivered the three worlds. Premadāsa places his hope in such a personality.
IDX.es_translation:
Iluminando las siete islas del mundo, Śhrī Navadvīpa-purī reluce debido a la presencia del rey de los dioses, Śhrī Viśhvambhara. En medio de los bhaktas de Śhrī Viśhvambhara se encuentra el renombrado Śhrīvāsa Paṇḍita, cuya ocupación en la vida es el śhrī-kṛṣṇa-kīrtana. 

¡Toda gloria a Paṇḍita Ṭhākura! Por una partícula de su misericordia, uno puede volverse un receptáculo de gaura-prema. Todos sus pasatiempos son extraordinarios. 

Dedicado exclusivamente al sevā de Gaurāṅga, no conoce a ningún semidiós o semidiosa. Acompañado de sus cuatro hermanos y sus sirvientes, él está siempre ebrio de prema realizando diferentes clases de kīrtana de día y de noche con Gaurāṅga y Sus devotos. 

Su esposa, Śhrī Mālinī-devī, a quien Mahāprabhu llama ‘madre’, es la joya cumbre de todas las mujeres castas. Nityānanda Prahbu reside en su casa, y ella Le ama como si fuera su propio hijo. Cuando ella ve a Nityānanda prabhu, de sus pechos fluye leche y de sus ojos lágrimas. 

Algunas veces, sabiendo que Mahāprabhu es el Señor Supremo, Śhrīvāsa Paṇḍita se inclina a Sus pies de loto, pero otras veces Lo sienta en su regazo y Lo alimenta. Para no interrumpir la danza extática de Mahāprabhu, él renunció a cualquier expresión de dolor cuando murió su hijo. Al oír esto, el Señor lloró. 

Nārāyaṇī, la sobrina de Śhrīvāsa Paṇḍita, fue la voz de la asamblea vaiṣṇava. Su hijo Śhrī Vṛndāvana dāsa describió los līlās de Chaitanya Mahāprabhu y de ese modo liberó los tres mundos. Prema dāsa pone en él (Śhrīvāsa Paṇḍita) sus esperanzas y aspiraciones.

hari-premonmattaṁ dhṛta-parama-sattvaṁ smita-mukham 
sadā ghūrṇan-netraṁ kara-kalita-vetraṁ kali-bhidaṁ

<highlight>(bhaje nityānandaṁ bhajana-taru-kandaṁ niravadhi)</highlight>
IDX.en_translation:
I constantly worship Nityānanda, the root of the tree of devotion. He has the shining, spotless luster of the autumn moon; His gait is like that of an elephant. He is maddened with love for Hari; He is the form of the supreme truth. His face is smiling. His eyes are always rolling. He holds a staff in His hand. He destroys the Kali age. 

I constantly worship Nityānanda, the root of the tree of devotion. He is the reservoir of rasas. He is the incomparable all-in-all of His own people. He is the Lord of Vasudhā and Jāhnavā, who are like His one life-breath. He is always maddened by love; He is supremely known to the dull-minded. 

I constantly worship Nityānanda, the root of the tree of devotion. He is most dear to the son of Śacī. He is desired by the whole universe. He is full of happiness. He has great mercy for delivering the jīvas drowning in the age of Kali. By the narration of Hari, He removes the swelling pride of the ocean of material existence. 

I constantly worship Nityānanda, the root of the tree of devotion. He says, “O brother! What will happen to men polluted by Kali? Make such an atonement by which they can go to You effortlessly.” Thus He counsels the Lord. 

I constantly worship Nityānanda, the root of the tree of devotion. He goes to every house, shouting with raised arms: “O brother! Constantly make the sound of “Hari, Hari” as much as you like! Then the responsibility for your crossing the ocean of material existence will fall upon Me.” 

I constantly worship Nityānanda, the root of the tree of devotion. He is the Agastya Muni who forcibly removes the ocean of material existence. He is the risen Moon, the friend of the lily of the increase of the ocean of welfare of the saintly. He is the sun-glare that destroys the dense darkness of the multitude of the wicked. 

I constantly worship Nityānanda, the root of the tree of devotion. He dances, sings, and calls out “Hari!” on every path. He wanders, He looks; He makes the people roar. He makes them saintly; He casts merciful glances. 

I constantly worship Nityānanda, the root of the tree of devotion. He holds the very soft lotus hand of His brother. His heart is surged with supreme bliss by looking at each other’s faces. He wanders; ah! He intoxicates the townspeople with sweetness. 

He who reads this unprecedented Nityānandāṣṭakam, which is the reservoir of rasas, the wealth of the best Rasikas and true Vaiṣṇavas, the storehouse of rasa, the essence, the deliverer of the multitude of the fallen—by remembrance (of Nityānanda), may the lotus of His two feet manifest constantly in his heart.
IDX.es_translation:
Su brillante rostro se asemeja a la luna llena de otoño, Su tez pura resplandece, Sus andares son como los de un elefante, está siempre intoxicado por el kṛṣṇa-prema y es la personificación de la energía espiritual pura (viśhuddha-sattva). Tiene un rostro sonriente, Sus ojos siempre dan vueltas, en Sus manos empuña una vara y [mediante el nāma-saṅkīrtana] destruye la influencia de Kali. Yo adoro eternamente a Śhrī Nityānanda Prabhu, la raíz del árbol del kṛṣṇa-bhakti. 

Él es la morada de todos los rasas, lo es todo para Sus devotos, está más allá de toda comparación, y es el esposo de Vasudhā y Jāhnavā-devī, quienes Le aman más que a sus propias vidas. Él está siempre enloquecido por el prema y solo es desconocido por las personas de inteligencia mundana. Yo adoro eternamente a Śhrī Nityānanda Prabhu, la raíz del árbol del kṛṣṇa-bhakti. 

Él es sumamente querido por el hijo de Madre Śhachī, es adorado por el universo entero y está siempre lleno de júbilo. Por Su infinita misericordia, Él rescata a las almas que se ahogan en esta era de Kali, y mediante la ejecución de śhrī-harināma-saṅkīrtana evapora el creciente orgullo en este océano de la existencia mundana. Yo adoro eternamente a Śhrī Nityānanda Prabhu, la raíz del árbol del kṛṣṇa-bhakti. 

“¡Oh, hermano Mío! Contaminada por los vicios de Kali-yuga, ¿qué va a ser de la humanidad?”. Por consiguiente, Él aconseja a Śhrī Kṛṣṇa Chaitanya, el Señor Supremo: “Por favor, diseña un método purificatorio mediante el cual puedan alcanzar fácilmente Tu refugio”. Yo adoro eternamente a Śhrī Nityānanda Prabhu, la raíz del árbol del kṛṣṇa-bhakti. 

“¡Oh, hermanos! Tan solo canten incesantemente los nombres de Śhrī Hari y déjenme a Mí la responsabilidad de liberarlos del océano del nacimiento y la muerte reiterados.” Él viajaba constantemente e iba de puerta en puerta declarando esto con los brazos en alto. Yo adoro eternamente a Śhrī Nityānanda Prabhu, la raíz del árbol del kṛṣṇa-bhakti. 

¡Qué extraordinario! Él es [como] Agastya Muni [que en una ocasión se tragó el océano entero], que traga a la fuerza el océano de nacimiento y muerte. Él es la luna creciente que hace que incremente el océano de la buena fortuna de las personas santas, y ante los rufianes Él es el brillante y abrasador sol que disipa la oscuridad de su ignorancia. Yo adoro eternamente a Śhrī Nityānanda Prabhu, la raíz del árbol del kṛṣṇa-bhakti. 

Él danza, canta y glorifica en voz alta los nombres de Śhrī Hari ― solo por verlo los devotos se llenan de dicha. Él vaga por todos los senderos lanzando miradas de soslayo a las personas santas con Sus misericordiosos ojos. Yo adoro eternamente a Śhrī Nityānanda Prabhu, la raíz del árbol del kṛṣṇa-bhakti. 

Con los corazones de ambos saturados del éxtasis más sublime al contemplar Sus respectivos rostros, Él sostuvo dulcemente la suavísima mano de loto de Su hermano. Cuando caminaba por doquier, Él deleitaba a todos con Su dulzura. Yo adoro eternamente a Śhrī Nityānanda Prabhu, la raíz del árbol del kṛṣṇa-bhakti. 

Que los pies de loto de Śhrī Nityānanda Prabhu se manifiesten brillantemente en los corazones de quienes recitan este incomparable y supremamente poderoso Nityānandāṣṭakam, que es el depósito del rasa, el tesoro de eminentes vaiṣṇavas rasika y la morada de la esencia del bhakti-rasa, y que libera a las almas caídas que simplemente lo recuerdan.

IDX.en_translation:
Prayer of the Surrendered Soul “May I be born even as a worm in the house of those who are attached only to the happiness of serving You, but let me not be born even as a Lord Brahmā in a house where You are not worshipped.” 

“I have obeyed the wicked commands of lust and other enemies in so many ways and for so long. They have no mercy, no shame, and give me no peace. O Lord of the Yadus! Abandoning them, and now having regained my intelligence, I have come to You for fearless shelter. Please engage me in Your personal service.” 

“O Lord of Vaikuṇṭha! My mind does not take pleasure in topics about You because it is polluted by sin, wicked, and very intense. It is afflicted by lust and tormented by happiness, distress, fear, and hankering. How can I, who am so wretched, think of Your path?” 

My wicked mind is polluted by sins and controlled by lust, happiness, grief, fear, and hankering. 

How will I develop attachment to topics about You? How, O Kṛṣṇa, will I contemplate Your pastimes? 

“O Infallible One! My unsatisfied tongue drags me in one direction, my genitals in another, my stomach, ears, nose, and restless eyes in others, and my working senses elsewhere. These many co-wives tear the householder apart.” 

The tongue pulls towards tastes, the genitals towards bad purposes. The belly pulls towards eating, a terrible calamity. 

The skin pulls towards soft beds, the ears towards talks. The nose pulls towards sweet scents, the eyes go towards sights. 

The working senses pull towards work; just as many wives attract the master of the house, my mind is pulled like that. 

This is my condition, O Son of Nanda. How shall I remember Your pastimes? 

“O Lord, let me have that great fortune, whether in this birth or another, or even as an animal, that I may become one of Your devotees and serve Your tender feet.” 

Whether in this birth as Brahmā or in any other existence, even if I am born as a beast or bird in Your creation... 

My only hope is this: that staying in the company of Your devotees, I may serve Your feet in various ways. 

“O Controller, for those who worship Your lotus feet, what is difficult to obtain among the four goals of life? Still, O Great One, I do not desire them. I am eager only to serve Your lotus feet.” 

O Kṛṣṇa! For one who has devotion to Your lotus feet, what is unattainable among the four goals of life? 

Still, I only want service to Your feet. I have no need for any other goal. 

“O Lord, I do not desire that liberation where the nectar of Your lotus feet is not present. Let the words flowing from the mouths of great souls about Your glories enter my heart. Give me ten thousand ears for this; this is my boon.” 

O Lord, I never want that benediction in which there is no happiness of serving Your feet. 

To hear the songs of Your qualities coming from the hearts of devotees, please arrange for me to have ten thousand ears. 

“I do not desire heaven, the position of Brahmā, sovereignty over the earth, rulership of the lower planets, yogic perfections, or liberation, if it means being separated from You, O Source of all opportunities.” 

Heaven, the place of Brahmā, the position of emperor, lordship over the lower worlds, the opulence of yoga... 

...liberation and so on—abandoning Your service, I do not beg for any of these. This is my sincere vow. 

“O Hari, I will become the servant of the servant of Your lotus feet. May my mind remember the qualities of the Lord of my life, may my words chant Your glories, and may my body work for You.” 

I was Your eternal servant, but being bound by the noose of illusion around my neck, I suffered various miseries in this material world. 

Now I hope again that becoming the servant of Your servant, and worshipping You, I may obtain a trace of Your devotion. 

O Lord of my life! Let my mind remember Your qualities again and again. Let my tongue sing Your name. Let my two hands find happiness doing Your work. I have offered my soul at Your feet.

I offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Śrīla Bhakti Dayita Mādhava Gosvāmī Mahārāja. His lotus feet are worshipped by hundreds of saintly persons. He is the foremost preacher of the religious practice for this age, and he possesses the power of eloquent speech. 

I offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Śrīla Mādhava Mahārāja. His body is very tall, enchanting, and has a golden complexion. His face always holds a gentle and sweet smile, and his beautiful hands extend to his knees. 

I offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Śrīla Mādhava Mahārāja. He was very diligent in his studies during childhood and heard the essence of the scriptures from his mother. He renounced his home for the sake of the highest spiritual truth. 

I offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Śrīla Mādhava Mahārāja. His body and mind are dedicated to the lotus feet of Śrīla Prabhupāda. He assumed the dress of a sannyāsī for his Guru’s mission and is the best benefactor to those who surrender. 

I offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Śrīla Mādhava Mahārāja. He is engaged in the activities dear to Śrīla Prabhupāda’s heart. He greatly respects the path of Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura and follows the path shown by the Gosvāmīs—Rūpa, Sanātana, and Raghunātha. 

I offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Śrīla Mādhava Mahārāja. He has the power to cleanse the heart more than any other means. His heart is gladdened by even a small service, and his mind is constantly engaged in the congregational chanting of Lord Hari’s names. 

I offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Śrīla Mādhava Mahārāja. He established great fame by building temples and was always absorbed in topics concerning the Guru and Lord Gaura. He is supremely patient in his own conduct. 

I offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Śrīla Mādhava Mahārāja. His compassionate heart attracts all the devotees. All his activities are worshipped by the people, and his feet are venerable in his own country and abroad. 

I offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Śrīla Mādhava Mahārāja. He is diligent in protecting the lineage of spiritual masters and is always engaged in bestowing honor upon the Guru’s associates. He values the words of his devoted servants. 

I offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Śrīla Mādhava Mahārāja. He is intensely attached to the devotional service of the Supreme Lord and is firm in following his vows. He delivers many souls at the lotus feet of Śrīla Prabhupāda. 

I offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Śrīla Mādhava Mahārāja. By his mercy, he forgives all offenders. He always guides the most fallen and sinful persons onto the right path.

Breaking the glorious rāsa dance circle, when He goes in search of Rādhā, 

Saying, “Show Yourself, Rādhe! Save My life!”, Kṛṣṇa cries in the forest.

La flauta emite el nombre de Rādhikā. “¡Ven aquí! ¡Ven aquí!, solicita Śyāmā. 

Cuando Kāna va en busca de Śrī Rādhā, la danza rāsa se detiene. 

Él solloza en el bosque exclamando: “¡Oh Rādhā, salva por favor Mi vida dándome Tu darśana! 

Al abrazar a Śrī Rādhā y reconciliarse con Ella en un bosquecillo apartado, Śrī Hari vuelve a la vida.

Llorando a los pies de loto de Rādhikā, Bhaktivinoda dice: 

“Considérame uno de Tus asociados personales y mantenme contigo como Tu sirvienta.”

Let my mind constantly remember Rādhā. Her beauty and qualities, heard of by the Lord of Madhu (Kṛṣṇa), are a natural obstacle to Cupid. 

She wears a beautiful line of vermillion on the nectar-path of the rasa of Her excellent parting. She is a streak of the beautiful moon born from the ocean of the family of Śrī Vṛṣabhānu. 

She is adorned with a soft, fragrant garland of jasmine flowers on Her beautiful braid. She defeats the play of the intoxicated, moving wagtail birds with Her large lotus eyes. 

She shames the excellent, graceful gait of the king of elephants intoxicated with rut. She has a very delicate, golden, fresh Campaka-like, fair, sweet, sweet body. 

Her soft creeper-like arms are adorned with jeweled armlets and beautiful rows of bracelets. At every step, She is a wonder of wonderful beauty, the best of enchanting young women. 

She mocks the orb of the moon with Her soft, gentle smile and beautiful face. Her large, beautiful hips are inlaid with a net of small bells and are a heap of new rasa. 

The beauty of Her golden pot-like breasts is concealed by a colorful bodice. She creates greed in the mind of Hari with the nectar-wine of Her quivering red lips. 

She is adorned with a beautiful chin, enchanting with the beauty of a black dot (musk). Her nose is beautiful and radiant, inlaid with gold, gems, and a large pearl. 

She is the ocean of the nectar of blazing passion (love), the essence-body, the form of happiness. She is the well of the nectar of musk for the deer of the bewildered mind of Mādhava, who falls into it. 

She has made the red silk cloth beautiful with anklets, necklaces, and enchanting earrings. Her lotus feet are worshipped by the moon-like people of Gokula, who are agitated by Cupid on every path. 

This song, the great secret of the form of Rādhā, is very wonderful, by Rasika Sarasvatī. It must be sung by one whose mind is eager for the rasa of Vṛndāvana.

IDX.en_translation:
Bathed and adorned, the charming Rāi converses with her gopī friends in her house. The gentle girl Kundalatā, sent by Yaśodā, then informs Jaṭilā. 

“O Jaṭilā! Listen to Yaśodā’s request. I will take Śrī Rādhā there; it has been decided that She will cook. After She finishes, I will bring your daughter-in-law back.” 

Although she fears Lord Kṛṣṇa, Jaṭilā agrees after hearing Yaśodā’s request. Rādhā, with her gopī friends, goes and bows down to Mother Yaśodā, then performs the cooking. 

Lord Kṛṣṇa gives up His sleep and milks the cows in the pasture. After bathing, He eats with His cowherd friends. Whatever remnants the Lord leaves, Śrīmati Rādhikā and Her friends relish with great joy.

Goddess Śraddhā has two natures, differing by being regulated or having spontaneous attraction. When faith arises under the direction of the scriptures, the Vedas call that regulated faith. 

When, by observing the pure service of the residents of Vraja to Kṛṣṇa, faith awakens, that chaste, greedy faith is pure devotion following spontaneous attachment. A practitioner obtains this by great fortune. 

The four Vedas sing about the differences in faith and devotion - the two types of devotion being regulated and spontaneous. What is practiced during the time of spiritual discipline is attained in the state of perfection; thus say the scriptures of devotion. 

Regulated devotion is slow-moving, while spontaneous devotion is very swift and quickly attains the state of spiritual ecstasy. One in whose mind a taste for the excellent practice on the path of spontaneous attachment arises, rushes to become a follower of Rūpa.

IDX.en_translation:
I worship Śrīla Gaurakiśora dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja, the pure devotee sheltered in Śrī Gauradhāma. He is the foremost follower of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, his form is faultless, and he shines with the brilliance of intense renunciation. 

I worship Śrīla Gaurakiśora dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja, who always rejects bad association and whose mind is immersed in the vow of serving Lord Gaurāṅga. He possesses the unique wisdom of seeing the non-difference between Gauḍa and Vraja. 

I worship Śrīla Gaurakiśora dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja. He eloquently sings the divine, hidden glories of Śrīdhāma Māyāpura. He is the worshipable, blessed, and foremost among the great Mahā-bhāgavatas. 

I worship Śrīla Gaurakiśora dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja, the crest jewel of the pure avadhūtas. He is a confidential devotee of Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, always absorbed in the mood of Vraja with deep attachment. 

I worship Śrīla Gaurakiśora dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja. He is charming, residing in a realm beyond lamentation. Unknowable to fools but approachable by the humble, he eternally experiences the divine pastimes of the Infallible Lord. 

I worship Śrīla Gaurakiśora dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja. He wields a fierce staff to punish deceitful dharma, yet he delights in the association of the saintly. He is a honeybee at the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya. 

I worship Śrīla Gaurakiśora dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja, who concluded his earthly pastimes on the holy day of Utthāna Ekādaśī in the sacred place of Kuliyā. 

O Dayita Dāsa! You are the shining sun of truth, destroying sins in this world and revealing spiritual pastimes. We, your insignificant servants, have surrendered to your lotus feet and pray for your causeless mercy day after day.

IDX.verses: śhrī-guru-charaṇa-padma, kevala bhakati-sadma, vando muñi sāvadhāna-mate jāṅhāra prasāde bhāi, e bhava tariyā jāi, kṛṣṇa-prāpti haya jāṅhā ha’te guru-mukhapadma-vākya, chittete kariyā aikya, āra nā kariha mane āśhā śhrī-guru-charaṇe rati, ei sei uttamā gati, je-prasāde pūre sarva āśhā chakṣu-dāna dilā jei, janme janme prabhu sei, divyajñāna hṛde prakāśhita prema-bhakti jāṅhā haite, avidyā vināśha jāte, vede gāy jāṅhāra charita śhrī-guru karuṇā-sindhu, adhama janāra bandhu, ‘lokanātha’ lokera jīvana hā hā prabho! kara dayā, deha’ more pada-cḣāyā, tuyā pade loinu śharaṇa (ebe jaśha ghuṣuk tribhuvana)
IDX.en_translation:
The lotus feet of the spiritual master are the sole abode of devotion; I worship them with great care. By his mercy, O brother, we cross over this material existence, and the attainment of Kṛṣṇa occurs through him. 

Making the words from the lotus mouth of the spiritual master one with my heart, I have no other desire. Love for the feet of the spiritual master is the supreme destination; by his mercy, all desires are fulfilled. 

He who has given the gift of spiritual vision is the master in every birth; divine knowledge is revealed in the heart. From him loving devotion comes, by which ignorance is destroyed; the Vedas sing his glories. 

The spiritual master is an ocean of mercy, a friend of the fallen souls; he is the master and the life of all people. O Lord! Be merciful, give me the shelter of your feet; I take refuge at your feet. (May your fame spread throughout the three worlds.)
IDX.es_translation:
Los pies de loto de śhrī guru son el manantial del inmaculado prema-bhakti. Yo adoro esos pies de loto con sumo cuidado. ¡Oh hermano!, por la misericordia de śrī guru se puede cruzar el universo material y alcanzar a Śhrī Kṛṣṇa. 

Haz que las palabras que emanan de la boca de loto de śhrī guru purifiquen tu corazón y lo hagan uno con el suyo. No aspires a ninguna otra cosa. El apego por sus pies de loto es el objetivo supremo. Por su misericordia, todos los deseos se satisfacen. 

Aquel que otorga visión trascendental e ilumina mi corazón con conocimiento divino es mi amo nacimiento tras nacimiento. De él emana prema-bhakti y por él se destruye la ignorancia. Las escrituras védicas alaban su carácter. 

Śhrī guru es un océano de misericordia, el amigo de los caídos, y la vida y alma de todos. ¡Oh maestro! Sé misericordioso y dame la sombra de tus pies de loto. A ellos me he rendido. (Que tu fama se difunda por los tres mundos.)

IDX.verses:
śhrī-guru-vaiṣṇava-kṛpā kata dine ha’be 
upādhi-rahita-rati chitte upajibe

sakhī dekhāibe more yugala-vilāsa 

dekhite dekhite rūpa, hoiba vātula 
kadamba-kānane jā’ra tyaji’ jāti-kula 

‘sveda’ ‘kampa’ ‘pulakāśhru’ ‘vaivarṇya’ ‘pralaya’ 
‘stambha’ ‘svarabheda’ kabe hoibe udaya 

bhāvamaya vṛndāvana heriba nayane 
sakhīra kiṅkarī ha’ye seviba du’jane 

kabe narottama-saha sākṣāt hoibe 
kabe vā ‘prārthanā’-rasa chitte praveśhibe 

chaitanyadāsera dāsa cḣāḍi’ anya rati 
karayuḍi’ māge āja śhrī-chaitanya mati
IDX.en_translation:
When will the mercy of my spiritual master and the devotees come? When will unalloyed love arise in my heart? 

When will my perfected spiritual body manifest? When will a companion show me the divine pastimes of the Divine Couple? 

Gazing upon their forms, I will become mad with love; in the kadamba forest, I will abandon all social conventions and family ties. 

When will perspiration, trembling, thrills of ecstasy, tears, and fainting—along with stupefaction and a choking voice—manifest in me? 

With my own eyes, I will behold the spiritual Vṛndāvana; becoming a maidservant of a companion, I will serve the Divine Couple. 

When will I meet Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura? And when will the essence of his prayers enter my heart? 

Abandoning all other attachments and becoming a servant of the servant of Caitanya, today, with folded hands, I beg for the spirit of Śrī Caitanya.

śhrī-guru-vaiṣṇava, tomāra charaṇa, 
smaraṇa nā kainu āmi 
viṣaya viṣama, viṣa bhāla māni, 
khāicḣu hoiyā kāmī 

sei viṣe more, jāriyā mārila, 
baḍoi viṣama haila 
janame janame, emana katoi, 
ātmaghātī pāpa kaila 

sei aparādhe, e bhava-saṁsāre, 
bāṅdhile e māyājāle 
tomā’ nā bhajiyā, āpanā khāiyā, 
āpani ḍubecḣi hele 

āra kata kāla, e duḥkha bhuñjiba, 
bhoga-deha nāhi jāya 
sahite nāriyā, kātara hoiyā, 
nivedicḣi tuyā pāya 

o rāṅgā charaṇa, paraśha kevala,

IDX.en_translation:
O Śrī Guru and Vaiṣṇava, I did not remember your feet. I considered the dangerous poison of sense objects as good, and being lusty, I consumed it. 

That poison burned me and killed me; it became very severe. In birth after birth, how much such self-killing sin have I committed! 

For that offense, in this material world, I was bound in this net of illusion. Not worshipping you, devouring myself, I have drowned myself with ease. 

How much longer shall I suffer this misery? The body for enjoyment does not go away. Unable to tolerate, being distressed, I am submitting at your feet. 

Only the touch of those reddish feet—considering this crisis, delivering me, take me, O Friend of the Poor, on the boat of your feet. 

Your service is eating nectar; make me do it and keep me. This Rādhāmohana is sold by a written contract; write the price in the sky.

IDX.en_translation:
We offer respects to Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Brahmā, Devarṣi Nārada, and Bādarāyaṇa. We offer respects to Śrī Madhva, Śrī Padmanābha, Śrīmān Nṛhari, and Mādhava. 

We offer respects to Akṣobhya, Jayatīrtha, Śrī Jñānasindhu, Dayānidhi, Śrī Vidyānidhi, Rājendra, and Jayadharma in chronological order. 

We praise Puruṣottama, Brahmaṇya, and Vyāsatīrtha. Then, with devotion, we praise Lakṣmīpati and Śrīmān Mādhavendra Purī. 

We worship their disciples, the Jagad-gurūs Śrī Īśvara Purī, Advaita Āchārya, and Nityānanda Prabhu. We worship the Lord, the disciple of Īśvara Purī, Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu. 

He, who is the ocean of mercy Himself, delivered the universe which was burning in the filth of Kali by the gift of Śrī Kṛṣṇa-prema. 

Mahāprabhu’s Svarūpa Dāmodara is His associate who gives pleasure. Then the two best of the Gosvāmīs, Rūpa and Sanātana. 

And Śrī Jīva and Raghunātha, the great-minded one who is dear to Rūpa. His beloved is the great poet Kṛṣṇa-dāsa Kavirāja. 

His dearest friend is the one dedicated to service, Narottama Dāsa Ṭhākura. The devotee following him is the always excellent Śrī Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura. 

Attached to him is the ornament of the Gauḍīya Vedānta teachers, Śrī Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa, who is our eternal shelter. 

Then the Vaiṣṇava-sārvabhauma, Śrī Jagannātha Dāsa Bābājī, who indicated the abode of Śrī Māyāpura and is dear to the saintly people. 

The best here, the very root of the preaching of śuddha-bhakti, is the divine Śrī Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura, renowned as dear to him. 

His non-different best friend, the topmost mahā-bhāgavata, is Śrī Gaura Kiśora Dāsa Bābājī, who is vairāgya personified. 

The dispeller of the mass of darkness of the false conclusions of the Māyāvādīs, he causes the lotus of the heart to bloom with the conclusions of viśuddha-bhakti. 

He is the Paramahaṁsa, celebrated in the kīrtana of Śrī Gaura, always very eager in the activities of preaching and proper conduct. 

Understandable by the people dear to Hari, known as Oṁ Viṣṇupāda Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura Prabhupāda. 

His best intimate associate is Śrī Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava, who is known as Kṛtiratna in the pleasure of Gaura-vāṇī. 

His two best intimate associates, celebrated in the kīrtana of Śrī Gaura, are Vāmana and Nārāyaṇa, the best of Gosvāmīs and masters. 

All of them belong to the lineage of Gaura and are the personifications of Paramahaṁsas. And we are their surrendered servants, eager to take their remnants.
