IDX.author: govinda dāsa
IDX.verses: śhrī-kṛṣṇa-chaitanya, balarāma nityānanda, pāriṣada-saṅge avatāra golokera prema-dhana, sabāre jāchiñā dila, nā loinu muñi durāchāra āre pāmara mana, marame rahala baḍa śhela saṅkīrtana-prema-bādale, saba hiyā ḍubala, mohe vidhi vañchita kaila śhrī-guru-vaiṣṇavapada, kalpataru-cḣāyā pāñā, saba jīva tāpa pāsarila muñi abhāgiyā viṣa-, viṣaye mātiyā roinu, hena juge nistāra nā haila āgune puḍiyā maro, jale paraveśha karo, viṣa khāñā maro mo pāpiyā ei mata kari’ jadi, maraṇa nā kare vidhi, prāṇa rahe ki sukha lāgiyā e hena gaurāṅga-guṇa, nā karinu śhravaṇa, hāya hāya, kari hā hutāśha ‘hare kṛṣṇa’-mahāmantra, mukha bhari’ nā loilāma, jīvanmṛta govindadāsa
IDX.en_translation:
Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya and Nityānanda, along with Their associates, have descended to this world. They distributed the treasure of divine love from Goloka to everyone, but I, a wicked soul, did not accept it. 

O my wretched mind! A great spear remains in my heart. In the shower of saṅkīrtana and divine love, all hearts were immersed, but destiny has cheated me through illusion. 

Having attained the shade of the wish-fulfilling tree of the feet of the Guru and the Vaiṣṇavas, all living entities forgot their miseries. I, an unfortunate soul, remained absorbed in poisonous sense objects, and thus I did not attain deliverance in this age. 

I would rather die by fire, drown in water, or die by eating poison. If destiny does not grant me death in this way, for what happiness does my life still remain? 

I did not hear the glorious qualities of such a Lord Gaurāṅga. Alas, I cry out in lamentation! I did not chant the Hare Kṛṣṇa Mahā-mantra to my heart’s content. I am but the living dead, says Govinda Dāsa.

IDX.first_line: śhrī kṛṣṇa chaitanya gorā śhachīra dulāla
IDX.search: sri krsna chaitanya gora sachira dulala ei se purave cḣila gokulera gopala keha bale janaki vallabha cḣila rama keha bale nandalala navaghana syama purave kaliya cḣila gopipreme bhora bhaviya radhara varana ebe hoila gora cḣala cḣala aruna nayana anuragi na paiya bhavera ora hoila vairagi sannyasi vairagi haiya bhrame dese dese tamu na paila radhara premera uddese govinda dasiya kaya kisori kisora svarupa ramera sane sei rase bhora
IDX.author: govinda dāsa
IDX.verses: śhrī kṛṣṇa-chaitanya gorā śhachīra dulāla ei se pūrave cḣila gokulera gopāla keha bale,- ‘jānakī-vallabha cḣila rāma’ keha bale, ‘nandalāla navaghana-śhyāma’ pūrave kāliyā cḣila gopīpreme bhorā bhāviyā rādhāra varaṇa ebe hoila gorā cḣala cḣala aruṇa nayāna anurāgī nā pāiyā bhāvera ora hoila vairāgī sannyāsī vairāgī haiyā bhrame deśhe deśhe tamu nā pāila rādhāra premera uddeśhe govinda dāsiyā kaya kiśhorī kiśhorā svarūpa-rāmera sane sei rase bhorā
IDX.en_translation:
Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya is the beloved golden Son of Mother Śacī. He was previously the Cowherd Boy of Gokula. 

Some say: “He was Rāma, the beloved of Jānakī”. Some say: “He is Nandalāla, dark like a fresh raincloud”. 

Previously He was dark-complexioned and absorbed in the love of the gopīs. Contemplating Rādhā’s mood and complexion, He has now become golden. 

His reddish eyes are brimming with tears and filled with deep affection. Not finding the limit of this sentiment, He became a vairāgī. 

Having become a sannyāsī and a vairāgī, He wanders from country to country. Still, He has not found the ultimate object of Rādhā’s love. 

Govinda Dāsa says: “The Divine Maiden and the youthful Lord are absorbed in that divine mellow along with Svarūpa Dāmodara”.

IDX.search: sri krsna gopala hare mukunda govinda he nanda kisora krsna ha sri yasoda tanaya prasida sri vallavi jivana radhikesa
IDX.author: unknown paramparāgata (traditional)
IDX.verses:
śhrī-kṛṣṇa gopāla hare mukunda, 
govinda he nanda kiśhora-kṛṣṇa 

hā śhrī-yaśhodā-tanaya prasīda, 
śhrī-vallavī-jīvana rādhikeśha
IDX.en_translation:
Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Gopāla, Hare, Mukunda, Govinda, O Nanda-kiśora Kṛṣṇa! 

O son of Mother Yaśodā, please be merciful! O Life of the gopīs, O Master of Rādhikā!
IDX.es_translation: ¡Oh, Śhrī Kṛṣṇa! ¡Gopāla! ¡Hari! ¡Mukunda! ¡Govinda! ¡Oh Nanda-kiśhora ¡Kṛṣṇa! ¡Otórgame Tu gracia, oh amado hijo de Yaśhodā! ¡Oh, vida de las gopīs! ¡Oh, Señor de Rādhikā!

IDX.first_line: śhrī kṛṣṇa kīrtane jadi mānasa tohāra
IDX.search: sri krsna kirtane jadi manasa tohara parama jatane tamhi labha adhikara trnadhika hina dina akinchana cḣara apane manabi sada cḣadi ahankara vrksasama ksama guna karabi sadhana pratihimsa tyaji anye karabi palana jivana nirvahe ane udvega na dibe para upakare nija sukha pasaribe hoileo sarvagune guni mahasaya pratisthasa cḣadi kara amani hrdaya krsna adhisthana sarva jive jani sada karabi sammana sabe adare sarvada dainya daya anye mana pratistha varjana charigune guni hoi karaha kirtana bhakativinoda kandi bale prabhu paya hena adhikara kabe dibe he amaya
IDX.author: sacchidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses: śhrī-kṛṣṇa kīrtane jadi mānasa tohāra parama jatane taṁhi labha adhikāra tṛṇādhika hīna dīna akiñchana cḣāra āpane mānabi sadā cḣāḍi’ ahaṅkāra vṛkṣasama kṣamā guṇa karabi sādhana pratihiṁsā tyaji’ anye karabi pālana jīvana-nirvāhe āne udvega nā dibe para-upakāre nija-sukha pāsaribe hoileo sarvaguṇe guṇī mahāśhaya pratiṣṭhāśhā cḣāḍi’ kara amānī hṛdaya kṛṣṇa-adhiṣṭhāna sarva jīve jāni’ sadā karabi sammāna sabe ādare sarvadā dainya, dayā, anye māna, pratiṣṭhā varjana chāriguṇe guṇī hoi’, karaha kīrtana bhakativinoda kāṅdi’ bale prabhu pāya hena adhikāra kabe dibe he āmāya
IDX.en_translation:
If your mind is set on the glorification of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, then with great care, attain the qualification for it. 

Always consider yourself more humble than a blade of grass, poor and insignificant, and give up all false ego. 

Practice the quality of forgiveness like a tree; giving up all vengeance, maintain others. 

Do not cause anxiety to others for the sake of your own livelihood; for the welfare of others, forget your own happiness. 

Even if you are a great soul endowed with all good qualities, give up the desire for prestige and keep your heart free from pride. 

Always knowing that Kṛṣṇa resides in all living entities, you should always respectfully honor everyone with affection. 

Humility, compassion, respecting others, and rejecting prestige—being qualified with these four virtues, perform congregational chanting. 

Bhaktivinoda cries and says at the feet of the Lord: “When will You grant me such qualification?”
IDX.es_translation:
Si deseas dedicar tu mente al śhrī kṛṣṇa-kīrtana, debes ganarte muy cuidadosamente la aptitud espiritual [requerida]. 

Domina tu orgullo falso, considérate siempre más caído e insignificante que una brizna de hierba, miserable e indigno. 

Cultiva una tolerancia como la de los árboles. Abandona toda clase de represalias, y cuida y ayuda a los demás. 

Durante tu vida, no causes ansiedad a nadie. Por el bien de los demás, olvida tu propia comodidad. 

Aunque seas una gran alma dotada de todas las cualidades, renuncia al deseo de recibir honores y vuelve tu corazón humilde. 

Consciente de que Śhrī Kṛṣṇa está situado dentro de todos los seres, respeta y muestra afecto a todos. 

Dotado de las cuatro virtudes de la humildad, la compasión, el respeto a los demás y la modestia, haz kīrtana del Señor. 

Llorando a los pies del Señor, Bhaktivinoda suplica: “¿Cuándo me concederás esas cualidades?”

IDX.first_line: śhrī kṛṣṇa seviba bali’ gṛha cḣāḍi’ kuñje chali’
IDX.search: sri krsna seviba bali grha cḣadi kunje chali jaite haya abhisari sakhi kunjasajja kare jabe vasakasajja hana tabe utkanthita krsna patha lakhi kala ullanghiya hari bhoga chihna dehe dhari aile hana khandita takhana sanketa paiya baise tabu kanta na aise vipralabdha nayika ta hana manera kalahe hari jana chali duhkha kari kalahantarita santapini mathurate kanta gela bahu dina na aila prosita bhartrka kangalini nijayatte kante peye krida kare kanta laye svadhina bhartrka se ramani nayikamatrera haya ei astadasodaya vipralambha sambhoga bodhini
IDX.author: sacchidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
śhrī-kṛṣṇa seviba bali’, gṛha cḣāḍi’ kuñje chali’, 
jāite haya ‘abhisārī’ sakhi 
kuñjasajjā kare jabe, ‘vāsakasajjā’ hana tabe, 
‘utkaṇṭhitā’ kṛṣṇa-patha lakhi’ 

kāla ullaṅghiyā hari, bhoga-chihna dehe dhari’, 
āile hana ‘khaṇḍitā’ takhana 
saṅketa pāiyā baise, tabu kānta nā āise, 
‘vipralabdhā’ nāyikā ta’ ha’na 

manera kalahe hari, jāna chali’ duḥkha kari’, 
‘kalahāntaritā’ santāpinī 
mathurāte kānta gela, bahu-dina nā āila, 
‘proṣita-bhartṛkā’ kāṅgālinī 

nijāyatte kānte peye, krīḍā kare kānta laye, 
‘svādhīna-bhartṛkā’ se ramaṇī 
nāyikāmātrera haya, ei aṣṭadaśhodaya, 
vipralambha-sambhoga-bodhinī
IDX.en_translation:
Thinking, “I will serve Śrī Kṛṣṇa,” leaving home and going to the grove, she becomes an “abhisārī”. When she decorates the grove, she then becomes a “vāsakasajjā”, and when watching for Kṛṣṇa’s path, she is an “utkaṇṭhitā”. 

When Hari arrives late, bearing the marks of enjoyment on His body, she then becomes a “khaṇḍitā”. When she waits after receiving a signal but her beloved does not come, she becomes a “vipralabdhā”. 

In a quarrel of the mind, Hari goes away sorrowfully; she is a “kalahāntaritā”, full of distress. When her beloved goes to Mathurā and does not return for a long time, she becomes a “proṣita-bhartṛkā”, a pauper in love. 

Having her beloved under her control, she plays with him; that woman is a “svādhīna-bhartṛkā”. These eighteen states arise for every heroine, illuminating both separation and union.

IDX.search: sri krsna virahe radhikara dasa ami ta sahite nari yugala milana sukhera karana jivana cḣadite pari radhika charana tyajiya amara ksaneke pralaya haya radhikara tare satabara mari se duhkha amara saya e hena radhara charana yugale paricharya paba kabe ha ha vraja jana more daya kari kabe vraja vane labe vilasa manjari anangamanjari sri rupamanjari ara amake tuliya laha nija pade deha mora siddhi sara
IDX.author: sacchidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
śhrī-kṛṣṇa-virahe, rādhikāra daśhā, 
āmi ta’ sahite nāri 
yugala-milana, sukhera kāraṇa, 
jīvana cḣāḍite pāri 

rādhikā-charaṇa, tyajiyā āmāra, 
kṣaṇeke pralaya haya 
rādhikāra tare, śhatabāra mari, 
se-duḥkha āmāra saya 

e hena rādhāra, charaṇa-yugale, 
paricharyā pā’ba kabe 
hā hā vraja-jana, more dayā kari’, 
kabe vraja-vane la’be 

vilāsa-mañjarī, anaṅgamañjarī, 
śhrī-rūpamañjarī āra 
āmāke tuliyā, laha nija-pade, 
deha mora siddhi-sāra
IDX.en_translation:
The condition of Rādhikā in separation from Śrī Kṛṣṇa - I cannot tolerate it. For the sake of the happiness of the divine couple’s union, I can give up my life. 

Abandoning Rādhikā’s feet even for a moment, is a great distress for me. For Rādhikā’s sake, I can die a hundred times; I will endure that agony. 

When will I attain the service At the lotus feet of such a Rādhā? Alas, alas, O people of Vraja, showing mercy to me, When will you take me to the forest of Vraja? 

O Vilāsa Mañjarī, Anaṅga Mañjarī, And Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī, Please lift me up and take me to your feet, Grant me the essence of ultimate perfection.
IDX.es_translation:
Soy incapaz de tolerar la condición de Rādhikā separada de Śhrī Kṛṣṇa. Por lo tanto, estoy totalmente dispuesto a abandonar mi vida en favor de Su feliz reencuentro. 

Me sentiría totalmente devastado si tuviese que renunciar a los pies de loto de Rādhikā aunque fuese por un instante. Por Ella yo toleraría la agonía de la muerte cientos de veces. 

¿Cuándo podré servir los pies de loto de Rādhikā? ¡Oh, residentes de Vraja! ¿Cuándo serán misericordiosos conmigo y me llevarán a los bosques de Vraja? 

¡Oh, Vilāsa Mañjarī! ¡Oh, Anaṅga Mañjarī! ¡Oh, Rūpa Mañjarī! Por favor, levántenme y llévenme cerca de sus pies de loto, y concédanme así la perfección suprema.

IDX.search: sri krsnachaitanya nityananda dui prabhu ei krpa kara jena na pasara kabhu hoila papistha janma na hoila takhane vanchita hoinu sei sukha darasane tathapiha ei krpa kara mahasaya e saba vihara mora rahuka hrdaya jaya jaya sri chaitanya nityananda raya tomara charana dhana rahuka hiyaya saparsade tumi nityananda jatha jatha krpa kara muni jena bhrtya hoi tatha samsarera para hana bhaktira sagare je dubibe se bhajuka nitaichandere hena dina hoibe chaitanya nityananda dekhiba vestita ki sakala bhakta vrnda sri chaitanya nityanandachanda pahun jana vrndavana dasa tacḣu padayuge gana
IDX.author: vṛndāvana-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: śhrī-kṛṣṇachaitanya nityānanda dui prabhu ei kṛpā kara jena nā pāsara kabhu hoila pāpiṣṭha-janma nā hoila takhane vañchita hoinu sei sukha-daraśhane tathāpiha ei kṛpā kara mahāśhaya e saba vihāra mora rahuka hṛdaya jaya jaya śhrī-chaitanya, nityānanda rāya tomāra charaṇa-dhana rahuka hiyāya sapārṣade tumi nityānanda jathā jathā kṛpā kara muñi jena bhṛtya hoi tathā saṁsārera pāra hañā bhaktira sāgare je ḍubibe, se bhajuka nitāichāṅdere hena dina hoibe chaitanya-nityānanda dekhiba veṣṭita ki sakala bhakta-vṛnda śhrī-chaitanya-nityānandachāṅda pahuṅ jāna vṛndāvana-dāsa tacḣu padayuge gāna
IDX.en_translation:
Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya and Nityānanda are my two Lords. Please grant this mercy, so that I never forget them. 

I was born a sinner; I was not present then. I was deprived of the sight of that happiness. 

Still, please grant this mercy, O great souls. May all these pastimes remain in my heart. 

All glories, all glories to Śrī Caitanya, Nityānanda Rāya. May the treasure of Your lotus feet remain in my heart. 

Wherever You are with Your associates, O Nityānanda, Please grant mercy so that I may be Your servant there. 

Crossing beyond this material world into the ocean of devotion, Whoever will dive, let them worship Nitāicāñda. 

Will such a day come when Caitanya and Nityānanda I will see surrounded by all devotees? 

Know that Śrī Caitanya-Nityānandacāñda are Lords. Vṛndāvana Dāsa sings at their lotus feet.

IDX.first_line: śhrī kṛṣṇa-chaitanya prabhu dayā kara more
IDX.search: sri krsna chaitanya prabhu daya kara more toma vina ke dayalu jagat samsare patita pavana hetu tava avatara mo sama patita prabhu na paibe ara ha ha prabhu nityananda premananda sukhi krpavalokana kara ami bada duhkhi daya kara sitapati advaita gosai tava krpabale pai chaitanya nitai ha ha svarupa sanatana rupa raghunatha bhatta yuga sri jiva ha prabhu lokanatha daya kara sri acharya prabhu srinivasa ramachandra sanga mage narottama dasa daya kara prabhupada sri dayitadasa vaisnavera krpa mage e adhama dasa daya kara gurudeva patita pavana sri charane seva mage e patitajana
IDX.author: narottama-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses: śhrī kṛṣṇa-chaitanya prabhu dayā kara more tomā’ vinā ke dayālu jagat-saṁsāre patita-pāvana-hetu tava avatāra mo sama patita prabhu nā pāibe āra hā hā prabhu nityānanda premānanda-sukhī kṛpāvalokana kara āmi baḍa duḥkhī gaura premamaya tanu paṇḍita gadādhara śhrīnivāsa haridāsa dayāra sāgara dayā kara sītāpati advaita gosāi tava kṛpābale pāi chaitanya-nitāi hā hā svarūpa, sanātana, rūpa, raghunātha bhaṭṭa-yuga, śhrī-jīva, hā prabhu lokanātha dayā kara śhrī-āchārya prabhu śhrīnivāsa rāmachandra-saṅga māge narottama-dāsa [dayā kara prabhupāda śhrī-dayitadāsa vaiṣṇavera kṛpā māge e adhama dāsa dayā kara gurudeva patita-pāvana śhrī-charaṇe sevā māge e patitajana]
IDX.en_translation:
O Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, please be merciful to me. Who else but You is merciful in this world? 

Your incarnation is for the purpose of delivering the fallen. O Lord, You will not find anyone as fallen as me. 

Alas, alas, Lord Nityānanda, who is joyful in divine love! Please cast Your merciful glance upon me; I am very distressed. 

<highlight>Gadādhara Paṇḍita’s body is filled with prema for Gaura. Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita and Haridāsa Ṭhākura are oceans of mercy.</highlight> 

Please be merciful, Advaita Gosāi, the Lord of Sītā. By the strength of Your mercy, I attain Caitanya and Nitāi. 

Alas, alas, Svarūpa, Sanātana, Rūpa, and Raghunātha! O two Bhaṭṭas, O Śrī Jīva, O Lord Lokanātha! 

Please be merciful, Śrīnivāsa Āchārya. Narottama dāsa begs for the association of Rāmacandra Kavirāja. 

Please be merciful, Prabhupāda Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī! This wretched servant begs for the mercy of the devotees. 

Please be merciful, Gurudeva, deliverer of the fallen! This fallen person begs for service at your divine feet.
IDX.es_translation:
¡Oh, Śhrī Kṛṣṇa Chaitanya Prabhu! Ten piedad de mí. Aparte de Ti, ¿quién en esta existencia material está tan lleno de compasión? 

El motivo de Tu aparición es liberar a las almas caídas. ¡Oh, Señor! No encontrarás a nadie tan caído como yo. 

¡Oh, Nityānanda Prabhu que estás siempre jubiloso debido al amor extático! Mírame con compasión, porque estoy sumamente triste. 

<highlight>El cuerpo de Gadādhara Paṇḍita está saturado de prema por Gaura. Śhrīvāsa Paṇḍita y Haridāsa Ṭhākura son océanos de misericordia.</highlight> 

¡Oh, Advaita Gosāi, esposo de Sītā! Sé bondadoso conmigo. Por el poder de Tu misericordia podré alcanzar sin duda a Śhrī Chaitanya-Nitāi. 

¡Oh, Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, Sanātana Gosvāmī, Rūpa Gosvāmī y Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī! ¡Oh, Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī y Śhrī Jīva Gosvāmī! ¡Oh, mi maestro Lokanātha Gosvāmī (concédeme tu misericordia)! 

¡Oh Śhrīnivāsa Āchārya Prabhu, ten misericordia de mí! Narottama dāsa implora la asociación de Rāmachandra Kavirāja. 

<highlight>¡Oh, Prabhupāda, sirviente del amado de Śhrī Rādhā! Muéstrame tu misericordia. Este sirviente caído suplica a los vaiṣṇavas que sean bondadosos.</highlight> 

 <highlight>¡Oh, Gurudeva, salvador de los caídos! Ten misericordia. Esta persona caída suplica que le otorgues servicio a tus pies de loto.</highlight>

IDX.verses: tuwā bhakti-pratikūla dharma jā’te raya parama jatane tāhā tyajiba niśhchaya tuwā bhakti-bahirmukha saṅga nā kariba gaurāṅga-virodhi-jana mukha nā heriba bhakti-pratikūla sthāne nā kari vasati bhaktira apriya kārye nāhi kari rati bhaktira virodhī grantha pāṭha nā kariba bhaktira virodhī vyākhyā kabhu nā śhuniba gaurāṅgavarjita sthāna tīrtha nāhi māni bhaktira vādhaka jñāna-karma tuccḣa jāni bhaktira vādhaka kāle nā kari ādara bhakti-bahirmukha nija-jane jāni para bhaktira bādhikā spṛhā kariba varjana abhakta-pradatta anna nā kari grahaṇa jāhā kicḣu bhakti-pratikūla bali’ jāni tyajiba jatane tāhā, e niśhchaya vāṇī bhakativinoda pari’ prabhura charaṇe māgaye śhakati prātikūlyera varjane
IDX.translation_intro: From The Harmonist, December 1928. Edited by Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī.
IDX.en_translation:
That which maintains as duty aversion to Thy service I will assuredly discard with the utmost care, 

I will not cultivate the society of those who refuse to serve, I will not see the faces of those who oppose Gaurāṅga. 

I will never dwell at the place that obstructs my devotion. I have no relish for work that contravenes the service of the Lord. 

I will never read the book that is opposed to devotion, Nor ever listen to interpretation that forbids Thy service. 

I will never regard as sacred any spot from which Gaurāṅga is banished. I hold as trivial the work and knowledge that hinder devotion. 

I do not esteem the season that stands in the way of Thy service; Those kindred who are disinclined to serve I hold as strangers. 

I will give up every desire that hampers devotion. I will not touch the food that is offered by atheists. 

Whatever I know to be contrary to devotion I will carefully avoid, this I do strongly affirm. 

Bhakativinode falling at the feet of the Lord Begs for strength to give up everything opposed to devotion.
IDX.es_translation:
Renunciaré cuidadosamente a cualquier [presunto] dharma que se oponga a los preceptos del bhakti. 

Jamás me asociaré con quienes rechazan el bhakti por Ti, y jamás miraré la cara de quienes sienten aversión por Śhrī Gaurāṅga. 

Nunca residiré en ningún lugar que sea perjudicial para el bhakti y nunca me apegaré a ninguna labor desacorde con el bhakti. 

Jamás leeré escritos que vayan en contra de la doctrina del bhakti ni prestaré oídos a discursos que se opongan al bhakti. 

No reconozco como tīrtha (lugar sagrado) ningún lugar que no esté relacionado con Śhrī Gaurāṅga. Considero totalmente vano cualquier karma o jñāna que constituya un obstáculo para el bhakti. 

Jamás celebro ninguna ocasión que sea un impedimento para el bhakti. Los familiares que no son favorables al bhakti son extraños para mí. 

Abandonaré cualquier deseo que perturbe el bhakti, y nunca aceptaré comidas ofrecidas por no-devotos. 

Renunciaré cuidadosamente a todo aquello que sepa que es desfavorable. Esta es mi promesa. 

Cayendo a los pies de loto del Señor, Bhaktivinoda suplica que se le conceda la fuerza para dominar todo aquello que es desfavorable para la devoción pura.

IDX.first_line: śhrī kṛṣṇachaitanya prabhu jīve dayā kari’
IDX.search: sri krsnachaitanya prabhu jive daya kari svaparsada sviya dhama saha avatari atyanta durlabha prema karibare dana sikhaya saranagati bhakatera prana dainya atmanivedana goptrtve varana avasya raksibe krsna visvasa palana bhakti anukulamatra karyera svikara bhakti pratikula bhava varjanangikara sadanga saranagati hoibe janhara tanhara prarthana sune sri nandakumara rupa sanatana pade dante trna kari bhakativinoda pade duhu pada dhari kandiya kandiya bale ami ta adhama sikhaye saranagati kara he uttama
IDX.author: sacchidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
śhrī-kṛṣṇachaitanya prabhu jīve dayā kari’ 
svapārṣada svīya dhāma saha avatari’ 

atyanta durlabha prema karibāre dāna 
śhikhāya śharaṇāgati bhakatera prāṇa 

dainya, ātmanivedana, goptṛtve varaṇa 
‘avaśhya rakṣibe kṛṣṇa’-viśhvāsa-pālana 

bhakti-anukūlamātra kāryera svīkāra 
bhakti-pratikūla-bhāva varjanāṅgīkāra 

ṣaḍaṅga śharaṇāgati hoibe jāṅhāra 
tāṅhāra prārthanā śhune śhrī-nandakumāra 

rūpa-sanātana-pade dante tṛṇa kari’ 
bhakativinoda paḍe duhū pada dhari’ 

kāṅdiyā kāṅdiyā bale- ‘āmi ta’ adhama 
śhikhāye śharaṇāgati kara he uttama”
IDX.translation_intro: From The Harmonist, July 1927. Edited by Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī.
IDX.en_translation:
Sree Krishna Chaitanya, the Supreme Lord, out of divine pity for jiva, With His own associates and His own abode descending 

The love of God that can only be obtained with the utmost difficulty to give freely away, Teaches to take refuge in Him: resignation, that is the very life of the devotee. 

Lowliness of spirit, dedication of self, loving acceptance of Him as protector, Cherishing faith that Krishna will surely protect. 

Assenting only to acts that are conducive to devotion, Promising to renounce conduct that is adverse to it-- 

In these sixfold ways, whoever takes refuge in Him, His prayer reaches the ears of the gracious Child of Nanda. 

At the feet of Rupa and Sanatana holding the straw between the teeth Falls Bhaktivinode clasping both the feet with his hands 

Crying all the while as he says: “I am the vilest, I do realise, Teach thou me resignation and make me the worthiest.”
IDX.es_translation:
Lleno de compasión por las entidades vivientes, Śhrī Kṛṣṇa Chaitanya Prabhu descendió a este mundo junto con Sus asociados personales y Su morada divina. 

Para otorgar el extraordinario tesoro del prema-bhakti, Él enseñó el proceso de śharaṇāgati, que es el alma y la vida de los devotos. 

Humildad, dedicación, aceptar que el Señor es nuestro único sustento y guardián, tener fe en que Kṛṣṇa nos protegerá… 

… aceptar los actos que son favorables para el bhakti y rechazar lo desfavorable. 

El hijo de Nanda Mahārāja escucha las oraciones de quien personifica estos seis aspectos del śharaṇāgati. 

Colocando paja entre sus dientes, Bhaktivinoda se postra ante Śhrī Rūpa y Sanātana Gosvāmīs y abraza sus pies de loto. 

Lamentándose, exclama: “¡Soy el más caído entre los hombres! Enséñenme rendición incondicional y conviértanme en un perfecto vaiṣṇava.”

IDX.first_line: śhrī kṛṣṇaḥ paramānando govindo nanda nandanaḥ
IDX.search: sri krsnah paramanando govindo nanda nandanah tamala syamala ruchih sikhanda krta sekharah pita kauseya vasano madhura smita sobhitah kandarpa koti lavanyo vrndaranya mahotsavah vaijayanti sfurad vaksah kaksatta lagudottamah kunjarpitaratir gunja punja manjula kanthakah karnikaradhya karna sri r dhrta svarnabha varnakah murali vadana patur vallavi kula vallabhah gandharvapti maha parva radharadhana pesalah iti sri krsna chandrasya nama vimsati samjnakam anandakhyam maha stotram jah pathech cḣrnuyach cha jah sa param saukhyam asadya krsna prema samanvitah sarva loka priyo bhutva sad gunavali bhusitah vraja raja kumarasya sannikarsam avapnuyat
IDX.author: rūpa gosvāmī
IDX.verses:
śhrī-kṛṣṇaḥ paramānando govindo nanda-nandanaḥ 
tamāla-śhyāmala-ruchiḥ śhikhaṇḍa-kṛta-śhekharaḥ 

pīta-kauśheya-vasano madhura-smita-śhobhitaḥ 
kandarpa-koṭi-lāvaṇyo vṛndāraṇya-mahotsavaḥ 

vaijayantī-sfurad-vakṣāḥ kakṣātta-laguḍottamaḥ 
kuñjārpitaratir guñjā-puñja-mañjula-kaṇṭhakaḥ 

karṇikārāḍhya-karṇa-śhrī-r-dhṛta-svarṇābha-varṇakaḥ 
muralī-vādana-paṭur vallavī-kula-vallabhaḥ 

gāndharvāpti-mahā-parvā rādhārādhana-peśhalaḥ 
iti śhrī-kṛṣṇa-chandrasya nāma viṁśhati-saṁjñakam 

ānandākhyaṁ mahā-stotraṁ jaḥ paṭhech cḣṛṇuyāch cha jaḥ 
sa paraṁ saukhyam āsādya kṛṣṇa-prema-samanvitaḥ 

sarva-loka-priyo bhūtvā sad-guṇāvali-bhūṣitaḥ 
vraja-rāja-kumārasya sannikarṣam avāpnuyāt
IDX.en_translation:
Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Bliss, Govinda, the Son of Nanda. His luster is dark like the Tamāla; He has made a crown of a peacock feather. 

He wears yellow silk cloth; He is adorned with a sweet smile. His beauty is that of millions of Cupids; He is the great festival of the forest of Vṛndā. 

His chest shines with the Vaijayantī garland; He holds an excellent staff under His arm. He is attached to the groves; His throat is charming with a cluster of Guñjā. 

His ears are wealthy with the Karṇikāra; He wears golden-colored pigments. He is expert in playing the flute; He is the beloved of the community of cowherd women. 

He is the great festival of the attainment of Gāndharvā; He is expert in the worship of Rādhā. Thus, these are the twenty names of Śrī Kṛṣṇa-candra. 

He who reads and he who hears this great Stotra named “Ānanda” (Bliss), attaining supreme happiness, endowed with love for Kṛṣṇa. 

Becoming dear to all people, adorned with a multitude of good qualities, he attains the vicinity of the Prince of Vraja.

IDX.en_translation:
I offer obeisances to Lalitā-devī, who is beautifully adorned with all good qualities. Seeing Rādhā on the path of the party of Kṛṣṇa, she immediately makes Her successful by fulfilling Her desire. 

Lalitā, Viśākhā, Citrā, Campakalatā, Raṅgadevī, Sudevī, Tuṅgavidyā, and Indurekhā. I offer my obeisances again and again to these eight Sakhīs. Still, Lalitā is my all-in-all, worshipped by everyone. 

O wish-fulfilling creeper of mercy, Lalitā! Obeisances to you. O Viśākhā, possessing cleverness and qualities equal to Rādhā! I praise you, O Campakalatā, who steals the mind of Acyuta! I bow to you, O friend Citralekhā, of wonderful character! 

O Śrī Raṅgadevī! O beloved! O stage for the limbs of love! Let there be obeisances to you, O giver of happiness, O beloved Sudevī! O Tuṅgavidyā, even in the abode of knowledge and pleasure! O Indulekhā, whose nails are like pieces of the full moon and who has a beautiful face! 

I take shelter of the maidservants headed by Rūpa Mañjarī in the play-grounds. They please the Great Queen of Vṛndāvana (Rādhā) with affection by offering betel, massaging Her feet, giving water, and arranging trysts—tasks which are unhesitatingly performed even by the group of Sakhīs who are dearer to Her than life. 

You are the form of Mahābhāva, the best of the beloveds of Kṛṣṇa. O Devi Rādhikā, bestower of loving devotion, I bow to You. 

O Rādhe, Queen of Vṛndāvana, River of the nectar of compassion! Please mercifully give me the service of Your own lotus feet. 

I worship Rādhā who has lotus eyes; I remember Rādhā who has a sweet smile on Her face; I speak of Rādhā who is melted by the burden of compassion. Therefore, I have no other goal. 

Alas, O Devi! Today, with a voice choked with piteous words, falling on the ground like a stick, I beg with intense distress: bestowing mercy on this ignorant person, O Gāndharvikā, please count me among Your own people. 

O Devi! I indeed never beg for anything else at any time except for the excellent service of Your lotus feet. Obeisances to Your friendship; obeisances always. May my taste be for Your service; may it be true. 

I bow to the Goddess Śrī Hari-priyā, Rādhā, the Queen of the Rāsa dance, beautiful, the supreme enchantress of Govinda, the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu. 

O You who enjoy the festival of the Rāsa dance! Obeisances to You, O Supreme Goddess! O Rādhā, dearer than the life of Kṛṣṇa! O Form of supreme bliss! 

I take shelter of Rādhikā, the beloved of the son of the King of Vraja. She has the luster of a spotless lotus, wears blue garments, has beautiful hair, a face like the moon, and eyes like a wagtail bird. She is charming, and shines with a pearl necklace on Her chest. She is an adolescent. 

When will I be the sweeper of the courtyard of the play-grove of the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu, the ocean of rasa? The Supreme Person with a peacock-feather crown (Kṛṣṇa) always speaks many plaintive words to Her maidservants. 

I remember with my mind the child Mukunda, who is placing His lotus foot with His lotus hand into His lotus mouth, sitting on the lap of the Queen of Vraja and smiling. 

I praise Kṛṣṇa in the form of Gopāla, the son of Yaśodā, dark like a fresh raincloud, with eyes like blue lotuses. 

I worship the child dark like a tamāla leaf, with restless eyes due to the blowing breath of the Queen of the Cowherds (Yaśodā), crawling on the earth with both knees, His lips like nectar with a slight fresh smile. 

We meditate on the root of Brahman, the protector of the dynasty of the people of Vraja, the athlete Śrīla Gopāla. His very sweet pastimes, His habit of playing the flute, holding the hill in His palm; His dark limbs put to shame the blue raincloud. 

Having abandoned sleep at dawn due to the sound of churning yogurt, entering the solitary room of the cowherd women, quickly extinguishing the lamps with the wind from His lotus mouth, having eaten the fresh butter—may the child Kṛṣṇa protect me. 

Holding the string of small bells with His left hand to silence them, bending down, smiling gently, moving on tiptoes; forbidding the smiling girls in front of Him with a glance of His eyes, Hari stole the fresh butter from behind His mother. 

Obeisances to the Lord of the brāhmaṇas, and to the benefactor of the cows and brāhmaṇas; to the benefactor of the world, to Kṛṣṇa, to Govinda, obeisances, obeisances. 

To remove the fear of material existence, the author of the scriptures gathered the essence of knowledge and realization, the essence of the Vedas, like a bee; and made the servants drink the nectar from the ocean. I bow to the First Person, the Best, named Kṛṣṇa. 

I worship Govinda, who is dedicated to playing the sweet flute, who is adorned with divine ornaments. His luster is like a blooming blue lotus, His face is like the moon, He is fond of the peacock feather ornament. He bears the Śrīvatsa mark, wears the large Kaustubha jewel, is dressed in yellow garments, and is beautiful. His body is worshiped by the lotus eyes of the gopīs, and He is surrounded by the herds of cows and cowherds. 

Musk tilaka on the forehead, Kaustubha on the chest, a fine pearl on the tip of the nose, a flute in the palm of the hand, a bracelet on the wrist. Sandalwood paste on the whole body, a pearl necklace on the neck—surrounded by the cowherd women, the Crest-jewel of Cowherds is victorious. 

Delightful with a peacock feather crown, with a musk tilaka, with cheeks touched by earrings. Lotus-eyed, conch-necked, with a face beautiful with a smile, with a flute placed on His lips. Dark, peaceful, three-fold bending, with garments like the sun’s rays, adorned with a Vaijayantī garland. I bow to Him standing in Vṛndāvana, surrounded by hundreds of young women, in the dress of a brāhmaṇa-cowherd. 

I praise the son of Nanda, the beloved of the gopīs, Śrī Govinda. Who is dark like a cloud, wearing supreme yellow garments. 

Obeisances to Kṛṣṇa, to Kṛṣṇa-candra, sporting in Vṛndāvana. Obeisances to You, the Lord of the cowherd women; obeisances to the Husband of Rādhikā. 

Obeisances to the son of the King of Cowherds, pleasing to millions of Cupids, with the luster of a blooming blue lotus, whose pastimes enchant the world. 

I praise the son of Śrī Nanda, whose body is sweet rasa, who is full of the highest sweetness. Who has placed the flute on His moon-face, endowed with a smile, incomparable, wearing excellent yellow garments. Lotus-eyed, expert in everything, like a fresh cloud, with a peacock-feather crown, the Shelter. With a body curved in three places, accompanied by the young women of Vraja, the Hero who destroyed Keśī and others. 

Obeisances to the lotus-eyed one, who delights in playing the flute. Who is accustomed to drinking the nectar of Rādhā’s lips, who wears a forest garland. 

Obeisances to Kṛṣṇa, Vāsudeva, Hari, the Supreme Soul. To the destroyer of the distress of the surrendered, to Govinda, obeisances, obeisances. 

Meditate on Rādhikā and Kṛṣṇa-candra in the solitary grove of Cupid. Their bodies are like gold and a raincloud; Their eyes are like blue and red lotuses. Their foreheads are excellent with musk; They wear garlands of mālatī and kunda flowers. Their dress is trembling and youthful; They are the Lords of blue and yellow garments. 

We meditate on Dāmodara, whose arm, bright with luster, is placed on Rādhā’s shoulder. Who dims the blue lotus on all sides with the rays of the blackness of His body. Who defeats the luster of saffron with the beauty of His silk garment. Who resides in the forest of Vṛndā; who is fragrant with garlands shining on His chest. 

All glories, all glories to this forest of Vṛndā of Murāri! Dearer than Vaikuṇṭha because of the presence of the very saintly ones. Where He always gives pleasure to the cows, protecting the gopīs; increasing love in the Rāsa dance with His sounding sweet flute. 

I bow to that Vṛndāvana, the form of sweetness. Which is filled with the multitudes of bliss of Indirā (Rādhā). Where the son of Nanda is delighted by the multitudes of bliss. Which is delighted by the beautiful bride of Govinda. 

Obeisances to You, O Holder of the Plow! Obeisances, O Wielder of the Club! Obeisances, O Husband of Revatī! Obeisances, O Affectionate to the Devotees! 

Obeisances, O Best of the Strong! Obeisances, O Holder of the Earth! O Enemy of Pralamba, obeisances to You! Protect me, O Elder Brother of Kṛṣṇa! 

Alas! This Hill, O friend, is the best of the servants of Hari! Because, being jubilant by the touch of the feet of Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, it offers respect to Them along with the cows and cowherd boys, with drinking water, good grass, caves, roots, and bulbs. 

Victory to Govardhana, the King of the mountains! Who was declared by the gopīs to be the best servant of Hari. Who was worshipped by Kṛṣṇa to stop the sacrifice of Indra. Who resided on the palm of His lotus hand for seven days. 

I bow my head to Govardhana Hill. Which was served by Hari with His own groups for seven days. Which became like a bee on the lotus hand of Acyuta; with fruits, roots, and caves. 

We praise the divine lake (Rādhā-kuṇḍa) dear to the Mistress of That One (Kṛṣṇa) maddened in battle (of love). Which is always a mine of astonishment of great rasa by the sweet pastimes of the Endless Hari and Rādhikā. Which is greatly effulgent and most fragrant in Vṛndāvana. 

O Śrī Sarovara (Lake)! My Mistress always plays here with Her Beloved with amorous sports. If You are thus dearer than the dear to Them, alas! show me Her, my life, today by mercy. 

Just as Rādhā is dear to Viṣṇu, so is Her Kuṇḍa dear. Among all the gopīs, She alone is the most beloved of Viṣṇu. 

I worship forever that dear lake (Śyāma-kuṇḍa). Which appeared from the lotus foot of Kṛṣṇa Himself at the killing of the wicked Ariṣṭa. Which is expanded like the spreading of honey; which is desired (iṣṭa) and named Ariṣṭa. Which is surrounded by steps made by Śrī Rādhā with affection. Which embraces the Lake of the Beloved (Rādhā-kuṇḍa) with love. 

May the daughter of the Sun (Yamunā) purify us. She is the vessel of supreme love for the son of Sadānanda (Nanda), the sun of consciousness and bliss. Her body is liquid Brahman. She is the destroyer of sins, the giver of welfare to the world. 

I bow to the Yamunā, delighted by Rādhā and Mukunda in the ocean of happiness. Whose lotus feet are served by the Ganges and other holy places. Who is great with the glory of the flood of the rasa of happiness of Goloka. Who has flooded everything with sweet water like nectar. 

The Gaṅgā destroys sins immediately; She is always to be worshiped, the destroyer of misery. Giver of happiness, giver of liberation, the Gaṅgā is indeed the supreme destination.

IDX.verses:
śhrī-nanda-nandana-dhana, tadīya vallabhāgaṇa, 
madhura-rasera ‘ālambana’ 
gopīgata-rati jāhāṅ, gopīchittāśhraya tāhāṅ, 
kṛṣṇa-mātra ‘viṣaya’ takhana 

jāhāṅ rati kṛṣṇa-gata, ratyāśhraya kṛṣṇa-chitta, 
gopī tāhāṅ ratira ‘viṣaya’ 
viṣaya-āśhraya dhare’, sthāyibhāva-rati chare, 
naile rati udgata nā haya 

vibhāvete ‘ālambana’, rase nitya prayojana, 
vraje tāi kṛṣṇa-gopīnātha 
madanamohana-dhana-vrajāṅganā, gopī-jana-, 
vallabha-rasika rādhānātha 

svīyā, parakīyā bhede, rasa-rasāntarāsvāde, 
nityānande virāje mādhava 
baḍa bhāgyavān jei, nije ālambana hoi’, 
āsvādaye se rasa-āsava
IDX.en_translation:
The treasure Śrī Nanda-nandana and His beloved consorts are the “ālambana” of madhura-rasa. Where rati is directed toward the gopīs and is sheltered in their hearts, Kṛṣṇa alone is then the “viṣaya”. 

Where rati is directed toward Kṛṣṇa, and the “āśraya” of that rati is Kṛṣṇa’s heart, the gopī is then the “viṣaya”. Holding both the “viṣaya” and “āśraya”, the permanent sentiment of rati unfolds; otherwise, rati does not manifest. 

The “ālambana” in the causes of emotion is eternally necessary for rasa; therefore, in Vraja, Kṛṣṇa is Gopīnātha. The treasure of Madana-mohana are the women of Vraja, the gopīs, and the beloved rasika, Rādhānātha. 

In the distinction of svīyā and parakīyā, in tasting various rasas, Mādhava resides in eternal bliss. He who is very fortunate, becoming the ālambana himself, tastes that intoxicating rasa.

IDX.author: prāchīna-stotram (ancient prayers)
IDX.verses:
śhrī-nārada uvācha: 
navīna-nīrada-śhyāmaṁ nīlendīvara-lochanam 
vallavī-nandanaṁ vande kṛṣṇaṁ gopāla-rūpiṇam 

sfurad-varhi-dalodvaddha-nīla-kuñchita-mūrdhajam 
kadamba-kusumodvaddha-vanamālā-vibhūṣitam 

gaṇḍa-maṇḍalasaṁsargi-chalat-kuñchita-kuntalam 
sthūlaṁ muktāfalodāra-hārodyotita-vakṣasam 

hemāṅga-tulākoṭi-kirīṭojjvala-vigraham 
manda-mārūta-saṅkṣobha-chalitāmvara-sañchayam 

rūchirauṣṭha-puṭa-nyasta-vaṁśhī-madhura-niḥsvanaiḥ 
lasad-gopālikā-cheto mohayantaṁ punaḥ punaḥ 

vallavī-vadanāmbhoja -madhu-pāna-madhu-vratam 
kṣobhayantaṁ manas tāsāṁ sasmerāpāṅga-vīkṣaṇaiḥ 

jauvanod bhinna dehābhiḥ saṁsaktābhiḥ parasparam 
vichitrāmvara-bhūṣābhir gopa-nārībhir āvṛtam 

prabhinnāñjana-kālindī-jala-keli-kalotsukam 
jodhayantaṁ kvachid gopān vyāharantaṁ gavāṁ gaṇam 

kālindī-jala-saṁsargi-śhītalānila-sevite 
kadamba-pādapaccḣāye sthitaṁ vṛndāvane kvachit 

ratna-bhūdhara-saṁlagna-ratnāsana-parigraham 
kalpa-pādapa-madhyastha-hema-maṇḍapikā-gatam 

vasanta-kusumāmoda-surabhī-kṛta-diṅ-mukhe 
govardhana-girau ramye sthitaṁ rāsa-rasotsukam 

savya-hasta-tala-nyasta-giri-varyāta-patrakam 
khaṇḍitākhaṇḍalon-mukta-muktāsāra-ghanāghanam 

veṇu-vādya-mahollāsa-kṛta-huṅkāra-niḥsvanaiḥ 
sa-vatsair unmukhaiḥ śhaśhvad gokulair abhivīkṣitam 

kṛṣṇam eva tu gāyadbhis tach-cheṣṭā-vaśha-vartibhiḥ 
daṇḍa-pāśhodyata-karair gopālai rūpa-śhobhitam 
nāradādyair muni-śhreṣṭhair veda-vedāṅga-pāragaiḥ 
prīti-susnigdhayā vāchā stūyamānaṁ parāt param 

ja evaṁ chintayed devaṁ bhaktyā saṁstauti mānavaḥ 
trisandhyaṁ tasya tuṣṭo’sau dadāti varam īpsitam 

rāja-vallabhatām eti bhavet sarva-jana-priyaḥ 
achalāṁ śhriyam āpnoti sa vāgmī jāyate dhruvam 

iti śhrī-nārada-pañcharātre 
jñānāmṛta-sāre chaturtha-rātre gopāla-stotraṁ nāma 
ṣaṣṭho’dhyāyaḥ
IDX.en_translation:
Śrī Nārada said: I offer my respectful obeisances to the son of the cowherd woman, Kṛṣṇa, whose form is that of a cowherd boy. His complexion is dark like a fresh raincloud, and His eyes resemble blue lotus flowers. 

His dark, curly hair is tied with a shining peacock feather, and He is adorned with a garland of forest flowers strung with Kadamba blossoms. 

His moving, curly locks of hair touch His round cheeks, and His broad chest is illuminated by a necklace of large pearls. 

His form shines with golden armlets, waistbands, and a crown. His garments flutter in the agitation of the gentle breeze. 

With the sweet sounds of the flute placed upon His beautiful lips, He again and again enchants the minds of the shining cowherd girls. 

He is the bee drinking the honey of the lotus faces of the cowherd women. He agitates their minds with His smiling sidelong glances. 

He is surrounded by the wives of the cowherds, who are decorated with wonderful clothes and ornaments, whose bodies are blossoming with youth, and who are attached to one another. 

He is eager for the artful sports in the waters of the Yamunā, which are dark like crushed collyrium. Sometimes He fights with the cowherd boys and sometimes He calls out to the herd of cows. 

Sometimes He stays in Vṛndāvana, in the shade of a Kadamba tree, served by the cooling breeze touching the waters of the Yamunā. 

He accepts a jeweled throne located on a jeweled mountain. He has entered a golden pavilion situated in the midst of desire trees. 

He stays on the beautiful Govardhana Hill, where the directions are perfumed by the fragrance of spring flowers, eager for the mellows of the Rāsa dance. 

He holds the best of mountains like an umbrella in the palm of His left hand, shielding Vraja from the dense clouds releasing torrents of rain sent by the angry Indra. 

He is constantly gazed upon by the herds of cows with their calves, who look up with faces lifted, making loud lowing sounds in great jubilation at the music of His flute. 

He is beautified by the cowherd boys, who sing only of Kṛṣṇa, who are under the control of His activities, and who hold sticks and ropes in their uplifted hands. He is the Supreme beyond the Supreme, praised with words full of affection by the best of sages led by Nārada, who are learned in the Vedas and Vedāṅgas. 

A human being who thinks of that Lord in this way and praises Him with devotion three times a day pleases Him, and He grants the desired boon. 

He becomes dear to the king and beloved by all people. He attains steady opulence and certainly becomes an orator. 

Thus ends the Gopāla-stotra in the sixth chapter of the fourth night of the Jñānāmṛta-sāra of the Śrī Nārada-pañcarātra.

IDX.verses: śhrī-rādhā-kṛṣṇa-padakamale mana kemane labhibe charama śharaṇa chiradina kariyā o-charaṇa-āśha ācḣe he basiyā e adhama dāsa he rādhe, he kṛṣṇa-chandra bhaktaprāṇa pāmare yugala-bhakti kara’ dāna bhaktihīna bali’ nā kara’ upekṣā mūrkha-jane deha’ jñāna-suśhikṣā viṣaya-pipāsā-prapīḍita dāse deha’ adhikāra yugala-vilāse chañchala jīvana-, srota pravāhiyā, kālera sāgare dhāya gela je divasa, nā āsibe āra, ebe kṛṣṇa ki upāya tumi patitajanera bandhu jāni he tomāre nātha, tumi ta’ karuṇā-jalasindhu āmi bhāgya-hīna, ati arvāchīna, nā jāni bhakati-leśha nija-guṇe nātha, kara’ ātmasāt, ghuchāiyā bhava-kleśha siddha-deha diyā, vṛndāvana-mājhe, sevāmṛta kara’ dāna piyāiyā prema, matta kari’ more, śhuna nija guṇagāna yugala-sevāya, śhrī-rāsa-maṇḍale, niyukta kara’ āmāya lalitā sakhīra, ayogyā kiṅkarī, vinoda dharicḣe pāya
IDX.en_translation:
O mind, how will you attain ultimate refuge at the lotus feet of Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa? 

Always hoping for those feet, this fallen servant is waiting. 

O Rādhe! O Kṛṣṇa-candra, life of the devotees! Please bestow devotion to the Divine Couple upon this sinner. 

Do not neglect me, calling me devoid of devotion. Please give good instruction in knowledge to this foolish person. 

To this servant afflicted by the thirst for material enjoyment, please grant the qualification for the pastimes of the Divine Couple. 

This restless life, flowing like a current, rushes into the ocean of time. The days that have passed will not come again. Now, O Kṛṣṇa, what is the way? 

You are the friend of the fallen. I know You, O Lord, indeed You are an ocean of the water of mercy. 

I am unfortunate, very insignificant, and do not know a trace of devotion. By Your own quality, O Lord, please accept me, removing the miseries of material existence. 

Granting me a spiritual body in Vṛndāvana, bestow the nectar of service. Making me drink love and intoxicating me, please listen to my singing of Your glories. 

Engage me in the service of the Divine Couple in the Śrī Rāsa-maṇḍala. Vinoda, an unworthy maidservant of Lalitā, holds onto Your feet.
IDX.es_translation:
¡Oh mente!, ¿cómo alcanzarás el refugio supremo a los pies de loto de Śhrī Śhrī Rādhā y Kṛṣṇa? 

Este vil sirviente, que ha deseado refugiarse en esos pies de loto desde tiempo inmemorial, simplemente espera. 

¡Oh, Rādhe! ¡Oh, Kṛṣṇachandra! Ustedes son la vida y el alma de los devotos. Concedan por favor bhakti por Ustedes a este abyecto pecador. 

No me abandonen diciendo que carezco de devoción. En lugar de ello, den a este ignorante sus auspiciosas enseñanzas sobre el conocimiento espiritual. 

Den por favor a este sirviente sediento de disfrute material la cualificación para servir en Sus pasatiempos amorosos. 

Esta agitada corriente de la vida fluye apresuradamente hacia el océano del tiempo [la muerte]. Los días que han pasado no volverán. ¡Ay de mí, Kṛṣṇa! ¿Qué puedo hacer? 

Ustedes son los amigos de los caídos. Sé bien quiénes son, amos míos; son el océano de la bondad. 

Soy desafortunado y extremadamente necio, y no tengo ni un atisbo de bhakti. Por Su magnanimidad, tomen mi alma y considérenme Suyo, y acaben así con mi sufrimiento material. 

Concédanme un cuerpo espiritual perfecto en la morada trascendental de Vṛndāvana y denme el néctar del servicio devocional. Después de hacerme beber prema y hacer que me embriague de dicha espiritual, escuchen mis canciones sobre Sus divinas cualidades. 

Bhaktivinoda, el indigno sirviente de Śhrī Lalitā Sakhī, se aferra a Sus pies de loto implorando ser ocupado en Su servicio en la arena de la danza rāsa.

IDX.verses:
śhrī-rādhikā-rūpa-guṇormi-chauraḥ 
prataptakārtasvarakānta-gauraḥ 
vedānta-vedāṅga-purāṇa-sāraḥ 
jīyāt sa gauraḥ karuṇā-vatāraḥ 

brahmendra-rudrastuta-pāda-padmaḥ 
audārya-mādhurya-guṇābdhisadma 
romāñcha-kampāśhru-pramoda-bhāraḥ 
jīyāt sa gauraḥ karuṇā-vatāraḥ 

svarūpa-rūpādika-prāṇa-nāthaḥ 
gopāla-govinda-mukunda-nāthaḥ 
daridra-durjātyagha-duḥkhadāraḥ 
jīyāt sa gauraḥ karuṇā-vatāraḥ 

māyāmata-dhvānta-nikārahārī 
vārāṇasī-nyāsi-samūha-tārī 
viśhuddha-sadbhakti-prasāra-kārī 
jīyāt sa gauraḥ karuṇā-vatāraḥ 

śhrī-digvijetṛ-dvija-darpahārī 
śhrī-sārvabhaumāti-prasāda-kārī 
aṣṭādaśhāvdeśha-purī-vihārī 
jīyāt sa gauraḥ karuṇā-vatāraḥ 

mahojjvala-premarasa-pradātā 
śhrī-nāma-sarvottama-bhakti-dhātā 
goloka-vṛndāvana-sad-vihāraḥ 
jīyāt sa gauraḥ karuṇā-vatāraḥ 

sadā harekṛṣṇa-sugāna-mattaḥ 
jogīndra-munīndra-samādhi-vittaḥ 
dattavrajaprema-sudhā-susāraḥ 
jīyāt sa gauraḥ karuṇā-vatāraḥ 

kavāṭa-vakṣo-nava-padma-netraḥ 
śhrī-saccḣidānanda-ghanāsugātraḥ 
svāṅga-prabhā-nindita-koṭimāraḥ 
jīyāt sa gauraḥ karuṇā-vatāraḥ 

nīlādri-śhuvrāṁśhu-sudhāchakorāḥ 
rathāgra-saṅgīta-sudhāvidhūraḥ 
śhrī-vaiṣṇava-vrāta-lasaccḣarīraḥ 
jīyāt sa gauraḥ karuṇā-vatāraḥ 

bhaktāvalī-mānasa-rāja-haṁsaḥ 
sannyāsi-bhūdeva-kulavataṁsaḥ 
śhrīmajjagannātha-śhachī-kumāraḥ 
jīyāt sa gauraḥ karuṇā-vatāraḥ 

gaura-stutiṁ gāyati bhakti-pūrvaṁ 
prāpnoti suprema-sudhāṁ saḥ sarvam 
tritāpa-dāvānala-duḥkha-muktaḥ 
pramodate kṛṣṇapadābja-bhaktaḥ
IDX.en_translation:
He who has stolen the waves of the beauty and qualities of Śrīmatī Rādhikā, whose complexion is golden like molten gold, and who is the essence of the Vedānta, Vedāṅgas, and Purāṇas—may that Lord Gaura, the incarnation of mercy, be victorious. 

He whose lotus feet are praised by Brahmā, Indra, and Śiva, who is the abode of the ocean of magnanimity and sweetness, and who bears the burden of ecstasy manifested as horripilation, trembling, and tears—may that Lord Gaura, the incarnation of mercy, be victorious. 

He who is the life and soul of Svarūpa Dāmodara and Rūpa Gosvāmī, who is the Lord of Gopāla, Govinda, and Mukunda, and who tears apart the misery, low birth, and sins of the poor—may that Lord Gaura, the incarnation of mercy, be victorious. 

He who removes the darkness of the illusory philosophy of Māyā, who delivered the group of sannyāsīs in Vārāṇasī, and who spreads pure, transcendental devotion—may that Lord Gaura, the incarnation of mercy, be victorious. 

He who removed the pride of the world-conquering brāhmaṇa, who bestowed great mercy upon Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭāchārya, and who enjoyed pastimes in Jagannātha Purī for eighteen years—may that Lord Gaura, the incarnation of mercy, be victorious. 

He who bestows the mellows of brilliant love, who establishes the supreme devotion to the Holy Name, and whose eternal pastimes are in Goloka Vṛndāvana—may that Lord Gaura, the incarnation of mercy, be victorious. 

He who is always intoxicated by the sweet singing of the Hare Kṛṣṇa mantra, who is the object of meditation for the best of yogīs and sages, and who gives the sweet essence of the love of Vraja—may that Lord Gaura, the incarnation of mercy, be victorious. 

He whose chest is broad like a door and whose eyes are like fresh lotus flowers, whose body is the condensed form of eternity, knowledge, and bliss, and whose bodily luster defeats millions of Cupids—may that Lord Gaura, the incarnation of mercy, be victorious. 

He who is like a cakora bird for the nectar of the moon of Nīlācala, who is agitated by the nectar of singing in front of the Ratha-yātrā chariot, and whose body shines amidst the assembly of Vaiṣṇavas—may that Lord Gaura, the incarnation of mercy, be victorious. 

He who is the royal swan in the minds of the devotees, who is the crown jewel of the sannyāsīs and brāhmaṇas, and who is the son of Jagannātha Miśra and Mother Śacī—may that Lord Gaura, the incarnation of mercy, be victorious. 

He who sings this praise of Lord Gaura with devotion obtains the nectar of pure love. Freed from the misery of the forest fire of the three-fold sufferings, the devotee of the lotus feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa rejoices.

IDX.en_translation:
O mind! Worship the merciful Śrī Rāmacandra, who removes the terrible fear of material existence. His eyes are like new lotuses, His face is like a lotus, His hands are like lotuses, and His feet are like reddish lotuses. 

He has the limitless beauty of countless Cupids, beautiful like a fresh blue cloud. His yellow garment shines like lightning, I bow to the husband of the daughter of Janaka. 

Worship the friend of the poor, the sun (of the solar dynasty), the destroyer of the demons and Diti’s lineage. The delight of the Raghu dynasty, the root of bliss, the moon of Kauśalyā, the son of Daśaratha. 

Beautiful with a crown on His head, earrings, and tilaka; His generous limbs are adorned. With long arms reaching His knees, holding a bow and arrow, He conquered Khara and Dūṣaṇa in battle. 

Thus says Tulasī Dāsa: O Lord who delights the minds of Śaṅkara, Śeṣa, and the sages! Please reside in the lotus of my heart, destroying the group of wicked enemies headed by lust.

IDX.verses:
śhrī-rudra uvācha: 
jitaṁ ta ātmavid-varya-svastaye svastirastu me 
bhabatārādhasā rāddhaṁ sarvasmā ātmane namaḥ 

namaḥ paṅkaja-nābhāya bhūta-sūkṣmendriyātmane 
vāsudevāya śhāntāya kūṭasthāya svarochiṣe 

saṅkarṣaṇāya sūkṣmāya durantāyāntakāya cha 
namo viśhva-prabodhāya pradyumnāyāntarātmane 

namo namo‛niruddhāya hṛṣīkeśhendriyātmane 
namaḥ parama-haṁsāya pūrṇāya nibhṛtātmane 

svargāpavarga-dvārāya nityaṁ śhuchiṣade namaḥ 
namo hiraṇya-vīryāya chāturhotrāya tantave 

nama ūrja iṣe trayyāḥ pataye jajña-retase 
tṛptidāya cha jīvānāṁ namaḥ sarva-rasātmane 

sarva-sattvātma-dehāya viśheṣāya sthavīyase 
namastrailokya-pālāya saha ojo-balāya cha 

artha-liṅgāya nabhase namo‛ntarbahirātmane 
namaḥ puṇyāya lokāya amusmai bhūrivarchase 

pravṛttāya nivṛttāya pitṛ-devāya karmaṇe 
namo‛dharma-vipākāya mṛtyave duḥkhadāya cha 

namasta āśhīṣāmīśha manave kāraṇātmane 
namo dharmāya bṛhate kṛṣṇāyākuṇṭha-medhase 
puruṣāya purāṇāya sāṅkhya-yogeśhvarāya cha 

śhakti-traya-sametāya mīḍhuṣe‛haṅkṛtātmane 
cheta-ākṛti-rūpāya namo vācho vibhūtaye 

darśhanaṁ no didṛkṣūṇāṁ dehi bhāgavatārchitam 
rūpaṁ priyatamaṁ svānāṁ sarvendriya-guṇaañjanam 

snigdha-prāvṛḍghana-śhyāmaṁ sarva-saundarya-saṁgraham 
chārvāyata-chaturbāhu sujāta-ruchirānanam 
padma-kośha-palāśhākṣaṁ sundara-bhru sunāsikam 
sudvijaṁ sukapolāsyaṁ sama-karṇa-vibhūṣaṇam 

prīti-prahasitāpāṅgamalakai rūpa-śhobhitam 
lasat-paṅkaja-kiñjalka-dukūlaṁ mṛṣṭa-kuṇḍalam 
sfurat-kirīṭa-valaya-hāra-nūpura-mekhalam 
śhaṅkha-chakra-gadā-padma-mālā-maṇyuttamardhimat 

siṁha-skandha-tviṣo bibhratsaubhaga-grīva-kaustubham 
śhriyānapāyinyā kṣipta-nikaṣāśhmorasollasat 

pūra-rechaka-saṁvigna-bali-valgudalodaram 
pratisaṁkrāmayadviśhvaṁ nābhyāvarta-gabhīrayā 

śhyāma-śhroṇyadhirochiṣṇu-dukūla-svarṇa-mekhalam 
sama-chārvaṅghri-jaṅghoru-nimna-jānu-sudarśhanam 

padā śharat-padma-palāśha-rochiṣā 
nakha-dyubhirno‛ntaraghaṁ vidhunvatā 
pradarśhaya svīyamapāsta-sādhvasaṁ 
padaṁ guro mārga-gurustamojuṣām 

etad-rūpamanudhyeyamātma-śhuddhimabhīpsatām 
jad-bhakti-yogo‛bhayadaḥ svadharmamanutiṣṭhatām 

bhabān bhakti-matā labhyo durlabhaḥ sarva-dehinām 
svārājyasyāpyabhimata ekāntenātmavid-gatiḥ 

taṁ durārādhyamārādhya satāmapi durāpayā 
ekānta-bhaktyā ko vāñcḣet-pāda-mūlaṁ vinā bahiḥ 

jatra niviṣṭa-maraṇaṁ kṛtānto nābhimanyate 
viśhvaṁ vidhvaṁsayan vīrya-śhaurya-visfūrjita-bhruvā 

kṣaṇārdhenāpi tulaye na svargaṁ nāpunarbhavam 
bhagavat-saṅgi-saṅgasya martyānāṁ kimutāśhīṣaḥ 

athānaghāṅghrestava kīrti-tīrthayo- 
rantarbahiḥ-snāna-vidhūta-pāpmanām 
bhūteṣbanukrośha-susattva-śhīlināṁ 
syāt-saṅgamo‛nugraha eṣa nastava 

na jasya chittaṁ bahirartha-vibhramaṁ 
tamoguhāyāṁ cha viśhuddhamāviśhat 
jad-bhakti-yogānugṛhītamañjasā 
munirrvichaṣṭe nanu tatra te gatim 

jatredaṁ vyajyate viśhvaṁ viśhvasminnavabhāti jat 
tat tvaṁ brahma paraṁ jyotirākāśhamiva vistṛtam 

jo māyayedaṁ puru-rūpayāsṛjad 
bibharti bhūyaḥ kṣapayatyavikriyaḥ 
jad-bhadra-buddhiḥ sadivātmaduḥsthayā 
tvamātma-tantraṁ bhagavan pratīmahi 

kriyā-kalāpairidameva joginaḥ 
śhraddhānvitāḥ sādhu jajanti siddhaye 
bhūtendriyā antaḥkaraṇopalakṣitaṁ 
vede cha tantre cha ta eva kovidāḥ 

tvameka ādyaḥ puruṣaḥ supta-śhakti- 
stayā rajaḥ-sattva-tamo vibhidyate 
mahānahaṁ khaṁ marudgnibārdharāḥ 
surarṣayo bhūta-gaṇā idaṁ jataḥ 

sṛṣṭaṁ sva-śhaktyedamanupraviṣṭa- 
śhchachaturvidhaṁ puramātmāṁśhakena 
atho vidustaṁ puruṣaṁ santamanta- 
rbhṛṅkte hṛṣīkairmadhu sāraghaṁ jaḥ 

sa eṣa lokānatichaṇḍa-vego 
vikarṣasi tvaṁ khalu kālayānaḥ 
bhūtāni bhūtairanumeya-tattvo 
ghanāvalī-vāyurivaaviṣahyaḥ 

pravṛddhamuccḣairiti kṛtya-chintayā 
pravṛddha-lobhaṁ viṣayeṣu lālasam 
tvamapramattaḥ sahasābhipadyase 
kṣullelihāno‛hirivākṣumantakaḥ 

kastvat-padābjaṁ vijahāti paṇḍito 
jaste‛vamāna-vyayamāna-ketanaḥ 
viśhaṅkayāsmada-gururarchati sma jad 
vinopapattiṁ manavaśhchaturdaśha 

atha tvamasi no brahman paramātman vipaśhchitām 
viśhvaṁ rudra-bhaya-dhvastamakutaśhchidbhayā gatiḥ 

idaṁ japata bhadraṁ vo viśhuddhā nṛpa-nandanāḥ 
svadharmamanutiṣṭhanto bhagavatyarpitāśhayāḥ 

tamevātmānamātmasthaṁ sarva-bhūteṣvavasthitam 
pūjayadhvaṁ gṛṇantaśhcha dhyāyantaśhchāsakṛddharim 

jogādeśhamupāsādya dhārayanto muni-vratāḥ 
samāhita-dhiyaḥ sarva etadabhyasatādṛtāḥ 

idamāha purāsmākaṁ bhagavān viśhvasṛkpatiḥ 
bhṛgbādīnāmātmajānāṁ sisṛkṣuḥ saṁsisṛkṣatām 

te vayaṁ noditāḥ sarve prajā-sarge prajeśhvarāḥ 
anena dhvasta-tamasaḥ sisṛkṣmo vividhāḥ prajāḥ 

athaidaṁ nityadā jukto japannavahitaḥ pumān 
achirāccḣreya āpnoti vāsudeva-parāyaṇaḥ 

śhreyasāmiha sarveṣāṁ jñānaṁ niḥśhreyasaṁ param 
sukhaṁ tarati duṣpāraṁ jñāna-naur-vyasanārṇavam 

ja imaṁ śhraddhayā jukto mad-gītaṁ bhagavat-stavam 
adhīyāno durārādhyaṁ harimārādhayatyasau 

vindate puruṣo‛musmād jad jadiccḣatyasatvaram 
mad-gīta-gītāt-suprītāt śhreyasāmeka-vallabhāt 

idaṁ jaḥ kalya utthāya prāñjaliḥ śhraddhayāmvitaḥ 
śhṛṇuyāccḣrāvayenmartyo muchyate karma-bandhanaiḥ 

gītaṁ mayedaṁ naradeva-nandanāḥ 
parasya puṁsaḥ paramātmanaḥ stavam 
japanta ekāgra-dhiyastapo mahat 
charadhvamante tata āpsyathepsitam
IDX.en_translation:
Śrī Rudra said: O Best of the Self-Realized! Victory to You! O Self of all, let there be auspiciousness for me. I offer my obeisances to You, who are served by You. 

Obeisances to the Lotus-naveled One, the Soul of the subtle elements and senses. To Vāsudeva, the peaceful, the unchanging, the self-effulgent. 

To Saṅkarṣaṇa, the subtle, the endless, and the destroyer. Obeisances to the awakener of the universe, Pradyumna, the inner soul. 

Obeisances, obeisances to Aniruddha, the Master of the senses, the Soul of the senses. Obeisances to the Paramahaṁsa, the Full, the concealed Soul. 

Obeisances to Him who is the door to heaven and liberation, who always dwells in the pure heart. Obeisances to Hiraṇya-vīrya, the expander of the Cātur-hotra sacrifice. 

Obeisances to Ūrja (strength), Iṣa (food), the Lord of the three Vedas, the source of sacrifice. To the giver of satisfaction to the jīvas, obeisances to the Soul of all rasas. 

To Him whose body is all-existence, the Specific, the Grossest. Obeisances to the Protector of the three worlds, along with Ojas (vitality) and Bala (strength). 

To the Meaning-gendered, the Sky, obeisances to the Inner and Outer Soul. Obeisances to the Pious World, to that One of great splendor. 

To the active, the renounced, the Worshipable Deity of the forefathers, to Karma. Obeisances to the result of irreligion, to Death, and to the giver of misery. 

Obeisances to You, the Lord of benedictions, to Manu, to the Causal Soul. Obeisances to Dharma, the Great, to Kṛṣṇa of stunted intelligence. To the Person, the Ancient, the Lord of Sāṅkhya and Yoga. 

To Him endowed with the three energies, to the Showerer, to the Ego-soul. To the form of Consciousness, obeisances to the manifestation of Speech. 

Give us, who are eager to see, the vision worshipped by the devotees. The form most dear to Your own, the collyrium for all the senses and qualities. 

Dark like a glistening raincloud, the reservoir of all beauty. With four beautiful long arms, and a well-formed, charming face. Eyes like lotus petals, beautiful eyebrows, beautiful nose. Beautiful teeth, beautiful cheeks and face, adorned with equal earrings. 

Beautified by sidelong glances laughing with love and by locks of hair. With a garment like the filaments of a shining lotus, and polished earrings. With shining crown, bracelets, necklaces, anklets, and girdle. Endowed with the excellent opulence of conch, disc, club, lotus, garland, and jewels. 

Bearing the Kaustubha on a beautiful neck, with the shoulders of a lion. Shining on the chest, defeating the touchstone with the never-departing Śrī (Lakṣmī). 

With an abdomen beautiful with folds agitated by breathing in and out. Deep with a navel-whirlpool that seems to draw the universe back in. 

With a golden belt on a shining cloth over dark hips. With symmetrical, beautiful feet, shins, thighs, and knees—beautiful to see. 

By Your feet, which have the luster of autumn lotus petals, and by the light of Your nails which destroys our inner sin. Show us Your own feet, which remove fear, O Guru! You are the Guru of the path for those in darkness. 

This form should be meditated upon by those desiring self-purification. Whose bhakti-yoga grants fearlessness to those performing their own duty. 

You are attainable by one who has devotion, but rare for all embodied beings. Even for the King of Heaven, the goal of the knowers of the Self is desired in solitude. 

Having worshipped Him who is difficult to worship, with unalloyed devotion rare even for the saintly. Who would desire anything outside, without the root of Your feet? 

Where death does not think to enter, absorbed. Destroying the universe with eyebrows flashing with heroism and valor. 

I do not weigh heaven or liberation against even half a moment of the association of those attached to the Lord. What to speak of the benedictions of mortals? 

Therefore, let us have the association of those whose sins have been washed away by bathing internally and externally in the holy rivers of Your glories and Your sinless feet. Who are endowed with compassion and good character towards living beings. This is Your mercy upon us. 

Whose mind, bewildered by external objects, does not enter the cave of darkness, being purified. By whose bhakti-yoga, graced easily, the sage sees Your path there. 

Where this universe is manifested, which shines in the universe. You are that Brahman, the Supreme Light, expanded like the sky. 

Who created this with the Maya of many forms, maintains it again, and destroys it, being unchanging. By whom the intelligence is different, as if existing, due to the bad state of the self. We understand You, the Lord, to be independent. 

With these activities, the yogis endowed with faith worship this very thing perfectly for perfection. Characterized by the elements, senses, and inner instrument, in the Veda and Tantra, they alone are the knowers. 

You are the One, the Original Person, whose energy is asleep. By that, passion, goodness, and ignorance are divided. From whom came this: the Mahat, the Ego, the Sky, Air, Fire, Water, Earth, the Suras, Sages, and hosts of beings. 

Created by Your own energy, having entered this fourfold city with a portion of Yourself. Then they know that Person to be existing within, who enjoys the honey made by bees with the senses. 

He, this one, of very fierce speed, You pull the worlds, driving Time. Beings by beings, the Truth inferred, like the wind the clouds, unbearable. 

Thinking loudly “This is to be done,” greedy, lusty for objects. You, always alert, suddenly seize the madman, like a hungry snake a mouse licking its lips. 

What learned person abandons Your lotus feet, when You remove the banner of disrespect? Out of fear, our Guru worshiped, without argument, the fourteen Manus. 

Now You are ours, O Brahman, O Supreme Soul of the wise! The universe is destroyed by the fear of Rudra; You are the destination of the fearless. 

Chant this, may it be well with you, O pure sons of the King! Performing your own duty, with minds offered to the Lord. 

Worship, praise, and meditate on that very Self situated in the self, situated in all beings—Hari. 

Accepting the order of yoga, observing the vow of silence, holding. With concentrated minds, all of you practice this with respect. 

This the Lord, the Master of the creators of the universe, spoke to us in the past. Desiring to create, to the sons like Bhṛgu who were desiring to create. 

We, all the Prajāpatis, urged by that in the creation of progeny. By this, our darkness destroyed, we desire to create various progeny. 

Now, a person constantly engaged in chanting this with attention. He quickly attains the ultimate good, devoted to Vāsudeva. 

Of all benedictions here, knowledge is the supreme beatitude. He crosses the ocean of misery, difficult to cross, on the boat of knowledge, happily. 

He who studies this hymn to the Lord sung by me with faith. He worships Hari, who is difficult to worship. 

A person obtains from Him whatever he desires quickly. From Him, the only beloved of benedictions, who is well-pleased by the song sung by me. 

A mortal who, rising at dawn, with folded hands and endowed with faith. Hears or causes to hear this, is released from the bondages of karma. 

This hymn of the Supreme Person, the Supreme Soul, sung by me, O sons of the King! Chanting with one-pointed minds, perform great austerity; at the end, you will obtain the desired from Him.

IDX.first_line: śhrī rūpa mañjarī kabe madhura vachane
IDX.search: sri rupa manjari kabe madhura vachane radha kunda mahima varnibe samgopane e chaudda bhuvanopari vaikuntha nilaya tada peksa mathura parama srestha haya mathuramandale rasalila sthana jatha vrndavana srestha ati suna mama katha krsnalila sthala govardhana sresthatara radha kunda sresthatama sarva sakti dhara radha kunda mahima ta kariya sravana lalayita haye ami padiba takhana sakhira charane kabe kariba akuti sakhi krpa kari dibe svarasiki sthiti
IDX.author: sacchidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
śhrī-rūpa mañjarī kabe madhura vachane 
rādhā-kuṇḍa-mahimā varṇibe saṁgopane 

e chaudda bhuvanopari vaikuṇṭha nilaya 
tada-pekṣā mathurā parama śhreṣṭha haya 

māthuramaṇḍale rāsalīlā sthāna jathā 
vṛndāvana śhreṣṭha ati śhuna mama kathā 

kṛṣṇalīlā-sthala govardhana śhreṣṭhatara 
rādhā-kuṇḍa śhreṣṭhatama sarva-śhakti-dhara 

rādhā-kuṇḍa-mahimā ta’ kariyā śhravaṇa 
lālāyita ha’ye āmi paḍiba takhana 

sakhīra charaṇe kabe kariba ākuti 
sakhī kṛpā kari’ dibe svārasikī sthiti
IDX.en_translation:
When will Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī, with sweet words, describe the glories of Rādhā-kuṇḍa to me in a secret place? 

Above the fourteen planetary systems lies the spiritual abode of Vaikuṇṭha. Yet, Mathurā is far superior to that. 

Within the district of Mathurā, Vṛndāvana is the most excellent place, where the Rāsa dance takes place. Please hear my words. 

Govardhana Hill, the site of Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes, is even more excellent. But Rādhā-kuṇḍa is the most excellent of all, possessing all spiritual potencies. 

Hearing the glories of Rādhā-kuṇḍa, I will fall down, overcome with great longing. 

When will I plead at the lotus feet of the sakhīs? By their mercy, the sakhīs will grant me my eternal position in the flow of divine love.

IDX.search: sri rupa paschate ami rahiba bhita hana dohe punah kahibena ama pane chana sadaya hrdaye dohe kahibena hasi kothaya paile rupa ei nava dasi sri rupa manjari tabe dohavakya suni manjunali dila more ei dasi ani ati namrachitta ami ihare janila sevakarya niya tabe hethaya rakhila hena tattva dohakara saksate kahiya narottame sevaya dibe niyukta kariya
IDX.author: narottama-dāsa ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
śhrī-rūpa-paśhchāte āmi rahiba bhīta hañā 
dohe punaḥ kahibena āmā pāne chāñā 

sadaya-hṛdaye dohe kahibena hāsi 
kothāy pāile rūpa! ei nava dāsī 

śhrī-rūpa-mañjarī tabe dohavākya śhuni

I will remain behind Śrī Rūpa, being afraid. Both will again say, looking at me. 

Smiling with kind hearts, Both will say: “Where did you get this new maidservant, Rūpa?” 

Then Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī, hearing the words of Both: “Mañjunālī brought this maidservant and gave her to me. 

I knew her to be very humble in heart; therefore I kept her here engaged in service.” 

Speaking such truths in the presence of Both, she will engage Narottama in service.

śhrī-rūpa-vadane, śhrī-śhachīkumāra 
svanāma-mahimā karala prachāra 

jo nāma so hari, kicḣu nāhi bheda 
so nāma satyamiti gāyati veda 

sabu upaniṣad, ratnamālā-dyuti, 
jhakamaki’ charaṇa-samīpe 
maṅgala-ārati, karaba anukṣaṇa, 
dviguṇita-pañchapradīpe 

chauddabhuvana māha, deva-nara-dānava, 
bhāga jākara balabān 
nāmarasa-pīyuṣa, piyoi anukṣaṇa, 
cḣoḍata karama-geyāna 

nityamukta punaḥ, nāma-upāsanā, 
satata karoi sāmagāne 
goloke baiṭhata, gāoye nirantara, 
nāma-viraha nāhi jāne 

sabu rasa-ākara, ‘hari’ itidvyakṣara,

tuyā pade māgahu nilaya
IDX.en_translation:
Through the mouth of Śrī Rūpa, the son of Śacī proclaimed the glories of His own Holy Name. 

That Name is Hari; there is no difference. The Vedas sing that the Name is the Truth. 

All the Upaniṣads, like the radiance of a garland of jewels, sparkle at His lotus feet. I will constantly perform auspicious worship with twice five lamps. 

In the fourteen worlds, among demigods, men, and demons, those whose fortune is strong constantly drink the nectar of the Holy Name, giving up fruitive activities and speculative knowledge. 

Eternally liberated souls worship the Holy Name, always singing in Vedic melodies. Seated in Goloka, they sing ceaselessly; they know no separation from the Holy Name. 

The two syllables “Hari”, the source of all mellows, are the shelter in all circumstances. Falling at the feet of the Holy Name, Bhaktivinoda says: “At Your feet, I beg for a dwelling.”

All glories to Śrī Śrī Guru, Gaurāṅga, Gāndharvikā, Giridhārī, and Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Vinoda-bihārī-jīu! 

Now your dīkṣā-guru’s name should be glorified. 

All glories to nitya-līlā-praviṣṭa Oṁ Viṣṇupāda Aṣṭottara-śata Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja! 

All glories to nitya-līlā-praviṣṭa Oṁ Viṣṇupāda Aṣṭottara-śata Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktivedānta Vāmana Gosvāmī Mahārāja! 

All glories to nitya-līlā-praviṣṭa Oṁ Viṣṇupāda Aṣṭottara-śata Śrī Śrīmad Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja! 

All glories to nitya-līlā-praviṣṭa Oṁ Viṣṇupāda Aṣṭottara-śata Śrī Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Gosvāmī Prabhupāda! 

All glories to nitya-līlā-praviṣṭa Paramahaṁsa Bābājī Śrī Śrīla Gaura Kiśora Dāsa Gosvāmī Mahārāja! 

All glories to nitya-līlā-praviṣṭa Śrī Śrīla Saccidānanda Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura! 

All glories to nitya-līlā-praviṣṭa Vaiṣṇava-sārvabhauma Śrīla Jagannātha Dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja! 

All glories to the entire Rūpānuga Gauḍīya Guru-varga! All glories to nitya-līlā-praviṣṭa Oṁ Viṣṇupāda Aṣṭottara-śata Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktivedānta Svāmī Mahārāja! 

All glories to nitya-līlā-praviṣṭa Oṁ Viṣṇupāda Aṣṭottara-śata Śrī Śrīmad Bhaktivedānta Trivikrama Gosvāmī Mahārāja! 

All glories to Gauḍīya Vedāntāchārya Śrīla Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa Prabhu! All glories to Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura! 

All glories to the three Lords: Śrīla Narottama, Śrīnivāsa, and Śyāmānanda! All glories to Śrīla Kṛṣṇa-dāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī Prabhu! All glories to Śrīla Vṛndāvana Dāsa Ṭhākura! 

All glories to the Six Gosvāmīs: Śrī Rūpa, Sanātana, Bhaṭṭa Raghunātha, Śrī Jīva, Gopāla Bhaṭṭa, and Dāsa Raghunātha! 

All glories to the associates of Gaura, including Śrī Svarūpa Dāmodara and Rāya Rāmānanda! All glories to Nāmāchārya Śrīla Haridāsa Ṭhākura! 

Say with love: All glories to Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, Prabhu Nityānanda, Śrī Advaita, Gadādhara, Śrīvāsa, and all the devotees of Gaura! 

All glories to Śrī Navadvīpa-dhāma, which consists of Antardvīpa (Māyāpura), Sīmantadvīpa, Godrumadvīpa, Madhyadvīpa, Koladvīpa, Ṛtudvīpa, Jahnudvīpa, Modadrumadvīpa, and Rudradvīpa! 

All glories to Śrī Vraja-maṇḍala-dhāma, consisting of the twelve forests, Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, the cowherd boys and girls, the cows, and Govardhana Hill! 

All glories to Śrī Rādhā-kuṇḍa, Śyāma-kuṇḍa, Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Tulasī, and Bhakti-devī! All glories to Śrī Jagannātha, Baladeva, Subhadrā, and Sudarśana-jīu! 

All glories to Śrī Gopīśvara Mahādeva! All glories to Śrī Yogamāyā Paurṇamāsī Devī! 

All glories to Śrīmatī Vṛndā Devī! All glories to Śrī Nṛsiṁha and Varāhadeva! All glories to the best of devotees, Śrī Prahlāda Mahārāja! 

All glories to the four Dhāmas, the four Sampradāyas, and the Āchāryas! All glories to Vrajapaṭṭana Śrī Caitanya Maṭha! 

All glories to Śrī Keśavajī Gauḍīya Maṭha and all its branch Maṭhas! All glories to Śrī Harināma-saṅkīrtana! 

All glories to the unlimited millions of Vaiṣṇavas! Chant “Hari! Hari!” in the bliss of Gaura-prema!

IDX.en_translation:
The essence of the brilliant transcendental mellow is naturally of two types: separation and union. Without the foundation of separation, union cannot be fully nourished; therefore, separation is a necessary arrangement. 

Prior attraction, transcendental pique, separation due to dwelling elsewhere, and the feeling of novelty despite constant union—these are the four types of separation. The preliminary stage before union attains the renown of “prior attraction”; it is born from seeing and hearing. 

For loving couples, the desired embrace, though steady, is opposed by the sentiment of pique. Pique with a cause and pique without a cause are both outcomes of pure affection; they are evidence of love’s delightful pastimes. 

By means of conciliation, creating a division of interest, giving gifts, and feigned neglect—through these well-arranged methods, pique with a cause is pacified. By considering the place, the time, and the sound of the flute, the festival of causeless pique very quickly comes to an end. 

From the apprehension of separation, a feeling of novelty naturally arises from the very nature of love. When the beloved departs for another country, village, or forest, that is the separation known as “absence.”

nara-mātraṁ tārayet kṛṣṇa-nāma śhrī-hari-bhakti-vilāsa śhrī-śhrī-jagannātha-deva-vandanā mahāmbhodhes tīre kanaka-ruchire nīla-śhikhare vasan prasādāntaḥ sahaja-bala-bhadreṇa balinā subhadrā-madhyasthaḥ sakala-sura-sevā-vasarado- jagannāthaḥ svāmī nayana-pathagāmī bhavatu me śhrī-śhrī-jagannāthāṣṭakama nīlāchala-nivāsāya nityāya paramātmane balabhadra-subhadrābhyāṁ jagannāthāya te namaḥ śhrī-śhrī-nṛsiṁha-deva-vandanā namaste narasiṁhāya prahlādāhlāda-dāyine hiraṇyakaśhipor-vakṣaḥ śhilā-ṭaṅka-nakhālaye śhrī-nṛsiṁha-purāṇa ito nṛsiṁhaḥ parato nṛsiṁho jato jato jāmi tato nṛsiṁhaḥ bahir-nṛsiṁho hṛdaye nṛsiṁho nṛsiṁham-ādiṁ śharaṇaṁ prapadye śhrī-nṛsiṁha-purāṇa śhrī-nṛsiṁha, jaya nṛsiṁha, jaya jaya nṛsiṁha prahlādeśha jaya padmā-mukha-padma-bhṛṅga vāgīśhā jasya vadane lakṣmīr-yasya cha vakṣasi jasyāste hṛdaye saṁvit taṁ nṛsiṁham-ahaṁ bhaje prahlāda-hṛdayā-hlādaṁ bhaktāvidyā-vidāraṇam śharad-indu-ruchiṁ vande pārīndra-vadanaṁ harim śhrī-bhāvārtha-dīpikā śhrī-śhrī-rāmachandra-vandanā nīlāmbuja-śhyāmala-komalāṅgaṁ sītā-samāropita-vāma-bhāgam pāṇau mahāsāyaka-chāruchāpaṁ namāmi rāmaṁ raghu-vaṁśha-nātham śhrī-rāma-charita-mānasa dakṣiṇe lakṣmaṇo dhanvī vāmato jānakī śhubhā purato mārutīr jasya taṁ namāmi raghūtamam śhrī-śhrī-daśhāvatāra-vandanā vedān uddharate jaganti vahate bhū-golam udvibrate daityān dārayate baliṁ cḣalayate kṣatra-kṣayaṁ kurvate paulastyaṁ jayate halaṁ kalayate kāruṇyam-ātanvate mleccḣān-mūrcḣayate daśhākṛti-kṛte kṛṣṇāya tubhyaṁ namaḥ śhrī-gīta-govindama
IDX.en_translation: śrī-yamunā-snāna-vandanā O Kalinda-tanayā! O Devī! O increaser of supreme bliss! I bathe in your waters; please liberate me from all offenses. śrī-rādhā-kuṇḍa-snāna-vandanā Possessing good fortune equal to Rādhikā, worshipped by all tīrthas. Be pleased, O Rādhikā-kuṇḍa! I bathe in your auspicious waters. śrī-śyāma-kuṇḍa-snāna-vandanā Manifested from the lotus foot of Kṛṣṇa on the pretext of killing Ariṣṭa. Protect me, a fallen soul; I bathe in your waters, O Śyāma-kuṇḍa! śrī-paurṇamāsī-vandanā Expert in arranging the various playful pastimes of the master of Rādhā, whose lotus feet are worshipped by Vraja. Worshipped by the entire universe for her mercy and other qualities. I bow my head to Śrī Paurṇamāsī. śrī-vṛndā-devī-vandanā O protectress of the moving and non-moving living entities of Vṛndāvana! O Vṛndā! By the good fortune of those two Rasikas, you are wealthy. Please grant mercy so that I may be counted among the attendants of Śrī Rādhikā. Devoid of devotion, tossed by hundreds of thousands of offenses into the waves of lust and other vices. O merciful one! I have taken shelter of you. O Vṛndā, I bow to your lotus feet. śrī-vraja-vāsi-vṛnda-vandanā Where Brahmā joyfully desires birth among the grass and bushes, always daily offering various activities. Those dear people who reside there in the land of Vraja are worshipable by me with supreme humility; they are inlaid with piety. śrī-gopīśvara-śiva-vandanā O master of the land of Vṛndāvana, glories to you, O Soma, O Soma-maule! Worshipped by Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanātana, and Nārada. O Gopīśvara, O enjoyer of Vraja, please bestow unconditional prema at your two lotus feet. Obeisances, obeisances unto you. śrī-tulasī-vandanā Mother of Mahā-prasāda, increaser of all good fortune. Remover of mental and physical diseases eternally, O Tulasī! Obeisances unto you. śrī-gaṅgā-vandanā The vessel of the Lord’s pastimes, whose body is nectarean rasa, whose greatness is loudly proclaimed by the assembly of sages, Śiva, Brahmā, and Indra. Filled with great mercy, I worship Gaṅgā, whose drops of water destroy the multitude of sins. śrī-vedavyāsa-deva-vandanā Whose father is Parāśara and who is the father of Śukadeva. I worship that Vyāsa, who resides in Badarī, Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana. śrī-śukadeva-vandanā Whom, leaving home without undergoing ceremonies, having no duties, Dvaipāyana called out “O Son!”, agitated by separation, and absorbed in him, the trees responded. I bow to that Muni who is the heart of all beings. Who spoke this essence of all scriptures, the unique lamp of knowledge for those desiring to cross the blinding darkness. Who spoke the confidential Purāṇa out of compassion for materialistic people. I surrender to that son of Vyāsa, the guru of munis. śrīmad-bhāgavata-vandanā That primeval Lord, the abode of mercy, the color of a Tamāla tree, the most beneficial incarnation. The bridge over the boundless ocean of material existence. We worship the Śrīmad Bhāgavatam. śrī-śrī-nāma-vandanā Glories, glories to the blissful form of the name of Murāri, which causes one to give up efforts in prescribed duties, meditation, and pūjā. Which, if taken even once somehow or other, bestows liberation to living entities. My supreme nectar, my only life and ornament. Sweeter than sweet, the most auspicious of auspicious things, the excellent fruit of the creeper of all Vedas, conscious by nature. Chanted even once, with faith or with negligence, O best of the Bhṛgus! The name of Kṛṣṇa delivers any human being. śrī-śrī-jagannātha-deva-vandanā On the shore of the great ocean, on the blue summit shining like gold. Residing inside the palace with his brother Balabhadra. Between them is Subhadrā; giving opportunity for service to all suras. May that Jagannātha Svāmī be visible to my eyes. To the resident of Nīlācala, the eternal Paramātmā. To Balabhadra and Subhadrā, and to you Jagannātha, obeisances. śrī-śrī-nṛsiṁha-deva-vandanā Obeisances to Narasiṁha, who gives joy to Prahlāda. Whose nails are like chisels on the stone-like chest of Hiraṇyakaśipu. Narasiṁha is here, Narasiṁha is there. Wherever I go, there is Narasiṁha. Narasiṁha is outside, Narasiṁha is in the heart. I take shelter of Narasiṁha, the origin. Śrī Narasiṁha, glories to Narasiṁha, glories glories to Narasiṁha. Lord of Prahlāda, glory to the bee of the lotus face of Padmā. On whose face is Vāgīśā, on whose chest is Lakṣmī. In whose heart is knowledge, I worship that Narasiṁha. The joy of Prahlāda’s heart, the destroyer of the devotees’ ignorance. Resplendent like the autumn moon, I bow to the lion-faced Hari. śrī-śrī-rāmacandra-vandanā Whose limbs are soft and dark like a blue lotus, with Sītā seated on his left side. Holding a great arrow and beautiful bow in his hands, I bow to Rāma, the lord of the Raghu dynasty. On the right is Lakṣmaṇa holding a bow, on the left is the auspicious Jānakī. In front is Mārutī, I bow to that best of the Raghus. śrī-śrī-daśāvatāra-vandanā You deliver the Vedas, support the worlds, lift the earth, tear apart the demon, deceive Bali, destroy the warrior class, conquer Paulastya, hold the plow, extend mercy, and bewilder the mlecchas. I offer obeisances to You, Kṛṣṇa, who assume these ten forms.
