IDX.verses: śhrīdāma bale ogo rāṇī, vidāya de tora nīlamaṇi laye jāba goṣṭha vihāre godhana chāraṇa kari, āmi diba tomāra hari nivedana kari joḍa kare rāṇī bale ki balili, nā pāṭhāva vanamālī tomārā sabāo jāo vane baḍa ha’le lālane, la’ye jeo kānane pāṭhāiba tomā sabā sane śhunare śhrīdāma bhāi, āmāra jāoyā ha’la nāi mā vidāya nāhi dila more jñāna-dāsa kahe śhuna, yaśhodāra jīvana jāni ki nā jāni vidāya kare
IDX.en_translation:
Śrīdāma says: “O Queen! Bid farewell to your Blue Jewel. I will take Him for pastimes in the pasture. Grazing the cows, I will give (back) your Hari. I make this request with folded hands.” 

The Queen says: “What did you say? I will not send Vanamālī. You all go to the forest too. When He grows up, take Him to the forest with affection. I will send Him with all of you.” 

“Listen, O brother Śrīdāma! My going has not happened. Mother did not give me farewell.” Jñāna Dāsa says: “Listen, I know Yaśodā’s life; I do not know if she will bid farewell or not.”

IDX.author: bhaktisiddhānta sarasvatī ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
śhrīmatī rādhikā-kṛṣṇakāntā-śhiromaṇi 
kṛṣṇapriya-madhye tāṅ’ra sama nāhi dhanī 

munigaṇa śhāstre rādhā-kuṇḍera varṇane 
gāndharvikā-tulya kuṇḍa karaye gaṇane 

nāradādi-priyavarge je prema durlabha 
anya sādhakete tāhā kabhu nā sulabha 

kintu, rādhā-kuṇḍe snāna jei jana kare 
madhura rasete tāṅ’ra snāne siddhi dhare 

aprākṛta-bhāve sadā yugala-sevana 
rādhā-pāda-padma labhe sei harijana 

śhrī-vārṣabhānavī kabe dayitadāsere 
kuṇḍa-tīre sthāna dibe nija-jana ka’re 

‘upadeśhāmṛta’ dhari’ rūpānuga-bhāve 
jīvana jāpile kṛṣṇa-kṛpā sei pā’be 

satya, tretā, dvāparera je-sakala bhakta 
kṛṣṇakṛpā labhiyācḣe gṛhastha-virakta 

bhāvī-kāle, vartamāne bhaktera samāja 
sakalera padarajaḥ jāche dīna āja 

bhakativinoda-prabhu anuga je-jana 
dayita-dāsera tā’ra pade nivedana 

dayā kari’, doṣa hari’, bala ‘hari! hari!’ 
‘upadeśhāmṛta’-vāri śhiropari dhari’
IDX.en_translation:
Śrīmatī Rādhikā is the crest-jewel of Kṛṣṇa’s beloveds. Among Kṛṣṇa’s beloveds, there is no one as rich in love as Her. 

In the scriptures describing Rādhā-kuṇḍa, the sages count the Kuṇḍa as equal to Gāndharvikā (Rādhā). 

The love that is rare even for the dear devotees like Nārada is never easily attainable by other practitioners. 

But one who bathes in Rādhā-kuṇḍa attains perfection in that sweet mellow through his bath. 

Serving the Divine Couple eternally in a transcendental mood, that devotee of Hari attains the lotus feet of Rādhā. 

When will Śrī Vārṣabhānavī, accepting him as Her own, give Dayita-dāsa a place on the bank of the Kuṇḍa? 

If one passes his life holding the “Upadeśāmṛta” in the mood of a follower of Rūpa Gosvāmī, he will obtain Kṛṣṇa’s mercy. 

All the devotees of Satya, Tretā, and Dvāpara yugas who were detached householders attained Kṛṣṇa’s mercy. 

Today, this lowly person begs for the dust of the feet of all the devotees in the society of devotees, both in the future and the present. 

Whoever is a follower of Bhaktivinoda Prabhu—Dayita-dāsa makes this submission at his feet. 

Be merciful, remove my faults, and say “Hari! Hari!”, holding the water of “Upadeśāmṛta” upon my head.

IDX.author: sacchidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
śhrīvāsa-vachana, śhravaṇa kariyā, 
sādhvī pativratāgaṇa 
śhoka parihari’, mṛta śhiśhu rākhi’, 
hari-rase dila mana 

śhrīvāsa takhana, ānande mātiyā, 
aṅgane āila punaḥ 
nāche gorā-sane, sakala pāsari, 
gāya nandasuta-guṇa 

chāri daṇḍa rātre, marila kumāra, 
aṅgane keha nā jāne 
śhrī-nāma-maṅgale, tṛtīya prahara, 
rajanī atīta gāne 

kīrtana bhāṅgile, kahe gaura-hari, 
āji kena pāi duḥkha? 
bujhi, ei gṛhe, kicḣu amaṅgala, 
ghaṭiyā harila sukha 

tabe bhakta-jana, nivedana kare, 
śhrīvāsa-śhiśhura kathā 
śhuni’ gorārāya, bale, hāya hāya, 
marame pāinu vyathā 

keha nā kahile, āmāre takhana, 
vipada-saṁvāda sabe 
bhakativinoda, bhakata-vatsala, 
snehete majila tabe
IDX.en_translation:
Hearing Śrīvāsa’s words, the chaste and devoted wives gave up their grief; leaving the dead child, they gave their minds to the nectar of the Lord’s service. 

Śrīvāsa then, intoxicated with bliss, came back to the courtyard. He danced with Lord Caitanya, forgetting everything, and sang the glories of the son of Nanda. 

Four units of time into the night, the boy died, but no one in the courtyard knew. The late night passed in the auspicious chanting of the Holy Name. 

When the congregational chanting ended, Lord Caitanya said, “Why do I feel sorrow today? I understand that some inauspiciousness has occurred in this house, taking away the happiness.” 

Then the devotees related the story of Śrīvāsa’s child. Hearing this, the Lord said, “Alas, alas! I feel pain in My heart! 

“Why did no one tell Me the news of this calamity then?” Bhaktivinoda says: the Lord, who is affectionate to His devotees, was then immersed in love.

IDX.verses: śhrīvāse kahena prabhu,- “tuhū mora dāsa tuyā prīte bāṅdhā āmi jagate prakāśha bhaktagaṇa-senāpati-śhrīvāsa-paṇḍita jagate ghuṣuka āji tomāra charita prapañcha-kārā-rakṣiṇī māyāra bandhana tomāra nāhika kabhu, dekhuka jagajjana dhana, jana, deha, geha āmāre arpiyā āmāra sevāra sukhe ācḣa sukhī hañā mama līlāpuṣṭi lāgi’ tomāra saṁsāra śhikhuka gṛhastha-jana tomāra āchāra tava preme baddha ācḣi āmi, nityānanda āmā-dūhe suta jāni’ bhuñjaha ānanda nityasattva suta jā’ra, anitya tanaye āsakti nā kare sei sṛjane pralaye bhaktite tomāra ṛṇī āmi chiradina tava sādhu-bhāve tumi kṣama mora ṛṇa” śhrīvāsera pā-ya bhaktivinoda kujana kākuti kariyā māge gaurāṅga-charaṇa
IDX.en_translation:
The Lord said to Śrīvāsa, “You are My servant. I am revealed in the world, bound by your love. 

O Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita, general of the devotees! Let your character be proclaimed throughout the world today. 

The bondage of illusion, which keeps the soul in the prison of the material world, never affects you; let all the world see this. 

Offering wealth, followers, body, and home to Me, you remain happy in the joy of My service. 

For the nourishment of My pastimes, let all householders learn from your life and conduct. 

I am bound by your love, and so is Nityānanda. Knowing us both as your sons, enjoy bliss. 

One whose son is the eternal truth does not become attached to transient sons in creation or dissolution. 

In devotion, I am indebted to you forever. Through your saintly nature, please forgive My debt.” 

Bhaktivinoda, the lowly one, at the feet of Śrīvāsa, earnestly begs for the lotus feet of Lord Caitanya.

IDX.verses:
śhrīvāsera prati, chaitanya-prasāda, 
dekhiyā sakala jana 
jaya śhrī-chaitanya, jaya nityānanda, 
bali’ nāche ghana ghana 

śhrīvāsa-mandire, ki bhāva uṭhila, 
tāhā ki varṇana haya 
bhāvayuddha-sane, ānanda-krandana, 
uṭhe kṛṣṇa-premamaya 

chāri bhāi paḍi’, prabhura charaṇe, 
prema-gadagada-svare 
kāṅdiyā kāṅdiyā, kākuti kariyā, 
gaḍi’ jāya prema-bhare 

“ohe prāṇeśhvara, e hena vipada, 
pratidina jena haya 
jāhāte tomāra, charaṇa-yugale, 
āsakti bāḍite raya 

vipada-sampade, sei dina bhāla, 
je-dina tomāre smari 
tomāra smaraṇa-, rahita je-dina, 
se-dina vipada, hari” 

śhrīvāsa-goṣṭhīra, charaṇe paḍiyā, 
bhaktivinoda bhaṇe 
tomādera gorā, kṛpā vitariyā, 
dekhāo durgata jane
IDX.en_translation:
Seeing the mercy shown to Śrīvāsa by Lord Caitanya, all the people repeatedly danced, chanting: “All glories to Śrī Caitanya! All glories to Nityānanda!” 

What emotions arose in the temple of Śrīvāsa? How can they ever be described? Amidst a war of ecstasies, the crying of joy, full of love for Kṛṣṇa, arose. 

The four brothers fell at the Lord’s feet with voices choked with love. Weeping and pleading, they rolled on the ground in great love. 

“O Lord of my life! May such distress happen every day, so that my attachment to Your lotus feet may continuously increase. 

In distress or prosperity, that day is good when I remember You. The day devoid of Your remembrance—that day is true distress, O Lord!” 

Falling at the feet of Śrīvāsa’s associates, Bhaktivinoda says: “May your Lord Caitanya, distributing His mercy, reveal Himself to all distressed souls.”

IDX.author: sacchidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses:
sthāyibhāvāviṣṭa-chitta, pāiyā vibhāvavitta, 
udbhaṭa bhāvete āpanāra 
prāṇa-vṛtte nyāsa kare, prāṇa sei nyāsabhare, 
deha-prati vikṛti chālāya 

vaivarṇya, romāñcha, sveda, stambha, kampa, svara-bheda, 
pralayāśhru e aṣṭavikāra 
sañchārī je bhāvachaya, harṣāmarṣa āra bhaya, 
viṣāda, vismayādi tā’ra 

pravṛttikāraṇa haya, līlākāle rase laya, 
āpane karāya anukṣaṇa 
dhūmāyitā, ujjvalitā, dīptā āra se uddīpta, 
ei chāri avasthā lakṣaṇa 

jā’ra jei adhikāra, sāttvika vikāra tā’ra, 
se lakṣaṇe haya ta’ udaya 
mahābhāva-daśhā jathā, su-uddīpta bhāva tathā, 
anāyāse sulakṣita haya
IDX.en_translation:
A mind absorbed in the permanent sentiment, upon receiving stimuli, spontaneously places itself in an extraordinary emotional state within the life-airs. The life-airs, thus filled, then cause transformations in the body. 

Discoloration, horripilation, perspiration, stupefaction, trembling, change of voice, and tears—these are the eight transformations. Transient emotions like joy, indignation, fear, despondency, wonder, and others also arise. 

They become the cause of actions, and during the divine pastimes, they merge into transcendental mellows, constantly manifesting themselves. Obscured, glowing, blazing, and fully manifest—these are the symptoms of the four stages. 

According to one’s qualification, their physical transformations indeed manifest with those symptoms. Just as in the state of highest ecstatic love, the highly inflamed emotional state is easily and clearly recognized.

ājānulambita vanamālā vilolita 
veṇu, vetra, viṣāṇa, kabala virājita 

amala-kamala jini’ charaṇasundara 
namo namo nandagopa-suta manohara 

kṛṣṇa, kṛṣṇa vṛṣṇikula-puṣkara-bhāṣkara 
pṛthvī-deva-dvija-paśhu-sindhu-śhaśhadhara 

uddharma-śhārvara-hara asura-saṁhārī 
arka-ādi-sarvasura-pujya adhikārī

tomāra padāravinda sevo nirantara

(śhrī-kṛṣṇaprema-taraṅgiṇī)
IDX.en_translation:
You are worthy of praise, O Lord! Dark like a fresh cloud. Dressed in yellow garments bright like lightning. 

Ornaments of fresh Guñjā decorating Your ears. Hair adorned with peacock feathers, joyful face. 

A forest garland hanging down to Your knees, swinging. Resplendent with flute, stick, horn, and morsel. 

Beautiful feet surpassing the spotless lotus. Obeisances, obeisances to the enchanting son of Nanda Gopa. 

Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa! Sun of the lotus of the Vṛṣṇi dynasty. Moon of the ocean of the earth, gods, brāhmaṇas, and cattle. 

Destroyer of the night of irreligion, slayer of the demons. The Authority worshipable by the Sun and all the gods. 

Let my obeisances remain until the end of the kalpa. I beg this boon, O Lord, at Your feet. 

May I serve Your lotus feet constantly. Give me this order, O Ocean of Mercy. 

(Excerpt from Śrī Kṛṣṇa-prema-taraṅgiṇī)

IDX.verses:
su-ramyādi guṇa-gaṇa, hoiyācḣe vibhūṣaṇa, 
lalanā-uchita jatadura 
pṛthupremā, su-mādhurya-, sampadera suprāchurya, 
śhrī-kṛṣṇavallabhā rasapura 

vallabhā ta’ dvi-prakāra, svīyā, parakīyā āra, 
mugdhā, madhyā, pragalbheti traya 
keha vā nāyikā tāhe, keha sakhī hoite chāhe, 
nije ta’ nāyikā nāhi haya 

nāyikāgaṇa-pradhāna, rādhā, chandrā-dui jana, 
saundarya-vaidagdhya-guṇāśhrayā 
sei dui madhye śhreṣṭha, rādhikā kṛṣṇera preṣṭha, 
mahābhāvasvarūpa-nilayā 

āra jata nitya-priyā, nija nija jūtha lañā, 
se du’yera karena sevana 
śhrī-rūpa-anuga jana, śhrī-rādhikā-śhrī-charaṇa, 
vinā nāhi jāne anya dhana
IDX.en_translation:
All charming qualities and more have become her adornments, as much as befits a beautiful woman. She possesses abundant love, great sweetness, and profuse opulence. She is Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s beloved, brimming with divine mellows. 

Beloveds are of two kinds: one’s own wife and another’s wife, and these are categorized into three: innocent, partially experienced, and fully experienced. Some among them are heroines, and some wish to be companions, but she herself is not merely a heroine. 

The chief among the heroines are Rādhā and Candrā, both being the abode of beauty, intelligence, and all good qualities. Among these two, Rādhikā is the greatest, Kṛṣṇa’s dearest, and the ultimate abode of the highest ecstatic love. 

And all other eternal beloveds, taking their respective groups, serve those two. The followers of Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī know no other wealth except the auspicious lotus feet of Śrī Rādhikā.

IDX.translation_intro: Generalmente se canta primero śhrī rādhā-kṛpā-kaṭākṣa-stava-rāja
IDX.en_translation:
I bow to the son of Nanda, whose face is beautiful, whose ears are adorned with jeweled earrings, and whose body is smeared with beautiful sandalwood paste. 

I bow to the son of Nanda, whose eyes are long and lotus-like, whose hair is adorned with a peacock feather, and who enchants millions of Cupids. 

I bow to the son of Nanda, who has a pearl on the tip of His beautiful nose, beautiful rows of teeth, and a body smooth and dark like a fresh rain cloud. 

I bow to the son of Nanda, whose hands are beautified by a flute, whose gait shames a regal elephant, and who is adorned with shining yellow garments. 

I bow to the son of Nanda, whose beautiful body has three graceful bends, whose nails shine like the moon, and who is adorned with priceless jewels. 

I bow to the son of Nanda, who possesses a fragrant bodily scent, who has the Kaustubha jewel shining on His chest, and who is marked with the glittering Śrīvatsa mark. 

I bow to the son of Nanda, who is a clever hero of Vṛndāvana, who is adorned with playful garments, and who humbles the pride of the king of demigods. 

I bow to the son of Nanda, who is the beautiful leader of the cowherd women, who always bestows happiness, and who enchants the minds of all the worlds. 

Whoever recites this eight-verse prayer to the son of Nanda with faith will cross the insurmountable ocean of material existence and attain His lotus feet.
IDX.es_translation:
Su rostro es encantador, Sus hermosas orejas están adornadas con pendientes colgantes de gemas y Su cuerpo está untado con fragante pasta de sándalo. Yo ofrezco praṇāma a ese Śhrī Nanda-nandana.. 

Sus ojos son alargados como los lotos, unas plumas de pavo real adornan Su cabeza, y encanta a millones de Cupidos. Yo ofrezco praṇāma a ese Śhrī Nanda-nandana. 

De Su hermosa nariz cuelga una perla de elefante, Sus dientes poseen un brillo natural [como las perlas] y Su tez resplandece como una fresca nube de lluvia. Yo ofrezco praṇāma a ese Śhrī Nanda-nandana. 

Sus manos están adornadas con una flauta, Su majestuoso andar supera al del rey de los elefantes, y está embellecido con una delicada prenda amarilla. Yo ofrezco praṇāma a ese Śhrī Nanda-nandana. 

Su postura curvada en tres lugares es sumamente atractiva, Sus uñas brillan como lunas y está adornado con valiosas joyas. Yo ofrezco praṇāma a ese Śhrī Nanda-nandana. 

Su cuerpo destila una exquisita fragancia y en Su amplio pecho relucen la joya kaustubha y la marca de Śhrīvatsa. Yo ofrezco praṇāma a ese Śhrī Nanda-nandana. 

Él es el experto amante de Vṛndāvana que se viste para potenciar Sus atractivos y lúdicos pasatiempos, y que libera a Indra de su orgullo. Yo ofrezco praṇāma a ese Śhrī Nanda-nandana. 

El exquisito amante de las doncellas de Vraja hace siempre felices a todas las entidades vivientes y encanta sus mentes. Yo ofrezco praṇāma a ese Śhrī Nanda-nandana. 

La persona que recite con mucha fe estos ocho versos en glorificación del hijo de Nanda, cruzará fácilmente el insalvable océano de la existencia material y alcanzará el refugio de Sus pies de loto.

I always offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Prabhupāda, which are worshiped by millions of good people—the best of personalities who uphold the religious principles for this age, and whose worshipable feet grant boons and fearlessness. 

I always offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Prabhupāda, the leader of the assembly of pure devotees enriched by worship, the sole shelter for those who are most fallen and compassionate, and whose inconceivable lotus feet are the destination for those deprived of true progress and even for those who have been deceived. 

I always offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Prabhupāda, whose long, extremely tender body is like molten gold, who defies the pride of golden lotus stems with his complexion, and whose moon-like feet are adored by millions of Cupids. 

I always offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Prabhupāda, who is like a moon delighting his own stars of servants, who is like a supreme lion roaring against the inimical, and whose lotus feet are a shelter for the foolish who seek refuge. 

I always offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Prabhupāda, who has extensively glorified the land of Lord Gaura, whose mercy is widely distributed throughout the universes, and whose lotus feet are offered to the pitiable souls by the Lord Himself. 

I always offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Prabhupāda, who is the world-teacher and the eternal shelter of the lineage of Lord Gaura, who is devoted to the service of his own spiritual master, Gaura Kiśora, and whose lotus feet are supremely revered by Bhaktivinoda. 

I always offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Prabhupāda, who upholds the glories of the Gosvāmīs—Raghunātha, Rūpa, and Sanātana—the poet of the souls whose glories are sung on earth, and whose lotus feet are befriended by Kavirāja and Narottama. 

I always offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Prabhupāda, who, out of mercy, has embodied the chanting of the glories of God, who removes the burden of the earth, and whose lotus feet are more affectionate and loving than those of a father. 

I always offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Prabhupāda, who is a wish-fulfilling tree for surrendered servants, who is superior to any ordinary tree—being steadfast, benevolent, and the best—and whose divine lotus feet are worshiped by the best of boon-givers. 

I always offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Prabhupāda, who is the best among the highest renunciants and the master of the ultimate truth, who has taken the vow of an ascetic for the upliftment of the fallen, and whose lotus feet are served by the kings of ascetics. 

I always offer my respectful obeisances to the lotus feet of Prabhupāda, who is the dear follower of the daughter of Vṛṣabhānu. I am merely a speck of dust at his lotus feet, which possess a greatly wonderful purifying power.
IDX.es_translation:
Sus dos pies de loto son adorados por un número incontable de personas santas y es la personalidad más competente para liderar el nāma-saṅkiīrtana, el proceso para la iluminación espiritual para esta era. Sus adorables pies de loto otorgan toda clase de bendiciones y liberan del temor. Yo ofrezco praṇāma eternamente a los pies de Śhrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura Prabhupāda. 

Él es el líder de la asamblea de los santos que son firmes en el bhajana. Él es sumamente compasivo y el único refugio de los caídos. Sus inconcebibles pies engañan a los engañadores. Yo ofrezco praṇāma eternamente a los pies de Śhrīla Prabhupāda. 

Su alta, dorada y suave figura se burla del orgullo de los lotos dorados. Sus pies semejantes a lunas son adorados por incontables cupidos. Yo ofrezco praṇāma eternamente a los pies de Śhrīla Prabhupāda. 

Él es la luna complaciente para sus sirvientes estrellas, y con la excelencia de un león rugiente aleja a los que son hostiles [haciéndoles huir despavoridos]. Al elegir el refugio de sus pies, los inocentes obtienen el beneficio supremo. Yo ofrezco praṇāma eternamente a los pies de Śhrīla Prabhupāda. 

Él difundió ampliamente las glorias de Śhrī Navadvīpa-dhāma, la sagrada morada de Śhrī Gaurāṅga; glorificó especialmente la misericordia de Śhrī Gaurāṅga por el mundo entero, y otorgó los sagrados pies de Gaurāṅga a los que estaban más necesitados de misericordia. Yo ofrezco praṇāma eternamente a los pies de Śhrīla Prabhupāda. 

Él es el refugio eterno y el guru universal para los devotos de Śhrī Gaurāṅga. Está siempre dedicado a servir a su divino maestro, Śhrīla Gaura-kiśhora dāsa Bābājī, y es la morada del respeto supremo por los pies de Śhrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura. Yo ofrezco praṇāma eternamente a los pies de Śhrīla Prabhupāda. 

Comparte renombre con los Gosvāmīs Raghunātha dāsa, Rūpa y Sanātana, es glorificado en el mundo entero por emular la lucidez filosófica de Śhrīla Jīva Gosvāmī, y tiene una relación de amistad con Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī y Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura. Yo ofrezco praṇāma eternamente a los pies de Śhrīla Prabhupāda. 

Él se revela misericordiosamente como la personificación del hari-kīrtana. Es un asociado eterno del Señor Gaura que nació para eliminar la pesada carga de la tierra, y su amorosa disposición es aún más afectuosa que la de un padre. Yo ofrezco praṇāma eternamente a los pies de Śhrīla Prabhupāda. 

Él es un árbol de los deseos [de bendiciones] para sus rendidos sirvientes. Su paciencia y generosidad hacen que el árbol se avergüence. Sus divinos pies son adorados por los mejores entre quienes ofrecen bendiciones. Yo ofrezco praṇāma eternamente a los pies de Śhrīla Prabhupāda. 

Él sobrepasa a todos los paramahaṁsas. Es el guardián del objetivo supremo de la vida (kṛṣṇa-prema). Acepta el hábito de un renunciante para rescatar a las almas caídas. Sus pies son cuidadosamente servidos por los más grandes sannyāsis. Yo ofrezco praṇāma eternamente a los pies de Śhrīla Prabhupāda. 

Él es el sirviente más amado de la hija del rey Vṛṣabhānu. Yo me he refugiado en sus pies colocando el polvo de estos [sobre mi cabeza]. Esos pies poseen el inmenso y extraordinario poder de purificar. Yo ofrezco praṇāma eternamente a los pies de Śhrīla Prabhupāda.

IDX.en_translation:
For the sake of happiness, I built this house, but it burned down in a fire. I went to bathe in the ocean of nectar, but everything turned to poison. 

O friend! What is written in my fate? Thinking it would be cool, I worshipped the moon, but instead, I saw the scorching rays of the sun. 

Thinking it was high ground, I climbed the mountain, only to fall into deep water. Seeking wealth, my poverty instead increased, and I carelessly lost the jewel I had. 

I established a city and bound the ocean, hoping to find a precious gem. But the ocean dried up and the jewel remained hidden, all due to the fault of my unfortunate past actions. 

Feeling thirsty, I worshipped the cloud, but instead, a thunderbolt struck. Chaṇḍīdāsa says: “My love for Lord Śyāma has remained like a spear in my heart.”

IDX.verses: śhuna, he rasika jana, kṛṣṇa-gaṇa agaṇana, ananta kahite nāhi pāre kṛṣṇa jagatera guru, kṛṣṇa vāñcḣā-kalpa-taru, nāvika se bhava-pārābāre hṛdaya-pīḍita jā’ra, kṛṣṇa-chikitsaka tā’ra, bhava-roga nāśhite chatura kṛṣṇa bahirmukha-jane, premāmṛta-vitaraṇe, krame laya nija antaḥpura karmabandha-jñānabandha-, āveśhe mānava andha, tā’re kṛṣṇa karuṇā-sāgara pāda-padma-madhu diyā, andhabhāva ghuchāiyā, charaṇe karena anuchara vidhimārgarata-jane, svādhīnatā ratnadāne, rāgamārge karāna praveśha rāga-vaśhavartī ha’ye, pārakīya-bhāvāśhraye, labhe jīva kṛṣṇa-premāveśha premāmṛta-vāridhārā, sadā pānarata tāṅ’rā, kṛṣṇa tāṅhādera bandhu, pati seisaba vraja-jana, sukalyāṇa-niketana, dīna hīna vinodera gati
IDX.en_translation:
Listen, O discerning people! The qualities of Kṛṣṇa are innumerable and infinite; no one can describe them all. Kṛṣṇa is the spiritual master of the world and the wish-fulfilling tree; He is the helmsman in the ocean of material existence. 

For those whose hearts are distressed, Kṛṣṇa is the physician, expert in destroying the disease of material existence. For those who are averse to Him, He distributes the nectar of love and gradually takes them into His inner chamber. 

Human beings are blinded by their absorption in the bondage of fruitive action and speculative knowledge; for them, Kṛṣṇa is an ocean of mercy. By giving them the honey of His lotus feet and removing their blindness, He makes them His servants. 

To those engaged in the path of rules, He bestows the jewel of independence and grants them entry into the path of spontaneous love. Becoming subservient to His spontaneous love and taking shelter of the mood of paramount love, the soul attains absorption in love for Kṛṣṇa. 

They are always engaged in drinking the current of the nectar of love; Kṛṣṇa is their friend and their master. Those residents of Vraja are abodes of great auspiciousness and the only refuge for poor, lowly Bhaktivinoda.
IDX.es_translation:
Escuchen esto los que saborean melosidades de néctar. Las cualidades trascendentales de Śhrī Kṛṣṇa son innumerables. El propio Señor Ananta [que posee millones de cabezas y bocas] es incapaz de describirlas todas. Kṛṣṇa es el maestro espiritual del universo entero. Él es un árbol de los deseos y el timonel que nos guía a través del océano de la existencia material. 

Kṛṣṇa es el doctor para los corazones enfermos; Él es experto acabando con la enfermedad de la existencia material. Distribuyendo a todas las almas que se oponen a Él el néctar del prema, Él las lleva gradualmente a Su morada confidencial. 

Los seres humanos están cegados por su absorción en las ataduras del karma y el jñāna, pero Kṛṣṇa, que es un océano de compasión, elimina su ceguera otorgándoles la miel de Sus pies de loto. De ese modo, Él los transforma en sirvientes de Sus pies de loto. 

Kṛṣṇa otorga la joya de la independencia a quienes siguen el vidhi-mārga, el sendero de los principios regulativos, y les permite entrar en el rāga-mārga, el sendero del servicio amoroso espontáneo. Controlada por ese amor y refugiándose en en el parakīyā-bhāva (amor de amante), la jīva obtiene amor extático por Kṛṣṇa. 

Esos devotos están siempre bebiendo de la fuente de néctar del prema, ya que Kṛṣṇa es su amigo y señor. Los residentes de Vraja, que son moradas de todo lo auspicioso, son el refugio del pobre y caído Bhaktivinoda.

IDX.en_translation:
I have heard from the mouths of the saints, everyone says: by the mercy of Śrī Rūpa, one attains the lotus feet of the Divine Couple. 

Ha! Ha! Prabhu Sanātana, Gaurāṅga’s family! All of you together fulfill my desire. 

May the mercy of Śrī Rūpa be upon me. He whose shelter is those feet—he is a great soul. 

When will Prabhu Lokanātha take me along and offer me at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa? 

Will such a thing happen to me—that the playful sakhīs will discipline this follower Narottama? 

A humble prayer to Śrī Rūpa and Sanātana.
IDX.es_translation:
He escuchado de labios de todos los sādhus que por la misericordia de Śhrī Rūpa se puede obtener los pies de loto de la Pareja Divina. 

¡Oh, Sanātana Prabhu! ¡Oh, asociados personales de Gaurāṅga! Todos unidos, colmen por favor mis deseos. 

Que Śhrī Rūpa Gosvāmī derrame su misericordia sobre mí. Quien se refugia en los pies de loto de Śhrī Rupa es una gran personalidad. 

¿Cuándo me llevará mi maestro, Śhrī Lokanātha Gosvāmī, con él y me ofrecerá a los pies de loto de Śhrī Rūpa? 

¿Cuándo llegará el día en que las narma-sakhīs instruirán a Narottama y lo convertirán en su fiel seguidor?

IDX.en_translation:
Listen, listen Lord Nityānanda! Listen, Haridāsa Ṭhākura! Spread My command everywhere. 

Go to every single house and beg this of the people: “Chant “Kṛṣṇa!”, worship Lord Kṛṣṇa, and follow His teachings.” 

Do not speak or cause to be spoken anything else besides this. Come back to Me at the end of the day and tell Me what happened. He speaks the Lord’s command, calling out repeatedly: 

“Chant “Kṛṣṇa!”, worship Kṛṣṇa, and take the Name of Kṛṣṇa. Lord Kṛṣṇa is your mother, father, wealth, and very life.” 

“For all of you, Lord Kṛṣṇa’s incarnation has come. Worship such a Kṛṣṇa and give up all unrighteous behavior.” 

Listen, O twice-born! Whatever sins you have committed—if you do not commit them again, I will take all of them away from you. 

Give up violence toward others, robbery, and all other unrighteous acts. Do not perform them again. 

Follow the path of righteousness and chant the Holy Name of Lord Hari. Then you will also be able to deliver others. 

Gather all the robbers and thieves by calling them to you, and lead everyone onto the path of righteousness.

Very charming, sweet-smiling, endowed with all good qualities, very powerful, youthful, and profound. Eloquent, sweet-speaking, wise, brilliantly confident, expert, clever, happy, and steadfast. 

Grateful, obliging, most beloved, excellent, best among the renowned, enchanting to women, and absorbed in playful pastimes. Of an eternally new form, an embodiment of pure beauty, very expert and diligent in playing the flute. 

He is a noble and self-controlled hero, a calm and peaceful hero, a gentle and playful hero, and an arrogant yet brave hero—the leader of women. Surrounded by attendants and jokers, well-served by clowns and close assistants, He is a dear playful friend. 

Endowed with these five types of assistants, the son of Nanda Mahārāja behaves in the mood of both husband and paramour. He is a favorable hero, a cunning hero, an impudent hero, and an impartial hero; thirsty for rasa and the very embodiment of rasa, He sports in the groves.

IDX.en_translation:
Under the pretense of worshipping the Sun-god, the playful Rāi leaves Her home to meet Her Beloved with Her gopī friends. On the bank of Rādhā-kuṇḍa, She beholds Lord Kṛṣṇa, and both become absorbed in Their mutual companionship. 

They experience all the symptoms of ecstatic love, and these emotional transformations become Their ornaments along with Their contrary moods and intense longing. Initiated into the sacrifice of love with Lalitā and other friends, They become lost in the happiness They achieve. 

Many forest pastimes occur—swinging, water sports, the stealing of the flute, the drinking of nectar, and again the worship of the Sun-god. How many pastimes they perform! Thereafter, with Their friends, Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa are absorbed in amorous play. 

In Rādhā-kuṇḍa, such unparalleled eternal pastimes occur every day. For those whose eyes of pure love are open, these become visible; otherwise, they cannot be seen.

svabhaktiyoga-lāsinaṁ sadā vraje vihāriṇaṁ

navojjvalādi-bhāvanā-vidhāna-karmapāragaṁ 
vichitra-gaura-bhakti-sindhu-rasabhaṅga-lāsinam 
surāga-mārga-darśhakaṁ vrajādi-vāsa-dāyakaṁ

mahāprabhormahārasa-prakāśhanāṅkuraṁ priyaṁ 
sadā mahārasāṅkura-prakāśhanādi-vāsanāṁ 
mahāprabhorvrajāṅganādi-bhāva-moda-kārakaṁ

sadāṣṭa-sāttvikānvitaṁ nijeṣṭa-bhakti-dāyakaṁ

naro‛pi jāti tūrṇameva nāryabhāva-bhājanam 
tamujjvalākta-chittametu chitta-matta-ṣaṭpado- 
bhajāmyahaṁ gadādharaṁ supaṇḍitaṁ guruṁ prabhum

IDX.en_translation:
I worship Gadādhara, the greatly learned guru and master, who always delights in the practice of bhakti-yoga and resides in Vraja, who is foremost among the beloved associates of Hari and dear to the Son of Śacī, who reveals the service of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, and who is a great personality. 

I worship Gadādhara, the greatly learned guru and master, who is expert in arranging the emotions of the newly brilliant and others, who delights in the varied rasas of the ocean of Gaura-bhakti, who guides us on the path of intense devotional attachment, and bestows residence in Vraja and other holy places. 

I worship Gadādhara, the greatly learned guru and master, who is honored by the multitude of devotees whose essence is the lotus feet of Śacī’s Son, who is most beloved by Kṛṣṇa, who resides in the lotus of Gaura’s heart, who embodies Mukunda in Gaura’s form, and who bestows one’s inherent spiritual nature. 

I worship Gadādhara, the greatly learned guru and master, who is the sole cause for revealing the service of the groves and other such things, who always gives the ecstatic love of the sakhīs, who is the embodiment of great rasa, who is the most excellent true guru, who bestows the lotus feet of those always surrendered to him. 

I worship Gadādhara, the greatly learned guru and master, who is the beloved sprout revealing Mahāprabhu’s great rasa, who always has the desire to reveal the sprout of great rasa, who brings joy in the mood of the gopīs of Vraja and others to Mahāprabhu. 

I worship Gadādhara, the greatly learned guru and master, who enhances devotion to the lotus feet honored by the multitude of best brāhmaṇas, who insists on revealing his own body as the soul of Rādhikā, who bestows the bright nectar through teaching all the scriptures of devotion. 

I worship Gadādhara, the greatly learned guru and master, by whose sweet nectar from the lotus feet of his beloved ones, he bestows Gaura-bhakti, the great rasa-ocean nectar, who is always accompanied by the eight bodily transformations of ecstatic love, who bestows devotion to his chosen Deity. 

I worship Gadādhara, the greatly learned guru and master, whose mind is steeped in the waves and colors of his unique sweet love; even a man whose mind is thus infused quickly attains the qualification for the mood of a woman; let my mind, like a maddened bee, approach him, whose heart is imbued with ujjvala-rasa. 

Whoever reads these eight verses on Gadādhara, which always bestow the nectar of great rasa, with great devotion, which describe the festival of the gopīs of Vraja, will attain the eligibility for the jewel of devotion to the lotus feet of Śacī’s Son, through the service of the lotus feet of Rādhikā and Gadādhara.

kṛṣṇa-sevā vinā tāṅ’ra udyama nāhika āra

ei rati prauḍha haya mahā-bhāva dāsa pāya

IDX.en_translation:
The self-perfected love for the Lord, combined with a realization of one’s relationship with Him, always keeps a person spiritually capable. Without service to Lord Kṛṣṇa, there is no other endeavor for such a person, and they never make any attempt for their own happiness. 

This mature love eventually leads one to become a servant of the highest spiritual emotions. There is no other attainment equal to this. This kind of most wonderful and astonishing desire for divine enjoyment—I find no words to describe it.

tapanamiśhrera putra raghunātha bhaṭṭāchārya 
prabhuke dekhite chale cḣāḍi’ sarvakārya 

kāśhī hoite chalilā gauḍapatha diyā 
saṅgete sevaka eka chale jhāṅpi laiyā 

eimate raghunātha āilā nīlāchale 
mahāprabhura charaṇe giyā mililā kutūhale 

daṇḍavat praṇāma kari’ paḍilā charaṇe 
prabhu raghunātha jāni’ kailā āliṅgane 

‘‘bhāla haila āilā, dekha kamalalochana 
āji āmāra ihā karibā prasāda-bhojana” 

govindere kahi eka vāsā deoyāilā 
svarūpādi bhaktagaṇa-sane milāilā 

eimate prabhu-sane rahilā aṣṭamāsa 
dine dine prabhu kṛpāya bāḍaye ullāsa 

madhye madhye mahāprabhura karena nimantraṇa 
ghara-bhāta karena, āra vividha vyañjana 

raghunātha bhaṭṭa-pāke ati sunipuṇa 
jei rāndhe, sei haya amṛtera sama 

parama santoṣe prabhu karena bhojana 
prabhura avaśhiṣṭa pātra bhaṭṭera bhakṣaṇa 

aṣṭamāsa rahi’ prabhu bhaṭṭe vidāya dilā 
‘vivāha nā kariha’ bali’ niṣedha karilā 

“vṛddha pitāmātāra jāi’ karaha sevana 
vaiṣṇava-pāśha bhāgavata kara adhyayana 

punarapi ekabāra āsiha nīlāchale” 
eta kahi’ kaṇṭhamālā dila tā’ra gale 

āliṅgana kari’, prabhu tā’re vidāya dilā 
preme gadagada bhaṭṭa kāṅdite lāgilā 

svarūpa-ādi bhakta ṭhāṅi ājñā māgiyā

chāri vatsara ghare pitāmātāra sevā kailā 
vaiṣṇava-paṇḍita ṭhāṅi bhāgavata paḍilā 

pitāmātā kāśhī pāile udāsīna haiyā 
punaḥ prabhura ṭhāṅi gela bhāvete galiyā 

pūrvavat aṣṭamāsa prabhupāśha cḣilā

“āmāra ājñāya raghunātha, jāha vṛndāvane

Tapanamiśra’s son, Śrīla Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī, set out to see the Lord, leaving all other duties behind. 

From Kāśī he journeyed by the path through Bengal, accompanied by a servant. 

In this way, Raghunātha arrived at Jagannātha Purī and eagerly met Mahāprabhu at His feet. 

Performing full obeisances, he fell at the Lord’s feet, and the Lord, knowing Raghunātha, embraced him. 

“It is good that you have come; behold the lotus-eyed Lord Jagannātha. Today you will partake of sanctified food with Me.” 

The Lord told Govinda to arrange a dwelling for him and introduced him to Svarūpa Dāmodara and other devotees. 

In this manner, he remained with the Lord for eight months, and day by day his joy increased by the Lord’s mercy. 

From time to time, he would invite Mahāprabhu to his home and cook various delicious preparations. 

Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa was very skilled in cooking; whatever he prepared was like nectar. 

With supreme satisfaction the Lord would eat, and Raghunātha would then partake of the Lord’s remnants. 

After eight months, the Lord bade him farewell and instructed him: “Do not marry. 

Go and serve your elderly parents, and study the Śrīmad Bhāgavatam with a devotee scholar. 

Come again to Purī once more.” Saying this, the Lord placed a garland around his neck. 

Embracing him, the Lord bade him farewell, and Raghunātha, overwhelmed with love, began to weep. 

Taking leave from Svarūpa Dāmodara and the other devotees, he returned to Varanasi. 

For four years he served his parents at home and studied the Bhāgavatam with a devotee scholar. 

When his parents passed away, he became detached and again went to the Lord, melting in divine emotion. 

As before, he stayed with the Lord for eight months, after which the Lord again gave him an order: 

“By My command, Raghunātha, go to Vṛndāvana and reside there with Rūpa and Sanātana. 

Always read the Bhāgavatam and chant the Holy Names of Lord Kṛṣṇa; soon the Lord will bestow His mercy upon you.” 

Saying this, the Lord embraced him, and by the Lord’s mercy, he became intoxicated with divine love. 

He had received a fourteen-cubit Tulasī garland from Lord Jagannātha, along with leftover betel leaves and rice from a festival. 

The Lord gave him those items, and he kept the garland, considering it his worshipable Deity. 

Receiving the Lord’s command, he came to Vṛndāvana and took shelter of Rūpa and Sanātana Gosvāmīs. 

In Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī’s assembly he would read the Bhāgavatam, and while reading, his mind would become overwhelmed with love. 

With tears, trembling, and a choked voice, he could sometimes not even continue reading. 

His voice was sweet like a cuckoo’s, and he was expert in the melodic modes; while reading one verse, he would express four different melodies. 

When Lord Kṛṣṇa’s sweet qualities came to his mind, he would be so overwhelmed with love that he knew nothing else. 

He surrendered at the feet of Lord Govinda, who was his life’s treasure. 

He instructed his disciples to build a temple for Lord Govinda and had ornaments made for the Deity. 

He would not listen to worldly gossip, nor would he speak it; his twenty-four hours were spent in worship and topics about Lord Kṛṣṇa. 

He would not hear any criticism of the devotees; he only knew that everyone was engaged in the worship of the Lord. 

During meditation, he would wear the garland given by Mahāprabhu and keep a token of the Lord’s remnants around his neck. 

By Mahāprabhu’s mercy, divine love flowed from him unimpeded. The Lord’s mercy upon Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa was indeed a great fruit.

IDX.translation_intro: Este aṣṭaka se canta en la métrica poética denominada ‘Tūṇaka’
IDX.en_translation:
His bodily effulgence derides the dark clouds, sapphires, and the most intense blue. His divine garments resemble the rising sun and rays of lightning. His beautiful limbs are anointed with white and yellow sandalwood paste. May that Son of Nanda Mahārāja grant me service to His lotus feet. 

His earrings are expert in dancing on His cheeks, mocking the king of birds, Garuḍa. His face, like the moon and a cluster of lotuses, breaks their pride. He increases His deep confidential love-ties with the gopīs. May that Son of the King of Cowherds grant me service to His lotus feet. 

His form, dress, and loving pastimes are ever-fresh. He is surrounded by friends who give Him joy with their playful jokes. The splendor of His pleasure-groves surpasses the celestial gardens of Indra. May that Son of the King of Cowherds grant me service to His lotus feet. 

He is glorified by His friends who are adorned with the gold of divine love. He is worshipped by the guardians of the world who bow their foreheads to the ground. He constantly offers His respects to the sages. May that Son of the King of Cowherds grant me service to His lotus feet. 

By His playful pastimes He killed Indra's pride and destroyed the demons Kāliya, Kaṁsa, and Vatsa. He nourishes His devotees with the showers of His various pastimes. He delights the residents of Vraja by His heroic character. May that Son of the King of Cowherds grant me service to His lotus feet. 

He satisfies Śrīmati Rādhā⋅rāṇī and the other gopīs with the intoxicating nectar of His Rāsa dance in the groves. He nourishes His companions with various playful pastimes. His loving character and fame delight the hearts of the entire world. May that Son of the King of Cowherds grant me service to His lotus feet. 

By His Rāsa dance, He shows the true path of pure devotion. His wonderful form and attire are the Cupid of all Cupids. He charms the gopīs with the glances from the corners of His eyes. May that Son of the King of Cowherds grant me service to His lotus feet. 

He longs to touch Śrīmati Rādhā⋅rāṇī while picking flowers. He is gladdened by the sight of Her beautiful face, which is lovely even in Her mock anger. He is the enchanting sandalwood paste smeared on Rādhā's chest. May that Son of the King of Cowherds grant me service to His lotus feet. 

Whoever praises the Beloved of Śrīmati Rādhā⋅rāṇī with these eight verses—He who is difficult even for the Goddess of Fortune to see—that person, with a satisfied heart, will be engaged in the forests of Vraja in the service of His feet.
IDX.es_translation:
El color de Su cuerpo derrota al brillo de una nube reciente de lluvia, al kājjala y al zafiro azul. Sus ropas amarillas son más radiantes que el azafrán, el sol naciente y el relámpago. Su cuerpo está untado con pasta de sándalo mezclado con alcanfor. Que ese Ballavendra-nandana Kṛṣṇa (el hijo del rey de los pastores) me bendiga con el servicio de Sus pies de loto. 

Sobre Sus mejillas se balancean unos pendientes con forma de delfines que son expertos danzarines. Su rostro echa por tierra el orgullo de la luna llena y de multitudes de lotos. Él estrecha las cadenas de las vraja-gopīs incrementando sus secretos sentimientos por Él. Que ese Ballavendra-nandana Kṛṣṇa me bendiga con el servicio de Sus pies de loto. 

Su belleza, Su atuendo, Sus gloriosos pasatiempos llenos de amor y todos Sus actos son siempre frescos y novedosos. Él está siempre rodeado de Sus amigos que Le deleitan con sus ocurrentes palabras mientras juegan. Los rayos que emanan de Sus encantadores bosques derrotan al celestial jardín Nandana de Indra. Que ese Ballavendra-nandana Kṛṣṇa me bendiga con el servicio de Sus pies de loto. 

Deleitado por Sus amigos, que están decorados con el oro del prema, Él es reverenciado por los señores de diferentes planetas [como Indra], que postran sus cabezas en el suelo. Y aun así, Él adora diariamente a los brahmanes y a Sus gurus en los momentos apropiados. Que ese Ballavendra-nandana Kṛṣṇa me bendiga con el servicio de Sus pies de loto. 

Él aplacó la ira de Indra y Kālīya-nāga sin esfuerzo alguno, y acabó fácilmente con Kaṁsa y Vatsāsura. La lluvia de Sus gozosos pasatiempos nutre a los devotos que son como pájaros chātaka (exclusivos). Él deleita a los Vrajavāsīs con Su valor, Su naturaleza inmaculada y Sus dulces pasatiempos. Que ese Ballavendra-nandana Kṛṣṇa me bendiga con el servicio de Sus pies de loto. 

Él satisface a Śhrīmatī Rādhikā y a las demás gopīs con el néctar de Sus pasatiempos en los kuñjas y con el rāsa-līlā. Él nutre a las sakhīs de Śhrīmatī Rādhikā con Sus pasatiempos amorosos y Sus bromas, y deleita los corazones de todos con Su prema, Su naturaleza, Su ingenio y Su fama. Que ese Ballavendra-nandana Kṛṣṇa me bendiga con el servicio de Sus pies de loto. 

Mediante la ejecución del rāsa-līla, Śhrī Kṛṣṇa muestra el sendero real del bhakti puro. Con Su belleza y atuendos agita las mentes de quienes agitan las mentes (cupidos). Con Sus miradas de soslayo Él insinúa Sus sentimientos a las gopīs. Que ese Ballavendra-nandana Kṛṣṇa me bendiga con el servicio de Sus pies de loto. 

Él anhela siempre el contacto de Śhrīmatī Rādhikā cuando Ella va a recoger flores y experimenta una inmensa dicha cuando obtiene el darśhana del rostro de Rādhikā, que se ve sumamente atractiva con esa picardía amorosa Suya. Él es la encantadora pasta de sándalo que adorna los pechos de Rādhikā. Que ese Ballavendra-nandana Kṛṣṇa me bendiga con el servicio de Sus pies de loto. 

Quien canta este aṣṭaka ora a Śhrī Kṛṣṇa, que es el amor del corazón de Rādhikā y cuyo darśhana no es posible ni para las diosas celestiales encabezadas por Lakṣmī. De este modo Lo complace no sólo a Él, sino también a Rādhikā y Sus compañeras, y Kṛṣṇa ocupará a ese devoto en el servicio de Sus pies de loto en Śhrī Vṛndāvana.

IDX.en_translation:
On the heated sand, like a drop of water—in the society of sons, friends, and wife, forgetting You, my mind, I dedicated myself to them. Now, of what use will I be? 

O Lord Mādhava! I am hopeless about the final outcome. You are the deliverer of the world and merciful to the poor; therefore, I place my faith in You. 

Half of my life I spent in sleep; how many days have passed in old age and childhood? In secluded groves, with women, I was intoxicated by amorous sports; when will I ever worship You? 

How many four-headed Brahmās die again and again, but You have no beginning or end. They are born from You and again they merge into You, just like the waves of the ocean. 

Vidyāpati says: “At the end, fearing the God of Death, I see no other refuge besides You. You are called the Beginningless Lord without origin; now the burden of delivering me is Yours.”

IDX.verses: ṭhākura vaiṣṇava-gaṇa, kari ei nivedana, mo baḍa adhama durāchāra dāruṇa-saṁsāra-nidhi, tāhe ḍubāila vidhi, keśhe dhari’ more kara pāra vidhi baḍa balabān, nā śhune dharama-jñāna, sadāi karama-pāśhe bāndhe nā dekhi tāraṇa-leśha, jata dekhi saba kleśha, anātha, kātare teñi kānde kāma, krodha, lobha, moha, mada, abhimāna saha, āpana āpana sthāne ṭāne aicḣana āmāra mana, fire jena andhajana, supatha-vipatha nāhi jāne nā loinu sat mata, asate majila chita, tuyā pāye nā karinu āśha narottama-dāse kaya, dekhi’ śhuni’ lāge bhaya, tarāiyā laha nija-pāśha
IDX.en_translation:
O venerable devotees, I make this petition: I am a very fallen and wicked person. Fate has drowned me in the terrible ocean of material existence; please grab me by the hair and carry me across. 

Fate is very powerful and does not listen to religious knowledge; it always binds me with the ropes of my own actions. I see no trace of deliverance—all I see is distress. I am helpless, and therefore I cry out in anguish. 

Lust, anger, greed, illusion, pride, and false ego—each pulls me toward its own place. Such is my mind that it wanders like a blind person, knowing neither the right path nor the wrong one. 

I did not accept good counsel, and my mind was absorbed in evil; I placed no hope in Your feet. Narottama dāsa says: seeing and hearing of this condition, I feel fear. Please deliver me and take me into Your company.
IDX.es_translation:
¡Oh, venerables vaiṣṇavas! Escuchen por favor mi humilde plegaria. Soy un alma totalmente caída e indigna, y el destino ha hecho que me esté ahogando en este terrible océano de la existencia material. Rescátenme de este océano agarrándome del cabello. 

Las leyes de la Providencia son muy poderosas y atan a uno con las cuerdas del karma sin tener en cuenta la religiosidad o el conocimiento de la persona. No encuentro ningún modo de librarme de esta condición y lo único que veo es sufrimiento. Indefenso y lleno de angustia, me lamento y lloro. 

La lujuria, la ira, la codicia, la confusión, la locura y el orgullo tiran de mí hacia sus respectivos terrenos, y mi mente va de un lado a otro como un ciego sin saber lo que es correcto e incorrecto. 

No he querido aceptar los principios virtuosos y, en lugar de ello, mi conciencia ha estado absorta en actividades irreligiosas. Jamás busqué el refugio de tus pies de loto. Narottama dāsa dice: “¡Oh, Vaiṣṇava Ṭhākura!, tengo miedo de todo cuanto veo y oigo a mi alrededor. Libérame y mantenme siempre cerca de ti.”

The feet of the Vaiṣṇava ṭhākura are the great treasure of the earth. Listen, oh brother, with a single mind. One who takes their shelter and worships, Kṛṣṇa never abandons them; all others simply die in vain.

It is written in the Purāṇas that holy water from pilgrimage sites is pure by nature, but all that is merely a deception of devotion. All these cannot compare to the water from the Vaiṣṇava’s feet, by which all desires are fulfilled. 

In the association of Vaiṣṇavas, the mind is joyful at every moment, and one always experiences the direct association of Kṛṣṇa. Humble Narottama Dāsa Ṭhākura weeps, his heart finds no patience: “Why has my condition become so broken?”

Los pies de loto de los venerables vaiṣṇavas son el mayor tesoro del mundo. ¡Oh hermano!, escucha por favor con mucha atención. Śhrī Kṛṣṇa jamás abandona a quien, habiéndose refugiado en los vaiṣṇavas, Le adora con amor. Otros mueren inútilmente.

Las cualidades purificantes del agua de los lugares sagrados están descritas en los Purāṇas, pero eso no otorga la riqueza del bhakti. En realidad, el agua de los lugares sagrados no es tan purificante como el agua que ha lavado los pies de los vaiṣṇavas, la cual satisface todos los deseos. 

El corazón se llena de gozo a cada momento en la compañía de los vaiṣṇavas, en la cual se tratan siempre temas relacionados con Kṛṣṇa. Con el corazón inquieto, Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura se lamenta: “¿Por qué he sido privado de su asociación?”

IDX.verses: tumi ta’ dayāra sindhu, adhama janāra bandhu, more prabhu kara avadhāna paḍinu asat bhole, kāma-timiṅgile gile, ohe nātha kara paritrāṇa jāvat janama mora, aparādhe hainu bhora, niṣkapaṭe nā bhajinu tomā tathāpi je tumi gati, nā cḣāḍiha prāṇapati, mora sama nāhika adhamā patita-pāvana nāma, ghoṣaṇā tomāra śhyāma, upekhile nāhi mora gati jadi hoi aparādhī, tathāpiha tumi gati, satya satya jena satīra pati tumi ta’ parama devā, nāhi more upekhibā, śhuna śhuna prāṇera īśhvara jadi kari aparādha, tathāpiha tumi nātha, sevā diyā kara anuchara kāme mora hata chita, nāhi śhune nija hita, manera nā ghuche durvāsanā more nātha aṅgīkuru, tumi vāñcḣā-kalpataru, karuṇā dekhuka sarvajanā mo-sama patita nāi, tribhuvane dekha chāi, ‘narottama-pāvana’ nāma dhara ghuṣuka saṁsāre nāma, patita uddhāra’ śhyāma, nijadāsa kara giridhara narottama baḍa duḥkhī, nātha more kara sukhī, tomāra bhajana-saṅkīrtane antarāya nāhi jāya, ei se parama-bhaya, nivedana kari anukṣaṇe
IDX.en_translation:
You are indeed an ocean of mercy and a friend of the fallen. O Lord, please be mindful of me. I have fallen into bad association and have been swallowed by the great whale of lust. O Master, please deliver me! 

All my life I have been absorbed in offenses and have not sincerely worshiped You. Yet You are my only refuge. Do not abandon me, O Lord of my life, for there is no one more fallen than me. 

The name “Purifier of the Fallen” is Your declaration, O dark-complexioned Lord! If You neglect me, I have no other shelter. Even if I am an offender, still You are my only refuge; this is as true as a chaste wife’s husband being her only refuge. 

You are indeed the Supreme Deity; You will not neglect me. Please hear, O Lord of my life! Even if I commit offenses, still You are my Master. Please make me Your servant by giving me service. 

My heart is ruined by lust; it does not hear what is good for itself. The evil desires of my mind do not cease. O Master, please accept me; You are the wish-fulfilling tree of desire. Let everyone witness Your mercy. 

There is no one as fallen as me in all the three worlds. Take the name “Purifier of Narottama!” Let this name resound throughout the world: “The Lord delivers the fallen!” Make me Your own servant, O lifter of the hill. 

Narottama is very distressed. O Lord, make me happy through worship and congregational chanting. The obstacles do not go away, and this is my greatest fear. I submit this prayer to You constantly.

IDX.en_translation:
I offer my obeisances to the son of Śacī, whose body is of a bright, golden complexion and who is ever filled with ecstatic love. He possesses a trace of compassion that purifies the three worlds. 

I offer my obeisances to the son of Śacī, whose heart is overwhelmed with emotions, whose loud roars threaten the wicked, and who is the merciful cause of destroying the fear of material existence. 

I offer my obeisances to the son of Śacī, who wears saffron garments, has beautiful cheeks, and whose toenails are more radiant than the moon. He delights in chanting His own names and qualities. 

I offer my obeisances to the son of Śacī, from whose lotus-like eyes a stream of tears flows, whose body exhibits new and fresh ecstatic emotions, and who dances with extremely slow, graceful movements. 

I offer my obeisances to the son of Śacī, whose charming and restless foot movements are beautiful, whose sweet feet are adorned with ankle bells, and whose cool face surpasses the moon. 

I offer my obeisances to the son of Śacī, who wears a waist-string, carries a water pot and a staff, whose divine body has a shaven head, and whose staff dispels the sins of the wicked. 

I offer my obeisances to the son of Śacī, whose body is adorned with dust and curly hair, whose trembling red lips are beautiful, and who is marked with a bright tilaka made of sandalwood paste. 

I offer my obeisances to the son of Śacī, whose eyes shame the red lotus petals, whose divine arms extend down to His knees, and whose youthful body is dressed as a dancer.
IDX.es_translation:
Su sublime cuerpo brilla con un resplandor dorado y realiza incesantemente pasatiempos embargado por sentimientos trascendentales (los bhāvas de Śhrīmatī Rādhikā). Una diminuta partícula de Su misericordia purifica los tres mundos. Yo ofrezco praṇāma al hermoso hijo de Madre Śhachī. 

Las transformaciones de bhāva de Su corazón hacen que Su voz se quiebre, Su estruendoso rugido atemoriza a los ateos, y Su compasión destruye el temor que suscita la existencia material. Yo ofrezco praṇāma al hermoso hijo de Madre Śhachī. 

Su vestimenta tiene el color azafrán del sol naciente, Sus mejillas son seductoras, las uñas de Sus manos y pies irradian un brillo que eclipsa la gloria de la luna llena, y experimenta una inmensa dicha al ejecutar el kīrtana de Sus nombres y virtudes. Yo ofrezco praṇāma al hermoso hijo de Madre Śhachī. 

De Sus ojos de loto fluyen ríos de lágrimas. Su cuerpo está decorado con transformaciones de bhāva siempre nuevas, y en Sus pasatiempos de danza Sus movimientos fluyen de un modo sumamente delicado. Yo ofrezco praṇāma al hermoso hijo de Madre Śhachī. 

Los inquietos movimientos de Sus hermosos pies son muy atractivos. Esos dulces pies están adornados con primorosas campanillas que tintinean. Su rostro es más refrescante que la luna. Yo ofrezco praṇāma al hermoso hijo de Madre Śhachī. 

Lleva una tela alrededor de Su cintura para sujetar Su kaupīna (ḍora), y en Sus manos sostiene un kamaṇḍalu y una daṇḍa 1. Su divino cuerpo está coronado con una cabeza rasurada. Con Su daṇḍa, Él destruye los pecados de las personas malvadas. Yo ofrezco praṇāma al hermoso hijo de Madre Śhachī. 

Los rizos de Su cabello están adornados con el polvo de la tierra [que se levanta cuando danza], y Sus cautivadores labios, carmesí como la fruta bimba, tiemblan. Su cuerpo está adornado con resplandeciente tilaka hecho de pasta de sándalo malaya. Yo ofrezco praṇāma al hermoso hijo de Madre Śhachī. 

La forma de Sus ojos derrota la alargada forma de un pétalo de loto rojizo. Sus hermosos brazos se extienden hasta Sus rodillas, y Su forma es agraciada con el atuendo de un joven bailarín. Yo ofrezco praṇāma al hermoso hijo de Madre Śhachī. 1 Kamaṇḍalu y daṇḍa – el recipiente para el agua y la vara que llevan los mendicantes.

IDX.en_translation:
Your lotus feet are worshiped by devoted ones like Śiva and others. Having attained the supreme abode of the Supreme Lord, You shine greatly. For all assemblies of surrendered devotees, You are the shining wish-fulfilling tree that fulfills their desires. O son of Śacī, O my Lord, O giver of liberation, please show mercy to me, the dull-witted. 

Indeed, even those with vast intelligence like Sārvabhauma are unable to fully describe You, who are considered a great incarnation. Who else, then, can be skillful enough? Therefore, I offer my supreme obeisances to You. O son of Śacī, O my Lord, O giver of liberation, please show mercy to me, the dull-witted. 

That which was not revealed in any way by the scriptures or even the Upanisads, and that which was not even revealed by incarnations in other ages—O ocean of mellows, You are now scattering that jewel of devotion on this earth. O son of Śacī, O my Lord, O giver of liberation, please show mercy to me, the dull-witted. 

You astonish the stage of dancing with Your own expanding love. You manifest the nectar of love for the assemblies of surrendered devotees, just like the three-eyed Lord Śiva. O You who are difficult to understand for those arrogant people tainted by false ego, O son of Śacī, O my Lord, O giver of liberation, please show mercy to me, the dull-witted. 

Those people born on earth who have taken birth in low families—You deliver even them with Your abundant and beautiful mercy. Thus, with a joyful heart, I take refuge in You. O son of Śacī, O my Lord, O giver of liberation, please show mercy to me, the dull-witted. 

From Your lotus-like mouth flows the sweet honey of gentle words. This creates a multitude of devotees who, like bees, are eager for that nectar. O ocean of jewel-like Holy Names which bring auspiciousness to all people! O son of Śacī, O my Lord, O giver of liberation, please show mercy to me, the dull-witted. 

Your face is sweet like the moon, and Your eyes are like shining, ever-awake lotus flowers. Your lips are beautiful like a cluster of smiles, and Your chest is broad. Your arms are powerful like raised snakes, and Your splendor is like millions of Cupids. O son of Śacī, O my Lord, O giver of liberation, please show mercy to me, the dull-witted. 

I am a wicked person on this earth, yet You are golden-colored like the ketakī flower. Even though I am full of various faults, You do not show even a trace of finding fault in me. Therefore, with a humble mind, I worship You, O Lord who are compassionate to the fallen. O son of Śacī, O my Lord, O giver of liberation, please show mercy to me, the dull-witted. 

O festival for the entire world! For those people who, with their minds fixed on Your lotus footprints, recite these eight verses—O delight of Śacī’s heart, O Lord whose fame shines like the moon—O Lord, please bestow upon them abundant good fortune born of Your own love.

vrajapure līlārasa-kathā gāna, yugalakiśhora dhyāna, prārthanā kariba abhilāṣe jīvane maraṇe ei, āra kicḣu nāhi chāi, kahe dīna narottama-dāse
IDX.en_translation:
Vṛndāvana is beyond the power of speech to describe—a spiritual abode dense with the bliss of divine love. In that place of manifest happiness there is no suffering from old age or death, and the mellows of Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes are always present. 

The love of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa defeats many-times refined gold; in their joyful waves, they are an ocean of mellows. Their eyes, like chakora birds, drink in that love; both are friends of the happiness of love. 

Rādhā, the best of beloveds, is enchanting on the left side and bears the effulgence of golden Kṛṣṇa. Her sari is red with affection, and she wears charming blue silk; ornaments adorn her every limb. 

Their eyes drink in the pastimes of beauty; both are the very life of the companions, who are immersed in joy. Beyond the perception of the Vedas, upon a jeweled altar, they serve the youthful Divine Couple daily. 

Why do you not worship the Lord, having obtained such a rare human birth? Why do you die entangled in the bonds of material existence? Give up other ritualistic activities and do not look toward mundane religion; instead, perform devotional service to the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa. 

Material objects lead toward danger; you do not worship the Lord of Vraja, the essence of happiness, the son of Nanda. Heaven, impersonal liberation, and the enjoyment of hellish material existence—all are the destruction and perversion of human birth. 

Do not place faith in the material body; the lord of death is a strict disciplinarian. The results of actions are an ocean of sorrow. Seeing and hearing this, worship according to the saintly scriptures and fix your attachment upon the lotus feet of the Divine Couple. 

Fruitive activities and speculative knowledge are merely pots of poison; those who eat them thinking them to be nectar always wander through various species, eating abominable things, and their birth leads only to degradation. 

One who has no attachment for Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa and yet calls another their lord knows nothing of loving devotional service. Such people have no trace of devotion; they meditate in illusion, and their worthless conceptions are in vain. 

People perform knowledge and work but do not know the yoga of devotion, thus remaining ignorant in many ways. Do not listen to them; knowing the ultimate reality, loving devotion is the life of the devotees. 

The Lord pervades the universe, and Brahmā and Śiva are His order-carriers; His pastimes are sweet. Whoever knows this truth is the most excellent, and I will always associate with such persons. 

Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Lord; become extremely thirsty for Him and worship Him with the mood of Vraja. In the company of devotees who relish divine mellows, always enjoy with great joy while residing in Vṛndāvana. 

Day and night, filled with spiritual emotion and meditating in the mind, I will always reside in the Vraja of Nanda. Know this statement to be true and never bring anything else into it; this is the authoritative word of Śrī Jīva Gosvāmī. 

Fix your mind upon the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa’s devotees and, according to their words, always become like the companions; joining their group, I will always wander in Vraja. 

Singing the narrations of the mellows of His pastimes and meditating on the youthful Divine Couple, I will pray with longing. In life and in death I desire nothing else—so says humble Narottama dāsa.

Vācya and Vācaka—these two are Your forms. Vācya is Your divine form, the embodiment of eternal knowledge and bliss. 

Vācaka is Your holy name, which in the form of syllables is the resting place of all souls’ bliss. 

In these two forms, Your manifestation is endless; out of mercy, You grant Your divine pastimes to the living entities. 

But I have known, O Lord, that Your name is even more merciful than Your form—this is wonderful. 

The Vedas declare that there is no difference between the Name and the Named. Still, the Name is more compassionate. 

If, even after committing offenses against Kṛṣṇa, one has faith in the Name and calls out names like Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, or Hari with a full heart, 

then the offenses vanish, and that person floats effortlessly in the ocean of bliss, in the vast expanse of divine mellows. 

Though one may offend the Deity form, one can cross over those offenses by taking shelter of the pure Name. 

Bhaktivinoda begs at the lotus feet of Śrī Rūpa for constant attachment to the Holy Name.

Speak, speak the Name of Lord Hari! Do not pretend. The country is surrounded by calamity. Knowing this truth, they have already fled—your ears, your teeth, and your hair. 

Behind them, your eyes and your speech have both broken their promise. Saying “mine, mine,” you die day and night while the messengers of the God of Death see this as a show. 

In this beautiful city, in every house, there is a terrible outpost of the God of Death. Counting the days and years of your punishment, on which day will he finally strike? 

Your wife, sons, and daughters-in-law all take care of themselves; everything is as bitter as neem. At the time of your death, they will bind your hands and neck and light the funeral pyre at your mouth. 

If you do not wholeheartedly chant the Name of Lord Hari, how will you ever cross over the messenger of death? Locana Dāsa says clearly: “You are dying only due to your own fault.”

The bank of Rādhā-kuṇḍa is the supreme place and the very abode of divine love.

I first offer my obeisances to the feet of my initiating spiritual master and all my instructing spiritual masters. 

Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī, Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī, Śrīla Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī, Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī, Śrīla Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī, and Śrīla Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī—these six are my instructing spiritual masters.

Taking shelter of this tree, a learned person obtains the fruit of auspiciousness: servitude in the pastimes of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa in the forest of Vṛndāvana. 

Having honored the Vaiṣṇavas, the brāhmaṇas, and all living entities eternally, I, being humble, sing this song based on the rasa of Vraja.

In the groves of Vraja, on the banks of the Yamunā, there is an enchanting platform beautifully decorated with flowers. 

The sight of the majestic trees and creepers delights the eyes, while many birds chirp upon their branches. 

The gentle Malayan breeze blows softly, and swarms of bees hover around, greedy for honey. 

The full moon of spring distributes its moonlight with constant affection. 

At such a time, the best of connoisseurs, the Holder of the Flute, began the rāsa dance. 

In the midst of hundreds of millions of gopīs, Hari dances with Rādhā in great joy. 

Singing Her songs, the Enchantress of Mādhava stole the hearts of everyone in the world. 

That chaste lady enchanted all moving and non-moving beings, and even Candrāvalī lost her composure. 

Having churned the mind of the Youth of Vraja, Rādhā then suddenly disappeared. 

Bhaktivinoda considers this a great calamity; today the rāsa dance has ended in the absence of Rādhā.
IDX.es_translation:
En los bosques de Vraja, a ambas orillas del Yamunā, hay encantadoras plataformas hermosamente decoradas con flores. 

Diversos árboles frutales y enredaderas proporcionan satisfacción a los ojos. Multitud de pájaros cantan en ellos dulcemente. 

Una refrescante brisa procedente de los montes Malaya sopla dulcemente, y un enjambre de abejas revolotea en busca de miel. 

La primaveral luna llena distribuye amorosa e incesantemente sus balsámicos rayos. 

En ese momento, Mūralīdhara Śhrī Kṛṣṇa, el supremo disfrutador de melosidades nectáreas, comienza la danza rāsa. 

Rodeado de millones de encantadoras pastorcillas, Śrī Hari baila en éxtasis con Rādhā. 

Entonando hermosas canciones, la seductora de Mādhava cautiva las mentes de todas las entidades vivientes. 

Todos los seres móviles e inmóviles son encantados por la casta Rādhā, la cual ha derrotado el orgullo de Chandrāvalī. 

Tras agitar el corazón de Vraja-kiśhora, Rādhārāṇī desaparece del vāsantī-rāsa. 

Bhaktivinoda prevé conflicto. En ausencia de Rādhā, la danza rāsa se ha detenido.

IDX.verses:
varaṇe taḍit, vāsa tārāvalī,

svānanda-sukhada-dhāma 

karpūra sevā, lalitāra gaṇa, 
rādhā jūtheśhvarī hana 
mameśhvarī-nātha, śhrī-nanda-nandana, 
āmāra parāṇa dhana 

śhrī-rūpa mañjarī, prabhṛtira sama, 
yugala sevāya āśha 
avaśhya serūpa, sevā pāba āmi,

IDX.en_translation:
Her complexion is like lightning, her garments are like a constellation of stars, and her name is Kamala Mañjarī. She is an abode of self-bliss and happiness. 

Camphor is in her service; among Lalitā’s associates, Rādhā is the leader of the group. The Lord of my mistress is Śrī-nanda-nandana; He is the treasure of my life. 

Like Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī and other friends, my hope is for the service of the Divine Couple. Certainly I will attain such service; this is my supreme and firm faith. 

When will this maidservant attain spiritual perfection, residing in Rādhā-kuṇḍa? Constantly engaged in the service of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, abandoning all previous memories?

IDX.title: vibhāvarī śheṣa
IDX.search: vibhavari sesa aloka pravesa nidra cḣadi utha jiva bala hari hari mukunda murari rama krsna hayagriva nrsimha vamana sri madhusudana vrajendranandana syama putana ghatana kaitabha satana jaya dasarathi rama yasoda dulala govinda gopala vrndavana purandara gopipriya jana radhika ramana bhuvana sundaravara ravanantakara makhana taskara gopi jana vastrahari vrajera rakhala gopa vrndapala chitta hari vamsi dhari jogindra vandana sri nanda nandana vraja jana bhayahari navina nirada rupa manohara mohana vamsivihari yasoda nandana kamsa nisudana nikunjarasa vilasi kadamba kanana rasa parayana vrndavipina nivasi ananda vardhana prema niketana fulasara yojaka kama gopangana gana chitta vinodana samasta gunagana dhama jamuna jivana keli parayana manasachandra chakora nama sudharasa gao krsna yasa rakha vachana mana mora

IDX.verses:
vibhāvarī-śheṣa, āloka praveśha, 
nidrā cḣāḍi’ uṭha jīva 
bala’ hari hari, mukunda murāri, 
rāma kṛṣṇa hayagrīva 

nṛsiṁha vāmana, śhrī-madhusūdana, 
vrajendranandana śhyāma 
pūtanā-ghātana, kaiṭabha-śhātana, 
jaya dāśharathi-rāma 

yaśhodā-dulāla, govinda-gopāla, 
vṛndāvana-purandara 
gopīpriya-jana, rādhikā-ramaṇa, 
bhuvana-sundaravara 

rāvaṇāntakara, mākhana-taskara, 
gopī-jana-vastrahārī 
vrajera rākhāla, gopa-vṛndapāla, 
chitta-hārī vaṁśhī-dhārī 

jogīndra-vandana, śhrī-nanda-nandana, 
vraja-jana-bhayahārī 
navīna nīrada, rūpa manohara, 
mohana-vaṁśhīvihārī 

yaśhodā-nandana, kaṁsa-nisūdana, 
nikuñjarāsa-vilāsī 
kadamba-kānana, rāsa-parāyaṇa, 
vṛndāvipina-nivāsī 

ānanda-vardhana, prema-niketana, 
fulaśhara-yojaka kāma 
gopāṅganā-gaṇa-, chitta-vinodana, 
samasta-guṇagaṇa-dhāma 

jāmuna-jīvana, keli-parāyaṇa, 
mānasachandra-chakora 
nāma-sudhārasa, gāo kṛṣṇa-yaśha, 
rākha vachana mana mora
IDX.en_translation:
The night ends and light enters; rise up, O soul, and leave your sleep. Chant the names of Hari, Mukunda, Murāri, Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, and Hayagrīva. 

Chant the names of Nṛsiṁha, Vāmana, Śrī Madhusūdana, and Śyāma. All glories to the killer of Pūtanā, the destroyer of Kaiṭabha, and to Rāma, the son of Daśaratha. 

He is Yaśodā’s darling, Govinda, Gopāla, and the Lord of Vṛndāvana. He is the beloved of the gopīs, the lover of Rādhā, and the most beautiful in all the world. 

He is the destroyer of Rāvaṇa, the butter-thief, and the one who stole the clothes of the gopīs. He is the cowherd of Vraja, the protector of the cowherds, the captivator of the mind, and the player of the flute. 

He is worshiped by the great yogis—the son of Nanda who removes the fears of the residents of Vraja. Like a fresh cloud with a charming form, He is the enchanting flute-player. 

He is the son of Yaśodā, the killer of Kaṁsa, and the one who enjoys the rāsa dance in the groves. In the kadamba forest, He is absorbed in the rāsa dance as a resident of the forests of Vṛndāvana. 

He is the enhancer of bliss, the abode of love, and more enchanting than Cupid. He is the enchanter of the minds of the cowherd girls and the abode of all good qualities. 

He is the life of the Yamunā, absorbed in pastimes—the moon for the chakora bird of the mind. O my mind, sing the glories of Kṛṣṇa, the nectar of the Holy Name, and follow these words of mine.
IDX.es_translation:
La noche ha terminado y empieza a brillar la luz (de la aurora). ¡Levántate, oh jīva, y abandona tu sueño! ¡Canta los nombres de Hari, Mukunda, Murāri, Rāma, Kṛṣṇa y Hayagrīva! 

[Canta] Nṛsiṁha, Vāmana, Śhrī Madhusūdana, Vrajendra-nandana y Śhyāma ― el exterminador de Pūtanā y destructor de Kaiṭabha! ¡Toda gloria al Señor Rāma, el hijo del Rey Daśharatha! 

Él es el hijo amado de Yaśhodā y el protector y sustentador de las vacas, sus pastizales, los gopas y las gopīs. Él es el rey de Vṛndāvana, el amado de las gopīs y el consorte de Śhrīmatī Rādhikā. Él es la belleza insuperable del mundo entero. 

Él acabó con la vida de Rāvāṇa, es un ladrón de mantequilla, roba las ropas de las jóvenes gopīs, y es el protector de las vacas de Vraja, el guardián de los gopas y el flautista que cautiva las mentes de todos. 

Él es el objeto de adoración de grandes yoguis, el hermoso hijo de Nanda, el que elimina los temores de los residentes de Vraja y una fresca nube de lluvia. Cuando va de un lado a otro tocando la flauta y seduciendo a todos, Su forma cautiva la mente. 

Él es el amado hijo de Yaśhodā y el heroico aniquilador de Kaṁsa. Lleva a cabo nectáreos pasatiempos en las arboledas de placer de Vraja, disfruta con la danza rāsa en el bosque de kadambas, y reside en el bosque de Vṛndāvana. 

Él incrementa la bienaventuranza y es la morada del prema, y es el Cupido trascendental que dispara flechas de flores [a las gopīs suscitando en ellas deseos trascendentales]. Él da placer a los corazones de las gopīs y es la morada de todas las buenas cualidades. 

Es la vida misma del Yamunā, está absorto en pasatiempos amorosos, y es la luna de la mente de las gopīs, que son como pájaros cakora que subsisten únicamente de los rayos de la luna. ¡Oh, mente! Haz caso de mis palabras y canta las glorias de Kṛṣṇa en la forma de estos santos nombres que están llenos de néctar.

When awakened love becomes active, then external manifestations of emotion arise. Revealing the inner emotions, it creates excellent external transformations, whatever is appropriate at that time. 

Dancing, singing, rolling on the ground, crying loudly, twisting the body, roaring, yawning, heavy breathing, disregard for public opinion, salivation, excessive reeling, hiccups and so on, and loud laughter. 

All born from the body and mind, these “ornaments” are excellent manifestations, declared to be twenty types. One is named “udbhāsvāra”; and disheveling of hair, a radiant scent, and disarray of clothing are other transformations. 

Lamentation, conversation, incoherent talk, repetition, denial, excessive messages, pretense, advice, commands, and indirect references—these are specific types of verbal manifestations.

O friend of the distressed! Whether You punish me or show me mercy, I have no other refuge but You. Even if a hundred million thunderbolts or pure fresh rain should fall, the chataka bird still praises the cloud. 

As I hear of the incomparable and difficult worship of the ancient devotees, my heart—devoid of even a trace of devotion—burns with despair. But upon hearing of Your all-pervading wave of compassion, O remover of sins, this heart, sprinkled with a drop of hope, attains coolness within.

vṛndāvana chintāmaṇi, chidānanda-ratnakhani, 
chinmaya apūrva-daraśhana 
taṁhi mājhe chamatkāra, kṛṣṇa vanaspati-sāra, 
nīlamaṇi tamāla jemana 

tāṅhe eka svarṇamayī, latā sarvadhāma-jayī, 
uṭhiyācḣe paramapāvanī 
hlādinī-śhaktira sāra, ‘mahābhāva’ nāma jā’ra, 
tribhuvanamohana-mohinī 

‘rādhā’-nāme parichita, tuṣiyā govinda-chita, 
virājaye parama-ānande 
sei latā-patra-fula, lalitādi sakhīkula, 
sabe mili’ vṛkṣe dṛḍha bāndhe 

latāra paraśhe prafulla tamāla 
latā cḣāḍi’ nāhi rahe konakāla 

tamāla cḣāḍiyā latā nāhi bāṅche 
se latā-milana sadā-kāla jāche

nā chāhe kakhana vinā kicḣu āra
IDX.en_translation:
On the other side of Virajā river, is the pure transcendental abode. Above that is Śrī Gokula, named the forest of Vṛndāvana. 

Vṛndāvana is a Cintāmaṇi, a mine of transcendental bliss jewels. It is a spiritual, unparalleled vision. Within it is a wonder: Kṛṣṇa is the essence of all trees, like a sapphire-like Tamāla tree. 

Upon Him is a golden creeper, conquering all abodes, risen, supremely purifying. She is the essence of the bliss-giving potency, whose name is Mahābhāva (the highest state of ecstatic love). She is enchanting even the enchanter of the three worlds. 

Known by the name Rādhā, pleasing the heart of Govinda, she shines in supreme bliss. That creeper’s leaves and flowers, the group of confidantes like Lalitā, all together, firmly bind the tree. 

By the touch of the creeper, the Kṛṣṇa tree is joyful. Without the creeper, it cannot exist at any time. 

Without the Tamāla, the creeper cannot survive. That creeper always yearns for union. 

Bhaktivinoda sees their union, and desires nothing else at any time.

viṣaya-vāsanārūpa chittera vikāra 
āmāra hṛdaye bhoga kare anivāra 

kata je jatana āmi karilāma hāya 
nā gela vikāra buddhi śheṣe prāṇa jāya 

e ghora vikāra more karila asthira 
śhānti nā pāila sthāna, antara adhīra 

śhrī-rūpa gosvāmī more kṛpā vitariyā 
uddhāribe kabe jukta-vairāgya arpiyā 

kabe sanātana more cḣāḍāye viṣaya 
nityānande samarpibe hoiyā sadaya 

śhrī-jīva gosvāmī kabe siddhānta-salile 
nibhāibe tarkānala, chitta jāhe jvale 

śhrī-chaitanya-nāma śhune udibe pulaka 
rādhā-kṛṣṇāmṛta-pāne hoiba aśhoka 

kāṅgālera sukāṅgāla durjana e-jana 
vaiṣṇava-charaṇāśhraya jāche akiñchana
IDX.en_translation:
The distortions of the mind in the form of material desires In my heart, they enjoy uncontrollably. 

Alas, how much effort I made! The distorted intelligence did not leave, and finally my life departs. 

These terrible distortions made me restless. Peace found no place, my inner self is agitated. 

When will Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī bestow mercy upon me, and deliver me by offering appropriate renunciation? 

When will Sanātana Gosvāmī free me from material objects, and, becoming merciful, surrender me to Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu? 

When will Śrī Jīva Gosvāmī, with the waters of established philosophical conclusions, extinguish the fire of arguments, in which my mind burns? 

Hearing the name of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu, when will ecstasy arise, and by drinking the nectar of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, when will I become free from sorrow? 

This person is a wicked soul, poorer than the poorest, a humble soul who begs for the shelter of the feet of the devotees of Viṣṇu.
IDX.es_translation:
Mi deseo por los objetos de los sentidos es una obstinación de la conciencia que me impele constantemente a querer disfrutar. 

A pesar de mis ilimitados esfuerzos, esa obsesión malsana no desaparece. Al final, la que se va en lugar de ella es mi vida. 

Este espantoso delirio me causa una gran perturbación. Mi corazón está inquieto, y por eso la paz no halla lugar en él. 

¿Cuándo me concederá su misericordia Śhrilā Rūpa Gosvāmī? ¿Cuándo me liberará impartiéndome el conocimiento del yukta- vairāgya? 

¿Cuándo me mostrará Śhrila Sanātana Gosvāmī su gran compasión haciendo que abandone el disfrute de los sentidos y me ofrecerá a Śhrī Nityānanda Prabhu? 

¿Cuándo verterá Śrilā Jīva Gosvāmī las aguas de la verdad concluyente y extinguirá el fuego de los argumentos falsos que quema mi corazón? 

Entonces, cuando escuche el nombre de Śhrī Chaitanya mis vellos se erizarán, y cuando beba el néctar de Śhrī Śhrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa me liberaré de todas mis lamentaciones. 

Esta alma impenitente suplica que se le conceda el refugio de los pies de loto de los vaiṣṇavas.
