IDX.verses: viṣaye sakale matta, nāhi kṛṣṇa-nāma-tattva, bhaktiśhūnya hoila avanī kalikāla-sarpaviṣe, dagdha jīva mithyā-rase, nā jānaye kebā se āpani nija kanyā-putrotsave, mātiyā ācḣaye sabe, nāhi anya śhubha karmaleśha jakṣa pūje madya-māṁse, nānārūpa jīva hiṁse, ei mata haila sarva-deśha dekhiyā karuṇā kari’, ‘kama-lākṣa’ nāma dhari’, avatīrṇa hailā gauḍadeśhe vraja-rāja-kumāra, sāṅgopāṅga avatāra, karāiba ei abhilāṣe sarva āge āguyāna, jīvere kariyā trāṇa, śhāntipure hoilā prakāśha sakala duṣkṛti jā’be, sabe kṛṣṇa-nāma pā’be, kahe dīna vaiṣṇavera dāsa
IDX.en_translation:
Everyone is intoxicated by material sense objects and knows nothing of the truth of the Holy Name of Kṛṣṇa. The entire world has become devoid of devotion. Bitten by the poisonous snake of Kali-yuga, living entities are scorched by the false tastes of illusion, and they do not even know who they really are. 

Everyone is busy celebrating the festivals of their own sons and daughters, and there is not even a trace of any other auspicious activity. They worship demons with meat and wine and commit violence against various living beings. This is the condition throughout the land. 

Seeing this and feeling great compassion, Lord Kṛṣṇa, assuming the name “Kamalākṣa” (the Lotus-eyed One), descended in the land of Gauḍa. His only desire was to cause the Prince of Vraja to incarnate along with all His associates. 

Taking the lead before everyone else to deliver the living entities, He manifested Himself in Śāntipura. Vaiṣṇava Dāsa says: “All sins will now be destroyed, and everyone will receive the Holy Name of Kṛṣṇa.”

vairāgī haiyā kare jihvāra lālasa 
paramārtha jāya, āra haya rasera vaśha 

vairāgī karibe sadā nāma-saṅkīrtana 
śhāka-patra-fala-mūle udara bharaṇa 

jihvāra lālase jei samāje veḍāya 
śhiśhnodara-parāyaṇa kṛṣṇa nāhi pāya 

vairāgī bhāi grāmyakathā nā śhunibe kāṇe 
grāmyavārtā nā kahibe jave milibe āne 

svapaneo nā kara bhāi strī-sambhāṣaṇa 
gṛhe strī cḣāḍiyā bhāi āsiyācḣa vana 

jadi chāha praṇaya rākhite gaurāṅgera sane 
cḣoṭa haridāsera kathā thāke jena mane 

bhāla nā khāibe, āra bhāla nā paribe 
hṛdayete rādhā-kṛṣṇa sarvadā sevibe 

baḍa hari-dāsera nyāya kṛṣṇa-nāma balibe vadane 
aṣṭa-kāla rādhā-kṛṣṇa sevibe kuñja-vane
IDX.en_translation:
A pure renunciant performs the congregational chanting of the Holy Names. He maintains his life only by eating what he receives through begging. 

If a renunciant depends on others for his needs, his purpose is not achieved, and Lord Kṛṣṇa neglects him. 

If a renunciant indulges the desires of his tongue, his spiritual goal is lost, and he becomes a slave to material tastes. 

A renunciant should always perform the congregational chanting. He should fill his belly only with vegetables, leaves, fruits, and roots. 

One who wanders through society just to satisfy the desires of the tongue, being dedicated only to his stomach and genitals, will never attain Lord Kṛṣṇa. 

O renunciant brother! Do not let mundane talk enter your ears. Do not speak of worldly news when you meet others. 

O brother! Do not even converse with women in your dreams. Remember, you have left your wife at home to come to the forest of renunciation. 

If you wish to maintain your love for Lord Gaurāṅga, then always keep the story of Choṭa Haridāsa in your mind. 

Do not eat palatable foods, and do not wear fine clothes. Always serve Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa within your heart. 

Like the senior Haridāsa Ṭhākura, always chant the Holy Names of Kṛṣṇa. During all eight periods of the day, serve Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in the groves of Vṛndāvana.

IDX.verses: viśhve udita, nāma-tapana, avidyā-vināśha lāgi’ cḣoḍata saba, māyā-vibhava, sādhu tāhe anurāgī harināma-prabhākara, avidyā-timirahara, tomāra mahimā kebā jāne ke hena paṇḍitajana, tomāra māhātmyagaṇa, uccḣaiḥsvare sakala bākhāne tomāra ābhāsa pahilahi bhāya e bhava-timira kavalitaprāya achire timira nāśhiyā prajñāna tattvāndha-nayane karena vidhāna sei ta’ prajñāna viśhuddhā bhakati upajāya hari-viṣayiṇī mati e adbhutalīlā satata tomāra bhakativinoda jāniyācḣe sāra
IDX.en_translation:
Risen in the world, the sun of the Holy Name destroys ignorance. Giving up all the opulence of illusion, the saintly soul becomes devoted to it. 

O Holy Name of Hari! You are the sun, the dispeller of the darkness of ignorance. Who indeed knows Your glory? What learned person can recount Your many glories and proclaim them all in a loud voice? 

Your glimmer first appears, and the darkness of this material existence is almost swallowed. 

Quickly destroying the darkness, supreme knowledge bestows sight upon the eyes that were blind to reality. 

That supreme knowledge is indeed pure devotion, which awakens an awakens an inclination focused on the Lord. 

This wonderful pastime is always Yours; Bhaktivinoda has understood its essence.

IDX.en_translation:
Vraja-dhāma is the eternal wealth, the two persons Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, Who have become one body absorbed in divine pastimes. Along with their abode, they have appeared in Gauḍa-deśa, Bringing their own eternal associates with them. 

O mind, know this as the absolute truth: In Navadvīpa, Gaura-hari, performing nāma-saṅkīrtana, Distributed the nectar of prema throughout Gauḍa. 

Under the pretext of sannyāsa, that same Hari in Nīlācala, Is Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, the master of ascetics. Taking Dāmodara and Rāmānanda, feeling supreme bliss, He revealed deep confidential truths in great detail. 

Teaching those truths and the ultimate goal to Raghunātha, He sent him to the presence of Śrī Rūpa. Śrī Dāsa Gosvāmī in Vraja, worshipping Kṛṣṇa with Rūpa, Has written the verses of “Manaḥ-śikṣā.” 

To be the servant of the servant of those whose hope is great, This Bhaktivinoda is most humble and possesses nothing. He sings this “Manaḥ-śikṣā Bhāṣā” wherever pure devotees are found, May they mercifully grant him a hearing.

IDX.en_translation:
Rādhā-Śyām, Śyāmā-Śyām! You give happiness to the minds of the people of Vraja. 

Peacock-feather crown, shark-shaped earrings, Vaijayantī garland around the neck. Sweet ankle-bells on the feet. Rādhā-Śyām, Śyāmā-Śyām! 

Beautiful face, eyes like lotus petals, Your crooked glance is captivating. Enchanting player of the flute. Rādhā-Śyām, Śyāmā-Śyām! 

Grazing cows in Vṛndāvana, stealing the minds of the gopīs. Holder of Śrī Govardhana. Rādhā-Śyām, Śyāmā-Śyām! 

Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, both have now met, incarnating as the Golden Form (Gaura). Preaching the religion of kīrtana. Rādhā-Śyām, Śyāmā-Śyām! 

Without You, I have no one else; the Name and Form are the Avatāra. I surrender at Your feet; Nārāyaṇa (Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī) surrenders. Rādhā-Śyām, Śyāmā-Śyām!

Whoever worships the son of the King of Vraja, their life is successful. There is no equal to them mentioned in the Vedas, and in the three worlds there is no other. 

If a human does not worship such a Lord, when they die, that wretched person will be struck by the lord of death, and worms in a hellish planet will consume them. 

Thereafter, the sinner will find no release in the material world. For them, there is never any progress or destination; they are uselessly wandering in their activities. 

Śrī Locana dāsa, hoping for devotion, speaks and writes the glories of Hari. I do not even wish to see the face of one who does not have the intelligence to appreciate such essential nectar.
IDX.es_translation:
Quien adora a Śhrī Vrajendra-nandana ha alcanzado el éxito en su vida. No hay nadie como Él en todos los Vedas o en los tres mundos. 

Quien no adora a Śhrī Mādhava morirá un día. Castigado por Yamarāja, esa persona abominable será comida por gusanos e insectos en el infierno llamado Raurava. 

No hay pecador más grande que él en el universo. Esa persona nunca podrá alcanzar la liberación; en lugar de ello, vaga inutilmente. 

Śhrī Lochana dāsa describe las cualidades de Śhrī Hari con el deseo de obtener bhakti y no mira jamás el rostro de la persona cuya mente no está fija en la esencia de todo el rasa, Śhrī Vrajendra-nandana.

vṛndāvane viharatoriha kelikuñje 
matta-dvipa-pravara-kautuka-vibhrameṇa 
sandarśhayasva juvayorvadanāravinda- 
dvandvaṁ vidhehi mayi devi! kṛpāṁ prasīda 

hā devi! kāku-bhara-gadgada-jāḍya vāchā 
jāche nipatya bhuvi daṇḍavadudbhaṭārtiḥ 
asya prasādamabudhasya janasya kṛtvā 
gāndharvike! nijagaṇe gaṇanāṁ vidhehi 

śhyāme! ramā-ramaṇa-sundaratā-variṣṭha- 
saundarya-mohita-samasta-jagajjanasya 
śhyāmasya vāma-bhuja-baddhatanuṁ kadāhaṁ

tvāṁ praccḣadena mudira-ccḣavinā pidhāya 
mañjīra-mukta-charaṇāñcha vidhāya devi! 
kuñje vrajendra-tanayena virājamāne 
naktaṁ kadā pramuditāmabhisārayiṣye? 

kuñje prasūna-kula-kalpita-keli-talpe 
saṁviṣṭayor-madhura-narma-vilāsa-bhājoḥ 
loka-trayābharaṇayośhcharaṇāmbujāni 
samvāhayiṣyati kadā juvayorjano‛yam? 

tvat-kuṇḍa-rodhasi vilāsa-pariśhrameṇa 
svedāmbu-chumbi-vadanāmburuha-śhriyau vām 
vṛndāvaneśhvari! kadā taru-mūla-bhājau 
samvījayāmi chamarī-chaya-chāmareṇa? 

līnāṁ nikuñja-kuhare bhavatīṁ mukunde 
chitraiva sūchitavatī ruchirākṣi! nāham 
bhugnāṁ bhruvaṁ na rachayeti mṛṣā-ruṣāṁ tvā- 
magre vrajendra-tanayasya kadā nu neṣye? 

vāgyuddha-keli-kutuke vraja-rāja-sūnuṁ 
jitvonmadāmadhika-darpa-vikāsi-jalpām 
fullābhir-ālibhir-analpam-udīryamāṇa- 
stotrāṁ kadā nu bhavatīmavalokayiṣye? 

jaḥ ko‛pi suṣṭhu vṛṣabhānu-kumārikāyāḥ 
samprārthanāṣṭakam-idaṁ paṭhati prapannaḥ

IDX.en_translation:
O Devi! Be pleased! Bestow mercy upon me! Show me the pair of lotus faces of You two sporting here in the play-groves of Vṛndāvana with the playful movements of the best of intoxicated elephants. 

Alas, O Devi! With a voice choked with the weight of piteous words, falling on the ground like a stick, I beg with intense distress: making this ignorant person an object of Your mercy, O Gāndharvikā, count me among Your own people. 

O Śyāmā! When will I worship You, whose body is bound by the left arm of Śyāma, who has enchanted all the people of the universe with a beauty superior to the beauty of the Husband of Ramā (Viṣṇu), and who possesses a wealth of form rare even for Indirā? 

O Devi! Covering You with a cloth of the color of a cloud and removing the anklets from Your feet, when will I joyfully make You go on a tryst at night in the bower where the Son of the King of Vraja is shining? 

When will this person massage the lotus feet of You two, the ornaments of the three worlds, who are seated on a play-bed made of multitudes of flowers in the bower and enjoying sweet, joking pastimes? 

O Queen of Vṛndāvana! When will I fan You two with a yak-tail whisk, seated at the root of a tree on the bank of Your Kuṇḍa, Your lotus faces kissing the drops of sweat from the fatigue of pastimes? 

O beautiful-eyed one! You are hiding in the hollow of a bower with Mukunda. “Citra herself indicated it; not I!”—when will I lead You, who are thus feigning anger with knitted eyebrows, before the Son of the King of Vraja? 

When will I see You, having conquered the Son of the King of Vraja in the curiosity of a war of words, intoxicated with pride, with speech expanding with great arrogance, being praised profusely by the blooming friends? 

Whoever surrenders and recites this prayer of eight verses to the Daughter of Vṛṣabhānu nicely, She, meeting with Her Beloved and holding joy, accepts a wave of mercy towards him.
IDX.es_translation:
Tú y Śhrī Kṛṣṇa disfrutan constantemente Sus pasatiempos amorosos en los bosques de placer de Śhrī Vṛndāvana, embelesados como dos elefantes embriagados. ¡Oh, Devī!, complácete conmigo y concédeme misericordiosamente el darśhana de Sus rostros de loto. 

¡Oh, Devī Gāndharvikā! Completamente abatido, me arrojo al suelo como una vara y, orando a Tus pies de loto con voz trémula y desesperada, Te imploro que seas misericordiosa con este necio y lo consideres Tuyo. 

¡Oh Śhyāmā! La belleza de Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa encanta al mundo entero, pero Tu belleza cuando Śhyāma Te abraza con Su brazo izquierdo es supremamente excelsa. ¿Cuándo podré adorarte a Ti, cuya belleza sin par supera incluso la de Lakṣmī-devī? 

¡Oh, Devī! ¿Cuándo Te cubriré con una prenda del color de una nube de lluvia, quitaré las campanillas tobilleras de Tus pies y Te conduciré llena de gozo a un maravilloso kuñja para un encuentro nocturno con Śhrī Nanda-nandana? 

Dentro del kuñja, en una cama hecha de diversos tipos de flores, Tú y Tu amado disfrutan de dulces y jubilosos pasatiempos. ¿Cuándo masajeará esta persona [entonces] Tus pies de loto que son el ornamento de los tres mundos? 

¡Oh Vṛndāvaneśhvari! Tras el esfuerzo de los juegos amorosos a orillas de Tu estanque, gotas de sudor acarician Tu rostro y el de Tu amado. ¿Cuándo abanicaré Sus cuerpos con una cāmara mientras Se sientan [a descansar] bajo la sombra de un árbol? 

¡Oh, Rādhikā de hermosos ojos! “Fue Chitra, no yo, quien reveló a Mukunda Tu escondite dentro del kuñja. No frunzas el ceño y Te enojes injustamente conmigo.”¿Cuándo Te apaciguaré así en presencia de Vrajendra-nandana? 

Cuando derrotas a Vrajendra-nandana en una batalla verbal, Te sientes inmensamente dichosa. Mientras Te regocijas con orgullo del poder de Tu oratoria, Tus encantadas sakhīs Te alaban. ¿Cuándo Te contemplaré en ese estado? 

Con las olas de Su misericordia, Śhrī Vṛabhānu-nandini Śhrī Rādhikā junto con Su amado Śhrī Kṛṣṇa Se sienten complacidos con la persona plenamente rendida que recita este Gāndharvā-samprārtanāṣtamkam con fe, y la consideran Suya.

vṛṣabha-danuja-nāśhān-antaraṁ jat sva-goṣṭhīm 
ayasi vṛṣabha-śhatro mā spṛśha tvaṁ vadantyām 
iti vṛṣa-ravi-putryāṁ kṛṣṇa-pārṣṇiṁ prakhātaṁ 
tad ati-vimala-nīraṁ śhyāma-kuṇḍaṁ gatir me 

tri-jagati nivasad jat tīrtha-vṛndaṁ tamoghnaṁ 
vraja-nṛpati-kumāreṇāhṛtaṁ tat samagram 
svayam idam avagāḍhaṁ jan mahimnaḥ prakāśhaṁ

jad ati-vimala-nīre tīrtha-rūpe praśhaste 
tvam api kuru kṛśhāṅgi! snānam atraiva rādhe 
iti vinaya-vachobhiḥ prārthanā-kṛt sa kṛṣṇas 
tad ati-vimala-nīraṁ śhyāma-kuṇḍaṁ gatir me 

vṛṣabha-danuja-nāśhād uttha-pāpaṁ samāptaṁ 
dyumaṇi-sakha-jayoccḣair varjayitveti tīrthaṁ 
nijam akhila-sakhībhiḥ kuṇḍam eva prakāśhyaṁ 
tad ati-vimala-nīraṁ śhyāma-kuṇḍaṁ gatir me 

jad ati sakala-tīrthais tyakta-vākyaiḥ prabhītaiḥ 
sa-vinayam abhiyuktaiḥ kṛṣṇa-chandre nivedya 
agatika-gati-rādhā varjanān no gatiḥ kā 
tad ati-vimala-nīraṁ śhyāma-kuṇḍaṁ gatir me 

jad ati-vikala-tīrthaṁ kṛṣṇa-chandraṁ prasusthaṁ 
ati-laghu-nati-vākyaiḥ suprasanneti rādhā 
vividha-chaṭula-vākyaiḥ prārthanāḍhyā bhavantī 
tad ati-vimala-nīraṁ śhyāma-kuṇḍaṁ gatir me 

jad ati-lalita-pādais tāṁ prasādyāpta-tair thyais 
tad atiśhaya-kṛpārdraiḥ saṅgamena praviṣṭaiḥ 
vraja-nava-yuva-rādhā-kuṇḍam eva prapannaṁ 
tad ati-vimala-nīraṁ śhyāma-kuṇḍaṁ gatir me 

jad ati-nikaṭa-tīre klapta-kuñjaṁ suramyaṁ 
subala-baṭu-mukhebhyo rādhikādyaiḥ pradattam 
vividha-kusuma-vallī-kalpa-vṛkṣādi-rājaṁ 
tad ati-vimala-nīraṁ śhyāma-kuṇḍaṁ gatir me 

paripaṭhati sumedhāḥ śhyāma-kuṇḍāṣṭakaṁ jo 
nava-jaladhara-rūpe svarṇa-kāntyāṁ cha rāgāt 
vraja-narapati-putras tasya labhyaḥ suśhīghraṁ 
saha sa-gaṇa-sakhībhī rādhayā syāt subhajyaḥ
IDX.en_translation:
After the slaying of the bull demon, when Rādhā told Lord Kṛṣṇa, “O enemy of the bull! Do not touch Me!”, Kṛṣṇa dug this pond with His heel. That very pure water of Śyāma-kuṇḍa is my refuge. 

All the holy places in the three worlds that destroy darkness were brought together by the Prince of Vraja. He personally immersed Himself in this pond, whose glories are now manifest. That very pure water of Śyāma-kuṇḍa is my refuge. 

Lord Kṛṣṇa, with humble words, requested Rādhā: “O slender-limbed one! O Rādhā! Please take a bath here in this pure water, which is praised as a holy place.” That very pure water of Śyāma-kuṇḍa is my refuge. 

Any sin arising from the slaying of the bull demon was considered finished by Lord Kṛṣṇa after He bathed here. But Rādhā, having victoriously rejected this holy place, manifested Her own pond along with all Her friends. That very pure water of Śyāma-kuṇḍa is my refuge. 

When all other holy places, terrified and speechless, humbly approached the moon-like Kṛṣṇa and submitted: “If Rādhā, the refuge of the helpless, avoids us, then what refuge do we have?”, the Lord showed His mercy. That very pure water of Śyāma-kuṇḍa is my refuge. 

When the other holy places were extremely distressed and Lord Kṛṣṇa was present, Rādhā became greatly pleased by their very humble words and prostrations, and then She Herself became rich with various playful prayers to the Lord. That very pure water of Śyāma-kuṇḍa is my refuge. 

Having pleased Her with their humble approach, all the holy places obtained Her own pond. They entered with excessive mercy, gathered together, and took refuge in the pond of the youthful Rādhā of Vraja. That very pure water of Śyāma-kuṇḍa is my refuge. 

On its nearby bank, charming groves are arranged. These groves were given to Subala and the Lord’s other friends by Śrīmati Rādhikā and Her companions. It is a royal place, abounding with various flowers, creepers, and desire trees. That very pure water of Śyāma-kuṇḍa is my refuge. 

Whoever, being intelligent, recites these eight verses in praise of Śyāma-kuṇḍa with love for Him who is like a fresh cloud and for Her with golden effulgence, quickly attains the Son of the King of Vraja. He will become worshipable by Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa and Their gopī companions.

vṛṣabha-danuja-nāśhān narma-dharmokti-raṅgair 
nikhila-nija-sakhībhir jat sva-hastena pūrṇam 
prakaṭitam api vṛndāraṇya-rājñyā pramodais 
tad ati-surabhi-rādhā-kuṇḍam evāśhrayo me 

vraja-bhuvi mura-śhatroḥ preyasīnāṁ nikāmair 
asulabham api tūrṇaṁ prema-kalpa-drumaṁ tam 
janayati hṛdi bhūmau snātur uccḣaiḥ priyaṁ jat

praṇaya-sura-latā syāt tasya goṣṭhendra-sūnoḥ 
sapadi kila mad-īśhā-dāsya-puṣpa-praśhasyā 
tad ati-surabhi-rādhā-kuṇḍam evāśhrayo me

tad ati-surabhi-rādhā-kuṇḍam evāśhrayo me 

avikalam ati devyāśh chāru kuṇḍāṣṭakaṁ jaḥ 
paripaṭhati tadīyollāsi-dāsyārpitātmā

IDX.en_translation:
After the slaying of the bull demon, when Rādhā and Her gopī friends filled this pond with Their own hands after a playful dispute with Lord Kṛṣṇa, and even though it was manifested with great joy by the Queen of Vṛndāvana herself—that extremely fragrant Rādhā-kuṇḍa alone is my refuge. 

In the sacred land of Vraja, for the dearest beloveds of Lord Kṛṣṇa, this pond quickly generates the desire-tree of divine love in the heart of anyone who bathes here. To that soul it is exceedingly dear. That extremely fragrant Rādhā-kuṇḍa alone is my refuge. 

Even the enemy of the Agha demon, Lord Kṛṣṇa, intensely desires to attain the merciful side-long glance of Śrīmati Rādhā-rāṇī here and eagerly follows Her while performing the service of bathing. That extremely fragrant Rādhā-kuṇḍa alone is my refuge. 

This is intensely the land of love for the moon of Vraja, Lord Kṛṣṇa, and it is as dear to Him as the crown-jewel of the gopīs herself. Even though known by Her Name, it is intimately connected to Her. That extremely fragrant Rādhā-kuṇḍa alone is my refuge. 

If any person here, by the grace of serving this pond, may quickly have the creeper of divine love for the Son of Nanda Mahārāja manifest in his heart—service which is praised as the flower of devotion to my Mistress. That extremely fragrant Rādhā-kuṇḍa alone is my refuge. 

The sweet groves on its banks, given beautiful names by Her own associates, are divided and sheltered by them. These groves are charming with the humming of bees and shine with desirable features. That extremely fragrant Rādhā-kuṇḍa alone is my refuge. 

On the beautiful platform on its bank, the Mistress reveals sweet and charming topics concerning the moon of Vraja among Her dearest friends. That extremely fragrant Rādhā-kuṇḍa alone is my refuge. 

Daily, with great delight and accompanied by the gopīs who are intoxicated with love, the Divine Couple sports here in the captivating waters filled with the fragrance of lotuses. That extremely fragrant Rādhā-kuṇḍa alone is my refuge. 

Whoever flawlessly recites these eight verses about the beautiful pond of the Goddess, with a soul dedicated to Her joyful service—the enemy of Madhu will very soon, even in this very body, reveal to him his Beloved Rādhā as He embraces Her with great joy.

The daughter of Vṛṣabhānu, newly filled with love, quickly set out for Her secret meeting. Her cheerful companions, like waves of love, emerged from the palace. 

As Her feet moved, Her anklets jingled, producing a very sweet and charming sound. With a swan-like gait, that delightful Lady arrived, accompanied by Her friends. 

The playful and clever Lord Kṛṣṇa, the crest-jewel of the wise, quickly met the Lady by Her side. As They both gazed upon each other, Their eyes shone with joy, as observed by Govinda Dāsa.

For serving the Feet Of the Daughter of Vṛṣabhānu I shall be Her protected maid; To serve constantly The pleasures of Sree Rādhā Shall be my endeavour. 

The Pleasure of Krishna By Sree Radha’s Happiness I shall experience in my mind; Abandoning Radha’s Feet To seek my union with Sree Krishna Shall never be my desire. 

The sakhīs are My best friends, Teachers of love frr the Divine Pair; By following their example I shall serve The Purpose-Tree of the Feet of Radha 

Whoever the person, Whatever his ways, Who breaks away from Rādhā, Myself who am Rādhā’s constant partisan Shall never brook his sight.
IDX.es_translation:
Para servir los pies de loto de la hija del rey Vṛsabhānu, me convertiré en Su sirvienta (pālya-dāsī) y me esforzaré siempre por hacerla feliz. 

Comprenderé en mi corazón el placer que Kṛṣṇa saborea con la felicidad de Śhrī Rādhā. Jamás abandonaré Sus pies de loto ni desearé disfrutar separadamente con Śhrī Kṛṣṇa. 

Las sakhīs son mis bienquerientes y gurus supremas en lo concerniente a los asuntos amorosos de la Pareja Divina. Siguiendo fielmente sus indicaciones, serviré los pies de loto de Śrī Rādhā, que son como árboles de los deseos. 

Quienes no se hallan dentro del séquito de Śhrī Rādhā pueden quedarse como están. Yo soy siempre parcial a Rādhikā y no considero a quienes no lo son.

IDX.verses: (yadi) gaurāṅga nahita, tabe ki hoita, kemane dharita de? rādhāra mahimā, premarasa-sīmā, jagate jānāta ke madhura vṛndā-, vipina-mādhurī-, praveśha chāturī-sāra varaja-yuvatī-, bhāvera bhakati, śhakati hoita kā’ra gāo punaḥ punaḥ, gaurāṅgera guṇa, sarala hoiyā mana e bhava-sāgare, emana dayāla, nā dekhi je ekajana gaurāṅga baliyā, nā genu galiyā, kemane dharinu de narahari-hiyā, pāṣāṇa diyā, kemane gaḍiyācḣe
IDX.en_translation:
If there were no Gaurāṅga, then what would have happened? How would I maintain my body? Who would have told the world about the glories of Rādhā and the limit of the rasa of love? 

The sweetness of the forest of sweet Vṛndā, the essence of the skill to enter it, the devotion of the mood of the damsels of Vraja—whose power would there be (to know this)? 

Sing again and again the qualities of Gaurāṅga, keeping the mind simple. In this ocean of material existence, I do not see even one person as merciful as Him. 

Saying “Gaurāṅga”, I did not melt; how have I maintained my body? Narahari’s heart—how has the Creator fashioned it with stone?
IDX.es_translation:
Si Śhrī Gaurāṅga no hubiera aparecido, ¿qué hubiera sido de nosotros? ¿Cómo hubiéramos sobrevivido? ¿Quién hubiera presentado al mundo las glorias de Śhrīmatī Rādhārāṇī y el pináculo del prema-rasa? 

¿Quién hubiera tenido la comprensión real para adentrarse en el dulce embeleso del bosque de Vṛndā-devī y la capacidad de rendir servicio devocional con los sentimientos de las doncellas de Vraja? 

Con un corazón sencillo, canta siempre las gloriosas cualidades de Gaurāṅga. No puedo ver a una sola persona tan compasiva como Él en este océano de la existencia material. 

Aunque canto ‘Gaurāṅga’, mi corazón no se ha derretido. ¿Por qué sigo manteniendo este cuerpo? ¿Cómo fue creado Narahari con una piedra en lugar de un corazón?

IDX.verses: yamunā-puline, kadamba-kānane, ki herinu sakhi! āja śhyāma vaṁśhī-dhārī, maṇi-mañchopari, kare līlā rasa-rāja kṛṣṇa-keli sudhā-prasravaṇa aṣṭa-dalopari, śhrī-rādhā śhrī-hari, aṣṭa-sakhī parijana sugīta-nartane, saba sakhī-gaṇe, tuṣicḣe yugala-dhane kṛṣṇa-līlā heri’, prakṛti sundarī, bistāricḣe śhobhā vane ghare nā jāiba, vane praveśhiba, o līlā-rasera tare tyaji’ kula-lāja, bhaja vraja-rāja, vinoda minati kare’
IDX.en_translation:
On the banks of the Yamunā, in a kadamba forest—what did I see today, my friend! Śyāma, the flute-holder, upon a jeweled platform, performs His pastimes as the King of Mellows. 

Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes are a fountain of nectar. Upon an eight-petaled lotus are Śrī Rādhā and Śrī Hari, with their eight principal companions as attendants. 

With beautiful singing and dancing, all the companions please the Divine Couple. Seeing Kṛṣṇa’s pastimes, beautiful nature spreads its splendor through the forest. 

I will not go home; I will enter the forest for the sake of those pastimes and their nectar. Giving up family honor, worship the King of Vraja—this is Bhaktivinoda’s humble prayer.
IDX.es_translation:
¡Oh sakhī! ¡No sabes lo que vi hoy! En un bosquecillo de kadambas en la ribera del Yamunā, un hermoso y negruzco flautista sentado en una plataforma incrustada de joyas realiza pasatiempos como el rey del rasa. 

Los pasatiempos amorosos de Śhrī Kṛṣṇa son como una cascada de néctar. En los ocho pétalos [del trono enjoyado] se encuentran Sri Rādhā y Śhrī Hari rodeados por Sus asistentes, las ocho sakhīs principales. 

Con sus canciones y su artística danza, las sakhīs complacen a su reverenciada Pareja Divina. Contemplando los pasatiempos de Kṛṣṇa, la hermosa energía espiritual difunde el esplendor del bosque de Vṛndāvana. 

Para saborear el néctar de esos pasatiempos, no regresaré a casa, sino que permaneceré en el bosque. Renuncia a la timidez derivada del temor a la familia y la sociedad, y simplemente adora al rey de Vraja. Esta es la humilde petición de Bhaktivinoda.

IDX.author: sacchidānanda bhaktivinoda ṭhākura
IDX.verses: yaśhomatī-nandana, vraja-vara-nāgara, gokula-rañjana kāna gopī-parāṇadhana, madana-manohara, kālīya-damana-vidhāna amala harināma amiya-vilāsā vipina-purandara, navīna-nāgara-vara, vaṁśhī-vadana, suvāsā vraja-jana-pālana, asura-kula-nāśhana, nanda-godhana-rākhowālā govinda, mādhava, navanīta-taskara, sundara nanda-gopālā yāmuna-taṭa-chara, gopī-vasana-hara, rāsa-rasika kṛpāmaya śhrī-rādhā-vallabha, vṛndāvana-naṭavara, bhakativinoda-āśhraya
IDX.en_translation:
The son of Yaśomatī, the chief lover of Vraja, Kṛṣṇa, who delights Gokula. The wealth of the gopīs’ lives, the enchanter of Cupid, and the subduer of the serpent Kāliya. 

Pure Harināma is a nectarine pastime. He is the Lord of the forests, the ever-fresh supreme lover, the flute-player adorned with beautiful garments. 

The protector of the people of Vraja, the destroyer of the demon dynasty, and the protector of Nanda’s cows. He is Govinda, Mādhava, the butter thief, and the beautiful cowherd boy of Nanda. 

He roams on the banks of the Yamunā, stole the garments of the gopīs, and enjoys the rāsa dance, full of mercy. He is the beloved of Śrī Rādhā, the supreme dancer of Vṛndāvana, and the shelter of Bhaktivinoda.
IDX.es_translation:
Kṛṣṇa es el amado hijo de Madre Yaśhodā, el héroe supremo de Vraja, el deleite de Gokula y Kāna [apodo afectuoso de Kṛṣṇa]. Él es el tesoro de la vida de las gopīs, el encantador de Cupido y quien castiga a la serpiente Kālīya. 

Estos inmaculados y sagrados nombres están infundidos con los dulces pasatiempos de Kṛṣṇa. Él es el rey de los bosques de Vraja y el amante eternamente lozano. Viste atuendos muy hermosos y sostiene una flauta en Su boca. 

Él sustenta a los residentes de Vraja, destruye a multitud de demonios y cuida el rebaño de vacas de Nanda Mahārāja. Él es Govinda (el que da placer a las vacas, a los gopas y a las gopīs) y Mādhava (el consorte de la suprema Lakṣmī). Es un ladrón de mantequilla y el hermoso pastorcillo de Nanda. 

Él pasea por las riberas del río Yamunā, roba las ropas de las jóvenes gopīs y disfruta de rasa en la danza rāsa. Está lleno de misericordia, es el amado de Srīmatī Rādhikā, el bailarín más experto de Vṛndavāna y el refugio de Bhaktivinoda.

yat-kiṅkarīṣu bahuśhaḥ khalu kāku-vāṇī 
nityaṁ parasya puruṣasya śhikhaṇḍa-mauleḥ 
tasyāḥ kadā rasa-nidher vṛṣabhānu-jāyās 
tat-keli-kuñja-bhavanāṅgana-marjanī syām 

yo brahma-rudra-śhuka-nārada-bhīṣma-mukhyair 
ālakṣito na sahasā puruṣasya tasya 
sadyo-vaśhī-karaṇa-chūrṇam ananta-śhaktiṁ 
taṁ rādhikā-charaṇa-reṇum anusmarāmi 

yasyāḥ kadāpi vasanāñchala-khelanottha- 
dhanyāti-dhanya-pavanena kṛtārtha-mānī 
yogīndra-durgama-gatir madhusūdano ‘pi 
tasyā namo ‘stu vṛṣabhānu-bhuvo diśhe ‘pi 

pādābjayos tava vinā vara-dāsyam eva 
nānyat kadāpi samaye kila devi yāche 
sākhyāya te mama namo ‘stu namo ‘stu nityaṁ 
dāsyāya te mama raso ‘stu raso ‘stu satyam 

hā devi kāku-bhara-gadgadayādya vāchā 
yāche nipatya bhuvi daṇḍavad udbhaṭārtiḥ 
asya prasādam abudhasya janasya kṛtvā 
gāndharvike nija-gaṇe gaṇanāṁ vidhehi 

anāradhya rādhā-padāmbhoja-reṇum 
anāśhritya vṛndāṭavīṁ tat-padāṅkam 
asambhāṣya tad-bhāva-gambhīra-chittān 
kutaḥ śhyāma-sindho rasasyāvagāhaḥ 

bhajāmi rādhām aravinda-netrāṁ 
smarāmi rādhāṁ madhura-smitāsyām 
vadāmi rādhāṁ karuṇa-bharārdrāṁ 
tato mamānyāsti gatir na kāpi 

mahā-bhāva-svarūpā tvaṁ 
kṛṣṇa-priyā-varīyasi 
prema-bhakti-prade devi 
rādhike tvāṁ namāmy aham 

rādhe vṛndāvanādhīśhe 
karuṇāmṛta-vāhini 
kṛpayā nija-pādābja- 
dāsyaṁ mahyaṁ pradīyatām 

vande nanda-vraja-strīṇāṁ 
pāda-reṇum abhīkṣṇaśhaḥ 
yāsāṁ hari-kathodgītaṁ 
punāti bhuvana-trayam 

tavaivāsmi tavaivāsmi 
na jīvāmi tvayā vinā 
iti vijñāya devi tvaṁ 
naya māṁ charaṇāntikam
IDX.translation_intro: Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja chose these ślokas and arranged them into: Rādhā-tattva, Kṛṣṇa-tattva, and Gaura-tattva.
IDX.en_translation:
“Oh Rādhikā! The Supreme Enjoyer who wears a crown of peacock feathers, falls at the feet of Your maidservants and propitiates them with many humble and grief-stricken words to be allowed entrance into Your kuñja [where both of You engage in playful amorous pastimes]. Let me become just one stick in the broom used by Your female companions to clean the kuñja of that ocean of rasa, the daughter of Vrisabhanu Maharaja.” 
(Rādhā Rasa Sudha Nidhi 8—Śrī Prabhodhananda Sarasvatī) 

“Following in the footsteps of our previous Acharyas, I meditate upon the footdust of Śrīmati Rādhikā, whose unlimited power instantly controls the Supreme Person Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who is not easily seen even by great souls like Brahma, Shiva, Sukadeva, Narada Muni and Bhishma.” 
(Rādhā Rasa Sudha Nidhi 4—Śrī Prabhodhananda Sarasvatī) 

“When He feels the occasional waft of the supremely glorious and playful breeze that has raised the hem of Śrīmati Rādhikā’s garment, Madhusudana Kṛṣṇa, the instigator of honey-flavoured pastimes, whose service is the rarely attained goal of great yogis, considers that His life has become meaningful. Thus, let us bow down even to the direction of the land of Vrishabhanu Maharaja.” 
(Rādhā Rasa Sudha Nidhi 2—Śrī Prabhodhananda Sarasvatī) 

“Oh Goddess Rādhike! My solemn vow is that I shall never beg for anything except that most exalted direct service to Your lotus feet. I offer my constant obeisances to the idea of becoming Your female friend, but the true sentiment of my heart is exclusively for a position as Your maidservant.” 
(Vilapa Kusumanjali 6—Raghunatha Das Goswami) 

“Oh Goddess Gāndharvike, in utter desperation I fall on the ground at Your feet like a stick and with a chocked voice I fully implore You to: ‘please be merciful to this foolish person and count me as one of Your own’.” 
(Śrī Gāndhavā Samprārthanāstakam 2—Śrīla Rupa Goswami) 

“Without worshiping the pollen of Śrī Rādhā’s lotus feet, without taking shelter of Vrindavana, which bears Her footprints, and without respectfully greeting the great souls whose hearts are filled with deep love for Her, how will one be able to plunge into the nectar ocean of love for Lord Kṛṣṇa?” 
(Śrī Stāvali—Sankalpa Prakasa Stotra 1—Raghunatha Das Goswami) 

“I worship Śrī Rādhā who has lotus eyes, I remember Śrī Rādhā who has a sweet smile, and I speak of Rādhā who is melted with compassion. In my life there is no other goal than Her service. She is my life and soul.” 
(Śrī Stāvali—Raghunatha Das Goswami) 

“Oh Śrimate Rādhārani, You are the exalted form of mahabhava [the highest pitch of transcendental sentiments], therefore You are the most dear to Kṛṣṇa. Oh Goddess, You alone are able to bestow pure love for the Supreme Lord; therefore I offer my humble obeisances unto You.” 
(Radhika Pranati 9) 

“Oh Srīmati Rādhikā, Oh queen of Vrindāvana, You are a river of nectarean mercy. Please mercifully bless me with the service of Your lotus feet.” 
(Hari Bhakti Vilasa—Śrīla Bhaktivinode Thakur) 

[Śrī Uddhava said:] “I repeatedly offer my respects to the dust from the feet of the women of Nanda Maharaja’s cowherd village. When these gopis loudly chant the glories of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the vibration purifies the three worlds.” 
(SB 10.47.63) 

“I am Yours! I am Yours! I cannot exist without You! Oh Goddess Rādhikā, please understand this and bring me to Your lotus feet.” 
(Śrī Stavāvali—Vilāpa Kusumānjali 96—Raghunatha Das Goswami)

IDX.translation_intro: Śrīla Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī Mahārāja chose these ślokas and arranged them into: Rādhā-tattva, Kṛṣṇa-tattva, and Gaura-tattva.
IDX.en_translation:
“Oh Rādhikā! The Supreme Enjoyer who wears a crown of peacock feathers, falls at the feet of Your maidservants and propitiates them with many humble and grief-stricken words to be allowed entrance into Your kuñja [where both of You engage in playful amorous pastimes]. Let me become just one stick in the broom used by Your female companions to clean the kuñja of that ocean of rasa, the daughter of Vrisabhanu Maharaja.” 
(Rādhā Rasa Sudha Nidhi 8—Śrī Prabhodhananda Sarasvatī) 

“Following in the footsteps of our previous Acharyas, I meditate upon the footdust of Śrīmati Rādhikā, whose unlimited power instantly controls the Supreme Person Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who is not easily seen even by great souls like Brahma, Shiva, Sukadeva, Narada Muni and Bhishma.” 
(Rādhā Rasa Sudha Nidhi 4—Śrī Prabhodhananda Sarasvatī) 

“When He feels the occasional waft of the supremely glorious and playful breeze that has raised the hem of Śrīmati Rādhikā’s garment, Madhusudana Kṛṣṇa, the instigator of honey-flavoured pastimes, whose service is the rarely attained goal of great yogis, considers that His life has become meaningful. Thus, let us bow down even to the direction of the land of Vrishabhanu Maharaja.” 
(Rādhā Rasa Sudha Nidhi 2—Śrī Prabhodhananda Sarasvatī) 

“Oh Goddess Rādhike! My solemn vow is that I shall never beg for anything except that most exalted direct service to Your lotus feet. I offer my constant obeisances to the idea of becoming Your female friend, but the true sentiment of my heart is exclusively for a position as Your maidservant.” 
(Vilapa Kusumanjali 6—Raghunatha Das Goswami) 

“Oh Goddess Gāndharvike, in utter desperation I fall on the ground at Your feet like a stick and with a chocked voice I fully implore You to: ‘please be merciful to this foolish person and count me as one of Your own’.” 
(Śrī Gāndhavā Samprārthanāstakam 2—Śrīla Rupa Goswami) 

“Without worshiping the pollen of Śrī Rādhā’s lotus feet, without taking shelter of Vrindavana, which bears Her footprints, and without respectfully greeting the great souls whose hearts are filled with deep love for Her, how will one be able to plunge into the nectar ocean of love for Lord Kṛṣṇa?” 
(Śrī Stāvali—Sankalpa Prakasa Stotra 1—Raghunatha Das Goswami) 

“I worship Śrī Rādhā who has lotus eyes, I remember Śrī Rādhā who has a sweet smile, and I speak of Rādhā who is melted with compassion. In my life there is no other goal than Her service. She is my life and soul.” 
(Śrī Stāvali—Raghunatha Das Goswami) 

“Oh Śrimate Rādhārani, You are the exalted form of mahabhava [the highest pitch of transcendental sentiments], therefore You are the most dear to Kṛṣṇa. Oh Goddess, You alone are able to bestow pure love for the Supreme Lord; therefore I offer my humble obeisances unto You.” 
(Radhika Pranati 9) 

“Oh Srīmati Rādhikā, Oh queen of Vrindāvana, You are a river of nectarean mercy. Please mercifully bless me with the service of Your lotus feet.” 
(Hari Bhakti Vilasa—Śrīla Bhaktivinode Thakur) 

[Śrī Uddhava said:] “I repeatedly offer my respects to the dust from the feet of the women of Nanda Maharaja’s cowherd village. When these gopis loudly chant the glories of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the vibration purifies the three worlds.” 
(SB 10.47.63) 

“I am Yours! I am Yours! I cannot exist without You! Oh Goddess Rādhikā, please understand this and bring me to Your lotus feet.” 
(Śrī Stavāvali—Vilāpa Kusumānjali 96—Raghunatha Das Goswami) 

“I meditate upon that Śrī Dāmodara — whose dark bodily lustre is millions of times more beautiful than the blue lotus flower, whose brilliant yellow silken garments rebuke the radiance of golden Kunkuma, whose residence is Śrī Vrindāvana Dhama, whose chest is beautified by a swinging vaijayantī garland, and whose splendorous left hand rests upon the right shoulder of Śrīmati Rādhika.” 
(Stavamala—Śrīla Rupa Goswami) 

“I worship Govinda, Whose complexion is the colour of a blossoming blue lotus. His face is like the moon, and He is fond of wearing a peacock feather on His crown. His chest bears the mark of Śrīvatsa and is adorned with the Kaustubha gem. He wears beautiful yellow garments, and His handsome form is worshiped by the gopis’ sidelong glances. His companions are the multitudes of cows and cowherd boys. He plays sweet melodies on the flute, and His body is decorated with glittering ornaments.” 
(Padyavali 46—Śrīla Rupa Goswami) 

“His forehead is decorated with musk tilaka, the Kaustubha jewel rests upon His broad chest, and an exquisite pearl hangs from the tip of His nose. The flute gracefully rests in His lotus hands and bracelets adorn His wrists. His entire form is anointed with chandana paste, and a necklace of pearls graces His attentive neck. All glories to the crest jewel of the gopas, Whom is surrounded by all the young vraja-gopis.” 
(Śrī Krishna Karnamrutham 2.108—Bilva Mangala Thakur) 

“Syamasundara is entering the forest of Vrindavana accompanied by His cowherd boyfriends. He wears a peacock feather in His turban, a yellow karnikara flower on His ears, a yellow-gold garment and a victory garland strung with five kinds of fragrant forest flowers. Thus He displays His form as the greatest of dancers. The nectar of His lips flows through the holes of the flute [and thus the glorious vibrations of His flute-song echoes throughout the forest groves]. Singing His glories, the cowherd boys follow from behind. In this way, Śrī Vrindavana-dhama [which is more charming than Vaikuntha], becomes delighted by the touch of His lotus feet.” 
(Venu Gita 5—SB 10.21.5) 

“Kṛṣṇa’s complexion is blackish-blue hue like a water-laden raincloud, and His splendid cloth, appears like a flash of lightning. Cresting his head is a peacock feather, and each limb of His body is decorated with exquisite patterns of paint made from coloured forest minerals. Springs of new leaves and blossoms adorn His body, and upon His neck an enchanting forest-flower garland of five colours hands down to His knees. Attired in this way like a dramatic dancer, He rests one hand on His friend’s shoulder, and with the other twirls a pastime lotus [as if to twirl our hearts]. Lilies grace His ears, curly locks of hair splash against His cheeks, and His lotus face blossoms with a gentle smile.” 
(SB 10.23.22—Kṛṣṇa’s description by Mathura’s Dvija-patnis) 

“Oh Master, in the entire universe, only You are worthy of being praised. Oh Vrajendra-nandana, son of the King of Vraja, Your body, appearing like a fresh rain-cloud, is adorned with a yellow cloth that glistens like lightening and appears amazingly brilliant. Because You are wearing makara [dolphin]-shaped earrings and a peacock feather on Your head, Your lotus face radiates an uncommon splendour. Around Your neck is a garland made of innumerable kinds of forest flowers and leaves. Tucked under Your arm are a herding stick and a buffalo horn. Your flute, which is tied by Your waist-belt, looks very beautiful. In Your lovely, soft hands is a morsel of yoghurt and rice. Even You are attracted by this cowherd boy attire of Yours. I simply fall to the ground like a stick again and again at Your feet, which are softer than lotuses and which are marked with all the auspicious signs.” 
(SB 10.4.1—Lord Brahma’s glorification to Kṛṣṇa) 

[Lord Brahma said:] “Therefore, Oh Bhagavan, You manifest Yourself in the hearts of Your devotees, who have received merely a slight trace of the mercy of Your lotus feet. Thus they become blessed and are the only ones who can understand the tattva [absolute truth] of the glory of Your transcendental form, composed of eternality, knowledge and bliss. Even after long-term enthusiastic endeavour in practices such as gyana and vairagya [knowledge and renunciation], a person can never actually know Your glories.” 
(SB 10.14.29) 

“My dear Lord, I therefore pray to be so fortunate that in this life as Lord Brahma or in another life, wherever I take my birth, I may be counted as one of Your devotees. I pray that wherever I may be, even among the animal species, I can engage in devotional service to Your lotus feet.” 
(SB 10.14.30) 

[Narada Muni continued:] “My dear Maharaja Yudhisthira, all of you [the Pandavas] are extremely fortunate, for the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, lives in your palace just like a human being. Great saintly persons know this very well, and therefore they constantly visit this house.” 
(SB 7.10.48) 

“Oh Shyāmasundara! Oh You whose head is adorned with peacock feathers! Your face is always graced with a playful smile, Your flute-playing is enchanting, and You are expert in relishing rasa with Śrīmati Rādhika. Because You are an ocean of mercy, I am appealing to You to please make me a kinkari [maidservant] at the lotus feet of Your beloved.” 
(Śrī Rādhā Prārthanā 2—Śrī Vitthalacharya) 

“How greatly fortunate are Nanda Maharaja, the cowherd men and all the other inhabitants of Vrajabhumi! There is no limit to their good fortune, because the Absolute Truth, the source of transcendental bliss, the eternal Supreme Brahma, has become their friend.” 
(SB 10.14.32) 

“What great auspicious activities did Nanda Baba perform? And what did Yashoda-maiya do that Śrī Hari sucked the milk of her breasts?” 
(SB 10.8.46) 

“I offer obeisances to Sacinandana, the son of Jagannatha Misra, and to His putras [His three sons], Kavi Karnapura Gosvami, Raghunandana Thakura, and Jiva Gosvami. These three boys were offered to the lotus feet of Mahaprabhu in their infancy by their mothers and fathers. Therefore, they are accepted as the sons of Mahaprabhu. The parents knew that if you offer your child to someone like Mahaprabhu, to the Lord or His devotees, then that child’s life will be perfect and successful.” 
(Chaitanya Bhagavata 1.1.2—Śrīla Jiva Goswami) 

“Let me offer my respectful obeisances unto Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahaprabhu, who is always pleased to accept anything given with faith and love by His devotees and is always ready to bestow mercy upon them.” 
(CC ant 10.1) 

“Let me offer my respectful obeisances unto Lord Śrī Caitanya Mahaprabhu, who is the Supreme Personality of God-head. He is the ocean of mercy who has appeared in Gaudadesha to give devotional service in ecstatic love without undesirable things.” 
(Anonymous) 

“I offer my humble obeisance again and again to that great soul who is known as Visvambhara [maintainer of the universe], Gaura, Chaitanya, Sachi-putra, the Husband of Laksmi and the Friend of All.” 
(Śrī Gaura Govindarcana Smarana Paddhati—Śrīla Dhyanacandra Gosvami) 

“Oh glorious adolescent moon of Śrī Navadvipa! Oh Lord of Śrī, Visvambhara. You are the king of all the Nagaras [flirtatious romantics]! Oh darling child of mother Sachi. Although You are stealing my mind, I know very well that You are Visnupriya’s golden Pranesvara [the master of her vital airs].” 
(Śrī Prabhodananda Sarasvatī) 

“I offer obeisances unto Śrī Chaitanya Chandra, whose form is the embodiment of blissful, transcendental pastimes, whose golden complexion is divinely beautiful, and who bestows unlimited nectar in prema-rasa [mellows love].” 
(Archana Diipika—Śrīla Bhaktivinode Thakur) 

“Let me take shelter of the Supreme Personality of God-head, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who has descended in the form of Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu to teach us real knowledge, His devotional service, and detachment from whatever does not foster Kṛṣṇa consciousness. He has descended because He is an ocean of transcendental mercy. Let me surrender unto His lotus feet.” 
(CC mad 6.254— Chaitanya Chandrodaya Nātaka) 

“Glory, glory to the divine womb of Mother Sachi! Glory, glory to the religious principles of giving loving devotional service to all! Glory, glory to the movable mountain that’s the abode of Śrī Gaura! Glory, glory to the Holy Name of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Chaitanya which bestows unlimited wealth [of prema-rasa]!” 
(Anonymous) 

“I have fallen into the ocean of birth and death, which is full of misery, and I am being devoured by the crocodiles and sharks of lust, anger, greed, and so forth. Furthermore, I am chained by wicked desires. Oh merciful Lord, my other request is that, after destroying the dense darkness of my offences, You make this miserable person drink the nectar of Your feet.” 
(Śrī Chaitanya Chandramrita 54—Śrī Prabhodananda Sarasvatī) 

“May Śrī Sachinanda Gaurahari, be brilliantly situated in the innermost core of your hearts. Resplendid with the radiance of molten gold, He has appeared in the age of Kali by His causeless mercy to bestow what no other incarnation has ever offered before—unnatojjvala-rasa, the most sublime and radiant mellow of devotional service in paramour love—manjari bhava, service to Śrīmati Rādhikā as Her confidential maidservants.” 
(CC adi 1.4 & Śrī Vidagdha Mādhava) 

“Śrīmati Rādhikā is Kṛṣṇa’s hladini-shakti [pleasure giving potency] and the embodiment of the transformation His pranaya [intimate love]. Since They are eka-atma-svarupa [one soul], She is intrinsically non-different from Kṛṣṇa and one in identity with Him. However, to enjoy the transcendental pleasure of Their loving pastimes, Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa have eternally manifested Themselves in these two apparently separate forms. Now these two transcendental identities, sevya and sevaka [the recipient of service and the expert servant], visaya-tattva and ashraya-tattva [the absolute enjoyer and the absolute source of shelter], have manifested in one svarupa (body) as Śrī Chaitanya Tattva. I repeatedly bow down to Sachinandanā who is the svarupa [form] of Kṛṣṇa and who is adorned with the bhava [internal emotions] of Śrīmati Rādhikā.” 
(CC adi 1.5—Śrī Svarupa Dāmodara’s Kadacha) 

“Desiring to understand the glory of Śrīmati Rādhikā’s mahimā [greatest love], the wonderful sweetness in Him that She alone relishes through Her madhurimā [wonderfully sweet love], and the happiness She feels when She relishes the sweetness of His saukhyam [joyous love], the Supreme Lord Hari, richly endowed with Her emotions, appeared from the womb of Śrīmati Sachi Devi, as the moon appears from the ocean.” 
(CC adi 1.6)

yugala smṛtisāra sādhya sādhana ei, āra nāi ihā boi, ei tattva sarvatattva-sāra jalada sundara-kānti, madhura madhura bhāti, vaidagadhi-avadhi suveśha supīta vasana dhara, ābharaṇa maṇivara, mayūra-chandrakā karu keśha mṛgamada suchandana, kuṅkumādi vilepana, mugdhakārī mūrati tribhaṅga navīna-kusumāvalī, śhrīaṅge śhobhaye bhāli, madhulobhe fire matta bhṛṅga īṣat madhurasmita, vaidagadhi-līlāmṛta, lubadhala vrajavadhūvṛnda charaṇa-kamala-para, maṇimaya sumañjīra, nakhamaṇi jini’ bālachandra nūpura-marāla-dhvani, kulavadhū-marālinī, śhuniyā rahite nāre ghare hṛdaye bāḍhaye rati, jena mile pati satī, kulera dharama jāya dūre kṛṣṇamukha-dvijarāje, saralā vaṁśhī virāje, jāra dhvani bhuvana mātāya śhravaṇera patha diyā, hṛdaye praveśha hañā, prāṇa ādi ākarṣi’ ānaya govinda-sevana satya, tāṅhāra sevaka nitya, vṛndāvana bhūmi tejomaya tāhāre yamunājala, kare nitya jhalamala, tāra tīre aṣṭa kuñja haya śhītala kiraṇa kara, kalpataru-guṇadhara, tarulatā ṣaḍṛtu-sevā pūrṇachandrasama jyoti, chidānandamaya mūrti, mahānanda daraśhana lobhā govinda ānandamaya, nikaṭe vanitāchaya, vihare madhura ati śhobhā dūhu preme ḍagamagi, dūhe dohā anurāgī, dūhu rūpe dūhu manolobhā vrajapura-vanitāra, charaṇa āśhraya sāra, kara mana ekānta kariyā anya bola gaṇḍagola, nāhi śhuna utarola, rākha prema hṛdaye bhariyā kṛṣṇa prabhu ekabāra, karibena aṅgīkāra, jena’ mana e satya vachana dhanya līlā vṛndāvana, rādhā-kṛṣṇa śhrī-charaṇa, dhanya sakhī mañjarīra gaṇa pāpa-puṇyamaya deha, sakala anitya eha’, dhana jana saba micḣā dhanda marile jāibe kothā, tāhāte nā pāo vyathā, tabu kārya kara sadā manda rājāra je rājyapāṭa, jena nāṭuyāra nāṭa, dekhite dekhite kicḣu naya hena māyā kare jei, parama īśhvara sei, tāṅre mana sadā kara bhaya pāpe nā kariha mana, adhama se pāpijana, tāre mana dūre parihari’ puṇya se sukhera dhāma, tāra nā loio nāma, ‘puṇya’, ‘mukti’ dui tyāga kari’ premabhakti-sudhānidhi, tāhe ḍuba niravadhi, āra jata kṣāranidhi prāya nirantara sukha pābe, sakala santāpa jābe, paratattva karile upāya anyera paraśha jena, nāhi haya kadāchana, ihāte hoibe sāvadhāna rādhā-kṛṣṇa nāma gāna, ei se parama dhyāna, āra nā kariha paramāṇa karmī, jñānī, micḣābhakta, nā ha’be tāya anurakta, śhuddhabhajanete kara mana vraja-janera jei mata, tāhe habe anugata, ei se parama tattvadhana prārthanā kariba sadā, śhuddhabhāve premakathā, nāma-mantre kariyā abheda āstika kariyā mana, bhaja rāṅgā śhrī-charaṇa, granthipāpa habe pariccḣeda rādhā-kṛṣṇa-śhrī-charaṇa, mātra paramārtha-dhana, sayatane hṛdayete loo dūhu nāma śhuni’ śhuni’, bhaktamukhe puni puni, parama ānanda sukha pāṅa hemagauratanu rāi, āṅkhi daraśhana chāi, rodana karaye abhilāṣe jaladhara ḍhara ḍhara, aṅga ati manohara, rūpete bhuvana parakāśhe sakhīgaṇa chāripāśhe, sevā kare abhilāṣe, parama se śhobhāsukha dhare ei mane āśhā mora, aicḣe rase hañā bhora, narottama sadāi vihare
IDX.en_translation:
May my devotion and love be always bound to the feet of the Divine Couple, the highest happiness. The names of Kṛṣṇa and Rādhā are the abode of devotional mellows; I fall at Their feet in supreme bliss. 

The remembrance of the mind is life’s most precious possession; sweet are Their names—the essence of the Divine Couple’s playful pastimes. This is the means and the goal; there is nothing beyond this truth, which is the essence of all truths. 

With a beautiful cloud-like complexion and sweet radiance, Kṛṣṇa is adorned in beautiful garments with supreme artistry. He wears brilliant yellow clothes and the best of jewels, and His hair is decorated with peacock feathers. 

Scented with musk, sandalwood paste, and vermilion, His enchanting form is bent in three places. Adorned with fresh flower garlands that beautify His divine body, intoxicated bees hover about Him, greedy for honey. 

A slight, sweet smile—the nectar of His expert divine pastimes—enchants the damsels of Vraja. Upon His lotus feet are jeweled ankle bells, and His fingernails are brighter than the crescent moon. 

Hearing the sound of His ankle bells, which is like the sound of swans, the chaste village women—like female swans themselves—cannot remain in their homes. Devotion grows in their hearts, as if husband and wife are meeting, and all worldly duties are cast aside. 

On Kṛṣṇa’s moon-like face, a simple flute shines, its sound intoxicating the universe. Entering through the path of the ears and into the heart, it attracts and brings forth the very life force. 

Serving Govinda is the truth, and His servants are eternal. The land of Vṛndāvana is effulgent, and the waters of the Yamunā always sparkle there; on its banks are eight groves. 

Cool rays of light shine there, and the trees and creepers possess the qualities of wish-fulfilling trees, offering service through the six seasons. His form is full of spiritual bliss and luminous like the full moon; I long to behold that great bliss. 

Govinda is full of joy, surrounded by groups of women; His pastimes are sweet and exceedingly beautiful. Both are overflowing with love and devoted to each other, captivated by each other’s beauty. 

The shelter of the feet of the women of Vraja is the essence; make your mind exclusive to them. Do not listen to other clamors and disturbances; keep love filled in your heart. 

Kṛṣṇa, the Master, will accept you; know this, O mind, for it is a true statement. Glorious are the pastimes of Vṛndāvana and the sacred feet of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa! Glorious are the companions and their attendants! 

This body, full of sin and piety, everything is temporary; wealth and people are all false illusions. Where will you go after death? You feel no pain about it, yet you always do evil deeds. 

The kingdom of a king is like an actor’s play; while you watch it, it becomes nothing. He who creates such illusion is the Supreme Lord; fear Him always, O mind. 

Do not set your mind on sin, for those who are sinful are degraded; cast them far away from your mind. Piety is the abode of happiness, but do not even utter its name; abandon both “piety” and “liberation.” 

Dive constantly into the nectar-ocean of loving devotion; all other oceans are like salty water. You will attain continuous happiness and all your distress will vanish if you make the Supreme Truth your means. 

May there never be contact with those who are not devotees; be careful in this regard. Singing the names of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa is the supreme meditation; do not do anything else, even a tiny bit. 

Do not be attached to fruitive workers, speculative philosophers, or false devotees; fix your mind on pure devotion. Follow the path of the people of Vraja; this is the supreme treasure of truth. 

Always pray for pure loving talks, considering the Name and the mantra as non-different from God. With a faithful mind, worship the beautiful red feet, and the knot of sin will be severed. 

The sacred feet of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa alone are the ultimate treasure; take them carefully into your heart. Hearing Their names again and again from the mouths of devotees, one attains supreme bliss and happiness. 

I desire to see the golden-complexioned Rādhā; I cry with longing. 

Like a fresh cloud, His form is most captivating, and His beauty illuminates the universe. 

The companions around her serve her with longing, holding that supreme beauty and happiness. This is my heart’s hope; immersed in such mellows, Narottama always sports.
